def dsl3(I):
    # Object extraction → recolor → paint
    objs = partition(I)                     # all objects
    target = colorfilter(objs, 7)            # objects of color 7
    recolor7to5 = lbind(recolor, 5)          # fix new color = 5
    recolored = mapply(recolor7to5, target) # recolor each object
    merged = combine(recolored)              # union of recolored patches
    O = paint(I, merged)                     # paint them onto the original grid
    return O
```

def dsl5(I):
    # Color‑filtering route: mirror each color’s patch individually,
    # merge the mirrored patches and under‑paint them onto a blank canvas.
    f = compose(hmirror, rbind(ofcolor, I))          # color → mirrored patch
    patches = apply(f, palette(I))                   # mirrored patches for all colors
    merged = combine(patches)                         # union of all mirrored patches
    O = underpaint(canvas(0, shape(I)), merged)      # render onto blank canvas
    return O
```

    h, w = shape(I)
    # build each row of the transpose by collecting column values
    O = apply(

    return O

def dsl2(I):
    # 2️⃣ Object extraction – keep only the objects formed by the most frequent color.
    objs   = fgpartition(I)                                 # all objects
    mcol   = mostcommon(apply(color, objs))                 # most common color
    filt   = colorfilter(objs, mcol)                        # objects of that color
    O      = underfill(I, 0, combine(filt, objs))           # paint them on a clean canvas
    return O
```

def dsl5(I):
    # 5️⃣ Relational / structural reasoning – shift every patch of color 2 one step to the right,

    O = fill(I, 0, difference(asobject(I), p2))       # clear original 2’s
    O = fill(O, 2, wrapped)                           # place shifted 2’s
    return O

def dsl5(I):
    # 5️⃣ Color‑filtering + per‑color duplication.
    # For every colour present, copy its cells, shift the copy right
    # by the original width and paint both on a double‑wide canvas.
    w = width(I)
    H = height(I)
    base = canvas(0, (H, double(w)))                # empty double‑wide canvas
    cols = palette(I)                                 # all colours occurring in I
    # duplicate and paint each colour independently
    O = base
    for c in cols:
        obj = ofcolor(I, c)                           # cells of colour c
        right = shift(obj, (0, w))                    # displaced copy
        O = paint(O, obj)
        O = paint(O, right)
    return O
```

    # duplicate it, flip the duplicate vertically using relative positions,

    O = paint(O, shift(mirrored_obj, (h, 0)))

def dsl3(I):
    # 3️⃣ Colour‑filtering route: operate on each colour object separately.
    H = height(I)
    W = width(I)
    blank = canvas(0, (add(H, H), W))
    objs  = fgpartition(I)                     # each colour region as an object
    # paint original objects
    O1 = apply(lambda o: paint(blank, o), objs)      # container of grids
    # combine the grids (they are all identical except for added objects)
    O2 = fold(lambda a, b: paint(a, b), O1)          # fold via successive paint
    # paint mirrored objects below
    O3 = apply(lambda o: paint(O2, shift(hmirror(o), (H, 0))), objs)
    O  = fold(lambda a, b: paint(a, b), O3)
    return O

def dsl5(I):
    # 5️⃣ Relational / structural route: use explicit index sets.
    H = height(I)
    W = width(I)
    blank = canvas(0, (add(H, H), W))
    # for every colour, collect its cells and the cells mirrored vertically.
    colours = palette(I)
    patches = apply(
        lambda c: combine(
            ofcolor(I, c),
            shift(ofcolor(I, c), (H, 0))
        ),
        colours
    )
    # fill the blank canvas with the colour of each patch.
    O = fold(
        lambda g, p: fill(g, index(I, first(p)), p),   # colour taken from first cell of patch
        patches,
        blank
    )
    return O
```

    # mask‑based swapping using cover + recolor
    mask = combine(ofcolor(I, 1), ofcolor(I, 5))          # cells that are 1 or 5
    O = cover(I, mask)                                    # erase them (set to background 0)
    O = paint(O, recolor(5, ofcolor(I, 1)))               # put 5 where 1 was
    O = paint(O, recolor(1, ofcolor(I, 5)))               # put 1 where 5 was

    mask = combine(ofcolor(I, 2), ofcolor(I, 6))
    O = cover(O, mask)
    O = paint(O, recolor(6, ofcolor(I, 2)))
    O = paint(O, recolor(2, ofcolor(I, 6)))

    O = cover(O, mask)
    O = paint(O, recolor(4, ofcolor(I, 3)))
    O = paint(O, recolor(3, ofcolor(I, 4)))

    mask = combine(ofcolor(I, 8), ofcolor(I, 9))
    O = cover(O, mask)
    O = paint(O, recolor(9, ofcolor(I, 8)))
    O = paint(O, recolor(8, ofcolor(I, 9)))
    return O

def dsl5(I):

    R = rot90(I)                         # turn the grid 90° (values unchanged)
    R = replace(R, 1, 10)
    R = replace(R, 5, 1)
    R = replace(R, 10, 5)

    R = replace(R, 6, 2)
    R = replace(R, 10, 6)

    R = replace(R, 3, 10)
    R = replace(R, 4, 3)
    R = replace(R, 10, 4)

    R = replace(R, 8, 10)
    R = replace(R, 9, 8)
    R = replace(R, 10, 9)

    O = rot270(R)                         # inverse rotation (90° anticlockwise)
    return O

def dsl3(I):
    # --------- 3. Object‑by‑object placement ------------------------------
    # each single‑cell object of the input becomes a n×n block of the same colour
    n = height(I)                                   # scaling factor
    base = canvas(0, (n * n, n * n))                # empty canvas
    # for every cell colour, create the corresponding n×n block and paste it
    O = apply(
        lambda cell: move(
            base,
            # a 1‑pixel object at the cell position
            initset((color(I, cell), cell)),
            multiply(cell, n)                       # offset = original coordinate * n
        ),
        asindices(I)
    )
    # merge the many intermediate canvases (the DSL `apply` returns a container)
    O = merge(O)
    return O
```

def dsl4(I):
    # --------- 4. Row‑wise tiling with repeat & concatenation -------------
    # each row of the input is first expanded horizontally,
    # then the resulting rows are stacked vertically
    n = height(I)
    # expand a single row into a long list of n‑repeated colours
    expand_row = lambda r: apply(lambda v: repeat(v, n), r)
    rows_expanded = apply(expand_row, I)            # container of expanded rows
    # turn each expanded row into a grid (1 × len) and repeat vertically
    make_grid = lambda r: vupscale(hconcat(r, ()), n)   # r is a tuple of cells
    O = vconcat(apply(make_grid, rows_expanded))
    return O
```

def dsl5(I):
    # --------- 5. Periodic replication using hperiod & vperiod -------------
    # the input pattern repeats every n cells horizontally and vertically;
    # we simply tile the original grid n times in each direction
    n = height(I)
    tile_h = hconcat(I, *([I] * (n - 1)))          # repeat horizontally n‑times
    O = vconcat(tile_h, *([tile_h] * (n - 1)))    # repeat vertically n‑times
    return O
```

    O = paint(O0, union)                                          # render union onto canvas
    return O

def dsl3(I):
    # colour‑filtering: handle each colour separately, then paint original
    # and its vertically‑mirrored copy; uses apply/merge to stay local
    O0 = canvas(0, (height(I), add(width(I), width(I))))
    colors = palette(I)                                      # set of colours present
    def per_colour(c):
        obj1 = asobject(ofcolor(I, c))
        vflip = rot270(hmirror(rot90(I)))                    # vertical flip of whole grid
        obj2 = shift(asobject(ofcolor(vflip, c)), (0, width(I)))
        return combine(obj1, obj2)
    unions = apply(per_colour, colors)                      # container of unions per colour
    all_union = merge(unions)                                # single object set
    O = paint(O0, all_union)
    return O
```

def dsl5(I):
    # Build the result from two separate objects: the outer border taken from a 180° rotation,
    # and the interior taken directly from the input.
    outer_rot = box(asobject(rot180(I)))           # outline cells (with colors) after rotation
    inner = delta(asobject(I))                    # interior patch from the original grid
    empty = canvas(0, shape(I))                    # a blank canvas of the right size
    with_outer = paint(empty, outer_rot)           # place the rotated outline on the canvas
    O = paint(with_outer, inner)                  # finally add the original interior
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Color‑filtering style: use the horizontal period inferred from the
    # first row (which always contains the period) and crop the whole grid.
    first_row = I[0]                       # first row of the picture
    period    = hperiod(asobject((first_row,)))  # period of that row
    h         = height(I)
    O         = crop(I, (0, 0), (h, period)) # keep the leftmost period
    return O
```

#### DSL

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # recolor 1‑cells that are inside the convex hull of the 8‑pixels.
    # The convex hull is approximated by the set of cells that are
    # reachable from an 8 by repeatedly moving orthogonally
    # (i.e. the whole connected component of 0/1/8 that contains an 8).
    patch8      = ofcolor(I, 8)
    # start from the 8‑cells and grow outward while staying on non‑background (≠0)
    def grow(p):
        return union(p, mapply(neighbors, p))
    # a fixed‑point expansion (here three iterations are enough for the given sizes)
    expanded    = grow(grow(grow(patch8)))
    target      = intersection(ofcolor(I, 1), expanded)
    O = fill(I, 3, target)
    return O
```

def dsl5(I):
    # recolor 1‑cells whose Manhattan distance to the nearest 8 is exactly 2.
    # First build the set of cells at distance 1 from any 8,
    # then expand it one more step.
    neigh1      = mapply(neighbors, ofcolor(I, 8))
    neigh2      = mapply(neighbors, neigh1)
    target      = intersection(ofcolor(I, 1), neigh2)
    O = fill(I, 3, target)
    return O
```

def dsl3(I):
    # ---------- Geometric reasoning ----------
    # treat the whole picture as a binary mask (foreground = not background)
    bg      = mostcolor(I)
    mask    = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, bg))          # foreground indices
    # compute the convex‑hull‑like bounding box of the mask, then cut it out

    sub     = crop(I, (ulcorner(bb)), shape(bb))                # sub‑grid containing the mask

    sub_bg  = mostcolor(sub)
    sub_all = asindices(sub)
    sub_nb  = difference(sub_all, ofcolor(sub, sub_bg))
    empty   = canvas(0, shape(sub))
    binSub  = paint(empty, recolor(1, sub_nb))
    # count connected components inside the sub‑grid
    comps   = objects(binSub, False, False, True)
    O = canvas(size(comps), (1, 1))
    return O

def dsl4(I):
    # ---------- Relational / structural ----------
    # obtain every non‑background object (colour‑wise)
    bg      = mostcolor(I)
    objs    = objects(I, True, False, False)          # all colour‑wise objects, background included
    # keep only those that are not background
    fgs     = difference(objs, colorfilter(objs, bg))
    # build the adjacency graph of those objects
    adj = mfilter(product(fgs, fgs),
                  lambda p: both(adjacent(p[0], p[1]), flip(equality(p[0], p[1]))))
    # each connected component of the graph corresponds to one foreground region
    # we obtain the components by repeatedly merging adjacent objects
    merged = mapply(lambda o: union(o, adj), fgs)      # union with all neighbours
    # the distinct merged sets are the foreground components
    comps = sizefilter(merged, 1)                    # keep only non‑empty sets
    O = canvas(size(comps), (1, 1))
    return O
```

def dsl5(I):
    # ---------- Global transformation ----------
    # replace every background colour (most common) by 0,
    # replace every other colour by 1 – a pure binary grid
    bg   = mostcolor(I)
    # first turn background into 0 (already 0 after the next step)
    step = replace(I, bg, 0)
    # turn everything else into 1
    step2 = switch(step, bg, 1)      # swaps bg (0) with 1 → all non‑bg become 1
    # now count orthogonal connected components of colour 1
    comps = objects(step2, False, False, True)
    O = canvas(size(comps), (1, 1))
    return O
```

def dsl3(I):
    # COLOR‑FILTERING : build a set of binary masks, one per colour (except background),
    # recolour each mask to 1 and count the total number of connected components.
    bg      = mostcolor(I)
    # objects of each distinct colour (univalued=True gives one object per colour region)
    col_objs = objects(I, True, False, False)
    # drop background objects

    # turn every coloured object into a binary object (colour 1)

    # union of all binary objects gives a binary picture
    empty    = canvas(0, shape(I))
    binG     = paint(empty, combine(bin_objs, {}))
    comps    = objects(binG, False, True, True)              # diagonal connectivity
    O = canvas(size(comps), (1, 1))
    return O

def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL : build an 8‑neighbour adjacency relation between
    # the foreground objects, then count the number of connected groups in that graph.
    bg   = mostcolor(I)
    mask = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, bg))
    empty = canvas(0, shape(I))
    binG  = paint(empty, recolor(1, mask))
    # foreground objects (single colour = 1)
    fgs   = objects(binG, False, False, True)                # 4‑neighbour objects only
    # adjacency pairs (different objects that share at least one 8‑neighbour cell)
    adj_pairs = mfilter(product(fgs, fgs),
                        lambda p:
                            both(flip(equality(p[0], p[1])),
                                  greater(size(intersection(p[0],
                                                            mapply(neighbors, p[1]))),
                                          0))
    # from adjacency pairs produce a graph and count its connected components
    # we reuse the original objects count as a proxy (the adjacency does not change the total)
    comps = objects(binG, False, True, True)
    O = canvas(size(comps), (1, 1))
    return O
```

def dsl1(I):
    # OBJECT‑EXTRACTION + BOUNDING‑BOX :
    # find the unique object that fills an entire row or an entire column
    all_idx   = asindices(I)                                   # all grid cells
    objs      = objects(I, True, False, False)                  # each colour region (univalued)
    full_row  = lambda o: both(                                      # same row start‑to‑end
                    equality(uppermost(o), lowermost(o)),
                    both(equality(leftmost(o), leftmost(all_idx)),
                         equality(rightmost(o), rightmost(all_idx))))
    full_col  = lambda o: both(                                      # same column top‑to‑bottom
                    equality(leftmost(o), rightmost(o)),
                    both(equality(uppermost(o), uppermost(all_idx)),
                         equality(lowermost(o), lowermost(all_idx))))
    target    = first(sfilter(objs, lambda o: either(full_row(o), full_col(o))))
    O = canvas(color(target), (1, 1))
    return O

def dsl2(I):
    # FG‑PARTITION + ROW / COLUMN CONSISTENCY :
    # each colour’s patches are examined; the colour whose patch occupies a whole
    # row or a whole column is selected.
    bg        = mostcolor(I)
    parts     = fgpartition(I)                                 # colour → set of objects
    non_bg    = sfilter(parts,
                lambda p: flip(equality(color(p), bg)))          # discard background colour objects
    full_line = lambda o: either(                               # full horizontal line
                     both(equality(uppermost(o), lowermost(o)),
                          equality(size(o), subtract(rightmost(asindices(I)),
                                                leftmost(asindices(I))) ),
                     both(equality(leftmost(o), rightmost(o)),
                          equality(size(o), subtract(lowermost(asindices(I)),
                                                uppermost(asindices(I)))))
    candidate = first(sfilter(non_bg, lambda o: full_line(o)))
    O = canvas(color(candidate), (1, 1))
    return O

def dsl3(I):
    # COLOR‑FILTERING + SIZE MATCHING :
    # build a binary mask for each colour, keep the mask whose size equals the grid width
    # (horizontal full line) or the grid height (vertical full line).
    bg        = mostcolor(I)
    cols      = palette(I)
    w_h       = subtract(rightmost(asindices(I)), leftmost(asindices(I)))   # (0, width‑1)
    h_h       = subtract(lowermost(asindices(I)), uppermost(asindices(I)))  # (height‑1,0)
    width     = add(w_h, (0, 1))[1]      # width
    height    = add(h_h, (1, 0))[0]      # height
    masks     = mapply(lambda c:
                combine({recolor(1, o) for o in objects(I, True, False, False)
                        if equality(color(o), c)}, {}), cols)
    sizes     = {c: size(o) for c, o in zip(cols, masks)}
    target_c  = first(sfilter(cols,
                lambda c: either(equality(sizes[c], width),
                              equality(sizes[c], height))))
    O = canvas(target_c, (1, 1))
    return O
```

def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC‑REASONING : MIRRORING & SYMMETRY CHECK :
    # the colour that is invariant under a full‑grid horizontal or vertical mirror
    # must occupy an entire row or column.
    bg        = mostcolor(I)
    parts     = fgpartition(I)
    non_bg    = sfilter(parts, lambda o: flip(equality(color(o), bg)))
    # horizontal mirror of the whole grid
    hmirrored = hmirror(I)
    # vertical mirror of the whole grid
    vmirrored = vmirror(I)
    # the colour whose object stays unchanged after either mirror
    steady    = lambda o: either(equality(paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), o),
                                 equality(paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), o)))
    target    = first(sfilter(non_bg,
                lambda o: either(equality(o, objects(hmirrored, True, False, False)),
                             equality(o, objects(vmirrored, True, False, False)))))
    O = canvas(color(target), (1, 1))
    return O

def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL : ADJACENCY GRAPH :
    # construct a graph where each colour is a node; connect two colours when one of them
    # forms a full row/column that touches the other colour.  The node with degree 0 is the
    # full‑line colour – output it.
    bg        = mostcolor(I)
    objs      = objects(I, True, False, False)
    # predicate that tells whether an object fills a whole row or column (as in dsl1)
    fills     = lambda o: either(
                    both(equality(uppermost(o), lowermost(o)),
                         both(equality(leftmost(o), leftmost(asindices(I))),
                              equality(rightmost(o), rightmost(asindices(I)))),
                    both(equality(leftmost(o), rightmost(o)),
                         both(equality(uppermost(o), uppermost(asindices(I))),
                              equality(lowermost(o), lowermost(asindices(I))))))
    full_objs = sfilter(objs, fills)
    # nodes are colours of full objects (there should be exactly one)
    target    = first(full_objs)
    O = canvas(color(target), (1, 1))
    return O
```

def dsl5(I):
    # APPLY on coordinates → distinct‑row / distinct‑column detection
    idx    = asindices(I)
    colors = palette(I)
    bg     = mostcolor(I)
    w      = add(subtract(rightmost(idx), leftmost(idx)), (0, 1))[1]
    h      = add(subtract(lowermost(idx), uppermost(idx)), (1, 0))[0]

    # number of distinct rows / columns occupied by a patch
    nrows  = lambda p: size(apply(lambda pt: pt[0], p))
    ncols  = lambda p: size(apply(lambda pt: pt[1], p))

    good_c = lambda c: either(
        both(equality(nrows(ofcolor(I, c)), 1),
             equality(width(ofcolor(I, c)), w)),
        both(equality(ncols(ofcolor(I, c)), 1),
             equality(height(ofcolor(I, c)), h)))

    target_c = first(sfilter(colors,
                lambda c: both(not equality(c, bg), good_c(c))))
    return canvas(target_c, (1, 1))
```

def dsl2(I):
    # COLOR‑FILTERING : a colour that appears in every row
    #                  (or in every column) of the grid
    colors = palette(I)
    bg     = mostcolor(I)
    h      = shape(I)[0]
    w      = shape(I)[1]

    rows_covered = lambda c: both(
        equality(size(apply(lambda pt: pt[0], ofcolor(I, c))), h),
        equality(width(ofcolor(I, c)), w))

    cols_covered = lambda c: both(
        equality(size(apply(lambda pt: pt[1], ofcolor(I, c))), w),
        equality(height(ofcolor(I, c)), h))

    good_c = lambda c: either(rows_covered(c), cols_covered(c))

    target_c = first(sfilter(colors,
                lambda c: both(not equality(c, bg), good_c(c))))
    return canvas(target_c, (1, 1))

def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / OCCURRENCE : compare each coloured object with
    #                          a full‑grid column or row generated by shoot
    h   = shape(I)[0]
    w   = shape(I)[1]
    bg  = mostcolor(I)

    # all full columns (top → bottom)
    cols = apply(lambda c: shoot((0, c), DOWN), interval(0, w, 1))
    # all full rows (left → right)
    rows = apply(lambda r: shoot((r, 0), RIGHT), interval(0, h, 1))

    objs = objects(I, True, False, False)

    col_match = lambda o: greater(
        size(mfilter(cols,
            lambda l: both(vmatching(o, l), equality(size(o), h)))), 0)

    row_match = lambda o: greater(
        size(mfilter(rows,
            lambda l: both(hmatching(o, l), equality(size(o), w)))), 0)

    full_obj = lambda o: either(col_match(o), row_match(o))

    target = first(sfilter(objs,
                lambda o: both(not equality(color(o), bg), full_obj(o))))
    return canvas(color(target), (1, 1))
```

    BG     = canvas(0, shape(I))               # empty background of the same size
    O      = paint(BG, MOVED)                  # place the shifted object onto the background
    return O

def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL TRANSFORMATION: cut off the last row and put it on top
    # split the grid into (height‑1) rows and the final row, then concatenate in swapped order
    H = height(I)                     # total number of rows
    W = width(I)                      # total number of columns
    last_row   = crop(I, (subtract(H, ONE), ZERO), (ONE, W))
    rest_rows  = crop(I, (ZERO, ZERO), (subtract(H, ONE), W))
    O = vconcat(last_row, rest_rows)  # new grid with rows shifted down by one
    return O
```

def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT EXTRACTION: move the whole non‑background object one step down
    fg = ofcolor(I, ONE)               # all cells whose colour is not the background (assume background = 0)
    moved = shift(fg, ONE)             # shift those cells down by one row (wrap‑around is handled later)
    # wrap the cells that fell off the bottom back to the first row
    overflow = filter(lambda p: greater(p[0], subtract(height(I), ONE)), moved)
    wrapped  = shift(overflow, multiply(negate(height(I)), ONE))
    cleaned  = difference(moved, overflow)
    final_fg = combine(cleaned, wrapped)
    O = paint(I, final_fg)             # repaint the moved object on the original background
    return O
```

    return O

def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL: move every coloured cell toward the lowest empty row beneath it
    fg       = ofcolor(I, ONE)                 # coloured cells
    empty    = ofcolor(I, ZERO)                # background cells
    # for each foreground cell, find the nearest empty cell directly below it
    target   = mapply(lambda p: gravitate(p, max({q for q in empty if q[1]==p[1]}, default=p)), fg)
    O        = paint(I, target)                # repaint using the new positions
    return O
```

def dsl1(I):
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Object‑extraction + axis‑aligned translation (horizontal or vertical)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)                     # all cells of color 2
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)                    # all cells of color 8

    # bounding‑box extrema
    up2   = uppermost(obj2)
    low2  = lowermost(obj2)
    left2 = leftmost(obj2)
    right2= rightmost(obj2)

    up8   = uppermost(obj8)
    low8  = lowermost(obj8)
    left8 = leftmost(obj8)
    right8= rightmost(obj8)

    # do the row intervals intersect ?
    rows_overlap = both(
        flip(greater(up8, low2)),
        flip(greater(up2, low8))
    )

    # horizontal shift amount (positive → right, negative → left)
    h_shift = branch(
        greater(left8, right2),                     # 8 is to the right of 2
        subtract(add(left8, -1), right2),            # move right until adjacent
        subtract(add(right8, ONE), left2)            # otherwise move left
    )

    # vertical shift amount (positive → down, negative → up)
    v_shift = branch(
        greater(up8, low2),                         # 8 is below 2
        subtract(add(up8, -1), low2),               # move down until adjacent
        subtract(add(low8, ONE), up2)                # otherwise move up
    )

    # choose the proper axis
    dr = branch(rows_overlap, 0, v_shift)
    dc = branch(rows_overlap, h_shift, 0)

    # translate the colour‑2 object
    moved2 = shift(obj2, astuple(dr, dc))

    # remove original colour‑2 cells and paint the moved ones
    cleared = cover(I, obj2)
    O = paint(cleared, moved2)
    return O
```

def dsl2(I):
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Global‑crop → translate → embed (uses cropping & underpaint)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    # bounding boxes of both objects
    bb2 = backdrop(obj2)
    bb8 = backdrop(obj8)

    # union of both bounding boxes -> minimal rectangle containing everything
    whole = combine(bb2, bb8)
    top, left = ulcorner(whole)
    bottom, right = lrcorner(whole)
    height = add(bottom, -top, ONE)
    width  = add(right, -left, ONE)

    # cut that rectangle out of the original grid
    sub = crop(I, astuple(top, left), astuple(height, width))

    # compute the translation that makes the two objects adjacent
    # (the same logic as in dsl1 but now on the sub‑grid)
    obj2_sub = ofcolor(sub, TWO)
    obj8_sub = ofcolor(sub, EIGHT)

    up2   = uppermost(obj2_sub)
    low2  = lowermost(obj2_sub)
    left2 = leftmost(obj2_sub)
    right2= rightmost(obj2_sub)

    up8   = uppermost(obj8_sub)
    low8  = lowermost(obj8_sub)
    left8 = leftmost(obj8_sub)
    right8= rightmost(obj8_sub)

    rows_overlap = both(
        flip(greater(up8, low2)),
        flip(greater(up2, low8))
    )

    h_shift = branch(
        greater(left8, right2),
        subtract(add(left8, -1), right2),
        subtract(add(right8, ONE), left2)
    )
    v_shift = branch(
        greater(up8, low2),
        subtract(add(up8, -1), low2),
        subtract(add(low8, ONE), up2)
    )
    dr = branch(rows_overlap, 0, v_shift)
    dc = branch(rows_overlap, h_shift, 0)

    # move the colour‑2 cells inside the sub‑grid
    moved2_sub = shift(obj2_sub, astuple(dr, dc))

    # create a clean sub‑grid (remove old 2s) and repaint moved ones
    cleared_sub = cover(sub, obj2_sub)
    new_sub = paint(cleared_sub, moved2_sub)

    # embed the modified sub‑grid back into the original canvas
    O = underpaint(I, new_sub)      # background cells of I are overwritten by new_sub
    return O
```

def dsl3(I):
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Relational reasoning using `position` and `gravitate`
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    # vector from 2‑object to 8‑object (row, col offset of their centres)
    vec = position(obj2, obj8)                # (dr, dc)

    # isolate the dominant axis (the one that is non‑zero after taking overlap)
    rows_overlap = both(
        flip(greater(uppermost(obj8), lowermost(obj2))),
        flip(greater(uppermost(obj2), lowermost(obj8)))
    )
    # compute a unit step towards adjacency on the relevant axis
    dr = branch(rows_overlap,
                subtract(add(uppermost(obj8), -1), lowermost(obj2)),   # vertical move
                0)
    dc = branch(rows_overlap,
                0,
                subtract(add(leftmost(obj8), -1), rightmost(obj2)))   # horizontal move

    # sign‑adjustment in case 8 lies on the opposite side
    dr = branch(greater(dr, 0), dr, branch(greater(dr, 0), dr, dr))
    dc = branch(greater(dc, 0), dc, branch(greater(dc, 0), dc, dc))

    moved2 = shift(obj2, astuple(dr, dc))
    cleared = cover(I, obj2)
    O = paint(cleared, moved2)
    return O

def dsl4(I):
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Geometric mirroring + translation (mirrors the whole scene then re‑mirrors)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # mirror the whole picture across the vertical axis, bring the 2‑object
    # next to the 8‑object (now they are on the opposite side), then undo the mirror.
    mirrored = vmirror(I)

    obj2_m = ofcolor(mirrored, TWO)
    obj8_m = ofcolor(mirrored, EIGHT)

    # after mirroring, the relative orientation is swapped;
    # we can reuse the axis‑aligned translation from dsl1 on the mirrored grid.
    up2   = uppermost(obj2_m); low2  = lowermost(obj2_m)
    left2  = leftmost(obj2_m); right2 = rightmost(obj2_m)
    up8   = uppermost(obj8_m); low8  = lowermost(obj8_m)
    left8  = leftmost(obj8_m); right8 = rightmost(obj8_m)

    rows_overlap = both(
        flip(greater(up8, low2)),
        flip(greater(up2, low8))
    )
    h_shift = branch(
        greater(left8, right2),
        subtract(add(left8, -1), right2),
        subtract(add(right8, ONE), left2)
    )
    v_shift = branch(
        greater(up8, low2),
        subtract(add(up8, -1), low2),
        subtract(add(low8, ONE), up2)
    )
    dr = branch(rows_overlap, 0, v_shift)
    dc = branch(rows_overlap, h_shift, 0)

    moved2_m = shift(obj2_m, astuple(dr, dc))
    cleared_m = cover(mirrored, obj2_m)
    new_m = paint(cleared_m, moved2_m)

    # undo the mirror to obtain the final answer
    O = vmirror(new_m)
    return O
```

def dsl5(I):
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Relational / structural reasoning using `gravitate`
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    # direction that would bring the 2‑object adjacent to the 8‑object
    dir_vec = gravitate(obj2, obj8)          # unit step (row, col) toward adjacency

    # move the whole 2‑object by that direction (which is guaranteed to be axis‑aligned)
    moved2 = shift(obj2, dir_vec)

    cleared = cover(I, obj2)
    O = paint(cleared, moved2)
    return O

def dsl4(I):
    # 4. Relational reasoning using gravitate + full distance
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    # unit direction that would bring 2‑object closer to 8‑object
    dir_vec = gravitate(obj2, obj8)          # (dr_sign, dc_sign)

    dr_sign = index(dir_vec, 0)
    dc_sign = index(dir_vec, 1)

    # overlapping axis detection (same as before)
    up2   = uppermost(obj2);   low2  = lowermost(obj2)
    up8   = uppermost(obj8);   low8  = lowermost(obj8)
    left2 = leftmost(obj2);    right2 = rightmost(obj2)
    left8 = leftmost(obj8);    right8 = rightmost(obj8)

    rows_overlap = both(
        flip(greater(up8, low2)),
        flip(greater(up2, low8))
    )

    # distance needed on the chosen axis (minus one cell for adjacency)
    vert_dist = branch(
        greater(dr_sign, ZERO),
        subtract(up8, add(low2, ONE)),
        subtract(low8, add(up2, ONE))
    horiz_dist = branch(
        greater(dc_sign, ZERO),
        subtract(left8, add(right2, ONE)),
        subtract(left2, add(right8, ONE))
    )

    dr = branch(rows_overlap, ZERO, multiply(dr_sign, vert_dist))
    dc = branch(rows_overlap, multiply(dc_sign, horiz_dist), ZERO)

    moved = recolor(TWO, shift(obj2, astuple(dr, dc)))
    cleared = cover(I, obj2)
    O = paint(cleared, moved)
    return O
```

def dsl5(I):
    # 5. Center‑of‑mass based alignment (use centre to decide axis, then shift edges)
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    # bounding‑box extrema
    up2   = uppermost(obj2);   low2  = lowermost(obj2)
    left2 = leftmost(obj2);    right2 = rightmost(obj2)
    up8   = uppermost(obj8);   low8  = lowermost(obj8)
    left8 = leftmost(obj8);    right8 = rightmost(obj8)

    # decide which axis already overlaps
    rows_overlap = both(
        flip(greater(up8, low2)),
        flip(greater(up2, low8))
    )

    # horizontal shift (if rows overlap) – bring right edge of 2 next to left edge of 8,
    # or left edge of 2 next to right edge of 8, depending on relative position.
    h_shift = branch(
        greater(left8, right2),
        subtract(left8, add(right2, ONE)),    # move right
        subtract(left2, add(right8, ONE))     # move left
    )

    # vertical shift (if columns overlap)
    v_shift = branch(
        greater(up8, low2),
        subtract(up8, add(low2, ONE)),        # move down
        subtract(up2, add(low8, ONE))        # move up
    )

    dr = branch(rows_overlap, ZERO, v_shift)
    dc = branch(rows_overlap, h_shift, ZERO)

    moved = recolor(TWO, shift(obj2, astuple(dr, dc)))
    cleared = cover(I, obj2)
    O = paint(cleared, moved)
    return O
```

def dsl4(I):
    # ── geometric reasoning via vertical mirroring ──
    # mirror, perform a pure horizontal shift (as if rows overlapped),
    # then un‑mirror.
    mirrored = vmirror(I)

    obj2 = ofcolor(mirrored, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(mirrored, EIGHT)

    up2   = uppermost(obj2);   low2  = lowermost(obj2)
    left2 = leftmost(obj2);    right2 = rightmost(obj2)
    up8   = uppermost(obj8);   low8  = lowermost(obj8)
    left8 = leftmost(obj8);    right8 = rightmost(obj8)

    # after vertical mirroring, vertical adjacency becomes horizontal,
    # so we always shift horizontally; vertical component stays zero.
    h_gap = branch(greater(left8, right2),
                   subtract(left8, add(right2, ONE)),
                   subtract(left2, add(right8, ONE)))

    dc = branch(flip(greater(up8, low2)),   # rows overlap in the mirrored view?
               h_gap, ZERO)                # if they already overlap vertically, no shift
    dr = ZERO

    moved    = recolor(TWO, shift(obj2, astuple(dr, dc)))
    cleared  = cover(mirrored, obj2)
    new_mid  = paint(cleared, moved)

    O = vmirror(new_mid)
    return O
```

def dsl5(I):
    # ── relational reasoning using object centroids ──
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    # centroids (center of mass) give a robust direction
    cen2 = centerofmass(obj2)
    cen8 = centerofmass(obj8)

    dr_sign = branch(greater(index(cen2, 0), index(cen8, 0)), NEG_ONE,
                branch(greater(index(cen8, 0), index(cen2, 0)), ONE, ZERO))
    dc_sign = branch(greater(index(cen2, 1), index(cen8, 1)), NEG_ONE,
                branch(greater(index(cen8, 1), index(cen2, 1)), ONE, ZERO))

    # bounding‑box gaps (always ≥ 0)
    up2   = uppermost(obj2);   low2  = lowermost(obj2)
    left2 = leftmost(obj2);    right2 = rightmost(obj2)
    up8   = uppermost(obj8);   low8  = lowermost(obj8)
    left8 = leftmost(obj8);    right8 = rightmost(obj8)

    rows_overlap = both(flip(greater(up8, low2)),
                         flip(greater(up2, low8)))

    h_gap = branch(greater(left8, right2),
                   subtract(left8, add(right2, ONE)),
                   subtract(left2, add(right8, ONE)))
    v_gap = branch(greater(up8, low2),
                   subtract(up8, add(low2, ONE)),
                   subtract(up2, add(low8, ONE)))

    dr = branch(rows_overlap, ZERO, multiply(dr_sign, v_gap))
    dc = branch(rows_overlap, multiply(dc_sign, h_gap), ZERO)

    moved = recolor(TWO, shift(obj2, astuple(dr, dc)))
    cleared = cover(I, obj2)
    O = paint(cleared, moved)
    return O
```

def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL‑CROP → SHIFT INSIDE SUB‑GRID → RE‑EMBED
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    # union of the two bounding boxes, then crop that region
    bb       = combine(backdrop(obj2), backdrop(obj8))
    top, left   = ulcorner(bb)
    bottom, right = lrcorner(bb)
    h = add(add(bottom, -top), ONE)
    w = add(add(right, -left), ONE)
    sub = crop(I, astuple(top, left), astuple(h, w))

    # same shift logic as the object‑extraction version, but applied to the cropped sub‑grid
    o2 = ofcolor(sub, TWO)
    o8 = ofcolor(sub, EIGHT)

    up2   = uppermost(o2);   low2  = lowermost(o2)
    left2 = leftmost(o2);    right2 = rightmost(o2)
    up8   = uppermost(o8);   low8  = lowermost(o8)
    left8 = leftmost(o8);    right8 = rightmost(o8)

    rows_overlap = both(flip(greater(up8, low2)),
                         flip(greater(up2, low8)))

    h_gap = branch(greater(left8, right2),
                   subtract(left8, add(right2, ONE)),
                   subtract(left2, add(right8, ONE)))
    v_gap = branch(greater(up8, low2),
                   subtract(up8, add(low2, ONE)),
                   subtract(up2, add(low8, ONE)))

    dr_sign = branch(greater(up2, low8), NEG_ONE,
                branch(greater(low2, up8), ONE, ZERO))
    dc_sign = branch(greater(left2, right8), NEG_ONE,
                branch(greater(right2, left8), ONE, ZERO))

    dr = branch(rows_overlap, ZERO, multiply(dr_sign, v_gap))
    dc = branch(rows_overlap, multiply(dc_sign, h_gap), ZERO)

    moved_sub   = recolor(TWO, shift(o2, astuple(dr, dc)))
    cleared_sub = cover(sub, o2)
    new_sub     = paint(cleared_sub, moved_sub)

    O = underpaint(I, new_sub)
    return O

    rot = rot90(I)                     # turn the picture 90° clockwise

    obj8 = ofcolor(rot, EIGHT)

    up2   = uppermost(obj2);   low2  = lowermost(obj2)
    left2 = leftmost(obj2);    right2 = rightmost(obj2)
    up8   = uppermost(obj8);   low8  = lowermost(obj8)
    left8 = leftmost(obj8);    right8 = rightmost(obj8)

    rows_overlap = both(flip(greater(up8, low2)),
                         flip(greater(up2, low8)))

    h_gap = branch(greater(left8, right2),
                   subtract(left8, add(right2, ONE)),

    new_rot = paint(cleared, moved)

    return O

def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑LEVEL GAP COMPUTATION (no cropping)
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    up2   = uppermost(obj2);   low2  = lowermost(obj2)
    left2  = leftmost(obj2);   right2 = rightmost(obj2)
    up8   = uppermost(obj8);   low8  = lowermost(obj8)
    left8  = leftmost(obj8);   right8 = rightmost(obj8)

    rows_overlap = both(flip(greater(up8, low2)),
                         flip(greater(up2, low8)))

    h_gap = branch(greater(left8, right2),
                 subtract(left8, add(right2, ONE)),
                 subtract(left2, add(right8, ONE)))
    v_gap = branch(greater(up8, low2),
                 subtract(up8, add(low2, ONE)),
                 subtract(up2, add(low8, ONE)))

    dr_sign = branch(greater(up2, low8), NEG_ONE,
                 branch(greater(low2, up8), ONE, ZERO))
    dc_sign = branch(greater(left2, right8), NEG_ONE,
                 branch(greater(right2, left8), ONE, ZERO))

    dr = branch(rows_overlap, ZERO, multiply(dr_sign, v_gap))
    dc = branch(rows_overlap, multiply(dc_sign, h_gap), ZERO)

    moved = recolor(TWO, shift(obj2, (dr, dc)))
    cleared = cover(I, obj2)
    O = paint(cleared, moved)
    return O

def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC REASONING: ROTATE ONLY IF VERTICAL GAP
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    up2   = uppermost(obj2);   low2  = lowermost(obj2)
    up8   = uppermost(obj8);   low8  = lowermost(obj8)

    rows_overlap = both(flip(greater(up8, low2)),
                         flip(greater(up2, low8)))

    # helper that shifts horizontally given left/right edges
    def horiz_shift(grid):
        o2 = ofcolor(grid, TWO)
        o8 = ofcolor(grid, EIGHT)
        left2  = leftmost(o2);   right2 = rightmost(o2)
        left8  = leftmost(o8);   right8 = rightmost(o8)
        gap = branch(greater(left8, right2),
                     subtract(left8, add(right2, ONE)),
                     subtract(left2, add(right8, ONE)))
        sign = branch(greater(left8, right2), ONE, NEG_ONE)
        dc = multiply(sign, gap)
        moved = recolor(TWO, shift(o2, (ZERO, dc)))
        cleared = cover(grid, o2)
        return paint(cleared, moved)

    # if the objects already share rows, shift directly; otherwise rotate
    O = branch(rows_overlap,
               horiz_shift(I),
               paint(cover(I, obj2),
                     recolor(TWO,
                             shift(ofcolor(rot90(I), TWO),
                                   (ZERO,
                                    multiply(
                                        branch(greater(leftmost(ofcolor(rot90(I), EIGHT)),
                                                     rightmost(ofcolor(rot90(I), TWO))),
                                        ONE, NEG_ONE),
                                        subtract(
                                            branch(greater(leftmost(ofcolor(rot90(I), EIGHT)),
                                                     rightmost(ofcolor(rot90(I), TWO))),
                                            add(rightmost(ofcolor(rot90(I), TWO)), ONE)))))))
    # rotate back if we rotated
    O = branch(rows_overlap, O, rot270(O))
    return O
```

def dsl1(I):
    # OBJECT‑LEVEL GAP using NORMALIZE (global‑crop → normalize → shift → de‑normalize)
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    # bounding box that contains both objects
    region = combine(backdrop(obj2), backdrop(obj8))

    # move the whole region to the origin
    n2 = normalize(obj2)
    n8 = normalize(obj8)

    # extreme coordinates inside the normalized patches
    up2   = uppermost(n2); low2  = lowermost(n2)
    left2 = leftmost(n2); right2 = rightmost(n2)
    up8   = uppermost(n8); low8  = lowermost(n8)
    left8 = leftmost(n8); right8 = rightmost(n8)

    rows_overlap = both(flip(greater(up8, low2)),
                         flip(greater(up2, low8)))

    h_gap = branch(greater(left8, right2),
                 subtract(left8, add(right2, ONE)),
                 subtract(left2, add(right8, ONE)))
    v_gap = branch(greater(up8, low2),
                 subtract(up8, add(low2, ONE)),
                 subtract(up2, add(low8, ONE)))

    dr = branch(rows_overlap, ZERO,
                multiply(branch(greater(up2, low8), NEG_ONE,
                              branch(greater(low2, up8), ONE, ZERO)),
                         v_gap))
    dc = branch(rows_overlap,
                multiply(branch(greater(left2, right8), NEG_ONE,
                         branch(greater(right2, left8), ONE, ZERO)),
                ZERO)

    moved_n2 = recolor(TWO, shift(n2, (dr, dc)))

    # move back to original coordinates (top‑left corner of the original region)
    offset = ulcorner(region)
    moved   = shift(moved_n2, offset)

    cleared = cover(I, obj2)
    O = paint(cleared, moved)
    return O
```

def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC REASONING: rotate‑and‑shift only when vertical gap exists
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    up2 = uppermost(obj2); low2 = lowermost(obj2)
    up8 = uppermost(obj8); low8 = lowermost(obj8)

    rows_overlap = both(flip(greater(up8, low2)),
                         flip(greater(up2, low8)))

    # ----- helper: pure horizontal shift inside a grid -----------------
    def horiz_shift(grid):
        o2 = ofcolor(grid, TWO)
        o8 = ofcolor(grid, EIGHT)
        left2  = leftmost(o2);   right2 = rightmost(o2)
        left8  = leftmost(o8);   right8 = rightmost(o8)

        gap  = branch(greater(left8, right2),
                     subtract(left8, add(right2, ONE)),
                     subtract(left2, add(right8, ONE)))
        sign = branch(greater(left8, right2), ONE, NEG_ONE)
        dc   = multiply(sign, gap)

        moved = recolor(TWO, shift(o2, (ZERO, dc)))
        cleared = cover(grid, o2)
        return paint(cleared, moved)

    # if already sharing rows → simple horizontal shift,
    # otherwise rotate, shift horizontally (which is vertical in original), rotate back
    O = branch(rows_overlap,
               horiz_shift(I),
               rot270(horiz_shift(rot90(I))))
    return O

def dsl5(I):
    # COMPOSITE RECONSTRUCTION: cut the grid, re‑assemble with H‑CONCAT
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    # gaps
    left2 = leftmost(obj2);   right2 = rightmost(obj2)
    left8 = leftmost(obj8);   right8 = rightmost(obj8)
    up2   = uppermost(obj2);   low2  = lowermost(obj2)
    up8   = uppermost(obj8);   low8  = lowermost(obj8)

    rows_overlap = both(flip(greater(up8, low2)),
                         flip(greater(up2, low8)))

    h_gap = branch(greater(left8, right2),
                 subtract(left8, add(right2, ONE)),
                 subtract(left2, add(right8, ONE)))
    v_gap = branch(greater(up8, low2),
                 subtract(up8, add(low2, ONE)),
                 subtract(up2, add(low8, ONE)))

    dr = branch(rows_overlap, ZERO,
                multiply(branch(greater(up2, low8), NEG_ONE,
                              branch(greater(low2, up8), ONE, ZERO)),
                         v_gap))
    dc = branch(rows_overlap,
                multiply(branch(greater(left2, right8), NEG_ONE,
                              branch(greater(right2, left8), ONE, ZERO)),
                ZERO)

    moved = recolor(TWO, shift(obj2, (dr, dc)))
    cleared = cover(I, obj2)

    # build the final picture by stitching vertical slices:
    #   top part (rows above the moved object),
    #   the row range that now contains the moved object,
    #   bottom part (rows below)
    top    = crop(cleared, (ZERO, ZERO), (up2, width(cleared)))
    middle = crop(paint(cleared, moved),
                  (up2 + dr, ZERO),
                  (height(moved), width(cleared)))
    bottom = crop(cleared,
                  (low2 + dr + ONE, ZERO),
                  (height(cleared) - (low2 + dr + ONE), width(cleared)))

    O = vconcat(vconcat(top, middle), bottom)
    return O
```

def dsl5(I):
    # ---------- RECONSTRUCTION WITH VERTICAL CONCAT ----------
    # After moving the 2‑object by the computed gap, rebuild the picture by
    # stacking the unchanged top part, the rows that now contain the moved object,
    # and the unchanged bottom part.
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    left2 = leftmost(obj2);   right2 = rightmost(obj2)
    left8 = leftmost(obj8);   right8 = rightmost(obj8)
    up2   = uppermost(obj2);  low2 = lowermost(obj2)
    up8   = uppermost(obj8);  low8 = lowermost(obj8)

    rows_overlap = both(flip(greater(up8, low2)),
                        flip(greater(up2, low8)))

    h_gap = branch(greater(left8, right2),
                subtract(left8, add(right2, ONE)),
                subtract(left2, add(right8, ONE)))
    v_gap = branch(greater(up8, low2),
                subtract(up8, add(low2, ONE)),
                subtract(up2, add(low8, ONE)))

    dr = branch(rows_overlap, ZERO,
                multiply(branch(greater(up2, low8), NEG_ONE,
                         branch(greater(low2, up8), ONE, ZERO)),
                         v_gap))
    dc = branch(rows_overlap,
                multiply(branch(greater(left2, right8), NEG_ONE,
                         branch(greater(right2, left8), ONE, ZERO)),
                ZERO)

    moved   = recolor(TWO, shift(obj2, (dr, dc)))
    cleared = cover(I, obj2)

    # three vertical slices
    top    = crop(cleared, (ZERO, ZERO), (up2, width(cleared)))
    middle = crop(paint(cleared, moved), (add(up2, dr), ZERO),
                  (height(moved), width(cleared)))
    bottom = crop(cleared, (add(low2, dr, ONE), ZERO),
                  (subtract(height(cleared), add(low2, dr, ONE)), width(cleared)))

    O = vconcat(vconcat(top, middle), bottom)
    return O
```

def dsl1(I):
    # ---------- H-MATCH / V-MATCH ----------
    # If the objects share any row, shift horizontally; otherwise shift vertically.
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    rows_overlap = hmatching(obj2, obj8)          # share a row → horizontal move
    cols_overlap = vmatching(obj2, obj8)          # share a column → vertical move

    # ----- horizontal quantities -----
    left2  = leftmost(obj2);   right2 = rightmost(obj2)
    left8  = leftmost(obj8);   right8 = rightmost(obj8)

    h_gap   = branch(greater(left8, right2),
                     subtract(left8, add(right2, ONE)),
                     subtract(left2, add(right8, ONE)))
    h_sign  = branch(greater(left8, right2), ONE, NEG_ONE)
    dc_h    = multiply(h_sign, h_gap)

    # ----- vertical quantities -----
    up2   = uppermost(obj2);   low2 = lowermost(obj2)
    up8   = uppermost(obj8);   low8 = lowermost(obj8)

    v_gap  = branch(greater(up8, low2),
                     subtract(up8, add(low2, ONE)),
                     subtract(up2, add(low8, ONE)))
    v_sign = branch(greater(up8, low2), ONE, NEG_ONE)
    dr_v   = multiply(v_sign, v_gap)

    # ----- pick the proper direction -----
    dr = branch(rows_overlap, ZERO, dr_v)
    dc = branch(rows_overlap, dc_h, ZERO)

    moved   = recolor(TWO, shift(obj2, (dr, dc)))
    cleared = cover(I, obj2)
    O = paint(cleared, moved)
    return O

def dsl2(I):
    # ---------- CENTER OF MASS + DOMINANT AXIS ----------
    # Move the 2‑object along the axis where the two centers are farther apart.
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    c2 = centerofmass(obj2)
    c8 = centerofmass(obj8)

    drc = subtract(c8[0], c2[0])          # row difference
    dcc = subtract(c8[1], c2[1])          # col difference

    # absolute differences (no builtin, use branch)
    abs_dr = branch(greater(drc, ZERO), drc, multiply(NEG_ONE, drc))
    abs_dc = branch(greater(dcc, ZERO), dcc, multiply(NEG_ONE, dcc))

    vertical = greater(abs_dr, abs_dc)      # True → move vertically

    # ----- vertical gap -----
    up2   = uppermost(obj2);   low2 = lowermost(obj2)
    up8   = uppermost(obj8);   low8 = lowermost(obj8)

    v_gap  = branch(greater(up8, low2),
                    subtract(up8, add(low2, ONE)),
                    subtract(up2, add(low8, ONE)))
    v_sign = branch(greater(up8, low2), ONE, NEG_ONE)
    dr_v   = multiply(v_sign, v_gap)

    # ----- horizontal gap -----
    left2  = leftmost(obj2);   right2 = rightmost(obj2)
    left8  = leftmost(obj8);   right8 = rightmost(obj8)

    h_gap  = branch(greater(left8, right2),
                    subtract(left8, add(right2, ONE)),
                    subtract(left2, add(right8, ONE)))
    h_sign = branch(greater(left8, right2), ONE, NEG_ONE)
    dc_h   = multiply(h_sign, h_gap)

    dr = branch(vertical, dr_v, ZERO)
    dc = branch(vertical, ZERO, dc_h)

    moved   = recolor(TWO, shift(obj2, (dr, dc)))
    cleared = cover(I, obj2)
    O = paint(cleared, moved)
    return O
```

def dsl3(I):
    # ---------- ROTATE‑AND‑SHIFT ----------
    # Turn a vertical problem into a horizontal one, solve it, then rotate back.
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    rows_overlap = hmatching(obj2, obj8)          # share a row → horizontal

    def horiz_shift(grid):
        o2 = ofcolor(grid, TWO)
        o8 = ofcolor(grid, EIGHT)

        left2  = leftmost(o2);   right2 = rightmost(o2)
        left8  = leftmost(o8);   right8 = rightmost(o8)

        gap  = branch(greater(left8, right2),
                     subtract(left8, add(right2, ONE)),
                     subtract(left2, add(right8, ONE)))
        sign = branch(greater(left8, right2), ONE, NEG_ONE)
        dc   = multiply(sign, gap)

        moved   = recolor(TWO, shift(o2, (ZERO, dc)))
        cleared = cover(grid, o2)
        return paint(cleared, moved)

    O = branch(rows_overlap,
               horiz_shift(I),
               rot270(horiz_shift(rot90(I))))   # rotate, shift horizontally, rotate back
    return O

def dsl4(I):
    # ---------- RECONSTRUCTION WITH VERTICAL CONCAT ----------
    # Compute the needed shift, paste the moved object, then rebuild the picture
    # by concatenating the unchanged top part, the rows that now contain the
    # moved object, and the unchanged bottom part.
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    left2  = leftmost(obj2);   right2 = rightmost(obj2)
    left8  = leftmost(obj8);   right8 = rightmost(obj8)
    up2    = uppermost(obj2);   low2  = lowermost(obj2)
    up8    = uppermost(obj8);   low8  = lowermost(obj8)

    rows_overlap = hmatching(obj2, obj8)          # share a row → horizontal move

    # ----- horizontal gap -----
    h_gap  = branch(greater(left8, right2),
                    subtract(left8, add(right2, ONE)),
                    subtract(left2, add(right8, ONE)))
    h_sign = branch(greater(left8, right2), ONE, NEG_ONE)
    dc_h   = multiply(h_sign, h_gap)

    # ----- vertical gap -----
    v_gap  = branch(greater(up8, low2),
                    subtract(up8, add(low2, ONE)),
                    subtract(up2, add(low8, ONE)))
    v_sign = branch(greater(up8, low2), ONE, NEG_ONE)
    dr_v   = multiply(v_sign, v_gap)

    dr = branch(rows_overlap, ZERO, dr_v)
    dc = branch(rows_overlap, dc_h, ZERO)

    moved   = recolor(TWO, shift(obj2, (dr, dc)))
    cleared = cover(I, obj2)

    # three vertical slices
    top    = crop(cleared, (ZERO, ZERO), (up2, width(cleared)))
    middle = crop(paint(cleared, moved), (add(up2, dr), ZERO),
                  (height(moved), width(cleared)))
    bottom = crop(cleared,
                  (add(low2, dr, ONE), ZERO),
                  (subtract(height(cleared), add(low2, dr, ONE)), width(cleared)))

    O = vconcat(vconcat(top, middle), bottom)
    return O

def dsl5(I):
    # ---------- GRAVITY + UNDERPAINT ----------
    # Move the 2‑object until its outline touches the 8‑object, then place it
    # under the cleared background.
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    obj8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    outline2 = box(obj2)
    outline8 = box(obj8)

    # minimal orthogonal offset that makes the two outlines adjacent
    move = gravitate(outline2, outline8)

    moved   = recolor(TWO, shift(obj2, move))
    cleared = cover(I, obj2)
    O = underpaint(cleared, moved)
    return O
```

    # tile the whole pattern 3×3 times
    row = hconcat(I, hconcat(I, I))               # 1 × 3 tiles

def dsl3(I):
    O = canvas(0, (height(I) * 3, width(I) * 3))
    P = asobject(I)                         # pattern object
    # work colour‑by‑colour (ignoring colour 0)
    colours = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    # for each colour, place the pattern at the positions that carry it
    for_c = lambda col: merge(
        apply(lambda loc: move(P, (loc[0] * 3, loc[1] * 3)),
              ofcolor(I, col)))

    return O

def dsl4(I):
    O   = canvas(0, (height(I) * 3, width(I) * 3))
    P   = asobject(I)                         # whole pattern
    # create a patch that is the pattern shifted to the origin (0,0)
    P0  = normalize(P)
    # repeat the shifted pattern three times horizontally and vertically,
    # then keep only the blocks whose anchor cell in I is non‑zero
    H   = hconcat(P0, hconcat(P0, P0))       # 1 × 3
    T   = vconcat(H, vconcat(H, H))          # 3 × 3 tiled pattern
    nz  = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))
    # build a mask of blocks to retain (background blocks become zeros)
    M   = canvas(0, (height(I) * 3, width(I) * 3))
    M   = paint(M, merge(apply(lambda loc:
                              move(asobject(canvas(1, (3, 3))),   # dummy object, only size matters
                              (loc[0] * 3, loc[1] * 3)), nz)))
    # finally combine tiled pattern with the mask
    O = underpaint(T, M)      # keep pattern where mask is non‑zero
    return O

    O = canvas(0, (height(I) * 3, width(I) * 3))
    P = asobject(I)                                           # whole pattern
    colours = difference(palette(I), initset(0))              # all non‑zero colours
    place = lambda col: merge(
                apply(lambda loc: shift(P, (loc[0] * 3, loc[1] * 3)),
                      ofcolor(I, col)))                     # positions that carry this colour
    O = paint(O, merge(apply(place, colours)))               # paint the pattern for every colour
    return O

def dsl4(I):
    # 4️⃣  Normalised pattern tiled, then masked with underpaint.
    P0 = normalize(asobject(I))                               # pattern shifted to origin
    H  = hconcat(P0, hconcat(P0, P0))                         # 1 × 3 repetition
    T  = vconcat(H, vconcat(H, H))                            # 3 × 3 tiled pattern
    nz = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))              # non‑zero anchors
    block = asobject(canvas(1, (3, 3)))                        # dummy block for the mask
    M = paint(canvas(0, (height(I) * 3, width(I) * 3)),
               merge(apply(lambda loc: shift(block, (loc[0] * 3, loc[1] * 3)),
                         nz)))                               # mask = 1 where we keep the pattern
    O = underpaint(T, M)                                      # keep pattern only on masked blocks
    return O
```

def dsl5(I):
    # 5️⃣  Build a binary mask, upscale it, and underpaint a fully tiled pattern.
    # full tiled pattern (all blocks filled)
    row = hconcat(I, hconcat(I, I))
    T   = vconcat(row, vconcat(row, row))
    # binary mask of non‑zero cells (size 3 × 3)
    nz = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))
    one = asobject(canvas(1, (1, 1)))                         # single‑cell object
    mask_small = paint(canvas(0, (height(I), width(I))),
                       merge(apply(lambda loc: shift(one, loc), nz))
    # upscale mask to 9 × 9 (each cell → 3 × 3 block)
    mask_big = vupscale(hupscale(mask_small, 3), 3)
    # keep the tiled pattern only where the mask is non‑zero
    O = underpaint(T, mask_big)
    return O
```

    ones   = ofcolor(I, ONE)                                 # cells colour 1
    plus   = combine(
                shift(ones, UP),
                combine(
                    shift(ones, DOWN),

                        shift(ones, LEFT),

    twos   = ofcolor(I, TWO)                                 # cells colour 2

                        shift(twos, add(DOWN, RIGHT))       # down‑right
                    )
                )
    diag4  = recolor(FOUR, diag)                           # 4‑colored diagonal around each 2

    O = paint(I, combine(plus7, diag4))                      # overlay on original
    return O

def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC REASONING – obtain opposite directions by mirroring
    ones = ofcolor(I, ONE)

    # up‑shift then mirror vertically gives the down counterpart
    up   = shift(ones, UP)
    down = vmirror(up)                                         # vertical mirror → down

    # left‑shift then mirror horizontally gives the right counterpart
    left = shift(ones, LEFT)
    right = hmirror(left)                                      # horizontal mirror → right

    plus7 = recolor(SEVEN,
                    combine(up,
                            combine(down,
                                    combine(left, right))))
    twos = ofcolor(I, TWO)

    # up‑left diagonal via NEG_UNITY, mirror horizontally → up‑right,
    # mirror vertically → down‑left, then vertical+horizontal → down‑right
    ul = shift(twos, NEG_UNITY)
    ur = hmirror(ul)                                            # up‑right
    dl = vmirror(ul)                                            # down‑left
    dr = vmirror(ur)                                           # down‑right

    diag4 = recolor(FOUR,
                    combine(ul,
                            combine(ur,
                                    combine(dl, dr))))
    O = paint(I, combine(plus7, diag4))
    return O

    # build neighbourhoods by applying adjacency primitives to every cell of a colour
    ones = ofcolor(I, ONE)
    twos = ofcolor(I, TWO)

    # orthogonal neighbours of each 1 → 7
    plus_patch = merge(apply(lambda loc: dneighbors(loc), ones))
    plus7      = recolor(SEVEN, plus_patch)

    # diagonal neighbours of each 2 → 4
    diag_patch = merge(apply(lambda loc: ineighbors(loc), twos))
    diag4      = recolor(FOUR, diag_patch)

    O = paint(I, combine(plus7, diag4))
    return O

    # Split the grid into its four quadrants, transform each
    # quadrant separately, then stitch them back together.
    rows, cols = shape(I)
    half_r = halve(rows)
    half_c = halve(cols)

    UR_t = vmirror(UR)           # left‑right mirror
    LL_t = hmirror(LL)           # up‑down mirror
    LR_t = rot180(LR)            # rotate 180°

    top    = hconcat(UL_t, UR_t)
    bottom = hconcat(LL_t, LR_t)
    O = vconcat(top, bottom)
    return O

def dsl4(I):
    # ---------- Relational shifting of mirrored copies ----------
    # Create the four symmetric copies, shift each to its quadrant
    # and overlay them on a blank canvas twice the size of the input.
    h, w = shape(I)
    canvas_big = canvas(0, (h * 2, w * 2))

    tl = toobject(ofcolor(I, leastcolor(I)), I)               # any colour works; we keep the whole picture
    tr = toobject(ofcolor(I, leastcolor(I)), I)               # will be mirrored later
    bl = toobject(ofcolor(I, leastcolor(I)), I)
    br = toobject(ofcolor(I, leastcolor(I)), I)

    # apply the required symmetries
    tr = toobject(ofcolor(vmirror(I), leastcolor(I)), vmirror(I))
    bl = toobject(ofcolor(hmirror(I), leastcolor(I)), hmirror(I))
    br = toobject(ofcolor(rot180(I), leastcolor(I)), rot180(I))

    # shift each quadrant to its place
    tr = shift(tr, (0, w))          # right
    bl = shift(bl, (h, 0))          # down
    br = shift(br, (h, w))          # down‑right

    # overlay everything
    O = merge({tl, tr, bl, br}, canvas_big)
    return O

def dsl5(I):
    # ---------- Colour‑periodic replication ----------
    # Replicate the whole picture periodically with period equal to the
    # input dimensions, then keep only the 2×2 block that starts at the origin.
    # The replication is performed by taking the Cartesian product of the
    # grid with itself and placing each copy at the appropriate offset.
    h, w = shape(I)

    # build a 2×2 repetition by shifting copies
    copy00 = toobject(ofcolor(I, leastcolor(I)), I)                     # original
    copy01 = shift(toobject(ofcolor(vmirror(I), leastcolor(I)), vmirror(I)),
                   (0, w))                                            # right‑mirrored copy
    copy10 = shift(toobject(ofcolor(hmirror(I), leastcolor(I)), hmirror(I)),
                   (h, 0))                                            # down‑mirrored copy
    copy11 = shift(toobject(ofcolor(rot180(I), leastcolor(I)), rot180(I)),
                   (h, w))                                            # 180° rotated copy

    O = merge({copy00, copy01, copy10, copy11})
    return O

def dsl4(I):
    # ---------- Periodic replication with cropping ----------
    # 1. Produce the 2×2 periodic pattern by repeating the 180° rotated
    #    picture together with its mirrors.

    base = rot180(I)

    period = vconcat(row0, row1)

    # cropping step to emphasise the periodic‑replication idea.
    O = crop(period, (0, 0), shape(period))
    return O

def dsl1(I):
    # --- Object‑extraction / placement strategy ---
    # foreground colour = most common non‑zero colour
    fg = argmax(
            difference(palette(I), initset(0)),
            lbind(colorcount, I)
         )
    # inverse pattern (swap 0 and fg)
    Z  = canvas(0, shape(I))
    Z1 = fill(Z, fg, ofcolor(I, 0))
    P  = fill(Z1, 0, ofcolor(I, fg))
    # empty output canvas (N·N)
    N   = height(I)                     # = width(I)
    O   = canvas(0, (N*N, N*N))
    # place a copy of P at every fg cell
    patches = apply(
                lambda idx: move(O, asobject(P), (idx[0]*N, idx[1]*N)),
                ofcolor(I, fg)
              )
    O = fold(patches, lambda acc, g: paint(acc, asobject(g)), O)
    return O
```

def dsl2(I):
    # --- Global transformation (down‑/up‑scale) ---
    fg = argmax(
            difference(palette(I), initset(0)),
            lbind(colorcount, I)
         )
    # build inverse pattern
    inv = replace(replace(I, fg, -1), 0, fg)   # temporary -1 for swapping
    inv = replace(inv, -1, 0)
    # upscale the whole inverse pattern N times, then mask it with the fg locations
    N   = height(I)
    big = vupscale(hupscale(inv, N), N)
    mask = upscale(
                replace(I, fg, 1),           # binary mask (1 where fg)
                N
           )
    O = fill(big, 0, ofcolor(mask, 0))       # keep blocks only where mask == 1
    return O
```

def dsl3(I):
    # --- Colour‑filtering approach ---
    fg = argmax(
            difference(palette(I), initset(0)),
            lbind(colorcount, I)
         )
    # inverse of the whole grid
    inv = replace(replace(I, fg, -1), 0, fg)
    inv = replace(inv, -1, 0)
    # extract the fg‑object, then tile it with the inverse pattern
    obj   = asobject(ofcolor(I, fg))
    tiled = hconcat(*apply(lambda _: inv, range(height(I))))   # repeat rows
    tiled = vconcat(*apply(lambda _: tiled, range(width(I)))) # repeat columns
    # finally keep only tiles that correspond to original fg cells
    O = paint(canvas(0, shape(tiled)), shift(asobject(inv), (0,0))
    O = cover(O, obj)                       # remove tiles where no fg exists
    return O
```

def dsl5(I):
    # Color‑filtering: build binary mask, upscale, then apply inverse pattern via cellwise multiplication
    fg   = argmax(difference(palette(I), initset(0)), lbind(colorcount, I))
    inv  = replace(replace(I, fg, 0), 0, fg)                # inverse pattern
    N    = height(I)
    # binary mask of foreground cells, expanded to N×N blocks
    mask = upscale(replace(I, fg, 1), N)
    # tile the inverse pattern by repeating it N times horizontally and vertically
    row  = apply(lambda _: inv, interval(0, N, 1))
    tiled_row = fold(row, lambda a b: hconcat(a, b), inv)   # build one full row
    tiled = apply(lambda _: tiled_row, interval(0, N, 1))
    tiled_grid = fold(tiled, lambda a b: vconcat(a, b), tiled_row)
    # keep only the tiled blocks where mask == 1
    O = fill(tiled_grid, 0, ofcolor(mask, 0))
    return O

def dsl5(I):
    # COLOR‑FILTERING: build a binary mask of the foreground, upscale it,
    # tile the original (non‑inverse) pattern, then keep only the tiled blocks
    # where the mask is 1.
    N      = height(I)
    fg     = argmax(difference(palette(I), initset(0)), lbind(colorcount, I))
    # binary mask (1 = foreground, 0 = background)
    mask   = replace(I, fg, 1)
    # upscale the mask to N×N blocks
    bigmask = upscale(mask, N)
    # tile the original input pattern N times horizontally and vertically
    row    = apply(lambda _: I, interval(0, N, 1))               # list of N rows
    tiled_row = fold(row, lambda a,b: hconcat(a,b), I)           # one full row
    tiled   = apply(lambda _: tiled_row, interval(0, N, 1))        # N identical rows
    tiled_grid = fold(tiled, lambda a,b: vconcat(a,b), tiled_row)
    # keep only cells whose bigmask is 1 (i.e. foreground blocks)
    O = fill(tiled_grid, 0, ofcolor(bigmask, 0))
    return O

def dsl3(I):
    # COLOR‑FILTERING + MASKED TILING:  build a binary mask of the dominant colour,
    # upscale it, tile the original (non‑inverted) pattern with hconcat/vconcat,
    # then keep only the blocks whose mask cell is 1.
    N      = height(I)
    fg     = argmax(difference(palette(I), initset(0)),
                    lbind(colorcount, I))
    mask   = replace(I, fg, 1)                                     # 1 = foreground
    bigmask = upscale(mask, N)                                    # each mask cell → N×N block
    # tile the whole input pattern N times horizontally and vertically
    row    = apply(lambda _: I, interval(0, N, 1))               # N copies of the row‑list
    tiled_row = fold(row, lambda a,b: hconcat(a,b), I)              # one full horizontal strip
    tiled   = apply(lambda _: tiled_row, interval(0, N, 1))       # N copies of the strip
    tiled_grid = fold(tiled, lambda a,b: vconcat(a,b), tiled_row) # full N‑by‑N tiling
    # zero‑out everything where the up‑scaled mask is 0
    O = fill(tiled_grid, 0, ofcolor(bigmask, 0))
    return O

def dsl4(I):

def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL‑TILING + MASKING
    # 1️⃣  dominant non‑zero colour
    fg = argmax(difference(palette(I), initset(0)),
                lbind(colorcount, I))
    N  = height(I)                                    # block size
    # 2️⃣  colour swap  (0 ↔ fg)  using a temporary colour (‑1)
    tmp = replace(I, 0, NEG_ONE)                       # 0 → -1
    tmp = replace(tmp, fg, 0)                          # fg → 0
    inv = replace(tmp, NEG_ONE, fg)                    # -1 → fg   →  inv is the inverted pattern
    # 3️⃣  tile the inverted pattern at **every** cell (including background)
    all_cells = asindices(I)
    tiled_obj = apply(lambda p: shift(asobject(inv),
                                      (p[0] * N, p[1] * N)), all_cells)
    tiled = paint(canvas(0, (N * N, N * N)), merge(tiled_obj))
    # 4️⃣  build a binary mask of the foreground and upscale it to block size
    mask = replace(I, fg, 1)                           # 1 = foreground
    bigmask = upscale(mask, N)                         # each mask cell → N×N block
    # 5️⃣  keep only blocks whose mask cell is 1
    O = fill(tiled, 0, ofcolor(bigmask, 0))
    return O

    return O

    sep      = ofcolor(I, 7)
    r        = lowermost(sep)                     # integer row index

def dsl2(I):
    # all objects, keep background (the 0‑cells)
    objs     = objects(I, False, False, False)
    # keep only the two background components (above / below the 7‑stripe)
    backs    = colorfilter(objs, 0)

    # turn the two components into normalized patches (upper‑left corner at (0,0))
    b0       = normalize(first(backs))                      # upper part
    b1_raw   = normalize(other(backs, b0))                # lower part
    # shift the lower part up by the height of the separator (row of 7s + 1)
    sep_row  = lowermost(ofcolor(I, 7))
    upvec    = subtract(astuple(0, 0), astuple(add(sep_row, 1), 0))
    b1       = shift(b1_raw, upvec)

    # intersect the two normalized background masks
    both0    = intersection(b0, b1)

    # output canvas has the size of one component (they are equal)
    sz       = shape(b0)                     # (h,w) of the upper component
    O        = canvas(0, sz)
    O        = fill(O, 8, both0)
    return O

    # split the grid as in dsl1
    sep      = ofcolor(I, 7)
    r        = lowermost(sep)
    w        = add(subtract(rightmost(sep), leftmost(sep)), 1)

    top      = crop(I, astuple(0, 0),         astuple(r, w))
    bot      = crop(I, astuple(add(r, 1), 0),
                        astuple(subtract(height(I), add(r, 1)), w))

    # colour‑cells (non‑zero) in each half
    top_nz   = ofcolor(top, 0)            # background of top
    bot_nz   = ofcolor(bot, 0)            # background of bot

    # bring the lower background into the same coordinates as the upper half

    bot_nz_up= shift(bot_nz, upvec)

    all_idx  = asindices(O)
    not_both = difference(all_idx, both0)
    O        = fill(O, 0, not_both)        # paint 0 where the condition fails
    return O

    w        = add(subtract(rightmost(ofcolor(I, 7)), leftmost(ofcolor(I, 7))), 1)

    # upper and lower halves
    top      = crop(I, astuple(0, 0),         astuple(r, w))
    bot      = crop(I, astuple(add(r, 1), 0),
                        astuple(subtract(height(I), add(r, 1)), w))

    # background cells (0) in each half
    top0     = ofcolor(top, 0)
    bot0     = ofcolor(bot, 0)

    # move the lower background upward by the vector that brings its
    # first cell next to the top‑half background (gravitate does exactly that)
    dirvec   = gravitate(first(bot0), first(top0))   # direction from bot→top
    bot0_up  = shift(bot0, dirvec)

    # cells that are 0 in both halves
    both0    = intersection(top0, bot0_up)

    O        = canvas(0, astuple(r, w))
    O        = fill(O, 8, both0)
    return O
```

    # 2️⃣  Relational alignment: after mirroring, shift the lower‑half zero mask
    #      so its first zero cell coincides with the first zero cell of the upper half.
    sep = ofcolor(I, 7)

    bot_raw  = crop(I, astuple(add(r, 1), 0),       astuple(subtract(height(I), add(r, 1)), w))
    bot_mir  = hmirror(bot_raw)

    top0 = ofcolor(top, 0)
    bot0 = ofcolor(bot_mir, 0)

    dirvec   = subtract(first(top0), first(bot0))   # translation needed for alignment
    bot0_aln = shift(bot0, dirvec)

    both0 = intersection(top0, bot0_aln)
    O = canvas(0, astuple(r, w))
    O = fill(O, 8, both0)
    return O

def dsl3(I):
    # 3️⃣  Object‑extraction + normalisation: treat the zero‑pixel sets as patches,
    #      normalise them (move to origin) then bring the lower patch up to the
    #      upper‑half origin before intersecting.
    sep = ofcolor(I, 7)
    r   = lowermost(sep)
    w   = add(subtract(rightmost(sep), leftmost(sep)), 1)

    top      = crop(I, ORIGIN,                     astuple(r,          w))
    bot_raw  = crop(I, astuple(add(r, 1), 0),       astuple(subtract(height(I), add(r, 1)), w))
    bot_mir  = hmirror(bot_raw)

    b0 = normalize(ofcolor(top, 0))
    b1 = normalize(ofcolor(bot_mir, 0))

    # move the lower‑half patch up by the height of the separator + 1 row
    upvec = subtract(astuple(0, 0), astuple(add(r, 1), 0))
    b1_up = shift(b1, upvec)

    both0 = intersection(b0, b1_up)
    O = canvas(0, astuple(r, w))
    O = fill(O, 8, both0)
    return O
```

    # 5️⃣  Paint‑by‑object: create the zero‑intersection as an object and
    #      paint it onto a blank canvas (using underpaint).
    sep = ofcolor(I, 7)
    r   = lowermost(sep)
    w   = add(subtract(rightmost(sep), leftmost(sep)), 1)

    top      = crop(I, ORIGIN,                     astuple(r,          w))
    bot_raw  = crop(I, astuple(add(r, 1), 0),       astuple(subtract(height(I), add(r, 1)), w))
    bot_mir  = hmirror(bot_raw)

    both0 = intersection(ofcolor(top, 0), ofcolor(bot_mir, 0))
    obj   = toobject(both0, canvas(0, astuple(r, w)))   # turn the index set into an object
    O     = canvas(0, astuple(r, w))
    O = underpaint(O, obj)      # paint 8 where the object lives
    O = recolor(8, obj)        # ensure painted colour is 8
    return O
```

def dsl5(I):
    # global transformation – compress the whole picture to remove the 7‑separator,
    # then rotate the result 180° and keep the cells that are zero both

    sep   = ofcolor(I, 7)
    r     = lowermost(sep)
    w     = add(subtract(rightmost(sep), leftmost(sep)), 1)

    both0 = intersection(ofcolor(part, 0), ofcolor(rot, 0))

    O     = canvas(0, astuple(r, w))
    O     = fill(O, 8, both0)
    return O

def dsl1(I):
    # geometric‑union: keep a zero cell of the top half if the same column
    # is zero either directly below or mirrored horizontally below.
    sep = ofcolor(I, 7)
    r   = lowermost(sep)
    w   = add(subtract(rightmost(sep), subtract(leftmost(sep), NEG_ONE))
    top = crop(I, ORIGIN, astuple(r, w))
    bot = crop(I, astuple(add(r, 1), 0), astuple(subtract(height(I), add(r, 1)), w)

    top0   = ofcolor(top, 0)
    bot0   = ofcolor(bot, 0)
    bot0_m = ofcolor(hmirror(bot), 0)          # zeros after horizontal mirror
    bot_union = combine(bot0, bot0_m)         # direct‑or‑mirrored zeros below
    both = intersection(top0, bot_union)      # keep only columns satisfying the rule

    O = canvas(0, astuple(r, w))
    O = fill(O, 8, both)
    return O
```

    both = intersection(top0, bot0)

    O = canvas(0, astuple(r, w))
    O = fill(O, 8, both)
    return O

def dsl5(I):
    # geometric‑reasoning: rotate both halves 180°, intersect zeros, rotate back
    sep = ofcolor(I, 7)
    r   = lowermost(sep)

    O = fill(O, 8, both)
    return O

def dsl3(I):
    # 3️⃣  Colour‑filter via masks: build binary masks (0→1, else 0) for the two halves
    #      and keep the cells that are 1 in both masks.
    sep = ofcolor(I, 7)
    r   = lowermost(sep)
    w   = add(subtract(rightmost(sep), leftmost(sep)), ONE)

    top = crop(I, ORIGIN, astuple(r, w))
    bot = crop(I, astuple(add(r, ONE), ZERO),
                astuple(subtract(height(I), add(r, ONE)), w))

    # binary masks: 1 where the colour is 0, 0 elsewhere
    mask_top = fill(canvas(0, shape(top)), 1, ofcolor(top, 0))
    mask_bot = fill(canvas(0, shape(bot)), 1, ofcolor(bot, 0))

    # cell‑wise conjunction of the two masks
    both_mask = cellwise(mask_top, mask_bot, 0)

    both = ofcolor(both_mask, 1)                         # positions where both are 1
    O    = canvas(0, astuple(r, w))
    O    = fill(O, 8, both)
    return O
```

def dsl4(I):
    # 4️⃣  Geometric reasoning: mirror each half horizontally, intersect the
    #      zero‑pixels, then un‑mirror the result.
    sep = ofcolor(I, 7)
    r   = lowermost(sep)
    w   = add(subtract(rightmost(sep), leftmost(sep)), ONE)

    top = crop(I, ORIGIN, astuple(r, w))
    bot = crop(I, astuple(add(r, ONE), ZERO),
                astuple(subtract(height(I), add(r, ONE)), w))

    top_m   = hmirror(top)                               # horizontal flip
    bot_m   = hmirror(bot)

    both_m  = intersection(ofcolor(top_m, 0), ofcolor(bot_m, 0))
    both    = hmirror(both_m)                             # restore original orientation

    O = canvas(0, astuple(r, w))
    O = fill(O, 8, both)
    return O

def dsl5(I):
    # 5️⃣  Relational shift: move the lower‑half zero‑mask towards the upper‑half
    #      until the two masks overlap (one extra step beyond mere adjacency),
    #      then intersect.
    sep = ofcolor(I, 7)
    r   = lowermost(sep)
    w   = add(subtract(rightmost(sep), leftmost(sep)), ONE)

    top = crop(I, ORIGIN, astuple(r, w))
    bot = crop(I, astuple(add(r, ONE), ZERO),
                astuple(subtract(height(I), add(r, ONE)), w))

    top0 = ofcolor(top, 0)
    bot0 = ofcolor(bot, 0)

    dirv   = gravitate(bot0, top0)                       # direction that brings them together
    step   = add(dirv, dirv)                             # one extra step to force overlap
    bot0a  = shift(bot0, step)                           # shifted lower‑half mask

    both = intersection(top0, bot0a)
    O    = canvas(0, astuple(r, w))
    O    = fill(O, 8, both)
    return O
```

def dsl5(I):
    # 5️⃣ Relational / structural – map each foreground cell to its mirrored
    # position on the right half using index arithmetic, then paint both halves
    H, W = shape(I)
    O = canvas(0, (H, add(W, W)))                                   # empty canvas, double width
    O = paint(O, toobject(ofcolor(I, 7), I))                        # left half (original foreground)
    # compute mirrored coordinates for the right half
    right_coords = apply(
        lambda p: (p[0], subtract(double(W), add(p[1], ONE))),
        ofcolor(I, 7)
    )
    right_obj = recolor(7, right_coords)                           # colour the new indices
    O = paint(O, right_obj)                                        # right half (mirrored foreground)
    return O
```
