```python
def dsl2(I):
    # Object‑extraction route: split the grid into 3×3 macro‑blocks,
    # compute the dominant non‑zero colour of each block with `mostcolor`,
    # and rebuild the 3×3 output from the resulting colours.
    rows = vsplit(I, THREE)                                 # three horizontal strips (3 rows each)
    blocks = apply(lambda r: hsplit(r, THREE), rows)        # each strip → three vertical blocks
    colors = apply(lambda blk_row: apply(mostcolor, blk_row), blocks)   # colour of each 3×3 block
    # turn the colours into 1×1 canvases and concatenate back to a 3×3 grid
    cells = apply(lambda row: apply(lambda c: canvas(c, (ONE, ONE)), row), colors)
    row_grids = apply(lambda r: hconcat(hconcat(r[0], r[1]), r[2]), cells)
    O = vconcat(vconcat(row_grids[0], row_grids[1]), row_grids[2])
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # Global – compress empty border, then place the compressed picture on the rows
    # that originally contained colour 1 (by padding with zeros to the original height).
    compressed = compress(I)                           # remove empty outer rows/cols
    rows_one   = ofcolor(I, ONE)                       # cells of colour 1
    bbox_one   = backdrop(rows_one)                    # its bounding rectangle
    top_one    = uppermost(rows_one)                    # top row of the 1‑object
    height_in  = height(I)
    # pad the compressed picture so that its top aligns with the original 1‑object rows
    pad_above  = vconcat(canvas(ZERO, (top_one, width(compressed))), compressed)
    O = vconcat(pad_above, canvas(ZERO, (height_in - top_one - height(compressed), width(compressed))))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # Object‑extraction – move every coloured object (except 0) onto the rows
    # occupied by colour 1, preserving horizontal positions.
    rows_one   = ofcolor(I, ONE)
    target_rows = backdrop(rows_one)                    # rectangle covering the 1‑object
    # start from a blank canvas
    blank = canvas(ZERO, shape(I))
    # for each non‑zero colour, shift it vertically onto the target rows
    colors   = palette(I)                               # all colours present
    def place(c):
        patch = ofcolor(I, c)
        # vertical offset so that the top of the patch aligns with the top of the 1‑object
        dr = subtract(uppermost(rows_one), uppermost(patch))
        moved = shift(patch, (dr, ZERO))
        return moved
    moved_patches = apply(place, colors)
    O = blank
    for p in moved_patches:
        O = paint(O, p)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Relational – expand every coloured object to fill its axis‑aligned bounding rectangle,
    # then intersect the result with the rows that contain colour 1.
    all_colors = palette(I)
    def expand(c):
        obj   = ofcolor(I, c)
        rect  = backdrop(obj)                         # its bounding rectangle
        filled = fill(I, c, rect)                     # recolour the whole rectangle
        return filled
    expanded = apply(expand, all_colors)
    # merge all expanded objects
    merged = canvas(ZERO, shape(I))
    for e in expanded:
        merged = paint(merged, e)

    # keep only the rows where colour 1 originally appeared
    rows_one = ofcolor(I, ONE)
    bbox_one = backdrop(rows_one)
    O = cover(merged, difference(ofindices(merged), ofindices(bbox_one)))  # clip to those rows
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL – remove empty outer rows/cols, then shift the compressed picture
    # vertically so its top aligns with the first row that contains colour 1.
    # After the shift, delete any completely‑empty columns (they are interior
    # blanks that do not contain a coloured cell).  The final canvas has the
    # original height; its width may shrink after column removal.
    comp      = compress(I)                                             # tight picture
    rows_one  = ofcolor(I, ONE)                                        # cells of colour 1
    top_one   = uppermost(rows_one)                                    # its top row (in the original grid)
    # vertical shift: pad with `top_one` empty rows above the compressed picture
    shifted   = vconcat(canvas(ZERO, (top_one, width(comp))), comp)    # now top of picture = top_one
    # keep only the original number of rows (crop bottom if we overflow)
    shifted   = crop(shifted, (ZERO, ZERO), (height(I), width(comp)))
    # delete any column that is completely zero
    empty_cols = ofcolor(shifted, ZERO)                                 # all zero cells
    col_box    = backdrop(empty_cols)                                   # full bounding box of zeros
    # keep only those columns that are **not** completely zero
    O          = cover(shifted, difference(ofcolor(shifted, ZERO), col_box))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC – for each colour compute the direction vector that brings its
    # topmost cell onto the topmost cell of colour 1, then move the whole
    # colour patch by that vector using gravitate (which yields the needed
    # displacement).  Finally paint the shifted objects.
    top_one     = ofcolor(I, ONE)                             # cells of colour 1
    ref_one     = initset({ulcorner(top_one)})                # top‑left cell of colour 1
    colors      = difference(palette(I), initset(ZERO))
    def move(c):
        src   = ofcolor(I, c)                                 # source cells
        drc   = gravitate(src, ref_one)                       # direction to align tops
        shifted = shift(src, drc)                              # apply displacement
        return recolor(c, shifted)                            # keep colour information
    shifted   = apply(move, colors)
    merged    = merge(shifted)
    O         = paint(canvas(ZERO, shape(I)), merged)
    return O
```

```python
    O         = paint(canvas(ZERO, shape(I)), merged)
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # 1.  Identify the colour that occurs least often (the “seed” colour)
    seed    = leastcolor(I)                               # 1 in all three trainings
    # 2.  All cells having that colour
    src     = ofcolor(I, seed)                            # set of (r,c)
    # 3.  Extract the set of rows and columns that contain a seed cell
    rows    = {r for (r, _) in src}                       # via set‑comprehension (allowed as DSL)
    cols    = {c for (_, c) in src}
    # 4.  Build a patch covering those complete rows and columns
    rows_pt = { (r, c) for r in rows for c in range(width(I)) }
    cols_pt = { (r, c) for c in cols for r in range(height(I)) }
    cross   = rows_pt | cols_pt                              # union → full cross
    # 5.  Write the cross with the seed colour, but turn the original
    #     seed cells into the next integer (seed+1 → 2)
    O1      = fill(I, seed, cross)                           # paint cross with seed
    O       = recolor(seed+1, src) | O1                       # recolour originals → 2
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    seed    = leastcolor(I)                                # 1
    src     = ofcolor(I, seed)                             # seed cells
    # Build the full cross (rows + columns of seed cells)
    rows    = { r for (r,_) in src }
    cols    = { c for (_,c) in src }
    cross   = { (r,c) for r in rows for c in range(width(I)) } | \
              { (r,c) for c in cols for r in range(height(I)) }
    # Adjacent cells (Manhattan distance = 1) to the cross, excluding the cross itself
    adj     = { n for p in cross for n in neighbors(p) } - cross
    # Paint:
    O = fill(I, seed, cross)          # cross → seed colour (1)
    O = recolor(3, adj) | O          # neighbours → 3
    O = recolor(seed+1, src) | O    # original seeds → 2
    return O
```

```python
    •  Paint the cross with the seed colour, turn the original seed cells into
       seed+1 (value 2) and colour every orthogonal neighbour of the cross with 3.
    """
    seed   = leastcolor(I)                     # the rare colour (1)
    src    = ofcolor(I, seed)                  # set of seed cells

    # ----- build the cross (full rows + full columns of every seed cell)
    def lines(p):
        h = combine(shoot(p, RIGHT), shoot(p, LEFT))   # whole row of p
        v = combine(shoot(p, DOWN),  shoot(p, UP))     # whole column of p
        return combine(h, v)
    cross  = merge(apply(lines, src))          # union of all rows/columns

    # ----- paint the cross with the seed colour
    O0 = fill(I, seed, cross)

    # ----- orthogonal neighbours of the cross (excluding the cross itself)
    nbrs   = merge(apply(neighbors, cross))
    adj    = difference(nbrs, cross)

    # ----- paint neighbours with 3 and original seeds with 2
    O1 = paint(O0, recolor(3, adj))
    O  = paint(O1, recolor(seed + 1, src))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    """
    COLOR‑FILTERING:
    •  Replace the rare colour (seed) by seed+1 (turn 1 → 2).
    •  Replace every orthogonal neighbour of a seed cell by colour 3.
    •  Leave all other cells unchanged.

    src    = ofcolor(I, seed)                  # seed cells

    nb1 = shift(src, UP)
    nb2 = shift(src, DOWN)
    nb3 = shift(src, LEFT)
    nb4 = shift(src, RIGHT)
    neigh = difference(combine(combine(nb1, nb2), combine(nb3, nb4)), src)

    O0 = paint(I, recolor(seed + 1, src))     # turn 1 → 2
    O  = paint(O0, recolor(3, neigh))          # turn neighbours → 3
    return O
```

```python
    •  Mirror the whole picture on the counter‑diagonal.
```

```python
    # paint neighbours with colour 3 and original seeds with colour 2
    O1 = paint(O0, recolor(3, adj))
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # geometric – shift a full‑grid cross built at the origin to each seed
    seed   = leastcolor(I)                     # 1
    src    = ofcolor(I, seed)                  # seed cells
    # a full‑grid cross centred at (0,0)
    base   = combine(
                combine(shoot(ORIGIN, RIGHT), shoot(ORIGIN, LEFT)),
                combine(shoot(ORIGIN, DOWN),  shoot(ORIGIN, UP)))
    # move that cross to every seed position and unite
    cross  = merge(apply(lambda p: shift(base, p), src))
    O0     = fill(I, seed, cross)               # paint cross with seed colour
    nbrs   = merge(apply(neighbors, cross))     # neighbours of the cross
    adj    = difference(nbrs, cross)            # external neighbours only
    O1     = paint(O0, recolor(3, adj))         # colour neighbours with 3
    O      = paint(O1, recolor(seed + 1, src)) # recolour original seeds with 2
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # relational – generate each full row/column line by shooting from the grid edges
    seed   = leastcolor(I)                     # 1
    src    = ofcolor(I, seed)                  # seed cells
    rows   = { r for (r, _) in src }
    cols   = { c for (_, c) in src }
    # horizontal lines: start at left edge of each row
    hlines = merge(apply(lambda r: shoot((r, 0), RIGHT), rows))
    # vertical lines: start at top edge of each column
    vlines = merge(apply(lambda c: shoot((0, c), DOWN), cols))
    cross  = combine(hlines, vlines)           # union of all rows and columns
    O0     = fill(I, seed, cross)              # paint the cross with seed colour
    nbrs   = merge(apply(neighbors, cross))    # neighbours of the cross
    adj    = difference(nbrs, cross)           # keep only the outside neighbours
    O1     = paint(O0, recolor(3, adj))        # colour neighbours with 3
    O      = paint(O1, recolor(seed + 1, src))# recolour original seeds with 2
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # colour‑filtering – recolour seeds and their neighbours first,
    # then paint the cross using the original seed colour
    seed   = leastcolor(I)
    src    = ofcolor(I, seed)
    # recolour seeds → 2
    Oa     = paint(I, recolor(seed + 1, src))
    # neighbours of the original seeds → 3
    neigh  = difference(merge(apply(neighbors, src)), src)
    Ob     = paint(Oa, recolor(3, neigh))
    # rows/cols that contain a seed
    rows   = { r for (r, _) in src }
    cols   = { c for (_, c) in src }
    cross  = combine(
                { (r, c) for r in rows for c in range(width(I)) },
                { (r, c) for c in cols for r in range(height(I)) })
    # fill the cross with the seed colour, but keep the recoloured seeds unchanged
    cross_without_src = difference(cross, src)
    Oc = fill(Ob, seed, cross_without_src)
    return Oc
```

```python
    O1        = paint(O0, recolor(3, adj2))
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑LEVEL: expand every 1×1 cell to a 3×3 block.
    # The blocks coming from the original grid occupy the
    # first and last vertical thirds; the blocks coming from
    # the horizontally‑mirrored grid are shifted down one third.
    # All blocks are painted on a blank 6×6 canvas.

    orig_objs   = objects(I, True, False, False)
    orig_blocks = apply(lambda o: upscale(toobject(o, I), 3), orig_objs)

    # – create 3×3 blocks for the mirrored cells and shift them down
    mirr_grid   = hmirror(I)
    mirr_objs   = objects(mirr_grid, True, False, False)
    mirr_blocks = apply(
        lambda o: shift(upscale(toobject(o, mirr_grid), 3), (3, 0)),
        mirr_objs)

    # – combine all blocks and paint them
    all_blocks  = combine(combine(orig_blocks, mirr_blocks))
    blank       = canvas(0, (6, 6))
    O = paint(blank, all_blocks)
    return O
```

```python
    R       = rot90(I)                                 # 90° cw
    top     = hupscale(R, 3)                           # original (rotated)
    middle  = hupscale(hmirror(R), 3)                  # mirrored (rotated)
    bottom  = hupscale(R, 3)                           # original (rotated)

    tiled   = vconcat(top, vconcat(middle, bottom))    # 6×6, still rotated
    O       = rot270(tiled)                           # rotate back
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL – construct the output by addressing rows
    # through explicit index arithmetic and a single conditional branch.
    idxs   = asindices(canvas(0, (6, 6)))                     # all 6×6 positions
    # map each index (i,j) → colour from the appropriate source band
    def colour_at(p):
        i, j = p
        # which source row (0‑1 original, 2‑3 mirrored, 4‑5 original) ?
        src_i = i % 2
        src_j = j % 2
        # choose original or mirrored column based on vertical band
        col = branch(i < 2 or i >= 4,
                     index(I, (src_i, src_j)),               # original
                     index(I, (src_i, 1 - src_j)))           # mirrored
        return col
    # build a 6×6 grid whose (i,j) cell is colour_at((i,j))
    O = tuple(tuple(colour_at((i, j)) for j in range(6)) for i in range(6))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT EXTRACTION: isolate all objects of colour 5, recolour each of them
    # according to the third (left/middle/right) in which its centre lies,

             4 if leftmost(o) >= 2*width(I)//3 else 1),
            o),
        objs5)

    O = paint(canvas0, combine(*recoloured))           # paint all recoloured objects
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL SHAPE‑CLASSIFICATION per vertical third
    strips = hsplit(I, 3)                     # three vertical strips
    s0, s1, s2 = strips[0], strips[1], strips[2]

    def strip_color(S):
        cnt  = colorcount(S, 5)               # number of 5‑pixels
        h    = height(S)
        top  = equality(uppermost(ofcolor(S, 5)), 0)
        bot  = equality(lowermost(ofcolor(S, 5)), decrement(h))
        top_line    = both(top, equality(lowermost(ofcolor(S, 5)), 0))
        bot_line    = both(bot, equality(uppermost(ofcolor(S, 5)), decrement(h)))
        single      = equality(cnt, 1)
        border      = equality(cnt, 8)          # full perimeter of a 3×3 block
        return branch(single, 4,
               branch(border, 3,
               branch(top_line, 6,
               branch(bot_line, 1, 9))))

    c0 = strip_color(s0)
    c1 = strip_color(s1)
    c2 = strip_color(s2)

    out0 = canvas(c0, shape(s0))
    out1 = canvas(c1, shape(s1))
    out2 = canvas(c2, shape(s2))
    O = hconcat(hconcat(out0, out1), out2)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC REASONING: use vertical mirroring to detect vertical symmetry;
    # symmetric thirds receive colour 3, otherwise colour is derived from the
    # number of 5‑pixels (as in dsl3).
    V = vmirror(I)                                     # vertical mirror
    strips = hsplit(I, 3)
    def sym_color(S, Vstrip):
        inter = intersection(ofcolor(S,5), ofcolor(Vstrip,5))
        sym   = greater(colorcount(inter,5), 0)         # any overlap → symmetric
        return branch(sym, 3,
               branch(equality(colorcount(S,5),1), 4,
               branch(equality(colorcount(S,5),8), 3,
               branch(equality(uppermost(ofcolor(S,5)),0), 6,
               branch(equality(lowermost(ofcolor(S,5)), decrement(height(S))), 1, 9))))
    c0 = sym_color(strips[0], hsplit(V,3)[0])
    c1 = sym_color(strips[1], hsplit(V,3)[1])
    c2 = sym_color(strips[2], hsplit(V,3)[2])
    out0 = canvas(c0, shape(strips[0]))
    out1 = canvas(c1, shape(strips[1]))
    out2 = canvas(c2, shape(strips[2]))
    O = hconcat(hconcat(out0, out1), out2)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL: decide colour of a third from its adjacency
    # to the four borders of that third.
    strips = hsplit(I, 3)
    def border_color(S):
        P   = ofcolor(S,5)                             # patch of 5‑pixels
        top = equality(uppermost(P), 0)
        bot = equality(lowermost(P), decrement(height(S)))
        lef = equality(leftmost(P), 0)
        rig = equality(rightmost(P), decrement(width(S)))
        # classification by border pattern
        return branch(and(top, not_(bot), not_(lef), not_(rig)), 6,          # only top
               branch(and(bot, not_(top), not_(lef), not_(rig)), 1,          # only bottom
               branch(and(lef, rig, top, bot), 3,                           # touches all four → perimeter
               branch(and(lef, top), 9,                                     # top‑left corner (diagonal)
               branch(equality(colorcount(P,5),1), 4, 9)))))
    c0 = border_color(strips[0])
    c1 = border_color(strips[1])
    c2 = border_color(strips[2])
    O = fill(fill(fill(I, c0, ofcolor(strips[0],5)),
               c1, ofcolor(strips[1],5)),
               c2, ofcolor(strips[2],5))
    return O
```

```python
    # ----- Global transformation -----
    # 1. recolor every 1 → 2, keep 0 unchanged
    recolored = recolor(TWO, ofcolor(I, ONE))

    extra     = vconcat(first_row, top_two)          # 3 rows: 1‑2‑1
```

```python
    # ----- Object‑extraction -----
    # 1. detect all cells of colour 1 as an object set
    ones = ofcolor(I, ONE)
    # 2. recolour that object to 2
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ----- Geometric reasoning -----
    # 1. recolour 1 → 2
    recolored = recolor(TWO, ofcolor(I, ONE))
    # 2. create a vertical mirror of the recoloured grid
    mirrored  = vmirror(recolored)
    # 3. overlay the mirrored image on top of the original (higher values win)
    overlay   = max(recolored, mirrored)   # element‑wise max using built‑in max as a placeholder
    # 4. extend the result by appending the top row three times
    h, w = shape(overlay)
    top    = crop(overlay, (0, 0), (1, w))
    extra  = vconcat(top, vconcat(top, top))
    O      = vconcat(overlay, extra)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ----- Relational / structural reasoning -----
    # 1. find the set of all non‑zero cells (colour 1)
    nz = ofcolor(I, ONE)
    # 2. compute its vertical period (distance between repeated rows)
    period = vperiod(nz)
    # 3. upscale the object vertically by the period (creates the needed extra rows)
    upscaled = vupscale(paint(canvas(ZERO, shape(I)), nz), period)
    # 4. recolour all 1 → 2 inside the up‑scaled grid
    O = recolor(TWO, ofcolor(upscaled, ONE))
    return O
```

```python
    H, W = shape(R)
    # 3. three rows to be appended: first row, second row, first row again
    r0 = crop(R, (0, 0), (1, W))
    r1 = crop(R, (1, 0), (1, W))
    extra = vconcat(r0, vconcat(r1, r0))
    # 4. final output
    O = vconcat(R, extra)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ---------- Object‑extraction ----------
    # 1. turn the 1‑cells into colour 2
    R = recolor(TWO, ofcolor(I, ONE))
    # 2. collect all 2‑cells as a patch
    cells2 = ofcolor(R, TWO)
    # 3. compute the vertical period of that patch
    p = vperiod(cells2)
    # 4. create a blank canvas with the original size, paint the recoloured cells on it
    base = paint(canvas(ZERO, shape(R)), cells2)
    # 5. upscale the canvas vertically by the period and then cut it back to original height
    up   = vupscale(base, p)
    H, W = shape(R)
    O    = crop(up, (0, 0), (H, W))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---------- Relational / structural ----------
    # 1. recolour 1 → 2
    R = recolor(TWO, ofcolor(I, ONE))
    # 2. extract the set of rows that contain at least one colour 2 cell
    rows = ofcolor(R, TWO)            # patch of all non‑zero cells
    # 3. compute the set of distinct row‑indices
    row_idxs = { r for (_, (r, _)) in rows }
    # 4. build a new grid consisting of the original rows plus a copy of the first row
    #    (we achieve this by painting the first row again on a canvas that is one row taller)
    H, W = shape(R)
    canvas_big = canvas(ZERO, (H + 1, W))
    first_row   = crop(R, (0, 0), (1, W))
    painted     = paint(canvas_big, ofcolor(R, TWO))
    O = paint(painted, ofcolor(first_row, TWO))
    # 5. crop back to the original height plus the added row
    O = crop(O, (0, 0), (H + 1, W))
    return O
```

```python
    Z1     = paint(Z, ofcolor(G, TWO))                           # paint the recoloured whole grid
    O      = paint(Z1, shifted)                                   # paint the shifted upper‑half patch
    return O
```

```python
    O       = paint(Z, mirrored)                                 # paint the mirrored patch on a clean canvas
    O       = paint(O, O1)                                        # overlay the original 2‑cells
    return O
```

```python
    above   = shift(upper, (NEG_ONE, ZERO))                      # cells one row above each 2‑cell
    dup     = intersect(upper, above)                            # cells that have a 2‑cell directly above
    shifted = shift(dup, (ONE, ZERO))                            # copy them one row lower
    Z       = canvas(ZERO, shape(G))                             # zero canvas of original size
    O1      = paint(Z, upper)                                    # paint original 2‑cells
    O       = paint(O1, shifted)                                 # paint the duplicated lower cells
    return O
```

```python
    Z1     = fill(Z, TWO, ofcolor(G, TWO))                       # original 2‑cells
    O      = fold(lambda acc, obj: fill(acc, TWO, obj), Z1, dup)  # merge all duplicates
    return O
```

```python
    # treat each 2‑cell as an object, duplicate those whose uppermost row lies in the
    # upper half, and merge the duplicates with the original pattern.

    top_objs = { o for o in twos if uppermost(o) < half }
    dup_objs = { shift(o, (half, ZERO)) for o in top_objs }   # shifted copies
    Z = canvas(ZERO, (add(h, half), w))         # canvas large enough
    Z0 = fill(Z, TWO, ofcolor(G, TWO))         # paint original 2‑cells
    # merge all duplicated objects at once (union of index sets)
    dup_union = combine(dup_objs, initset())    # union of the duplicated objects
    O = fill(Z0, TWO, dup_union)                # paint the duplicated copy
    return O
```

```python
    G = switch(I, ONE, TWO)                                   # 1 → 2

    return O
```

```python
    G = switch(I, ONE, TWO)                                   # recolour
    h, w = shape(G)
    half = divide(h, TWO)
```

```python
    # union of those objects as a patch of indices
    upper_union = combine(*upper_objs) if upper_objs else frozenset()
    # grids representing the upper‑half patch (original size half×w)
    base = canvas(ZERO, (half, w))
    upper_grid = fill(base, TWO, upper_union)
    # condition: lower‑half indices of colour‑2 equal upper‑half indices
    lower_union = ofcolor(crop(G, (half, ZERO), (half, w)), TWO
    cond = equality(upper_union, lower_union[0])  # compare index sets
    upper_fixed = branch(cond, upper_grid, hmirror(upper_grid))
    # place the copy below the original pattern
    shifted = shift(ofcolor(upper_fixed, TWO), (half, ZERO))
    Z = canvas(ZERO, (add(h, half), w))
    Z0 = fill(Z, TWO, ofcolor(G, TWO))
    O = fill(Z0, TWO, shifted)
    return O
```

```python
    adj_ones = intersection(shift(six, DOWN), ones)

    return replace(step2, 6, 8)
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # Geometric – colour the whole left‑most non‑8 column with 7,
    # then erase every other non‑8 colour (turn to 8).
    non8     = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 8))
    leftcol  = valmin(non8, lambda p: p[1])                # smallest column index
    rows     = interval(0, len(I), 1)
    colpatch = { (r, leftcol) for r in rows }
    painted  = fill(I, 7, colpatch)                      # colour that column 7
    return replace(painted, 6, 8)                         # turn remaining 6 → 8 (all other colours already 8)
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Object‑based: for every non‑8 object, colour its centre 7
    # and erase the whole object (turn to background 8).
    objs      = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 8)            # objects whose colour is not 8
    centres   = mapply(lambda o: {center(o)}, objs)       # set of centre cells
    painted   = fill(I, 7, centres)                      # paint centres 7
    # erase every original non‑8 cell
    non8cells = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 8))
    return fill(painted, 8, non8cells)
```

```python
    patch   = combine(ofcolor(I, 1), ofcolor(I, 6))          # all 1‑ and 6‑cells
    start   = ulcorner(patch)                               # top‑left corner of the bounding box
    dims    = shape(patch)                                   # height & width of that box
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # start from a blank canvas of the same size
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    # extract every colored object (including its color)
    objs = objects(I, True, False, True)
    # create both vertical and horizontal mirrors of each object
    vmir = apply(vmirror, objs)          # vertical flip (mirror across horizontal axis)
    hmir = apply(hmirror, objs)          # horizontal flip (mirror across vertical axis)
    # union of original objects and their mirrors
    all_objs = combine(combine(objs, vmir), hmir)
    # paint every object onto the blank canvas
    O = apply(lambda obj: paint(O, obj), all_objs)[0]
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # locate the unique pixel whose color appears exactly once
    uniq_color = leastcommon(apply(lambda o: color(o), objects(I, True, False, True)))
    uniq_pix   = ofcolor(I, uniq_color)          # set of coordinates with that color
    # compute its horizontal and vertical reflections
    h_ref = apply(lambda c: (c[0], subtract(shape(I)[1] - 1, c[1])), uniq_pix)
    v_ref = apply(lambda c: (subtract(shape(I)[0] - 1, c[0]), c[1]), uniq_pix)
    # build patches from the reflections
    h_patch = toobject(h_ref, I)
    v_patch = toobject(v_ref, I)
    # add the reflected patches to the original grid
    O = paint(I, h_patch)
    O = paint(O, v_patch)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # Rare‑color propagation: take the colour that occurs the fewest non‑zero cells
    # and reflect its cells across the vertical axis defined by the most common colour.
    # 1️⃣  pick rare colour
    rare   = argmin(palette(I), lambda c: branch(c == 0, 10**9, colorcount(I, c)))
    # 2️⃣  axis centre = column of the most common colour’s centre of mass
    common = argmax(palette(I), lambda c: branch(c == 0, -1, colorcount(I, c)))
    axis   = second(centerofmass(ofcolor(I, common), 1)        # column index of centre
    # 3️⃣  cells of the rare colour
    rare_cells = ofcolor(I, rare)
    # 4️⃣  mirror each cell left↔right across the axis
    mirrored = apply(lambda p: (p[0],
                               add(axis,
                                   subtract(p[1], axis)), rare_cells)
    # 5️⃣  turn the mirrored indices back into an object (preserving colour)
    mir_obj = toobject(mirrored, I)
    # 6️⃣  overlay on the original grid
    O = paint(I, mir_obj)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):

    # and copy every coloured cell one period away in each direction.
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Axis‑extension: find the longest horizontal line of a non‑zero colour,
    # then extend that line left and right until the grid border.
    # 1️⃣  identify the longest horizontal line
    hlines = apply(lambda o: o if hline(o) else initset(None), objects(I, True, False, True))
    longest = argmax(hlines, lambda o: size(o))
    # 2️⃣  its row index
    row = first(center(longest))
    # 3️⃣  build a full‑row patch of the same colour
    col_set = apply(lambda p: p[1], toindices(longest))
    colour  = color(longest)
    full_row = initset((row, c) for c in interval(0, width(I), 1))
    full_obj = recolor(colour, full_row)
    # 4️⃣  paint the extended row onto the original grid
    O = paint(I, full_obj)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # -------- geometric mirroring ----------
    # 1️⃣  colour that occurs the fewest non‑zero cells  (rare)
    rare   = argmin(palette(I), lambda c: branch(c == 0, 10**9, colorcount(I, c)))
    # 2️⃣  colour that occurs the most non‑zero cells (common)
    common = argmax(palette(I), lambda c: branch(c == 0, -1,   colorcount(I, c)))
    # 3️⃣  centre of mass of the common colour → symmetry centre
    ctr    = centerofmass(ofcolor(I, common))                 # (rc, cc)
    # 4️⃣  all cells of the rare colour
    rcells = ofcolor(I, rare)
    # 5️⃣  mirrors of each rare cell w.r.t. that centre
    hmir   = apply(lambda p: (p[0],
                              add(ctr[1], subtract(ctr[1], p[1]))), rcells)
    vmir   = apply(lambda p: (add(ctr[0], subtract(ctr[0], p[0])),
                              p[1]), rcells)
    bmir   = apply(lambda p: (add(ctr[0], subtract(ctr[0], p[0])),
                              add(ctr[1], subtract(ctr[1], p[1]))), rcells)
    # 6️⃣  union of original rare cells and all their mirrors
    allpts = combine(combine(combine(rcells, hmir), vmir), bmir)
    # 7️⃣  recolour the union with the rare colour and paint over the input
    obj    = recolor(rare, allpts)
    O      = paint(I, obj)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # -------- shift‑to‑centre → global mirrors ----------
    rare   = argmin(palette(I), lambda c: branch(c == 0, 10**9, colorcount(I, c)))
    common = argmax(palette(I), lambda c: branch(c == 0, -1,   colorcount(I, c)))
    comobj = ofcolor(I, common)                     # patch of common colour
    ctr    = centerofmass(comobj)                   # its centre
    # shift the whole grid so that this centre coincides with the grid centre
    gc     = (height(I)//2, width(I)//2)             # grid centre (integer)
    delta  = subtract(gc, ctr)                     # vector to move the centre
    I0     = shift(I, delta)                       # whole grid shifted
    # now perform global vertical and horizontal mirrors on the rare colour
    rcells = ofcolor(I0, rare)
    vr     = apply(vmirror, {rcells})               # vertical mirror
    hr     = apply(hmirror, {rcells})               # horizontal mirror
    both   = apply(vmirror, hr)                     # both mirrors
    allpts = combine(combine(rcells, vr), combine(hr, both))
    obj    = recolor(rare, allpts)
    # paint and shift back
    O0     = paint(I0, obj)
    O      = shift(O0, subtract(ctr, gc))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # -------- crop to common‑colour bounding box ----------
    rare   = argmin(palette(I), lambda c: branch(c == 0, 10**9, colorcount(I, c)))
    common = argmax(palette(I), lambda c: branch(c == 0, -1,   colorcount(I, c)))
    comobj = ofcolor(I, common)
    # minimal sub‑grid that contains all common cells
    sub    = subgrid(comobj, I)                     # returns a sub‑grid
    # coordinates of rare cells expressed inside that sub‑grid
    # (they keep their absolute indices – we will later translate them)
    rcells = ofcolor(I, rare)
    # centre of mass of the common colour *inside* the sub‑grid
    ctr    = centerofmass(ofcolor(sub, common))
    # mirrors inside the sub‑grid (global vmirror/hmirror now act w.r.t. sub‑grid centre)
    hmir   = apply(lambda o: hmirror(o), {rcells})
    vmir   = apply(lambda o: vmirror(o), {rcells})
    bmir   = apply(lambda o: hmirror(vmirror(o)), {rcells})
    allpts = combine(combine(rcells, hmir), combine(vmir, bmir))
    # recolour and embed back into the original grid
    obj    = recolor(rare, allpts)
    O      = paint(I, obj)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # -------- colour‑filter → global mirrors ----------
    # remove the most common colour, mirror what remains globally, then restore the common colour
    common = argmax(palette(I), lambda c: branch(c == 0, -1, colorcount(I, c)))
    # background‑only grid (common colour turned to 0)
    B      = replace(I, common, 0)
    # all non‑zero cells now belong to the rare colour(s)
    rare_cells = ofcolor(B, lambda v: v != 0)
    # apply global mirrors to those cells
    hmir   = apply(lambda p: (p[0],
                              width(I)-1-p[1]), rare_cells)   # horizontal flip
    vmir   = apply(lambda p: (height(I)-1-p[0], p[1]), rare_cells) # vertical flip
    bmir   = apply(lambda p: (height(I)-1-p[0],
                              width(I)-1-p[1]), rare_cells)   # both
    allpts = combine(combine(rare_cells, hmir), combine(vmir, bmir))
    # colour of the rare cells (they are all the same)
    rare   = argmin(palette(I), lambda c: branch(c == 0, 10**9, colorcount(I, c)))
    obj    = recolor(rare, allpts)
    # paint rare mirrors on the original grid, then restore the common colour (already present)
    O      = paint(I, obj)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ---- object‑extraction ----
    # 1. locate the whole line of 1’s (they are collinear with slope 1)
    # 2. build the complete main diagonal of the grid
    # 3. cut away the part of the diagonal that ends at the last 1
    # 4. colour the remaining cells with 2
    ones        = ofcolor(I, 1)
    last_one    = astuple(lowermost(ones), rightmost(ones))
    h, w        = shape(I)
    last_cell   = subtract(astuple(h, w), astuple(1, 1))            # (h‑1,w‑1)
    full_diag   = connect(astuple(0, 0), last_cell)                # whole main diagonal
    prefix_diag = connect(astuple(0, 0), last_one)                # part up to the last 1
    to_fill     = difference(full_diag, prefix_diag)               # cells after the last 1
    O = fill(I, 2, to_fill)
    return O
```

```python
    # 1. the three 1‑pixels are equally spaced; their column‑step equals the row‑step

    line        = shoot(start, vec)                   # cells to the border
    O = fill(I, 2, line)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ---- global transformation (crop + underpaint) ----
    # 1. cut out the sub‑grid that starts right after the last 1 and reaches the bottom‑right
    # 2. fill that whole sub‑grid with 2 (it is completely background)
    # 3. paste the coloured sub‑grid back only on the background cells (underpaint)
    ones        = ofcolor(I, 1)
    last_one    = astuple(lowermost(ones), rightmost(ones))
    start       = increment(last_one)
    h, w        = shape(I)
    dims        = subtract(astuple(h, w), start)      # (remaining rows, remaining cols)
    sub_canvas  = canvas(2, dims)                     # a block of 2’s
    O           = underpaint(I, toobject(ofcolor(sub_canvas, 2), I))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---- colour‑filtering (fill only the diagonal beyond the farthest 1) ----
    # 1. the farthest 1 from the origin determines how far the diagonal is already occupied
    # 2. the main diagonal of the whole grid is built, then the prefix up to that distance
    #    is removed; the rest is coloured 2.
    ones        = ofcolor(I, 1)
    max_dist   = valmax(ones, lambda p: manhattan(initset((0, 0)), initset(p)))
    h, w       = shape(I)
    last_cell  = subtract(astuple(h, w), astuple(1, 1))
    full_diag  = connect(astuple(0, 0), last_cell)           # whole main diagonal
    # the cell that corresponds to the maximal Manhattan distance
    cut_len    = add(divide(max_dist, 2), 1)                 # because dist( (r,r) ) = 2r
    cut_point  = astuple(cut_len, cut_len)
    prefix     = connect(astuple(0, 0), cut_point)           # occupied part of the diagonal
    to_fill    = difference(full_diag, prefix)               # still‑empty diagonal cells
    O = fill(I, 2, to_fill)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # relational/structural: compute the step vector from the first to the last 1,
    # then shoot from the cell after the last 1.
    ones      = ofcolor(I, 1)
    pts       = tuple(sorted(ones))                                    # ordered list of 1‑positions
    full_vec  = subtract(pts[-1], pts[0])                             # total displacement
    step_cnt  = add(size(pts), -1)                                     # number of intervals (len‑1)
    step      = divide(full_vec, step_cnt)                             # elementary (Δr,Δc)
    start     = increment(pts[-1])                                     # first empty cell after the line
    line      = shoot(start, step)                                     # continuation of the line
    O = fill(I, 2, line)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # colour‑filtering with cover & underpaint:
    # build a full canvas of 2’s, keep only the main diagonal,
    # erase the prefix up to the last 1, then underpaint onto the original grid.
    h, w          = shape(I)
    canvas2       = canvas(2, astuple(h, w))                           # whole grid filled with 2
    full_diag     = connect(astuple(0, 0), subtract(astuple(h, w), astuple(1, 1)))
    diag_only     = cover(canvas2, difference(ofcolor(canvas2, 2), full_diag))
    ones          = ofcolor(I, 1)
    last_one      = astuple(lowermost(ones), rightmost(ones))
    prefix_diag   = connect(astuple(0, 0), last_one)
    to_fill       = cover(diag_only, prefix_diag)                     # erase the occupied prefix
    O = underpaint(I, toobject(to_fill, I))                           # paint the remaining 2’s on background
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL (periodicity):
    #   The horizontal and vertical periods of the 1‑pixels give the step (Δr,Δc)
    #   of the diagonal; continue the line from the cell after the last 1.
    ones     = ofcolor(I, 1)
    step_h   = hperiod(ones)                                            # horizontal period
    step_v   = vperiod(ones)                                            # vertical period
    step     = astuple(step_h, step_v)                                   # (Δr, Δc)
    last_one = astuple(lowermost(ones), rightmost(ones))
    start    = increment(last_one)
    line     = shoot(start, step)                                        # continuation of the diagonal
    O        = fill(I, 2, line)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # GLOBAL – rotate, draw the missing column, then rotate back
    # after a 90° clockwise rotation the main diagonal becomes a vertical line
    R          = rot90(I)
    ones_R     = ofcolor(R, 1)                                     # 1‑pixels are already on the same vertical line
    last_one_R = astuple(lowermost(ones_R), rightmost(ones_R))
    start_R    = increment(last_one_R)                             # first empty cell below the last 1 in the rotated view
    col_R      = shoot(start_R, astuple(0, 1))                     # vertical ray downwards
    R_filled   = fill(R, 2, col_R)                                 # paint the ray in the rotated grid
    O          = rot270(R_filled)                                  # rotate back to original orientation
    return O
```

```python
    unit_step  = divide(delta, delta)                                  # normalise to (1,1)
    start      = increment(last_one)                                   # cell right after the last 1
    line       = shoot(start, unit_step)                              # continue the diagonal
    O          = fill(I, 2, line)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):

    # keep only the part that is missing,

    ones       = ofcolor(I, 1)

    O          = underpaint(I, mask_obj)                               # paint only where background is 0
    return O
```

```python
    R2        = fill(R, 2, col_R)

    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL – use the displacement between the first two 1‑pixels
    # as a unit step, then draw that step repeatedly from the last 1.
    ones        = ofcolor(I, 1)
    first_one   = ulcorner(ones)
    # locate the second 1 by moving one step down‑right from the first one
    second_one  = astuple(increment(first_one)[0], increment(first_one)[1])
    unit_step   = subtract(second_one, first_one)          # (gap,gap)
    last_one    = astuple(lowermost(ones), rightmost(ones))
    start       = increment(last_one)                       # cell after the last 1
    continuation = shoot(start, unit_step)                 # repeated step until border
    O           = fill(I, 2, continuation)                # colour the new cells with 2
    return O
```

#### DSL

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL TRANSFORMATION:
    #   1.  Identify all non‑zero cells.
    #   2.  Compute the height and width of their bounding box.
    #   3.  Split each dimension into tens and units (using divide / multiply / subtract).
    #   4.  Write the four digits into a 2×2 grid (row 0 → height, row 1 → width).
    nz        = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))          # non‑zero cells
    box       = backdrop(nz)                                   # bounding‑box patch
    h         = height(box)                                    # height
    w         = width(box)                                     # width
    ht        = divide(h, 10)                                  # height tens
    hu        = subtract(h, multiply(ht, 10))                  # height units
    wt        = divide(w, 10)                                  # width tens
    wu        = subtract(w, multiply(wt, 10))                  # width units
    base      = canvas(0, (2, 2))                              # 2×2 zero canvas
    step1     = fill(base, ht, initset((0, 0)))                # (0,0) ← ht
    step2     = fill(step1, hu, initset((0, 1)))               # (0,1) ← hu
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT EXTRACTION:
    #   Keep only the objects whose colour is the most frequent (the dominant colour).
    #   Then output a grid that contains exactly those objects (all other cells become 0).
    objs          = fgpartition(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=False)
    dom_color     = mostcommon({color(o) for o in objs})
    dom_objs      = {obj for obj in objs if color(obj) == dom_color}
    base          = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O             = paint(base, combine(*dom_objs))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # COLOR FILTERING:
    #   Replace every occurrence of colour 8 with 1, every 0 with 8,
    #   and finally turn the temporary 1 back into 0.
    #   (effectively swaps the background colour 0 and the dominant colour 8).
    step1 = replace(I, 8, -1)          # mark former 8’s
    step2 = replace(step1, 0, 8)       # background → 8
    O     = replace(step2, -1, 0)       # former 8’s → background
    return O
```

```python
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL:
    #   Locate the unique 2‑coloured object and the unique 3‑coloured object.
    #   Move the 2‑object so that its centre coincides with the centre of the 3‑object.
    obj2   = toobject(ofcolor(I, 2), I)
    obj3   = toobject(ofcolor(I, 3), I)
    delta  = subtract(center(obj3), center(obj2))
    O      = move(I, obj2, delta)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL MIN/MAX APPROACH:
    #   Compute extreme row/column indices of colour 8 with valmin/valmax,
    #   turn them into height and width, then write the digits.
    pts   = ofcolor(I, 8)                                 # all 8‑cells
    rmin  = valmin(pts, lambda p: p[0])
    rmax  = valmax(pts, lambda p: p[0])
    cmin  = valmin(pts, lambda p: p[1])
    cmax  = valmax(pts, lambda p: p[1])
    h     = add(subtract(rmax, rmin), 1)                # number of rows occupied
    w     = add(subtract(cmax, cmin), 1)                # number of columns occupied
    ht    = divide(h, 10)
    hu    = subtract(h, multiply(ht, 10))
    wt    = divide(w, 10)
    wu    = subtract(w, multiply(wt, 10))
    base  = canvas(0, (2, 2))
    O     = fill(fill(fill(fill(base, ht, initset((0, 0))),
                      hu, initset((0, 1))),
                 wt, initset((1, 0))),
                 wu, initset((1, 1)))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # split the grid into rows
    rows = hsplit(I, TEN)                        # ten rows (height = 15, but hsplit works with any size)
    # for each row: keep cells that lie strictly right of the rightmost 8
    def fill_row(row):
        r8 = ofcolor(row, 8)
        # if the row contains an 8, compute its rightmost column index
        col = valmax(r8, lambda p: p[1])        # column of the farthest 8
        # generate a horizontal line of the whole row, shift it right of that column
        line = hline(r8)                         # true if any 8 in this row
        mask = shoot((0, col+1), (0, 1))          # line to the right edge
        mask = intersect(mask, ofcolor(row, 0))  # keep only original zeros
        return recolor(1, mask)
    # apply the row‑wise filler to every row and re‑assemble
    filled = apply(fill_row, rows)
    O = vconcat(*filled)
    return O

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3️⃣  Color‑filter – “zero with an 8 on its left”
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    zeros = ofcolor(I, 0)
    eights = ofcolor(I, 8)
    # for each zero, check whether there exists an 8 with the same row and a smaller column
    def left_of_eight(z):
        row, col = z
        left_eights = {p for p in eights if p[0] == row and p[1] < col}
        return bool(left_eights)
    left_zeros = {z for z in zeros if left_of_eight(z)}
    O = recolor(1, left_zeros)
    return O
```

#### DSL

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---- Row‑wise – for every empty row copy the “right‑of‑last‑8” pattern from the row above
    rows     = hsplit(I, TEN)                        # split into 15 single‑row grids
    # helper: fills an empty row using the rightmost 8 of the row directly above
    def fill(row, above):
        has8    = colorcount(ofcolor(row, 8), 8) > 0                # row contains an 8 ?
        rightcol= valmax(ofcolor(above, 8), lambda p: p[1]) if has8 else None
        mask    = shoot((0, rightcol + 1), (0, 1)) if (rightcol is not None and rightcol < 9) else frozenset()
        mask    = intersection(mask, ofcolor(row, 0))
        return recolor(1, mask)
    # apply the helper to every pair (row, row‑above); the first row stays unchanged
    filled   = (rows[0],) + tuple(mapply(lambda pair: fill(pair[1], pair[0]),
                                   zip(rows[:-1], rows[1:])))
    O        = vconcat(*filled)
    return O
```

```python
    eights    = ofcolor(I, 8)
```

```python
    mask      = combine(*parity)
    O         = paint(I, recolor(1, mask))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # OBJECT‑EXTRACTION + CONDITIONAL – for each 8‑object decide
    #   * if its leftmost cell is at column 0 → fill to the right
    #   * otherwise                        → fill to the left
    objs     = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    def fill(o):
        lm = leftmost(o)                     # leftmost column of the object
        # choose direction based on whether the object touches the left border
        dir_vec = branch(lm == 0, (0, 1), (0, -1))
        # shoot from the cell just outside the object in the chosen direction
        start   = shift(backdrop(o), dir_vec)
        ray     = shoot(start, dir_vec)
        return intersection(ray, ofcolor(I, 0))

    mask_all = merge(mapply(fill, objs))
    O        = paint(I, recolor(1, mask_all))
    return O
```

```python
    # extend a horizontal ray from the right‑most cell of each row that contains that object.

    mask_all = merge(mapply(fill_row, objs))
    O        = paint(I, recolor(1, mask_all))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # PERIODIC – determine the horizontal period of the 8‑pattern,
    # then fill every cell that lies to the right of any 8 within one period.
    period    = hperiod(ofcolor(I, 8))                                 # distance between repeated 8‑blocks
    # build a template row that contains 8s at their original columns
    template  = canvas(0, shape(I))
    template  = paint(template, ofcolor(I, 8))
    # shift the template repeatedly to the right by the period and collect all 0‑cells
    shifts    = {multiply((0, period), k) for k in interval(0, width(I) // period + 1, 1)}
    tiled     = union({shift(template, d) for d in shifts})
    mask      = intersection(tiled, ofcolor(I, 0))
    O         = paint(I, recolor(1, mask))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑LEVEL – treat each 8‑object separately.
    # For a component that is only one row high we fill its own row;
    # for a taller component we fill the first row below it.
    objs = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    def fill_one(o):
        top    = uppermost(o)                                 # first row of the component
        bot    = lowermost(o)                                 # last row of the component
        right  = valmax({c for (_, c) in o}, lambda x: x)     # right‑most column of the component
        # choose the row to start the ray:
        row0   = branch(greater(bot, top), bot + 1, top)    # below if height > 1 else same row
        start  = astuple(row0, right + 1)                     # cell just right of the component
        ray    = shoot(start, (0, 1))                        # horizontal ray to the right
        return intersection(ray, ofcolor(I, 0))               # keep only background cells

    mask_all = merge(mapply(fill_one, objs))                 # union of all masks
    O        = paint(I, recolor(1, mask_all))                # colour them with 1
    return O
```

```python
    mir    = hmirror(I)                                     # left–right flip
    rays   = mapply(lambda p: shoot((p[0], p[1] + 1), (0, 1)),
                   ofcolor(mir, 8))
    mask   = intersection(rays, ofcolor(mir, 0))
    painted = paint(mir, recolor(1, mask))
    O      = hmirror(painted)                              # restore orientation
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # PERIODIC‑TILE – compute the horizontal repetition period of the 8‑pixels,
    # tile the pattern with that period and colour any newly created background
    # cells.
    period = hperiod(ofcolor(I, 8))                        # distance between repeats
    tmpl   = paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), ofcolor(I, 8))      # empty grid with 8‑pixels
    shifts = {multiply((0, period), k) for k in interval(0,
              width(I) // period + 1, 1)}                  # all horizontal shifts
    tiled  = combine({shift(tmpl, d) for d in shifts})    # super‑position of tiles
    mask   = intersection(tiled, ofcolor(I, 0))
    O      = paint(I, recolor(1, mask))
    return O
```

```python
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Relational / structural: for every 5‑component, count how many
    # other 5‑components it touches orthogonally.
    # The component is then recoloured with a number 1‑4 that equals
    # (touch count + 1).  Isolated components become 1, two neighbours become 3, etc.
    comps     = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 5)             # all 5‑objects
    def touch_count(o):
        others = difference(comps, initset(o))
        touching = apply(lambda x: adjacent(initset(o), x), others)
        return size(filter(lambda b: b, touching))
    def recol(o):
        cnt = touch_count(o)
        newc = ((cnt) % 4) + 1
        return recolor(newc, o)
    recolored = apply(recolor, comps)
    O = underpaint(I, combine(recolored, initset()))      # paint recoloured objects
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Relational/structural: each 5‑component gets a colour equal to
    # (number of other 5‑components that lie to its left) + 1.
    comps = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 5)

    def left_count(o):
        # count components whose leftmost column is smaller than that of o
        lc_o   = leftmost(o)
        others = difference(comps, initset(o))
        smaller = apply(
            lambda x: less(leftmost(x), lc_o),
            others)
        return add(size(filter(lambda b: b, smaller)), 1)

    recoloured = apply(
        lambda o: recolor(modulo(left_count(o), 4) + 1, o),
        comps)

    O = underpaint(I, combine(recoloured, initset(())))
    return O
```

```python
    R  = rot90(I)

    # colour 3 appears four columns to the right of the leftmost 5

    # colour 4 appears six columns to the right of the leftmost 5

    # build three tiny objects (single cells) at the appropriate columns

    obj3 = apply(lambda p: recolor(3, {(p[0], col3)}), mask)
    obj4 = apply(lambda p: recolor(4, {(p[0], col4)}), mask)

    # overlay the three colour‑objects on the globally‑replaced grid
    O = paint(R, combine(combine(obj2, obj3), obj4))
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    comps = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 5)          # each 5‑blob as an object
    L     = leftmost(ofcolor(I, 5))                # column of the overall leftmost 5

    def colour_of(o):
        # distance (in steps of 2 columns) from the global leftmost 5
        d   = divide(subtract(leftmost(o), L), TWO)
        idx = modulo(d, FOUR)                      # 0‑3
        # base cyclic order [2,3,1,4]  (used when L is even)
        base_even = branch(equality(idx, 0), 2,
                     branch(equality(idx, 1), 3,
                     branch(equality(idx, 2), 1, 4)))
        # same order shifted when L is odd → [4,2,3,1]
        base_odd  = branch(equality(idx, 0), 4,
                     branch(equality(idx, 1), 2,
                     branch(equality(idx, 2), 3, 1)))
        return branch(even(L), base_even, base_odd)

    recoloured = apply(lambda o: recolor(colour_of(o), o), comps)
    O = underpaint(I, recoloured)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    comps = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 5)           # each 5‑blob
    # order the components from left to right (by leftmost column)
    sorted = hsort(comps, key=leftmost)            # hsort is simulated by ordering primitive
    # assign colours 2,3,1,4 cyclically in that order
    colours = initset((2, 3, 1, 4))

    def assign(o, i):
        col = index(colours, modulo(i, FOUR))
        return recolor(col, o)

    recoloured = apply(lambda pair: assign(pair[0], pair[1]),
                      zip(sorted, interval(0, size(sorted), 1)))
    O = underpaint(I, recoloured)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ---- GLOBAL TRANSFORMATION -------------------------------------------------
    # 1. locate every 5‑pixel
    mask = ofcolor(I, 5)
    L    = leftmost(mask)                     # column of the leftmost 5

    # 2. mapping from column to new colour
    def col_to_val(c):
        step = divide(subtract(c, L), TWO)                # (c-L)//2
        q    = divide(step, FOUR)                         # quotient  step//4
        r    = subtract(step, multiply(q, FOUR))          # remainder  step%4
        even_map = branch(equality(r, 0), 2,
                    branch(equality(r, 1), 3,
                    branch(equality(r, 2), 1, 4)))
        odd_map  = branch(equality(r, 0), 4,
                    branch(equality(r, 1), 2,
                    branch(equality(r, 2), 3, 1)))
        return branch(even(L), even_map, odd_map)

    # 3. recolour each 5‑pixel according to its column
    recoloured = apply(lambda p: recolor(col_to_val(p[1]), {p}), mask)

    # 4. paint the new colours over the original grid (replaces the 5’s)
    O = paint(I, recoloured)
    return O
```

```python
            return branch(even(Lobj), even_map, odd_map)
        return recolor(col_to_val(leftmost(o)), o)

    recoloured = apply(recolour_obj, comps)
    O = paint(I, combine(*recoloured))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ---- PIXEL‑LEVEL COLOUR FILTERING -----------------------------------------
    mask = ofcolor(I, 5)
    L    = leftmost(mask)

    def col_to_val(c):
        step = divide(subtract(c, L), TWO)
        q    = divide(step, FOUR)
        r    = subtract(step, multiply(q, FOUR))
        even_map = branch(equality(r, 0), 2,
                    branch(equality(r, 1), 3,
                    branch(equality(r, 2), 1, 4)))
        odd_map  = branch(equality(r, 0), 4,
                    branch(equality(r, 1), 2,
                    branch(equality(r, 2), 3, 1)))
        return branch(even(L), even_map, odd_map)

    recoloured = apply(lambda p: recolor(col_to_val(p[1]), {p}), mask)
    O = paint(I, recoloured)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---- RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL (ORDER BY LEFTMOST COLUMN) -------------------
    comps   = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 5)          # each 5‑blob
    ordered = order(comps, leftmost)                  # tuple sorted left‑to‑right

    # colour cycle to use
    cycle   = initset((2, 3, 1, 4))

    def colour_at(idx):
        pos = modulo(idx, FOUR)                       # idx % 4  (modulo via arithmetic)
        # pos 0→2, 1→3, 2→1, 3→4
        return branch(equality(pos, 0), 2,
               branch(equality(pos, 1), 3,
               branch(equality(pos, 2), 1, 4)))

    def recolour_pair(pair):
        obj, i = pair
        col = colour_at(i)
        return recolor(col, obj)

    # build (object, index) pairs
    indices = interval(0, size(ordered), 1)
    pairs   = apply(lambda t: (t[0], t[1]), zip(ordered, indices))

    recoloured = apply(recolour_pair, pairs)
    O = paint(I, combine(*recoloured))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL : use the positions of the topmost cells as anchors
    comps          = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 5)
    tops           = apply(uppermost, comps)                     # set of topmost cells
    ordered_tops   = order(tops, lambda c: c)                    # sort by row (top‑most first)
    idxs           = interval(0, size(ordered_tops), 1)
    # map each anchor cell to the colour it should give
    anchor_to_col  = apply(lambda t: (t[0], add(ONE, t[1])), zip(ordered_tops, idxs))
    # for every object, find its anchor (the topmost cell) and recolour accordingly
    recoloured = apply(
        lambda o: recolor(
            next(filter(lambda a: a[0] in o, anchor_to_col))[1],
            o),
        comps)
    O = paint(I, combine(*recoloured))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # GLOBAL TRANSFORMATION : build a column‑wise colour map then fill whole columns
    cols           = lefthalf(righthalf(I))                     # full width (dummy to get dimensions)
    height_grid    = height(I)
    width_grid     = width(I)
    # create an empty canvas
    canvas_grid    = canvas(ZERO, (height_grid, width_grid))
    # extract the 5‑objects (vertical lines)
    comps          = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 5)
    ordered        = order(comps, uppermost)
    idxs           = interval(0, size(ordered), 1)
    # colour for each component = index+1
    coloured       = apply(lambda p: (p[0], add(ONE, p[1])), zip(ordered, idxs))
    # fill each component’s column with its colour
    result = apply(
        lambda t: fill(canvas_grid, t[1], t[0]),
        coloured)
    # the last filled grid contains all colours
    O = result[-1]                                            # last element of the sequence
    return O
```

```python
    # COLOR‑FILTERING – replace colour 5 by a rank that depends on the
    # object's topmost row, using a lookup table built from the objects.
    objs      = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), FIVE)
    ordered   = order(objs, uppermost)

    mapping   = dict(pair(ordered, ranks))                           # turn list of pairs into dict

              recolor(mapping[object_of(cell, objs)],        # rank for the object containing the cell
                       {cell}),
              ofcolor(I, FIVE))
    O = paint(I, merge(O))                                            # paint all recoloured cells
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # -------- Object‑centric approach (extract, recolour, overlay) --------
    # 1️⃣ Remove all 6‑cells from the original grid (set them to 0).

    # 2️⃣ Rotate the original grid, turn its 6‑cells into 9‑cells.
    rot  = rot180(I)
    rot  = replace(rot, 6, 9)
    # 3️⃣ Take the 9‑cells that just appeared after the rotation.
    nine_patch = ofcolor(rot, 9)
    # 4️⃣ Paint those 9‑cells onto the base grid where the 6‑cells were removed.
    O = paint(base, nine_patch)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC – move every 6‑cell to its 180° symmetric location,
    # then recolour the moved cell to 9 (leaving everything else untouched)
    six_patch = ofcolor(I, 6)                # indices of all 6‑cells
    sym_shift = add(shape(I), (0, 0))        # vector (h‑1, w‑1)
    # compute symmetric positions by adding the shift and then negating the coordinates
    sym_patch = apply(lambda p: add(p, sym_shift), six_patch)
    sym_patch = apply(lambda p: (sym_shift[0]-p[0], sym_shift[1]-p[1]), sym_patch)
    nine_obj = recolor(9, sym_patch)        # turn the symmetric positions into a 9‑object
    base = replace(I, 6, 0)                 # clear original 6‑cells
    O = paint(base, nine_obj)                # paint the new 9‑cells
    return O
```

```python
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL – reflect each 6‑cell through the centre
    # of the grid, take the colour that sits there (after 6→9),
    # and write it back onto the original location.
    six = ofcolor(I, 6)
    centre = divide(add(shape(I), (1, 1)), 2)          # centre of the grid (rounded down)
    # reflection through the centre
    refl = apply(lambda p: (add(multiply((2, 2), centre), (-1, -1))[0] - p[0],
                           add(multiply((2, 2), centre), (-1, -1))[1] - p[1]), six)

    R = replace(I, 6, 9)               # colour change on the whole picture
    reflcol = toobject(refl, R)        # colours at the reflected positions

    O = replace(I, 6, 0)
    O = paint(O, toobject(six, reflcol))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL – shift the whole 6‑patch by the vector that would bring it
    #            adjacent to the background (here it is the zero vector) and recolour.
    six   = ofcolor(I, 6)                               # patch of all 6‑cells
    zero  = ofcolor(I, 0)                              # background cells
    vec   = gravitate(six, zero)                        # direction to move six towards zero (0,0 here)
    moved = shift(six, vec)                            # shift by that vector (no net movement)
    recol = recolor(9, moved)                           # recolour the (unchanged) patch
    O = paint(I, recol)                                # paint back onto the grid
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    H, W = shape(I)                          # grid size
    O = canvas(0, (H, W))                    # start with all‑zero canvas

    # ---- columns of colour 2 -------------------------------------------------
    cols2 = apply(lambda rc: rc[1], ofcolor(I, TWO))                     # column indices
    col_patches = apply(lambda c: shoot((0, c), DOWN), cols2)             # vertical lines
    O = fill(O, TWO, combine(*col_patches))                             # colour 2 columns

    # ---- rows of colour 1 ----------------------------------------------------
    rows1 = apply(lambda rc: rc[0], ofcolor(I, ONE))                      # row indices
    row1_patches = apply(lambda r: shoot((r, 0), RIGHT), rows1)            # horizontal lines
    O = fill(O, ONE, combine(*row1_patches))                             # colour 1 rows (override)

    # ---- rows of colour 3 ----------------------------------------------------
    rows3 = apply(lambda rc: rc[0], ofcolor(I, THREE))                    # row indices
    row3_patches = apply(lambda r: shoot((r, 0), RIGHT), rows3)
    O = fill(O, THREE, combine(*row3_patches))                           # colour 3 rows (override)

    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    H, W = shape(I)
    O = canvas(0, (H, W))

    # colour 2: mirror the single cell vertically across the whole height
    pts2 = ofcolor(I, TWO)
    col_patches = apply(lambda p: connect(p, (H-1, p[1])), pts2)   # downwards
    col_patches = apply(lambda p: combine(p, connect(p, (0, p[1]))), col_patches)
    O = fill(O, TWO, combine(*col_patches))

    # colour 1 and 3: mirror the single cell horizontally across the whole width
    for col, val in ((ONE, ONE), (THREE, THREE)):
        pts = ofcolor(I, col)
        row_patches = apply(lambda p: connect(p, (p[0], W-1)), pts)   # rightwards
        row_patches = apply(lambda p: combine(p, connect(p, (p[0], 0))), row_patches
        O = fill(O, val, combine(*row_patches))

    return O
```

```python
    H, W = shape(I)
    O = canvas(0, (H, W))

    # centre of each colour decides if it should be a row (centre nearer horizontally) or column
    centre2 = center(ofcolor(I, TWO))
    centre1 = center(ofcolor(I, ONE))

    row = centre1[0]
    O = fill(O, ONE, shoot((row, 0), RIGHT))

    # colour 3 → horizontal line through its centre row
    row = centre3[0]
    O = fill(O, THREE, shoot((row, 0), RIGHT))
```

```python
    # OBJECT EXTRACTION – normalise each singleton object then project
    H, W = shape(I)
    O = canvas(0, (H, W))

    objs = objects(I, True, False, True)          # each coloured pixel as an object

    obj2 = first(colorfilter(objs, TWO))

    col2 = leftmost(norm2)                         # now 0, but we take original column via shift later
    # original column = column of any cell of obj2
    col2 = leftmost(obj2)

    obj1 = first(colorfilter(objs, ONE))
    row1 = uppermost(obj1)
    O = fill(O, ONE, connect((row1, 0), (row1, W - 1)))

    obj3 = first(colorfilter(objs, THREE))
    row3 = uppermost(obj3)
    O = fill(O, THREE, connect((row3, 0), (row3, W - 1)))

    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # 4️⃣  Global‑trim approach:
    #    - trim the grid to the minimal bounding box containing all coloured pixels,
    #    - draw the three lines inside the trimmed grid (using the *center* of each colour),
    #    - embed the trimmed result back into the original grid.
    H, W = shape(I)

    # bounding box of all non‑zero cells
    all_cells = combine(ofcolor(I, ONE),
                       combine(ofcolor(I, TWO), ofcolor(I, THREE)))
    bb_all = backdrop(all_cells)
    ul = ulcorner(bb_all)                     # upper‑left corner of the bounding box

    # sub‑grid that tightly surrounds the three pixels
    T = subgrid(bb_all, I)                    # trimmed input (same size as its bbox)

    # draw lines inside the trimmed grid
    h, w = shape(T)
    Otrim = canvas(0, (h, w))

    c2 = center(ofcolor(T, TWO))
    Otrim = fill(Otrim, TWO, connect((0, c2[1]), (h - 1, c2[1])))

    c3 = center(ofcolor(T, THREE))
    Otrim = fill(Otrim, THREE, connect((c3[0], 0), (c3[0], w - 1)))

    c1 = center(ofcolor(T, ONE))
    Otrim = fill(Otrim, ONE, connect((c1[0], 0), (c1[0], w - 1)))

    # place the trimmed result back into a full‑size canvas
    O = canvas(0, (H, W))
    O = move(O, asobject(Otrim), ul)

    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # 5️⃣  Purely *color‑filter* based:
    #    - keep only the 2‑pixel, expand it to a column,
    #    - keep only the 3‑pixel, expand it to a row,
    #    - keep only the 1‑pixel, expand it to a row.
    H, W = shape(I)
    O = canvas(0, (H, W))

    # column from the 2‑pixel (use its column index)
    col2 = leftmost(ofcolor(I, TWO))
    O = fill(O, TWO, connect((0, col2), (H - 1, col2)))

    # row from the 3‑pixel (use its row index)
    row3 = uppermost(ofcolor(I, THREE))
    O = fill(O, THREE, connect((row3, 0), (row3, W - 1)))

    # row from the 1‑pixel (use its row index)
    row1 = uppermost(ofcolor(I, ONE))
    O = fill(O, ONE, connect((row1, 0), (row1, W - 1)))

    return O
```

```python
    # ─ Object extraction + template shift ─
    # 1. Extract each coloured pixel as a one‑cell object.
    # 2. Build a full‑column template and a full‑row template.

    base_h = connect((0, 0), (0, W - 1))        # horizontal line (full row)

    row1_obj = first(objects(I, False, False, True) &
                     colorfilter(_, ONE))
    off1 = position(initset((0, 0)), row1_obj)
    O = fill(O, ONE, shift(base_h, (off1[0], 0)))

    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ─ Rotate‑based geometric construction ─
    # Rotate the whole picture 90° clockwise, draw the three lines there
    # (where the column of the 2‑pixel becomes a row, etc.), then rotate back.
    H, W = shape(I)

    R = rot90(I)                                 # 90° clockwise
    h, w = shape(R)
    Orot = canvas(0, (h, w))

    # in the rotated view the 2‑pixel is a row → draw a full row
    r2 = leftmost(ofcolor(R, TWO))               # becomes row index
    Orot = fill(Orot, TWO, connect((0, r2), (h - 1, r2)))

    # 3‑pixel and 1‑pixel become columns → draw full columns
    c3 = uppermost(ofcolor(R, THREE))
    Orot = fill(Orot, THREE, connect((c3, 0), (c3, w - 1)))

    c1 = uppermost(ofcolor(R, ONE))
    Orot = fill(Orot, ONE, connect((c1, 0), (c1, w - 1)))

    O = rot270(Orot)                             # inverse rotation
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ─ Direction selection via `branch` and shooting ─
    # From each coloured pixel shoot a line to the border:
    #   2 → DOWN, 3 → RIGHT, 1 → RIGHT.
    H, W = shape(I)
    O = canvas(0, (H, W))

    p2 = first(ofcolor(I, TWO))
    dir2 = branch(equal(color(p2, TWO), True), DOWN, RIGHT)
    O = fill(O, TWO, shoot(p2, dir2))

    p3 = first(ofcolor(I, THREE))
    dir3 = branch(equal(color(p3, THREE), True), DOWN, RIGHT)   # will choose RIGHT
    O = fill(O, THREE, shoot(p3, dir3))

    p1 = first(ofcolor(I, ONE))
    dir1 = branch(equal(color(p1, ONE), True), DOWN, RIGHT)     # will choose RIGHT
    O = fill(O, ONE, shoot(p1, dir1))

    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ── Global‑style propagation (vertical → horizontal → cascade) ──
    # 1. columns that contain a 1 become full columns
    cols_one = {c for (_,c) in ofcolor(I, ONE)}
    O = fill(I, ONE, {(r,c) for c in cols_one for r in range(height(I))})

    # 2. rows that now touch both left and right border become full rows
    rows_l = {r for (r,c) in ofcolor(O, ONE) if c == 0}
    rows_r = {r for (r,c) in ofcolor(O, ONE) if c == width(I)-1}
    O = fill(O, ONE, {(r,c) for r in rows_l & rows_r for c in range(width(I))})

    # 3. cascade: repeatedly turn any 2 that is orthogonal‑adjacent to a 1 into 1
    def step(G):
        twos = ofcolor(G, TWO)
        ones = ofcolor(G, ONE)
        adj  = {cell for cell in twos if adjacent({cell}, ones)}
        return fill(G, ONE, adj)

    O = power(step, height(I)*width(I))      # enough repetitions to fill whole components
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ── Relational / gravitation version ──
    # 1. move every 1 one step towards the nearest vertical border,
    #    then fill the whole columns that now contain a 1
    h = width(I)
    left_border  = {(r,0) for r in range(height(I))}
    right_border = {(r,h-1) for r in range(height(I))}
    grav_one = {add(p, gravitate({p}, left_border | right_border)) for p in ofcolor(I, ONE)}
    O = fill(I, ONE, grav_one)                     # add the shifted 1s
    cols_one = {c for (_,c) in ofcolor(O, ONE)}
    O = fill(O, ONE, {(r,c) for c in cols_one for r in range(height(I))})

    # 2. rows that now have a 1 at both borders become full rows
    rows_l = {r for (r,c) in ofcolor(O, ONE) if c == 0}
    rows_r = {r for (r,c) in ofcolor(O, ONE) if c == width(O)-1}
    O = fill(O, ONE, {(r,c) for r in rows_l & rows_r for c in range(width(O))})

    # 3. cascade adjacency turn‑over (identical to dsl1)
    def step(G):
        twos = ofcolor(G, TWO)
        ones = ofcolor(G, ONE)
        adj  = {cell for cell in twos if adjacent({cell}, ones)}
        return fill(G, ONE, adj)

    O = power(step, height(I)*width(I))
    return O
```

```python
    O = fill(O, ONE,
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
```

```python
    # dilate it with the 4‑neighbourhood, intersect that with the 2‑objects,
    # and recolour the intersecting 2‑objects.
    cols = {c for (_, c) in ofcolor(I, ONE)}
    leftc  = valmin(cols, lambda x: x)
    rightc = valmax(cols, lambda x: x)
    band = {(r, c) for c in interval(leftc, rightc + 1, 1)
                     for r in interval(0, height(I), 1)}
    O = fill(I, ONE, band)

    # cells that are orthogonally adjacent to the band
    adj_cells = merge(apply(neighbors, ofcolor(O, ONE)))

    twos = {obj for obj in fgpartition(I)
            if color(obj) == TWO and intersection(obj, adj_cells) != frozenset()}
    O = fill(O, ONE, {(r, c) for obj in twos for (_, (r, c)) in obj})
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC – build a single‑row mask of the band,
    # then repeat that row vertically to obtain the full band.
    cols = {c for (_, c) in ofcolor(I, ONE)}
    leftc  = valmin(cols, lambda x: x)
    rightc = valmax(cols, lambda x: x)

    # one‑row canvas
    row = canvas(0, (1, width(I)))
    band_row = {(0, c) for c in interval(leftc, rightc + 1, 1)}
    row_filled = fill(row, ONE, band_row)

    # repeat the row to the height of the original grid
    O = vupscale(row_filled, height(I))

    twos = {obj for obj in fgpartition(O)
            if color(obj) == TWO and adjacent(obj, ofcolor(O, ONE))}
    O = fill(O, ONE, {(r, c) for obj in twos for (_, (r, c)) in obj})
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # Global transformation: trim empty border, prepend a zero column (shifting everything right),
    # then crop back to the original size.
    T = trim(I)                                 # remove empty outer rows/cols
    h, w = shape(T)                             # height and width of trimmed grid
    Z = canvas(ZERO, (h, 1))                    # column of zeros
    shifted = hconcat(Z, T)                     # prepend zero column (right‑shift)
    O = crop(shifted, (0, 0), shape(I))        # restore original dimensions
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL bottom‑row restoration:
    # shift every coloured cell right, then repaint the cells that belong to the
    # bottom row of each object (the cells that have no neighbour below).
    all_cells   = asobject(I)                                          # all non‑zero cells
    shifted     = shift(all_cells, RIGHT)                              # whole picture shifted right
    # cells that have a neighbour below = intersection with the picture shifted up
    has_below   = intersection(all_cells, shift(all_cells, UP))
    bottom_rows = difference(all_cells, has_below)                     # true bottom rows
    empty       = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O1          = paint(empty, shifted)                               # shifted picture
    O           = paint(O1, bottom_rows)                               # restore bottom rows
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑LEVEL transformation (apply per object):
    # for each foreground object shift all cells except its bottom row.
    objs = fgpartition(I)

    def transform(obj):
        # bottom row of this object (no cell below it)
        has_below   = intersection(obj, shift(obj, UP))
        bottom_row  = difference(obj, has_below)
        non_bottom  = difference(obj, bottom_row)
        shifted     = shift(non_bottom, RIGHT)
        empty       = canvas(0, shape(I))
        return paint(paint(empty, shifted), bottom_row)   # object after its transformation

    # apply the transformation to every object and merge the results
    transformed = apply(transform, objs)                     # set of objects (grids)
    # union of all transformed objects: start from empty canvas and underpaint each one
    base = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O    = foldl(lambda acc g: underpaint(acc, g), base, transformed)  # foldl not native,
    # emulate the fold with repeated apply‑underpaint using mapply
    O    = underpaint(base, combine(*transformed))        # combine merges the object sets
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # RELATIONAL rule based on vertical adjacency:
    # any coloured cell that has another coloured cell directly below it
    # is moved one step to the right; all other cells stay.
    all_cells   = asobject(I)
    # cells that have a neighbour below = intersection with picture shifted up
    movable     = intersection(all_cells, shift(all_cells, UP))
    static      = difference(all_cells, movable)           # bottom rows, stay in place
    shifted_mov = shift(movable, RIGHT)
    empty       = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O1          = paint(empty, shifted_mov)
    O           = paint(O1, static)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # COLOR‑FILTERED processing: treat each non‑zero colour independently,
    # applying the same relational rule as dsl3 to each colour.
    colors      = difference(palette(I), {ZERO})           # all foreground colours
    empty       = canvas(0, shape(I))

    def process(col):
        patch       = ofcolor(I, col)                     # cells of this colour
        movable     = intersection(patch, shift(patch, UP))
        static      = difference(patch, movable)
        shifted_mov = shift(movable, RIGHT)
        return paint(paint(empty, shifted_mov), static)

    coloured_grids = apply(process, colors)               # one grid per colour
    # overlay the colour grids (they never overlap)
    O = foldl(lambda acc g: underpaint(acc, g), empty, coloured_grids)
    # emulate the fold with a single combine since colours are disjoint
    O = underpaint(empty, combine(*coloured_grids))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC: use the bounding box (box) to isolate the left‑most column.
    objs = fgpartition(I)

    def tr(o):
        b        = box(o)                                 # rectangle covering the object
        # cells whose column equals the left side of the box
        leftcol   = { (r, c) for (r, c) in toindices(o) if c == min(c for (_,c) in b) }
        leftcol   = frozenset(leftcol)
        leftcol   = initset(leftcol)                       # turn into a patch
        # bottom cells of that column
        has_below = intersection(leftcol, shift(leftcol, UP))
        bottom    = difference(leftcol, has_below)
        movable   = difference(leftcol, bottom)
        shifted   = shift(movable, RIGHT)
        keep      = difference(o, movable)
        empty     = canvas(0, shape(I))
        return paint(paint(empty, shifted), keep)

    # note: the comprehension above is expressed only with primitives;
    # the set‑construction is simulated via toobject/fromindices.
    # We obtain leftcol by intersecting the object with its left‑most vertical line.
    def left_column(o):
        # vertical line at the leftmost x‑coordinate of the object
        leftmost = leftmost(o)
        line     = { p for p in toindices(o) if p[1] == leftmost }
        return initset(line)

    def tr(o):
        leftcol   = left_column(o)
        has_below = intersection(leftcol, shift(leftcol, UP))
        bottom    = difference(leftcol, has_below)
        movable   = difference(leftcol, bottom)
        shifted   = shift(movable, RIGHT)
        keep      = difference(o, movable)
        empty     = canvas(0, shape(I))
        return paint(paint(empty, shifted), keep)

    return underpaint(canvas(0, shape(I)), combine(*apply(tr, objs)))
```

```python
        keep      = difference(toindices(o), movable)
        return combine(recolor(col, shifted), recolor(col, keep))

    transformed = apply(proc, objs)
    return underpaint(canvas(0, shape(I)), merge(transformed))
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # -------------------------------------------------
    # 4️⃣  Geometric reasoning (vertical‑line objects):
    #     • find colour‑5 objects whose width equals 1
    #       (i.e. pure vertical strips),
    #     • keep those strips as they are,
```
