```python
    objs5      = colorfilter(all_objs, FIVE)
    # objects that are exactly one cell wide → vertical lines
    vert_objs  = sfilter(objs5, lambda o: equal(width(o), 1))
    # cells belonging to any vertical‑line object
    vert_patch = difference(ofcolor(I, FIVE),
                             difference(ofcolor(I, FIVE),
                                        union(*vert_objs)))
    # cells of colour 5 that are *not* part of a vertical line
    other_patch = difference(ofcolor(I, FIVE), vert_patch)
    O = fill(I, TWO, other_patch)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # -------------------------------------------------
    # 5️⃣  Relational / centre‑column rule:
    #     • compute the central column of the whole 5‑mass,
    #     • preserve only those 5‑cells that lie in that column,
    #     • turn every other 5‑cell into colour 2.

    # centre of mass of the 5‑cells → (row, col)
    centre = centerofmass(five_cells)
    centre_col = centre[1]
    # keep only the cells whose column equals the centre column
    keep = sfilter(five_cells, lambda p: equal(p[1], centre_col))
    # everything else turns to 2
    to_paint = difference(five_cells, keep)
    O = fill(I, TWO, to_paint)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # Geometric reasoning – keep only those 5‑cells that lie in columns whose
    # total count of 5’s equals the maximal column count; all other 5’s become 2.
    five_cells  = ofcolor(I, FIVE)
    # column → number of 5‑cells in that column
    col_counts  = apply(lambda p: p[1], five_cells)       # extract column index
    freq        = fgpartition(tuple(tuple([c] for c in col_counts)), False, False, True)
    max_cnt     = valmax(freq, lambda s: size(s))
    # columns that reach the maximal count
    good_cols   = {p[1] for p in five_cells if size({q for q in five_cells if q[1] == p[1]}) == max_cnt}
    keep        = sfilter(five_cells, lambda p: p[1] in good_cols)
    other       = difference(five_cells, keep)
    O = fill(I, TWO, other)
    return O
```

```python
    centre_col = divide(w, TWO)                                   # integer centre column
    objs5      = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), FIVE)                # all colour‑5 objects
    keep_objs  = sfilter(objs5,
                         lambda o: contained(centre_col,
                                             apply(lambda p: p[1], toindices(o))))
    keep       = merge(apply(toindices, keep_objs))                # union of the kept cells
    other_fives= difference(ofcolor(I, FIVE), keep)
    O = fill(I, TWO, other_fives)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Relational reasoning: among the columns that have the maximal 5‑count,

    five       = ofcolor(I, FIVE)
    w          = width(I)
    cols_range = interval(0, w, 1)
    maxcnt     = valmax(cols_range,
                        lambda c: size(sfilter(five, lambda q: q[1] == c)))
    maxcols    = sfilter(cols_range,
                         lambda c: size(sfilter(five, lambda q: q[1] == c)) == maxcnt)
    leftmost   = valmin(maxcols, lambda c: c)                     # smallest column index among the maxima
    keep       = sfilter(five, lambda p: p[1] == leftmost)
    other_fives= difference(five, keep)
    O = fill(I, TWO, other_fives)
    return O
```

```python
    #   its leftmost cell touches the left border of the grid.

    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑EXTRACTION – keep every non‑background object,
    # recolour the 0‑objects to 2 and repaint everything on a blank canvas.
    objs        = fgpartition(I)                                 # all objects (incl. 0‑objects)
    zero_objs   = colorfilter(objs, 0)                           # only the 0‑objects
    other_objs  = mfilter(objs, lambda o: color(o) != 0)         # all objects whose colour is not 0
    # recolour the 0‑objects to colour 2
    recoloured  = mapply(lambda o: recolor(2, toindices(o)), zero_objs)
    # union of the already‑correct objects and the recoloured ones
    all_objs    = combine(other_objs, recoloured)
    # paint everything on a fresh canvas whose background is colour 1
    O = paint(canvas(1, shape(I)), all_objs)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ---------- Global transformation ----------
    # Remove the outermost border, then restore it unchanged.
    # (trim removes one-cell border; we put the trimmed part back
    #  together with the original border using vconcat/hconcat.)
    trimmed = trim(I)                               # global trim
    top    = crop(I, (0, 0), (1, width(I)))       # original top row
    bottom = crop(I, (height(I)-1, 0), (1, width(I)))   # original bottom row
    left   = crop(I, (0, 0), (height(I), 1))       # original left column
    right  = crop(I, (0, width(I)-1), (height(I), 1))   # original right column
    # rebuild the grid (border stays the same, interior is trimmed)
    middle = hconcat(vconcat(left, trimmed), right)
    O      = vconcat(top, vconcat(middle, bottom))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ---------- Color‑filtering ----------
    # Replace every cell of the most common color that has at least two
    # orthogonal neighbours of a different color with that neighbour colour.
    main_col   = mostcolor(I)                                    # dominant colour
    other_cols = difference(palette(I), initset(main_col))        # set of other colours
    # start from the original grid

    # for each secondary colour c:
    O = mapply(lambda c:
                # cells of main colour adjacent (4‑dir) to at least two c‑cells
                recolor(c,
                        intersection(
                            ofcolor(O, main_col),
                            # neighbours of colour c taken twice (self‑intersection)
                            delta(ofcolor(O, c))
                        )
                ),
                other_cols)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ---------- Global transformation ----------
    # Remove the outermost one‑pixel border, then put the original border back.
    trimmed = trim(I)                                           # interior without border
    top    = crop(I, (0, 0),                (1, width(I)))       # original top row
    bottom = crop(I, (height(I)-1, 0),      (1, width(I)))       # original bottom row
    left   = crop(I, (0, 0),                (height(I), 1))     # original left column
    right  = crop(I, (0, width(I)-1),       (height(I), 1))     # original right column
    middle = hconcat(vconcat(left, trimmed), right)            # rebuild interior with side borders
    O      = vconcat(top, vconcat(middle, bottom))             # re‑attach top & bottom
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ---------- Object extraction ----------
    # Keep the largest object (by cell count) and paint it on a canvas filled with the
    # colour that appears least often in the whole picture (the background colour).
    bg      = leastcolor(I)                                    # background colour
    objects = fgpartition(I)                                    # all foreground objects
    biggest = argmax(objects, lambda o: size(o))               # the biggest one
    canvas  = canvas(bg, shape(I))                              # empty canvas with bg
    O       = paint(canvas, biggest)                            # paint the object
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ---------- Color‑filtering ----------
    # Any cell that has the dominant colour and at least three orthogonal neighbours
    # of a different colour is recoloured to the most common neighbour colour.
    dom      = mostcolor(I)                                     # dominant colour
    others   = difference(palette(I), initset(dom))             # the set of other colours
    O = I
    O = mapply(
            lambda c:
                recolor(
                    c,
                    intersection(
                        ofcolor(O, dom),                         # cells of dominant colour
                        delta(ofcolor(O, c))                     # cells adjacent to colour c
                    )
                ),
            others
        )
    return O
```

```python
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # Object‑extraction – keep every object of the most frequent colour
    # and paint them on a canvas filled with the least frequent colour.
    bg        = leastcolor(I)                                   # background colour
    objects   = fgpartition(I)                                   # all foreground objects
    dom_col   = mostcolor(I)                                     # dominant colour
    dom_objs  = colorfilter(objects, dom_col)                    # only those objects
    canvas    = canvas(bg, shape(I))                             # empty canvas
    # combine all dominant objects (combine works on two arguments, we fold)
    combined  = fold(lambda a, b: combine(a, b), dom_objs)       # union of all objects
    O = paint(canvas, combined)                                 # draw them
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # Geometric – intersect the picture with its vertical mirror;
    # keep the common cells, fill the rest with the background colour.
    bg      = leastcolor(I)                                     # background colour
    mir     = vmirror(I)                                        # vertical mirror
    common  = intersection(                                     # cells that are equal in both grids
                ofcolor(I, mostcolor(I)),                        # (any colour, we will mask later)
                ofcolor(mir, mostcolor(I))
            )
    O = underfill(I, bg, delta(common))                        # write bg everywhere else,
    O = paint(O, common)                                        # then paint the common cells
    return O
```

```python
    canvas_grid = canvas(bg, shape(I))                        # empty background canvas

    O = apply(lambda o: paint(canvas_grid, o), objs)
    # the above produces a container of grids; the final grid is the last element
    return last(O)
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL – keep the outermost frame of the picture untouched,
    # recolour every interior cell with the most frequent colour.
    h, w      = shape(I)
    top       = crop(I, (0, 0), (1, w))                # first row
    bottom    = crop(I, (h-1, 0), (1, w))              # last row
    left      = crop(I, (0, 0), (h, 1))                # first column
    right     = crop(I, (0, w-1), (h, 1))              # last column
    frame     = vconcat(hconcat(top, bottom), hconcat(left, right))
    dom       = mostcolor(I)                           # dominant colour
    inner     = replace(I, leastcolor(I), dom)          # colour‑swap everywhere
    # restore the unchanged border
    O = paint(inner, frame)
    return O
```

```python
    # with the most common colour of the whole picture.
    h, w        = shape(I)
    top_row     = crop(I, (0, 0), (1, w))
    bot_row     = crop(I, (h-1, 0), (1, w))

    right_col   = crop(I, (0, w-1), (h, 1))

    dom         = mostcolor(I)                     # dominant colour
    recoloured  = fill(I, dom, interior)           # paint interior
    # put the original border back (same colours as in I)
    O = paint(recoloured, toobject(border_mask, I))
    return O
```

```python
    # COLOUR‑FILTERING – turn every non‑dominant cell that touches a dominant
    # cell into the dominant colour, but keep the original outer frame.
    dom = mostcolor(I)
    other = difference(palette(I), initset(dom))
    # cells of a non‑dominant colour that are orthogonal neighbours of a dominant cell
    masks = apply(lambda c: intersection(ofcolor(I, c),
                                        delta(ofcolor(I, dom))),
                 other)
    grow = combine(*masks)                                 # union of all those cells
    h, w = shape(I)
    top    = asindices(crop(I, (0, 0), (1, w)))
    bottom = asindices(crop(I, (h-1, 0), (1, w)))
    left   = asindices(crop(I, (0, 0), (h, 1)))
    right  = asindices(crop(I, (0, w-1), (h, 1)))
    border = combine(combine(top, bottom), combine(left, right))
    interior = difference(grow, border)
    recoloured = fill(I, dom, interior)                     # recolour the interior part
    O = paint(recoloured, toobject(border, I))             # restore border
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # Relational – turn the proper 3‑cells into 5 and the rest of the 3‑cells into 7,
    # also handle the 5‑cells that touch a 3.
    # 3 with a 7 on its left → 5
    left7      = shift(ofcolor(I, 7), RIGHT)
    three_left7= intersection(ofcolor(I, 3), left7)

    # 3 that is the second cell of a leading “33…’’ block (column‑0 is 3) → 5
    col0       = difference(asindices(I), shift(asindices(I), RIGHT))
    col0_3     = intersection(col0, ofcolor(I, 3))
    second3    = intersection(ofcolor(I, 3), shift(col0_3, RIGHT))

    to5        = combine(three_left7, second3)                     # all cells that become 5

    # 5 that sits left of a 3 → only the 5 becomes 7
    left5_of_3 = intersection(ofcolor(I, 5), shift(ofcolor(I, 3), LEFT))

    # 5 that sits right of a 3 → both the 5 and that 3 become 7
    right5_of_3= intersection(ofcolor(I, 5), shift(ofcolor(I, 3), RIGHT))
    three_of_right5 = shift(right5_of_3, LEFT)

    # 3 whose left neighbour is a 5 (pattern 5‑3) must stay unchanged
    three_left5 = intersection(ofcolor(I, 3), shift(ofcolor(I, 5), RIGHT))

    # all remaining 3‑cells become 7
    three_rest = difference(difference(ofcolor(I, 3), to5), three_left5)

    # union of every cell that has to be recoloured to 7
    to7 = combine(three_rest, left5_of_3)
    to7 = combine(to7, right5_of_3)
    to7 = combine(to7, three_of_right5)

    O = fill(fill(I, 5, to5), 7, to7)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # Global – replace every colour that is not 7 by 7, then restore the unique
    # pattern “7 followed by a run of 3’s’’ (or a leading run of 3’s) according to the rule.
    all_non7   = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 7))
    O1        = fill(I, 7, all_non7)                     # everything non‑7 → 7

    # locate the unique row that contains a run of 3’s next to a 7 or at the border
    rows      = {r for (r, _) in asindices(I)}
    def run_mask(r):
        row_idx = canvas(r, (1, width(I)))                # single‑row selector (creates a 1×w grid)
        row      = subgrid(row_idx, I)                   # the whole row
        three    = ofcolor(row, 3)
        left7    = intersection(three, shift(ofcolor(row, 7), RIGHT))
        col0_3   = intersection(three, difference(asindices(row), shift(asindices(row), RIGHT)))
        second   = intersection(three, shift(col0_3, RIGHT))
        return combine(left7, second)

    mask_row  = union(*[run_mask(r) for r in rows])
    O2        = fill(O1, 5, intersection(mask_row, shift(ofcolor(I, 7), RIGHT)))
    O         = fill(O2, 7, difference(mask_row, intersection(mask_row, shift(ofcolor(I, 7), RIGHT))))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # Object‑extraction – treat each maximal horizontal 3‑run as an object.
    # The run that touches a 7 on its left (or starts at column 0) is the “target’’.
    three     = ofcolor(I, 3)
    runs      = fgpartition(rotate(three, 0))            # each horizontal run becomes an object
    left7run  = {obj for obj in runs if intersection(obj, shift(ofcolor(I, 7), RIGHT))}
    startrun  = {obj for obj in runs if intersection(obj, col0)}
    target    = union(*left7run) if left7run else union(*startrun)
    second    = shift(target, RIGHT)                    # second cell of the run
    to5       = intersection(second, three)
    to7_3     = difference(three, union(to5, target))
    O         = fill(fill(I, 5, to5), 7, to7_3)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Periodic – compute the horizontal period of the 3‑pattern (always 1),
    # then shift the pattern of “3 with left‑neighbour 7’’ onto the row that
    # contains the longest run of 3’s.

    longest   = argmax(runs, lambda o: size(o))
    left7mask  = intersection(longest, shift(ofcolor(I, 7), RIGHT))
    to5       = intersection(ofcolor(I, 3), left7mask)
    to7_3     = difference(ofcolor(I, 3), to5)
    O         = fill(fill(I, 5, to5), 7, to7_3)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ---------- Global‑replace style ----------
    # 1.  turn everything that is not 7 into 7
    all_non7 = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 7))
    G       = fill(I, 7, all_non7)

    # 2.  cells that must become 5:
    #     – a 3 whose left neighbour is 7
    #     – the second 3 in a vertical run that starts in column 0
    left7   = intersection(ofcolor(I, 3), shift(ofcolor(I, 7), RIGHT))
    col0    = difference(asindices(I), shift(asindices(I), LEFT))
    col0_3  = intersection(col0, ofcolor(I, 3))
    second3 = intersection(ofcolor(I, 3), shift(col0_3, DOWN))
    to5     = combine(left7, second3)

    # 3.  recolour those cells to 5 (everything else is already 7)
    O = fill(G, 5, to5)
    return O
```

```python
    # ---------- Object‑extraction style ----------
    #   treat each maximal vertical run of 3’s as an object.
    three      = ofcolor(I, 3)
    runs       = fgpartition(three)                     # each 3‑run → object
    #   keep the objects that either touch a 7 on the left
    #   or are the second cell of a run that starts in column 0
    left7_obj  = {obj for obj in runs
                  if intersection(obj, shift(ofcolor(I, 7), RIGHT))}
    col0       = difference(asindices(I), shift(asindices(I), LEFT))
    start_obj  = {obj for obj in runs if intersection(obj, col0)}
    second_obj = {obj for obj in runs
                  if intersection(shift(obj, DOWN), col0_3 := intersection(col0, three))}
    target_objs = combine(combine(*left5_obj := left7_obj or set(),
                              *second_obj), *start_obj)      # union of the three possibilities
    to5        = target_objs                               # all cells of selected objects become 5
    to7        = difference(three, to5)                      # remaining 3’s become 7
    O          = fill(fill(I, 5, to5), 7, to7)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL – use the gravitate primitive to keep only those 3‑cells
    # whose nearest 7 lies to the right, and those 3‑cells that lie below a
    # left‑most column 3.  Then recolour the identified cells to 5.
    G      = replace(I, 5, 7)
    three  = ofcolor(I, 3)
    seven  = ofcolor(I, 7)

    # keep a 3‑cell if moving it towards the whole 7‑patch goes RIGHT
    left_mask = apply(
        lambda p: branch(gravitate({p}, seven) == RIGHT, {p}, frozenset()),
        three)

    col0   = difference(asindices(I), shift(asindices(I), LEFT))
    top3   = intersection(col0, three)
    down_mask = intersection(three, shift(top3, DOWN))

    mask   = combine(left_mask, down_mask)
    O      = fill(G, 5, mask)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ---------- Strategy 2 : Object‑based endpoint recoloring ----------
    # 1. Split the grid into monochrome objects (including background).
    objs = fgpartition(I)
    # 2. Keep only the non‑background objects (color > 0).
    non_bg = mfilter(objs, lambda o: color(o) > 0)
    # 3. For each object, recolor its leftmost cell with 4 and its rightmost cell with 2.
    def recolor_endpoints(o):
        c = color(o)                     # original color of the object
        l = leftmost(o)                  # column index of leftmost cell in the object
        r = rightmost(o)                 # column index of rightmost cell in the object
        # collect the cells that sit on the leftmost column of o
        left_cells  = { (r0, l) for (r0, c0) in o if c0 == l }
        # collect the cells that sit on the rightmost column of o
        right_cells = { (r0, r) for (r0, c0) in o if c0 == r }
        # recolor the two patches
        after_left  = recolor(4, left_cells)
        after_right = recolor(2, right_cells)
        # combine the two recolorings
        return combine(after_left, after_right)

    # 4. Build a patch that contains all new recolorings.
    new_patches = apply(recolor_endpoints, non_bg)

    # 5. Paint the new recolorings on top of the original grid.
    O = I
    for p in new_patches:
        O = paint(O, p)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---------- Strategy 5 : Relational – distance to the nearest border ----------
    # Cells that are at Manhattan distance 1 from the outer border become 4,
    # cells that are at distance 2 become 2, everything else stays unchanged.
    h, w = shape(I)
    # all border cells
    border = { (0, c) for c in range(w) } | { (h-1, c) for c in range(w) } | \
            { (r, 0) for r in range(h) } | { (r, w-1) for r in range(h) }
    # distance‑1 cells
    d1 = { p for b in border for p in neighbors(b) if 0 <= p[0] < h and 0 <= p[1] < w }
    # distance‑2 cells (neighbors of distance‑1 that are not already border or d1)
    d2 = { p for d in d1 for p in neighbors(d)
           if 0 <= p[0] < h and 0 <= p[1] < w and p not in border and p not in d1 }
    # recolor
    O = recolor(4, d1)
    O = recolor(2, d2)
    # background stays 0
    O = fill(O, 0, set())
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # Object‑based endpoint recoloring
    #  – for every non‑background object recolor the cells that lie on its
    #    leftmost column with 4,
    #    the cells that lie on its rightmost column with 2.
    #  – left‑side (4) is painted after right‑side (2) so that width‑1
    #    objects keep colour 4.
    objs      = fgpartition(I)                                      # all objects
    non_bg   = mfilter(objs, lambda o: color(o) > 0)                # ignore bg
    # left‑most cells of every object
    lefts = apply(
        lambda o: recolor(
            4,
            { (r, c) for (col, (r, c)) in o if c == leftmost(o) }
        ),
        non_bg
    )
    # right‑most cells of every object
    rights = apply(
        lambda o: recolor(
            2,
            { (r, c) for (col, (r, c)) in o if c == rightmost(o) }
        ),
        non_bg
    )
    # paint right side first, then left side (4 overrides 2 on width‑1 objects)
    O = I
    for p in rights:   O = paint(O, p)
    for p in lefts:    O = paint(O, p)
    return O
```

```python
    # Geometric mirroring with colour priority
    #  – mirror the whole picture vertically,
    #    recolour every non‑background cell of the mirrored picture with 4,
    #    recolour every original non‑background cell with 2.
    #  – because 4 is painted after 2 it overwrites any overlap.

    mir_patch  = apply(lambda o: { (r, c) for (col, (r, c)) in o }, non_bg_mir)
    mir_cells  = combine(*mir_patch)          # union of all mirrored cells
    patch_mir  = recolor(4, mir_cells)

    # cells of the original picture (all non‑zero colours)
    objs_ori   = fgpartition(I)

    ori_patch  = apply(lambda o: { (r, c) for (col, (r, c)) in o }, non_bg_ori)
    ori_cells  = combine(*ori_patch)
    patch_ori  = recolor(2, ori_cells)

    O = I
    O = paint(O, patch_ori)   # paint original 2‑s
    O = paint(O, patch_mir)   # then mirrored 4‑s (priority)
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Periodicity – colour the first and last column of each horizontal period
    #  – horizontal period of the non‑zero pattern is obtained with hperiod().
    #    Cells that lie in the leftmost column of each period are recoloured 4,
    #    cells that lie in the rightmost column of each period are recoloured 2.
    #  – 4 is painted after 2 so it has priority where periods have width 1.
    objs      = fgpartition(I)
    non_bg    = mfilter(objs, lambda o: color(o) > 0)
    # union of all cells belonging to any non‑background object
    all_cells = combine(*apply(lambda o: { (r, c) for (col, (r, c)) in o }, non_bg))

    # horizontal period of the whole pattern (same for every row because of regularity)
    p         = hperiod(ofcolor(I, color(first(non_bg))))   # any non‑zero colour works
    # start columns of each period
    starts    = interval(0, w := shape(I)[1], p)
    # left‑most column indices of the periods
    left_cols = { c for c in starts }
    # right‑most column indices of the periods
    right_cols = { c-1 for c in starts if c-1 >= 0 }

    left_patch  = { (r, c) for (r, c) in all_cells if c in left_cols }
    right_patch = { (r, c) for (r, c) in all_cells if c in right_cols }

    O = I
    O = paint(O, recolor(2, right_patch))   # 2 first
    O = paint(O, recolor(4, left_patch))    # 4 on top
    return O
```

#### DSL

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ---- OBJECT‑LEVEL: recolor the leftmost column of each connected component with 4
    #                  and the rightmost column with 2 (2 painted first, then 4)
    objs    = fgpartition(I)                                 # all colour‑connected objects
    non_bg  = mfilter(objs, lambda o: color(o) > 0)          # drop the background object
    # left‑most cells of every object
    lefts   = apply(lambda p: recolor(4,
                         {(r, c) for (r, c) in p if c == leftmost(p)}),
                    non_bg)
    # right‑most cells of every object
    rights  = apply(lambda p: recolor(2,
                         {(r, c) for (r, c) in p if c == rightmost(p)}),
                    non_bg)
    O = I
    for p in rights: O = paint(O, p)      # 2 first
    for p in lefts: O = paint(O, p)      # 4 overwrites when width‑1
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---- GLOBAL ROW‑WISE EXTREMA: work on the union of all coloured cells,
    #                               colour the left‑most and right‑most cell of each row.
    objs      = fgpartition(I)
    non_bg    = mfilter(objs, lambda o: color(o) > 0)
    all_cells = combine(*non_bg)                           # union of every object
    left_mask  = difference(all_cells, shift(all_cells, LEFT))
    right_mask = difference(all_cells, shift(all_cells, RIGHT))
    O = paint(paint(I, recolor(2, right_mask)), recolor(4, left_mask))
    return O
```

```python
    masks   = apply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), colours)                # cells of a given colour

                     {(r, c) for (r, c) in b if c == leftmost(b)}),
                    boxes)

    rights = apply(lambda b: recolor(2,
                     {(r, c) for (r, c) in b if c == rightmost(b)}),
                    boxes)

    O = I
    for p in rights: O = paint(O, p)
    for p in lefts:  O = paint(O, p)
    return O
```

#### DSL

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # GLOBAL ROW‑WISE EXTREMA: work on the union of all coloured cells.
    # Cells that have no neighbour on the left are left‑most,
    # cells that have no neighbour on the right are right‑most.
    colours   = {c for c in palette(I) if c > 0}
    masks     = apply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), colours)
    all_cells = apply(lambda m: m, masks)        # identity, just to keep a container

    # union of every colour‑mask
    union = reduce(lambda a, b: combine(a, b), all_cells)   # fold using combine

    left_mask  = difference(union, shift(union, LEFT))
    right_mask = difference(union, shift(union, RIGHT))

    O = paint(paint(I, recolor(2, right_mask)), recolor(4, left_mask))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL‑TRANSFORM: find the leftmost / rightmost column that contains any
    # non‑zero colour in the whole grid and colour those columns (4 = left, 2 = right).
    colours   = {c for c in palette(I) if c > 0}
    masks     = apply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), colours)

    leftmost_col  = minimum(apply(lambda m: leftmost(m), masks))
    rightmost_col = maximum(apply(lambda m: rightmost(m), masks))

    lefts  = apply(lambda m: recolor(4,
                {(r, c) for (r, c) in m if c == leftmost_col}), masks)
    rights = apply(lambda m: recolor(2,
                {(r, c) for (r, c) in m if c == rightmost_col}), masks)

    O = I
    for p in rights: O = paint(O, p)
    for p in lefts : O = paint(O, p)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC‑REASONING: for each colour take its *border* (outline)
    # and colour the vertical sides of that border.
    colours = {c for c in palette(I) if c > 0}
    masks   = apply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), colours)

    borders = apply(lambda m: border(m), masks)               # outline of each colour

    lefts  = apply(lambda b: recolor(4,
                {(r, c) for (r, c) in b if c == leftmost(b)}), borders)
    rights = apply(lambda b: recolor(2,
                {(r, c) for (r, c) in b if c == rightmost(b)}), borders)

    O = I
    for p in rights: O = paint(O, p)
    for p in lefts : O = paint(O, p)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL‑STRUCTURE: compute the global leftmost/rightmost columns that
    # contain *any* coloured cell (using the union of all colour masks) and
    # recolour only those cells that belong to the original colours.
    colours = {c for c in palette(I) if c > 0}
    masks   = apply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), colours)

    # global extremes
    leftmost_col  = minimum(apply(lambda m: leftmost(m), masks))
    rightmost_col = maximum(apply(lambda m: rightmost(m), masks))

    lefts  = apply(lambda m: recolor(4,
                {(r, c) for (r, c) in m if c == leftmost_col}), masks)
    rights = apply(lambda m: recolor(2,
                {(r, c) for (r, c) in m if c == rightmost_col}), masks)

    O = I
    for p in rights: O = paint(O, p)
    for p in lefts : O = paint(O, p)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL‑COMBINE: union of all colour masks, then colour the extreme columns.
    colours   = {c for c in palette(I) if c > 0}
    masks     = apply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), colours)          # patches of each colour
    union     = combine(masks)                                # all coloured cells together
    leftcol   = leftmost(union)                               # global leftmost column
    rightcol  = rightmost(union)                              # global rightmost column
    lefts     = recolor(4, sfilter(union, lambda rc: rc[1] == leftcol))
    rights    = recolor(2, sfilter(union, lambda rc: rc[1] == rightcol))
    O = I
    O = paint(O, rights)
    O = paint(O, lefts)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑EXTRACTION: work on each connected component, then take the global extremes.
    objs      = fgpartition(I)                                 # all objects (including background)
    coloured  = mfilter(objs, lambda o: color(o) > 0)           # drop background
    # column extremes of every object
    lefts_obj = apply(lambda o: leftmost(toindices(o)), coloured)
    rights_obj= apply(lambda o: rightmost(toindices(o)), coloured)
    leftcol   = minimum(lefts_obj)                              # global leftmost
    rightcol  = maximum(rights_obj)                             # global rightmost
    # all coloured cells again
    all_cells = combine(apply(lambda o: toindices(o), coloured))
    lefts     = recolor(4, sfilter(all_cells, lambda rc: rc[1] == leftcol))
    rights    = recolor(2, sfilter(all_cells, lambda rc: rc[1] == rightcol))
    O = I
    O = paint(O, rights)
    O = paint(O, lefts)
    return O
```

```python
    # then colour the cells that lie on the global extreme columns.
    colours   = {c for c in palette(I) if c > 0}
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC‑REASONING: draw the bounding rectangle of all coloured cells,
    # keep only the rectangle sides that actually intersect the original colours.
    colours   = {c for c in palette(I) if c > 0}
    masks     = apply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), colours)
    union     = combine(masks)                                 # all coloured cells
    rect      = box(toindices(union))                          # outline of the bounding box
    leftcol   = leftmost(rect)
    rightcol  = rightmost(rect)
    # vertical sides of the rectangle
    left_side  = sfilter(rect, lambda rc: rc[1] == leftcol)
    right_side = sfilter(rect, lambda rc: rc[1] == rightcol)
    # intersect with original coloured cells so we only colour existing material
    lefts  = recolor(4, intersection(left_side, union))
    rights = recolor(2, intersection(right_side, union))
    O = I
    O = paint(O, rights)
    O = paint(O, lefts)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # all cells of colour 5
    S = ofcolor(I, 5)                                   # FrozenSet[(r,c)]

    # right‑most 5 in each row  – keep those that have no other 5
    # in the same row with a larger column index
    def is_rightmost(idx):

        return not any((r2 == r and c2 > c) for (r2, c2) in S)

    R = mfilter(S, is_rightmost)                        # right‑most 5s
    L = difference(S, R)                                # all other 5s

    O = fill(I, 2, L)                                   # replace them by 2
    O = fill(O, 8, R)                                   # replace right‑most by 8
    return O
```

```python
    rows = hsplit(I, h)                                   # tuple of 1‑row grids
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # each 5 cell is a separate object
    objs = fgpartition(I)                                 # set of 1‑cell objects
    five_objs = colorfilter(objs, 5)                       # keep only colour‑5 objects

    # map each object to a tuple (row, col, obj)
    def to_trip(o):
        (r, c), = {(r, c) for (c, (r, _)) in o}          # extract its index
        return (r, c, o)
    trips = apply(to_trip, five_objs)

    # for each row keep the object with maximal column
    def key_max(t): return t[1]                           # column
    rightmost_per_row = {}
    for (r, c, o) in trips:
        if r not in rightmost_per_row or c > rightmost_per_row[r][0]:
            rightmost_per_row[r] = (c, o)

    R = { o for (_, o) in rightmost_per_row.values() }   # patches of right‑most 5s
    L = difference(five_objs, R)                         # the rest of the 5‑objects

    O = fill(I, 2, union(*L))                             # 5 → 2   (union of all patches)
    O = fill(O, 8, union(*R))                             # right‑most 5 → 8
    return O


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5)  Column‑wise scanning using gravitate (relational / structural)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    S = ofcolor(I, 5)                                     # all 5 cells

    # build a patch containing, for each row, the cell that lies farthest to the right
    # we let each 5 “gravitate” towards the rightmost 5 of its row;
    # the ones that do not move are already the right‑most ones.
    def target(idx):
        r, c = idx
        # candidate cells in the same row
        same_row = {(rr, cc) for (rr, cc) in S if rr == r}
        # the farthest column
        maxc = max(cc for (_, cc) in same_row)
        return (r, maxc)

    R = {idx for idx in S if target(idx) == idx}          # right‑most 5s
    L = difference(S, R)                                   # the others

    O = fill(I, 2, L)                                     # 5 → 2
    O = fill(O, 8, R)                                     # right‑most 5 → 8
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Object‑centric: treat each 5 as a 1‑cell object, compute per‑row max column
    objs = fgpartition(I)                 # all objects
    five_objs = colorfilter(objs, 5)       # keep only colour‑5 objects
    # positions of the 5‑objects
    pos = apply(lambda o: ulcorner(o), five_objs)          # {(r,c),...}
    # for every row, keep the cell with the greatest column index
    rows = interval(0, height(I), 1)                     # all row indices
    def row_max(r):
        cols = {c for (rr, c) in pos if rr == r}
        return {(r, max(cols))} if cols else frozenset()
    R = union(*apply(row_max, rows))                     # right‑most 5s
    L = difference(ofcolor(I, 5), R)                      # the remaining 5s
    O = fill(I, 2, L)                                    # 5 → 2
    O = fill(O, 8, R)                                    # right‑most 5 → 8
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL + PAINT: start with a full‑8 canvas and paint back everything that is NOT a 5‑object.
    # objects of color 5 are removed, all other objects stay unchanged.
    base       = canvas(8, shape(I))                           # all cells = 8
    objs       = fgpartition(I)                                 # all objects in the input
    five_objs  = colorfilter(objs, 5)                           # only the 5‑objects
    other_objs = difference(objs, five_objs)                    # everything else
    O          = paint(base, merge(other_objs))                # paint the non‑5 objects onto the 8‑canvas
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT EXTRACTION – keep only the most frequent non‑zero colour
    c = mostcolor(I)                     # colour that appears the most (including 0)
    # if the most frequent colour is the background, pick the next one
    c = branch(c == 0,
               mostcolor(replace(I, 0, -1)),   # temporary trick to avoid background
               c)
    patch = ofcolor(I, c)                # all cells of that colour
    O = fill(I, c, patch)                # paint only that colour, everything else becomes 0
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL – extract every coloured object, shift each object
    #   to the upper‑left corner (normalisation) and repaint them on a blank canvas.
    objs      = fgpartition(I)                 # set of all objects (including their colour)
    normed    = apply(normalize, objs)          # move every object to origin
    combined  = merge(normed)                   # union of all normalised patches
    blank     = canvas(0, shape(I))              # empty grid of original size
    O = underpaint(blank, combined)            # paint the normalised objects onto the blank grid
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC REASONING – rotate the whole grid 180° and overlay it
    # with the original (the overlay keeps the original colour where it is non‑zero).
    R           = rot180(I)                                          # 180° rotation
    ORIGINAL    = asobject(I, I)                                     # original as an object
    ROTATED_OBJ = asobject(R, I)                                     # rotated as an object
    COMBINED    = merge({ORIGINAL, ROTATED_OBJ})                     # union of both objects
    O           = underpaint(canvas(0, shape(I)), COMBINED)          # render on blank canvas
    return O
```

```python
                    OBJS)

    O          = underpaint(canvas(0, shape(I)), COMBINED)                    # paint on blank canvas
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL – align every object horizontally with the leftmost column
    # of the most frequent colour object (the “reference” object).
    OBJS       = fgpartition(I)                                      # all objects
    REF_COLOR  = mostcolor(I)                                        # colour that appears most
    REF_OBJ    = argmax(OBJS, lambda o: color(o) == REF_COLOR)       # one of the objects of that colour
    REF_LEFT   = leftmost(toindices(REF_OBJ))                       # its leftmost column index
    SHIFTED    = apply(
                    lambda o:
                        shift(
                            toindices(o),
                            astuple(0,
                                    subtract(REF_LEFT,
                                             leftmost(toindices(o))))
                        ),
                    OBJS)                                            # shift each object
    COMBINED   = merge(SHIFTED)                                      # reunite shifted objects
    O          = underpaint(canvas(0, shape(I)), COMBINED)           # render on blank canvas
    return O
```

```python
    # and shift the remaining rows upward, keeping the original width.

                    I)                                      # keep non‑empty rows

    O         = vconcat(COMPRESSED, PAD)
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # set of all 8‑objects (4‑connected, background excluded)
    objs = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    # helper that maps an object to a colour based on its cardinality
    def obj_to_colour(obj):
        sz = size(obj)                     # number of cells in the object
        col = branch(sz == 9, 2,
               branch(sz == 5, 3, 1))      # fallback colour 1
        return fill(I, col, obj)           # recolour this object

    # recolour every object and merge the results
    recoloured = apply(obj_to_colour, objs)      # collection of grids
    O = I
    # overlay the recoloured pieces (they all share the same background)
    O = fold(lambda a, b: paint(a, b), recoloured, O)   # custom fold via apply is allowed
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    objs = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    # map each object to its centre of mass
    centres = apply(lambda o: centerofmass(o), objs)

    # build a set of objects that have a neighbour at distance 1
    neighbour_sets = initset(frozenset())
    for o1 in objs:
        for o2 in objs:
            if o1 != o2:
                d = manhattan(centerofmass(o1), centerofmass(o2))
                neighbour_sets = insert(o1, neighbour_sets) if d == 1 else neighbour_sets

    # recolour according to neighbour presence
    def colour_by_neighbour(o):
        col = branch(contains(neighbour_sets, o), 3,
               branch(any(manhattan(centerofmass(o), centerofmass(p)) == 1 for p in objs if p != o), 2, 1))
        return fill(I, col, o)

    O = apply(colour_by_neighbour, objs)
    O = fold(lambda a, b: paint(a, b), O, I)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ---------- GLOBAL TRANSFORMATION ----------
    # 1. Remove the original colour (8) completely.
    # 2. Down‑scale the picture by a factor of 2 (integer division of coordinates).
    # 3. Replace every non‑zero cell of the down‑scaled picture by colour 2.
    # This yields a simple size‑reduction that keeps the overall layout.
    G = replace(I, 8, 0)                # erase the 8‑foreground
    S = downscale(G, 2)                  # integer down‑scale (keeps shape)
    O = replace(S, 0, 2)                # colour the remaining pattern
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ---------- OBJECT‑LEVEL BORDER / INTERIOR / ISOLATED ----------
    # 1. Detect every 8‑object (4‑connected, background excluded).
    # 2. For each object decide:
    #        – touches the outer border          → colour 1
    #        – has at least one interior cell    → colour 2
    #        – otherwise (no interior cell)      → colour 3
    # 3. Paint the coloured objects on a clean canvas.
    objs = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    def colour_obj(patch):
        # does the patch touch the outer grid border ?
        is_border = bordering(patch, I)

        # four shifted versions of the patch
        up    = shift(patch, UP)
        down  = shift(patch, DOWN)
        left  = shift(patch, LEFT)
        right = shift(patch, RIGHT)

        # cells that have all four orthogonal neighbours inside the patch
        interior = intersection(patch,
                               intersection(up,
                                           intersection(down,
                                                       intersection(left, right))))
        has_interior = size(interior) > 0

        col = branch(is_border, 1,
               branch(has_interior, 2, 3))

        # recolour the patch to the selected colour
        return recolor(col, patch)          # returns an object (col, loc) set

    coloured_objs = apply(colour_obj, objs)   # set of coloured objects
    canvas = replace(I, 8, 0)                # background without the original colour
    O = paint(canvas, combine(coloured_objs))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ---------- COLOR‑FILTERING ----------
    # 1. Keep only the 8‑foreground.
    # 2. Split the foreground into its connected components.
    # 3. Keep the largest component (by size) and colour it 2,
    #    colour every other component 3.
    # 4. Merge the recoloured components back onto a zero background.
    fg   = ofcolor(I, 8)                     # all 8‑cells
    comps = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    # size of each component
    sizes = apply(lambda o: size(o), comps)

    # biggest size
    biggest = argmax(sizes, lambda x: x)

    def recolour(comp):
        col = branch(size(comp) == biggest, 2, 3)
        return recolor(col, comp)

    recoloured = apply(recolour, comps)
    O = paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), combine(recoloured))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---------- RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL REASONING ----------
    # 1. Extract every 8‑object.
    # 2. For each object compute its centre of mass.
    # 3. Two objects are “touching” if the Manhattan distance
    #    between their centres of mass equals 1.
    # 4. Objects that touch at least one other become colour 3,
    #    otherwise colour 1.
    # 5. Paint the coloured objects onto a zero background.
    objs = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    # map each object to its centre of mass (a point)
    centres = apply(lambda o: centerofmass(o), objs)

    # build a set of objects that have at least one neighbour at distance 1
    touching = initset(frozenset())
    # we cannot write explicit loops; instead we build all pairs,
    # filter those at distance 1 and collect the first component of each pair.
    pairs = product(objs, objs)                     # all ordered pairs
    close  = mfilter(pairs,
                     lambda p: p[0] != p[1] and
                               manhattan(centerofmass(p[0]),
                                         centerofmass(p[1])) == 1)
    touching = apply(lambda p: p[0], close)        # objects that appear in a close pair
    touching_set = combine(touching)               # unified set of objects

    def recolour(o):
        col = branch(contains(touching_set, o), 3, 1)
        return recolor(col, o)

    recoloured = apply(recolour, objs)
    O = paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), combine(recoloured))
    return O
```

```python
    objs = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # COLOR‑FILTERING: keep the three size‑groups of the 8‑components
    #   – the largest group (always the interior blocks) → 2
    #   – the medium‑sized group (border blocks) → 1
    #   – the smallest group (isolated single‑pixel blocks) → 3
    comps = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    sizes = apply(lambda o: size(o), comps)                # size of each component
    max_sz = valmax(sizes, lambda x: x)                    # biggest size
    min_sz = valmin(sizes, lambda x: x)                    # smallest size
    med_sz = valmin(setdifference(sizes, {max_sz, min_sz}),
                    lambda x: x)                           # middle size (if any)

    def recol(o):
        s = size(o)
        col = branch(s == max_sz, 2,
               branch(s == med_sz, 1, 3))
        return recolor(col, o)

    recoloured = apply(recol, comps)
    O = paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), merge(recoloured))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL: objects that touch another object become 3,
    # otherwise become 1.  Afterwards, objects that touch the outer frame
    # are recoloured to 1 (overriding the previous rule) and interiors
    # (objects that contain an interior cell) become 2.
    objs = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    # pairs of distinct orthogonally‑adjacent objects
    pairs = product(objs, objs)
    close = mfilter(pairs,
                    lambda p: p[0] != p[1] and adjacent(p[0], p[1]))
    touching = apply(lambda p: p[0], close)          # objects that touch somebody
    touching_set = merge(touching)

    def initial_recol(o):
        col = branch(contained(touching_set, o), 3, 1)
        return recolor(col, o)

    prelim = apply(initial_recol, objs)

    # border objects → 1
    def border_recol(p):
        col = branch(bordering(p, I), 1, color(p))
        return recolor(col, p)

    # interior objects → 2
    def interior_recol(p):
        interior = intersection(
            p,
            intersection(shift(p, UP),
                intersection(shift(p, DOWN),
                    intersection(shift(p, LEFT),
                                 shift(p, RIGHT)))))
        col = branch(size(interior) > 0, 2, color(p))
        return recolor(col, p)

    step1 = apply(border_recol, prelim)
    O = apply(interior_recol, step1)
    O = paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), merge(O))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # COLOR‑FILTERING: start from all 8→2, then overlay border objects (touch frame) →1,
    # finally overlay size‑1 objects →3
    base = replace(I, 8, 2)

    objs          = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)
    border_objs   = mfilter(objs, lambda o: bordering(o, I))
    singleton_objs = mfilter(objs, lambda o: size(o) == 1)

    O1 = paint(base, merge(apply(lambda o: recolor(1, o), border_objs)))
    O2 = paint(O1,   merge(apply(lambda o: recolor(3, o), singleton_objs)))
    return O2
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # BOUNDING‑BOX: components that fully fill their bounding box are “solid”
    # → colour 2, the rest (touching edge of component) →1, singletons →3
    objs = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    solid = mfilter(
        objs,
        lambda o: size(o) == size(backdrop(o))   # full rectangle
    )
    rest  = difference(objs, solid)
    singles = mfilter(rest, lambda o: size(o) == 1)

    def recol(o):
        return branch(contained(solid, o), recolor(2, o),
               branch(contained(singles, o), recolor(3, o),
               recolor(1, o))

    return paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), merge(apply(recol, objs)))
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL‑PIXEL: classify every 8‑cell by its orthogonal neighbours
    # interior (all 4 neighbours also 8) →2,
    # edge (at least one background neighbour) →1,
    # isolated (size‑1 component) →3
    objs = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    def cell_type(o):
        # o is a single‑cell object (size 1)
        interior = intersection(
            shift(o, UP),
            shift(o, DOWN),
            shift(o, LEFT),
            shift(o, RIGHT)
        )
        return branch(size(intersection(o, interior)) > 0, recolor(2, o),
               recolor(1, o))

    # recolor all non‑singleton cells
    non_single = mfilter(objs, lambda o: size(o) > 1)
    recolored_non = merge(apply(lambda o: merge(apply(cell_type, {c}) for c in o), non_single))

    # recolor singletons to 3
    singles = mfilter(objs, lambda o: size(o) == 1)
    recolored_single = recolor(3, union(singles))

    return paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), merge({recolored_non, recolored_single}))
```

```python
    neigh = combine(shift(mask, UP),
            combine(shift(mask, DOWN),
```

```python
    singles = difference(border, intersection(border, neigh))

    return paint(
        canvas(0, shape(I)),
        merge([recolor(2, interior), recolor(1, border), recolor(3, singles)])
    )
```

```python
def dsl2(I):

    # interior (inside the outline) → 2, isolated cells → 3.

        border   = difference(outline, singles)

        return merge([
            recolor(2, interior),
            recolor(1, border),
            recolor(3, singles)
        ])

    return paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), merge(apply(recol, objs)))
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC‑MIRRORING: cells that survive both horizontal
    # and vertical mirroring are interior (2); border (1);
    # isolated cells (3) as before.
    mask = ofcolor(I, 8)

    hmir = hmirror(mask)          # horizontal mirror
    vmir = vmirror(mask)          # vertical mirror

    neighbours = combine(shift(mask, UP),
                   combine(shift(mask, DOWN),
                       combine(shift(mask, LEFT), shift(mask, RIGHT))))
    singles   = difference(mask, neighbours)

    border = difference(mask, combine(interior, singles))

    return paint(
        canvas(0, shape(I)),
        merge([recolor(2, interior), recolor(1, border), recolor(3, singles)])
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL‑CENTER: for each connected component,
    # cells that are not on the object's outermost rows/columns are interior (2);
    # outermost cells are border (1); isolated cells (3).
    objs = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    def recol(o):
        # rows and columns occupied by the object
        top    = uppermost(o)
        bottom = lowermost(o)
        leftc  = leftmost(o)
        rightc = rightmost(o)

        # interior = cells whose row is strictly between top/bottom
        #            and whose column is strictly between left/right
        rows   = interval(top + 1, bottom, 1)   # rows not on edge
        cols   = interval(leftc + 1, rightc, 1)  # cols not on edge
        interior = ofcolor(I, 8)                # start from all 8‑cells
        interior = intersect(interior,
                     initset((r, c)) for r in rows for c in cols)  # keep only interior rows/cols

        # isolated cells: no orthogonal neighbour inside the same object
        neigh = combine(shift(o, UP),
                 combine(shift(o, DOWN),
                     combine(shift(o, LEFT), shift(o, RIGHT))))
        singles = difference(o, neigh)

        border = difference(o, combine(interior, singles))

        return merge([
            recolor(2, interior),
            recolor(1, border),
            recolor(3, singles)
        ])

    return paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), merge(apply(recol, objs)))
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # colours that may act as seeds (all colours > 1)
    seeds   = mfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c > 1)

    # start from the original grid
    O = I

    # for each seed colour c:
    #   – take its orthogonal out‑box,
    #   – intersect it with the cells that are colour 1,
    #   – recolour that intersection to c,
    #   – paint the recoloured object back onto the grid.
    O = apply(
            lambda c:
                paint(
                    O,
                    recolor(
                        c,
                        intersection(
                            outbox(ofcolor(I, c)),
                            ofcolor(I, 1))
                    )
                ),
            seeds)

    # `apply` returns a container; the last element of the container
    # is the fully updated grid.
    return last(O)
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    idxs = asindices(I)                      # all coordinate pairs

    # compute a new colour for every position
    new_vals = apply(
                  lambda p:
                      branch(
                          equal(
                              size(
                                  mfilter(
                                      apply(lambda n: index(I, n), neighbors(p)),
                                      lambda v: v > 1)),
                              0),
                          # no seed neighbour → keep original colour
                          index(I, p),
                          # at least one seed neighbour → take the maximum
                          valmax(
                              mfilter(
                                  apply(lambda n: index(I, n), neighbors(p)),
                                  lambda v: v > 1),
                              lambda v: v)),
                  idxs)

    # rebuild a grid from the list of values (row‑wise)
    # the helper `reshape` is a thin wrapper around `vconcat` /
    # `hconcat` that is allowed as a primitive composition.
    O = reshape(new_vals, shape(I))
    return O
```

```python
    G = vconcat(I, vmirror(I))
```

```python
                                box(ofcolor(G, c)),
                                ofcolor(G, 1))
                         ),
                seeds)

    G2 = paint(G, combine(patches))

    # keep only the part that corresponds to the original size
    O = lefthalf(G2)
    return O
```

```python
    # global‑mask construction: build a single mask that contains every
    # 1‑cell that belongs to at least one colour‑>1 bounding box,
    # then recolour those cells with the colour of the (unique) box

                        lambda c: recolor(

                                        ofcolor(I, 1))

    # union of all coloured patches gives the final coloured grid
    O = paint(I, merge(colored_patches))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # relational neighbourhood rule:
    # a 1‑cell becomes the colour of the nearest (Manhattan) non‑1
    # cell that shares the same bounding‑box row or column.
    # Because each colour‑>1 occupies a single rectangular region,
    # the nearest such cell is exactly the seed colour whose box
    # contains the 1‑cell.
    seeds = sfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c > 1)

    # build, for every seed colour, the set of 1‑cells that lie inside
    # its orthogonal bounding box.
    patches = apply(
                lambda c:
                    recolor(
                        c,
                        intersection(
                            box(ofcolor(I, c)),   # bounding box of colour c
                            ofcolor(I, 1)         # the 1‑cells
                        )
                    ),
                seeds)

    O = paint(I, merge(patches))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # global transformation with `cover`: first erase all 1‑cells,
    # then paint the full bounding‑boxes of the seed colours.
    seeds   = sfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c > 1)
    boxes   = apply(lambda c: box(ofcolor(I, c)), seeds)      # pure boxes, no masking
    base    = cover(I, ofcolor(I, 1))                        # remove every 1‑cell
    O = paint(base, merge(apply(lambda b,c: recolor(c, b), boxes, seeds)))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # -------- GLOBAL‑TRANSFORM ----------
    # For every colour > 1 build the orthogonal bounding box of *all* its cells,
    # keep only the 1‑cells that lie inside it and recolour them with that colour.
    # The whole operation is performed by one parallel “apply‑mapply” pass.
    seeds   = sfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c > 1)                 # colours to treat
    boxes   = apply(lambda c: box(ofcolor(I, c)), seeds)           # their boxes
    patches = mapply(
                lambda c, b: recolor(
                                c,
                                intersection(b, ofcolor(I, 1))   # 1‑cells inside the box
                              ),
                seeds,
                boxes)
    O = paint(I, merge(patches))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # -------- OBJECT‑EXTRACTION ----------
    # Treat every *object* (connected component) of colour > 1 as a separate entity.
    # For each object take its orthogonal out‑box, intersect it with the set of 1‑cells
    # and recolour that intersection with the object’s colour.
    objs    = sfilter(fgpartition(I), lambda o: color(o) > 1)      # objects of colour >1
    patches = apply(
                lambda o: recolor(
                            color(o),
                            intersection(
                                outbox(o),                     # orthogonal box of the object
                                ofcolor(I, 1)                  # all 1‑cells
                            )
                         ),
                objs)
    O = paint(I, merge(patches))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # -------- GEOMETRIC‑REASONING ----------
    # For every colour > 1 locate its extreme corners (UL and LR).  Connect the two
    # corners, turn the resulting segment into a rectangle with `box`, intersect with
    # the 1‑cells and recolour the result.
    seeds   = sfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c > 1)
    patches = apply(

                            c,
                            intersection(
                                box(

                                        ulcorner(ofcolor(I, c)),   # upper‑left corner
                                        lrcorner(ofcolor(I, c))    # lower‑right corner
                                    )
                                ),
                                ofcolor(I, 1)                   # all 1‑cells
                            )
                         ),
                seeds)
    O = paint(I, merge(patches))
    return O
```

#### DSL

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # -------- RELATIONAL‑STRUCTURAL ----------
    # First erase all 1‑cells (`cover`).  Then, for each colour > 1, paint the part of
    # its bounding box that originally contained a 1‑cell.  The mask is built by
    # intersecting the box with the original set of 1‑cells, ensuring that no other
    # colour is overwritten.
    seeds   = sfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c > 1)
    boxes   = apply(lambda c: box(ofcolor(I, c)), seeds)
    mask    = apply(lambda b: intersection(b, ofcolor(I, 1)), boxes)   # keep only original 1‑cells
    patches = mapply(lambda c, m: recolor(c, m), seeds, mask)          # recolour those cells
    base    = cover(I, ofcolor(I, 1))                                 # grid without any 1‑cell
    O = paint(base, merge(patches))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # relational / structural (underpaint + colour‑swap)
    # instead of painting over the whole grid, we first erase the 1‑cells,
    # then we swap the colour >1 with 1 only inside the colour’s box.
    seeds   = sfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c > 1)
    boxes   = apply(lambda c: box(ofcolor(I, c)), seeds)
    masks   = apply(lambda b: intersection(b, ofcolor(I, 1)), boxes)
    swaps   = prapply(lambda c, m: switch(I, 1, c), seeds, masks)   # flip 1↔c inside mask
    base    = cover(I, ofcolor(I, 1))                               # clear original 1‑cells
    O = underpaint(base, merge(swaps))                             # only fill cleared cells
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # global‑style transformation: create an empty canvas, paint the
    # colour‑specific boxes on it, then overlay the result on the original
    # grid keeping everything except the original 1‑cells unchanged.
    seeds   = sfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c > 1)
    boxes   = apply(lambda c: box(ofcolor(I, c)), seeds)
    patches = prapply(lambda c, b: recolor(c, b), seeds, boxes)
    empty   = canvas(0, shape(I))                         # all‑zero background
    coloured = paint(empty, merge(patches))               # colour‑filled boxes
    # keep only the cells that were 1 in the input
    mask    = ofcolor(I, 1)
    recoloured = paint(cover(I, mask), merge(patches))
    O = paint(I, merge(patches))                          # final overlay
    return O
```

```python
    # 1️⃣  Object‑extraction + vertical periodicity
    #    – extract the 8‑object,

    O      = replace(I, 8, col)                     # recolour the 8‑object
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2️⃣  Relational – number of “holes” inside the 8‑object
    #    – area = height × width of the bounding box,
    #    – cnt  = number of 8 cells,
    #    – holes = area – cnt,
    #    – colour decided from the amount of holes.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    patch8 = ofcolor(I, 8)
    area   = multiply(height(patch8), width(patch8))
    cnt    = colorcount(patch8, 8)
    holes  = subtract(area, cnt)
    col    = branch(greater(holes, 30), 2,          # many holes → 2
                branch(greater(holes, 10), 3, 7)) # medium → 3, else 7
    O      = replace(I, 8, col)
    O      = replace(O, 1, 0)
    return O
```

```python
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4️⃣  Geometric reasoning – compare height and width
    #    – the larger dimension decides the colour:
    #      very tall/wide  → 7,
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # 5️⃣  Relational – proportion of empty cells inside the bounding box.
    p8      = ofcolor(I, 8)
    area    = multiply(height(p8), width(p8))          # bbox area
    filled  = colorcount(p8, 8)                       # 8‑pixels inside the bbox
    empty   = subtract(area, filled)                 # empty cells inside the bbox
    # avoid division‑by‑zero by adding ONE to the denominator
    prop    = divide(empty, add(filled, ONE))         # floor‑ratio
    col     = branch(greater(prop, 2), 7,
               branch(greater(prop, 1), 3, 2))
    O       = replace(I, 8, col)
    O       = replace(O, 1, 0)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ── GEOMETRIC‑REASONING ──
    #   Use the centre of mass of the 8‑object.  If it lies in the upper‑half
    #   of its bounding box we colour it 7, else if it lies in the lower‑half we
    #   colour it 3, otherwise colour 2.
    p8          = ofcolor(I, 8)
    c_mass      = centerofmass(p8)                            # (row, col) of COM
    c_box       = center(p8)                                  # centre of the bbox
    above       = greater(c_mass[0], c_box[0])                 # COM below centre ?
    col         = branch(above, 3,
                 branch(greater(c_box[0], c_mass[0]), 7, 2))
    O           = replace(I, 8, col)
    O           = replace(O, 1, 0)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ── RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL ──
    #   Measure the Manhattan distance between the 8‑object and the separate 1‑object.
    #   If they touch (distance = 0) we erase the 8‑object (colour 0);
    #   otherwise we recolour it according to how far apart they are:
    #   distance ≤ 3 → 7, distance ≤ 6 → 3, else 2.
    p8          = ofcolor(I, 8)
    p1          = ofcolor(I, 1)
    d           = manhattan(p8, p1)                           # minimal distance
    col         = branch(equality(d, 0), 0,
                 branch(greater(d, 6), 2,
                 branch(greater(d, 3), 3, 7)))
    O           = replace(I, 8, col)
    O           = replace(O, 1, 0)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC‑REASONING (centre of mass vs bbox centre)
    #   Compare the centre of mass of the 8‑object with the centre of its
    #   bounding box in both vertical and horizontal directions.
    p8          = ofcolor(I, 8)
    com         = centerofmass(p8)                         # (r,c) of centre of mass
    cbox        = center(p8)                               # (r,c) of bbox centre
    vert_below  = greater(com[0], cbox[0])                   # COM lower than box centre?
    horiz_right = greater(com[1], cbox[1])                   # COM right of box centre?
    col = branch(vert_below,
            branch(horiz_right, 7, 3),                     # lower‑right → 7, lower‑left → 3
            2)                                            # otherwise → 2
    O   = replace(I, 8, col)
    O   = replace(O, 1, 0)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL (distance between 8‑ and 1‑objects)
    #   Measure Manhattan distance between the two objects and colour
    #   according to how far apart they are.
    p8 = ofcolor(I, 8)
    p1 = ofcolor(I, 1)
    d  = manhattan(p8, p1)                                 # minimal distance
    col = branch(equality(d, 0), 0,                         # touching → erase 8
          branch(greater(d, 6), 2,                         # far → 2
          branch(greater(d, 3), 3, 7))                    # medium → 3, close → 7
    O   = replace(I, 8, col)
    O   = replace(O, 1, 0)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL – size + interior density decides new colour,
    # then erase any 1‑pixels that lie inside the 8‑bbox.
    p8        = ofcolor(I, 8)
    sz        = size(p8)
    interior  = intersection(p8, shift(p8, UP))
    interior  = intersection(interior, shift(p8, DOWN))
    interior  = intersection(interior, shift(p8, LEFT))
    interior  = intersection(interior, RIGHT)
    cnt_int   = size(interior)
    col = branch(greater(sz, 50), 7,
           branch(greater(cnt_int, 0), 3, 2))
    O = replace(I, 8, col)                     # recolour the 8‑object
    bbox      = backdrop(p8)                    # bounding rectangle of the 8‑object
    ones      = ofcolor(I, 1)
    to_clear  = intersection(ones, bbox)      # 1‑pixels inside the bbox
    O = cover(O, to_clear)                    # erase them
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑LEVEL – work on the isolated 8‑object, count its interior,
    # recolour it, and clear any other colour that touches the object.
    p8        = ofcolor(I, 8)
    interior  = intersection(p8, shift(p8, UP))
    interior  = intersection(interior, shift(p8, DOWN))
    interior  = intersection(interior, shift(p8, LEFT))
    interior  = intersection(interior, RIGHT)
    cnt_int   = size(interior)
    sz        = size(p8)
    col = branch(greater(sz, 50), 7,
           branch(greater(cnt_int, 0), 3, 2))
    O = replace(I, 8, col)
    # find every non‑zero cell that is adjacent (4‑neighbour) to the 8‑object
    nbrs      = union(shift(p8, UP), shift(p8, DOWN), shift(p8, LEFT), shift(p8, RIGHT))
    other     = intersection(nbrs, ofcolor(I, 1))
    O = cover(O, other)                       # erase those neighbours
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ----------  COLOR‑FILTER + REACHABILITY ----------
    # cells of colour 0 that cannot reach the outer border are
    # interior to a 2‑frame.  Find all such zero‑components.
    zero_objs   = colorfilter(objects(I, True, False, True), 0)
    exterior    = apply(lambda o: bordering(o, I), zero_objs)
    interior    = difference(zero_objs, exterior)

    comps       = list(interior)                     # frozenset order is deterministic
    colours     = [8, 4, 3, 5, 6, 7]                 # fallback list
    O = I
    O = mapply(lambda pair: fill(O, pair[1], pair[0]),
               zip(comps, colours[:size(comps)]))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):

    # pick the unique 2‑pixel (the “source”) and move it until it
    # touches any interior zero‑region, then colour that whole region.
    source        = first(ofcolor(I, 2))

    exterior      = apply(lambda o: bordering(o, I), zero_objs)
    interior_objs = difference(zero_objs, exterior)

    # direction that brings the source next to the interior region
    move_vec = gravitate({(source, (0,0))},
                         {(p, (0,0)) for p in interior_cells})

    # colour the whole interior with the colour of the moved source +2
    newcol = add(color(I, moved_source), 2)
    O = fill(I, newcol, interior_cells)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # OBJECT‑EXTRACTION + AREA‑BASED COLOURING
    # 2‑colored closed rectangles → their interiors.
    # smallest interior → 8, largest → 3, remaining interiors → 4
    borders    = colorfilter(objects(I, True, False, True), 2)
    interiors = apply(lambda o: difference(backdrop(o), o), borders)

    smallest = argmin(interiors, lambda o: size(o))      # interior with fewest cells
    largest  = argmax(interiors, lambda o: size(o))      # interior with most cells
    rest     = difference(merge(interiors), combine(smallest, largest))

    O = fill(I, 8, smallest)
    O = fill(O, 3, largest)
    O = fill(O, 4, rest)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL‑GRAVITATE + RECOLOURING
    # the first 2‑pixel is moved until it touches any interior zero region;
    # the touched region is filled with the source colour plus 2.
    source = first(ofcolor(I, 2))

    zero_objs = colorfilter(objects(I, True, False, True), 0)
    exterior  = apply(lambda o: bordering(o, I), zero_objs)
    interior  = difference(zero_objs, exterior)
    interior_cells = merge(interior)

    move_vec    = gravitate({(source, (0, 0))},
                           {(p, (0, 0)) for p in interior_cells})
    moved_src   = add(source, move_vec)

    newcol = add(index(I, source), 2)          # source colour (2) + 2 → 4
    O = fill(I, newcol, interior_cells)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # RELATIONAL‑NEIGHBOR‑FILL
    # Find every zero cell that is completely surrounded (4‑connected) by 2‑cells.
    # Recolour those cells with the colour that is two higher than the surrounding 2.
    borders   = colorfilter(objects(I, True, False, True), 2)
    border_cells = merge(borders)

    zeros     = ofcolor(I, 0)
    # zero is interior iff all its 4‑neighbors belong to the same 2‑border object
    interior0 = apply(lambda z: both(
                    contained(z, border_cells),
                    all( contained(p, border_cells) for p in neighbors(z))
                , zeros)                       # this yields a set of zero cells
    O = fill(I, add(2, 2), interior0)       # 2 + 2 → 4 (or whatever the border colour is)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # MIRROR‑ZERO‑PATTERN
    # Take the zero region inside each 2‑frame, mirror it horizontally and
    # vertically inside the same frame, then recolour the whole mirrored patch
    # with the smallest unused non‑background colour.
    frames   = colorfilter(objects(I, True, False, True), 2)
    zeros    = ofcolor(I, 0)

    # interior zero cells for each frame
    interior0 = apply(lambda f: intersection(difference(backdrop(f), f),
                                            zeros), frames)

    # mirror each interior patch horizontally and vertically, then unite
    horiz    = apply(hmirror, interior0)
    vert     = apply(vmirror, interior0)
    mirrored = merge(combine(interior0, horiz, vert))

    newcol   = minimum(difference({3,4,5,6,7,8,9}, palette(I)))
    O = fill(I, newcol, mirrored)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # GLOBAL – work on each frame separately, then merge the coloured interiors
    borders = colorfilter(objects(I, True, False, True), 2)

    # for every 2‑frame: extract its interior, colour it, then put it back
    coloured = apply(
        lambda o:
            let interior = intersection(difference(backdrop(o), o), ofcolor(I, 0))
            let ranked   = order(apply(toindices,
                                    objects(fill(I, 0, interior), True, False, True)),
                               lambda p: size(p))
            let small    = first(ranked)
            let large    = last(ranked)
            let rest     = difference(merge(apply(toindices,
                                                objects(fill(I, 0, interior), True, False, True)),
                                      combine(small, large))
            let coloured_small = fill(I, 8, small)
            let coloured_large = fill(coloured_small, 3, large)
            fill(coloured_large, 4, rest),
        borders)

    # merge the individually coloured interiors
    O = cover(I, merge(coloured))
    return O
```

```python
    zero_objs = colorfilter(objects(I, True, False, True), 0)

    interiors = apply(
        lambda p: branch(not bordering(p, I), p, frozenset()),

    interiors = apply(
        lambda p: branch(greater(size(p), 0), p, frozenset()),
        interiors)

    ranked   = order(interiors, lambda p: size(p))
    smallest = first(ranked)
    largest  = last(ranked)
    rest     = difference(merge(interiors), combine(smallest, largest))

    O = fill(I, 8, smallest)
    O = fill(O, 3, largest)
    O = fill(O, 4, rest)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # OBJECT‑BASED REPAINT: convert interior patches to objects,
    # recolour them, then underpaint the original grid
    borders   = colorfilter(objects(I, True, False, True), 2)

    interiors = apply(
        lambda o: intersection(difference(backdrop(o), o), ofcolor(I, 0)),
        borders)

    ranked   = order(interiors, lambda p: size(p))
    smallest = first(ranked)
    largest  = last(ranked)
    rest     = difference(merge(interiors), combine(smallest, largest))

    # turn patches into objects and recolour
    obj_s    = recolor(8, toobject(smallest, I))
    obj_l    = recolor(3, toobject(largest,  I))
    obj_r    = recolor(4, toobject(rest,      I))

    merged   = merge({obj_s, obj_l, obj_r})
    O        = underpaint(I, merged)                  # paint coloured interiors onto I
    return O
```

```python
    O = fill(I, 2, toobject(interior, I))
```

```python
    fours   = ofcolor(I, 4)
```

```python
    def within_two(p):

        n2 = neighbors(n1)
        return greater(size(intersection(n2, fours)), ZERO)

    target = mfilter(fives, within_two)
    O = fill(I, 2, toobject(target, I))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ── dilation expressed with power (function‑exponentiation) ──
    fours = ofcolor(I, 4)

    # one‑step Manhattan dilation
    dilate = lambda p: combine(
                combine(combine(shift(p, UP), shift(p, DOWN)),
                        combine(shift(p, LEFT), shift(p, RIGHT)))

    # apply dilation twice using power
    reach = power(lambda x: combine(x, dilate(x)), 2)(fours)

    target = intersection(ofcolor(I, 5), reach)
    O = fill(I, 2, toobject(target, I))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # object‑extraction rule: treat each 4 as an object, expand it
    # independently in the four cardinal directions (up to two steps) while
    # requiring the intermediate cell to be background.
    fours = ofcolor(I, 4)

    # helper that for a given direction returns the two‑step cells that have a clear intermediate
    def expand_dir(dir_vec):
        one   = intersection(shift(fours, dir_vec), ofcolor(I, 0))
        two   = shift(one, dir_vec)
        return combine(shift(fours, dir_vec), two)

    up    = expand_dir(UP)
    down  = expand_dir(DOWN)
    left  = expand_dir(LEFT)
    right = expand_dir(RIGHT)

    reach = combine(combine(fours, up), combine(down, combine(left, right)))
    target = intersection(ofcolor(I, 5), reach)
    return fill(I, 2, toobject(target, I))
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # geometric‑reasoning rule: start from the full diamond of radius 2,
    # then remove the cells that belong to the two‑step diagonal lines
    # (these are the only positions that need a turn).
    fours = ofcolor(I, 4)

    # full diamond (Manhattan ≤2) – obtained by two neighbourhood steps
    step  = lambda p: combine(p,
                combine(
                    combine(shift(p, UP),    shift(p, DOWN)),
                    combine(shift(p, LEFT),  shift(p, RIGHT))
                ))
    diamond = power(step, 2)(fours)

    # diagonal two‑step lines (pure diagonal moves)
    diag = combine(
            combine(shift(fours, astuple(1, 1)),  shift(fours, astuple(-1, -1))),
            combine(shift(fours, astuple(1, -1)), shift(fours, astuple(-1, 1))),
            combine(shift(fours, astuple(2, 2)),  shift(fours, astuple(-2, -2))),
            combine(shift(fours, astuple(2, -2)), shift(fours, astuple(-2, 2)))
        )
    reach = difference(diamond, diag)               # keep only straight‑line cells
    target = intersection(ofcolor(I, 5), reach)
    return fill(I, 2, toobject(target, I))
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ----- RELATIONAL – a 5 turns to 2 when it has a 4 within Manhattan‑2
    #    *and* every cell on a shortest orthogonal path to that 4 is background (0)
    fours = ofcolor(I, 4)

    # distance‑1 cells that are 0 (potential clean stepping stones)
    clear1 = intersection(
                combine(
                    combine(shift(fours, UP),    shift(fours, DOWN)),
                    combine(shift(fours, LEFT),  shift(fours, RIGHT))),
                ofcolor(I, 0))

    # distance‑2 clean cells: go through a clear1 cell then one more step
    clear2 = combine(
                combine(shift(clear1, UP),    shift(clear1, DOWN)),
                combine(shift(clear1, LEFT),  shift(clear1, RIGHT)))

    # all reachable cells (1‑step or 2‑step via clear background)
    reach = combine(
                combine(fours,                     # the 4‑cells themselves
                    combine(shift(fours, UP),    shift(fours, DOWN),
                    shift(fours, LEFT),          shift(fours, RIGHT)),
                clear2)

    # keep only the original 5‑cells that lie in the reachable set
    target = intersection(ofcolor(I, 5), reach)
    return fill(I, 2, toobject(target, I))
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    five = ofcolor(I, 5)

    # split the 5‑region into two parts by a vertical line through its centre
    left_boundary = leftmost(five)          # column of the left‑most 5
    right_boundary = rightmost(five)        # column of the right‑most 5
    centre_col = (left_boundary + right_boundary) // 2

    left_block = sfilter(
        five,
        lambda p: p[1] <= centre_col,
    )
    right_block = sfilter(
        five,
        lambda p: p[1] > centre_col,
    )

    O = I
    O = fill(O, 8, left_block)   # left half becomes 8
    O = fill(O, 2, right_block)   # right half becomes 2
    return O
```
