```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL‑TRANSFORMATION: cut out the 5‑region, keep only columns that contain
    # more than one 5‑pixel, then paste the column mask back.
    five      = ofcolor(I, 5)
    ul        = ulcorner(five)                     # upper‑left corner of the 5‑region
    lr        = lrcorner(five)                     # lower‑right corner
    dims      = add(subtract(lr, ul), (ONE, ONE))  # height‑width of the bounding box
    crop_five = crop(I, ul, dims)                  # isolated 5‑region (background kept)
    # partition the isolated region – each connected component is a vertical strip
    col_objs  = partition(crop_five)
    # keep only those strips that have at least two cells (i.e. true vertical parts)
    thick     = sizefilter(col_objs, TWO)
    # recombine and shift back to original coordinates
    mask_trim = combine(*tuple(thick))
    mask      = shift(mask_trim, ul)
    O = replace(I, 5, 8)
    O = fill(O, 2, mask)
    return O
```

```python
    vertical   = combine(
        intersection(five, shifted),           # has neighbour on the right

    )

    O = replace(I, 5, 8)
    O = fill(O, 2, vertical)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL‑TRANSFORMATION
    # 1) locate the whole 5‑region, cut it out, and compute its bounding box.
    # 2) inside that box, keep only the central vertical strip (the column whose
    #    index is the average of the left‑most and right‑most columns).
    # 3) paste the strip back, replace the original 5’s with 8’s and colour the
    #    strip with 2.
    five   = ofcolor(I, 5)
    ul      = ulcorner(five)
    lr      = lrcorner(five)
    dims    = add(subtract(lr, ul), (ONE, ONE))
    crop    = crop(I, ul, dims)                     # isolated 5‑region
    left    = leftmost(five)                        # column index of left edge
    right   = rightmost(five)                       # column index of right edge
    centre  = divide(add((ZERO, left), (ZERO, right)), TWO)  # average column
    strip   = sfilter(ofcolor(crop, 5),
                      lambda p: p[1] == centre[1])  # keep only central column
    strip_g = shift(strip, ul)                     # move back to original pos
    O = replace(I, 5, 8)
    O = fill(O, 2, strip_g)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑EXTRACTION
    # Work on each connected component of colour 5.
    # For a component take its bounding box, then keep the cells that lie on the
    # column that appears most often inside that box (the “vertical spine” of the
    # component).  Finally replace 5→8 and colour the spine with 2.
    comps   = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 5)               # set of 5‑objects
    def spine(obj):
        ulc   = ulcorner(obj)
        lrc   = lrcorner(obj)
        # count how many cells each column contains
        cols   = apply(
                    lambda p: p[1],
                    obj
                )
        # most frequent column index
        bestc  = argmax(cols, lambda c: sizefilter(ofcolor(obj, c), ONE))
        return sfilter(obj, lambda p: p[1] == bestc[1])
    spines  = mapply(spine, comps)
    O = replace(I, 5, 8)
    O = fill(O, 2, combine(*tuple(spines)))
    return O
```

```python
    # Work on each connected component of colour 5.
    # For a component keep the column that occurs most often inside its

    # with 2.

    spines = mapply(spine, comps)
    O = replace(I, 5, 8)
    O = fill(O, 2, combine(*tuple(spines)))
    return O
```

```python
        up        = shift(comp, UP)
        down      = shift(comp, DOWN)
        interior  = intersection(intersection(comp, up), down)
        cols      = apply(lambda p: p[1], interior)
        return sfilter(comp, lambda p: p[1] in cols)            # column‑wise subset of this component

    spines = mapply(comp_spine, comps)                         # one spine per component
    O      = replace(I, 5, 8)
    O      = fill(O, 2, merge(spines))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Relational/structural: draw a line from the leftmost 5 to the rightmost 1,
    # recolour it 2 and then mirror horizontally
    five   = ofcolor(I, 5)                 # 5‑cells
    ones   = ofcolor(I, 1)                 # 1‑cells
    p5     = leftmost(five)                # column of leftmost 5
    p1     = rightmost(ones)               # column of rightmost 1
    r5 = uppermost(five)                  # row of topmost 5
    r1 = lowermost(ones)                  # row of bottommost 1
    start = (r5, p5)                       # upper‑left extreme
    end   = (r1, p1)                       # lower‑right extreme
    line  = connect(start, end)             # line between the two extremes
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Relational / structural: draw the shortest Manhattan line between any 5 and any 1,
    # then mirror it horizontally
    five = ofcolor(I, 5)
    ones = ofcolor(I, 1)
    pairs = product(five, ones)                         # all (5,1) pairs
    best  = argmin(pairs, lambda p: manhattan(p[0], p[1]))  # pair with minimal distance
    line  = connect(best[0], best[1])                   # line between the chosen cells
    base  = canvas(0, shape(I))
    painted = fill(base, 2, line)                       # colour the line with 2
    mir = hmirror(painted)                               # horizontal mirror
    O = compress(mir)                                   # crop to occupied region
    return O
```

```python
        # shift the object until its upper‑most and left‑most cells touch the border
        up   = gravitate(obj, { (0, c) for c in range(width(I)) })
        left = gravitate(move(I, obj, up), { (r, 0) for r in range(height(I)) })
        shifted = move(I, obj, add(up, left))
        return paint(empty, shifted)
    O = apply(place, colors)          # apply to every colour, combine by painting
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---------- RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL REASONING ----------
    # Treat each coloured component as a patch.  For every pair of patches,
    # compute the vector that would make the first patch adjacent to the second
    # (using gravitate).  Then move the first patch by that vector, processing
    # patches in order of increasing colour so that later patches overwrite earlier ones.
    cols = sorted(palette(I) - {0})
    empty = canvas(0, shape(I))
    def pack(col):
        src = ofcolor(I, col)
        # find the nearest already‑placed patch (if any)
        placed = ofcolor(empty, col)           # empty at first iteration
        dir_vec = gravitate(src, placed) if size(placed) > 0 else (0,0)
        shifted = move(I, src, dir_vec)
        return paint(empty, shifted)
    O = apply(pack, cols)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL – compute a common translation that brings the
    # upper‑most, left‑most object to the origin and apply it to every coloured object
    objs      = fgpartition(I)                         # set of all colour objects
    # reference object: the one with smallest (row, col) coordinate
    ref       = argmin(objs, lambda o: add(uppermost(o), leftmost(o)))
    up        = gravitate(ref, {(0, c) for c in range(width(I))})
    left      = gravitate(move(I, ref, up),
                           {(r, 0) for r in range(height(I))})
    offset    = add(up, left)                           # vector moving reference to (0,0)
    # shift every object by the same offset
    shifted   = apply(lambda o: shift(o, offset), objs)
    combined  = combine(*shifted)                       # union of all shifted objects
    empty     = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = paint(empty, combined)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT EXTRACTION – extract each colour object, move it to the
    #   top‑left corner of its own bounding box, then concatenate the
    #   resulting sub‑grids horizontally (preserving left‑to‑right order)
    objs      = fgpartition(I)                                      # coloured objects
    ordered   = order(objs, lambda o: leftmost(o))                    # left‑most first
    subgs     = apply(lambda o: subgrid(o, I), ordered)            # each object's minimal sub‑grid
    # fold the list of sub‑grids left‑to‑right using hconcat
    combined  = apply(lambda a: apply(lambda b: hconcat(a, b), subgs), subgs[0:1])[0]
    empty     = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = paint(empty, asobject(combined))
    return O
```

```python
    shifted    = apply(lambda o: shift(o, offset), objs)           # move every object
    united     = combine(*shifted)                                  # union of all shifted objects
    empty      = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O          = paint(empty, united)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL – compute a single translation that brings the
    #   upper‑most, left‑most coloured object to the origin and
    #   apply that very same translation to **every** coloured object.
    objs      = fgpartition(I)                       # all coloured objects
    # reference object: one with the smallest (row, col) coordinate
    ref       = argmin(objs, lambda o: add(uppermost(o), leftmost(o)))
    # vector that moves the reference to the top border
    up_vec    = gravitate(ref,
                         {(0, c) for c in interval(0, width(I), 1)})
    # then moves it to the left border
    left_vec  = gravitate(move(I, ref, up_vec),
                         {(r, 0) for r in interval(0, height(I), 1)})
    offset    = add(up_vec, left_vec)               # total translation
    shifted   = apply(lambda o: shift(o, offset), objs)  # move *all* objects
    united    = combine(*shifted)                   # union of shifted objects
    empty     = canvas(0, shape(I))
    return paint(empty, united)
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL – for each coloured object compute the vector that moves
    #   it as far up as possible, then as far left as possible; apply that
    #   vector to the object and finally unite all shifted objects.
    objs      = fgpartition(I)                                   # all objects
    # shift a single object up then left
    shift_up_left = lambda o: (
        let_up   := gravitate(o, {(0, c) for c in interval(0, width(I), 1)}),
        let_left := gravitate(move(I, o, let_up),
                               {(r, 0) for r in interval(0, height(I), 1)}),
        shift(o, add(let_up, let_left))
    )
    shifted   = apply(shift_up_left, objs)                       # move every object
    united    = apply(lambda o: o, shifted)                        # set of objects
    empty     = canvas(0, shape(I))
    return paint(empty, united)
```

```python
    #                (move its bounding box to the origin) while preserving
    #                its colour, then redraw all objects together.

    normed = apply(norm, objs)                         # set of normalised objects
    united = merge(normed)                             # one object containing all
    empty  = canvas(0, shape(I))
    return paint(empty, united)
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL – for each coloured object move it as far up as possible,
    #              then as far left as possible, keeping its colour.
    objs = fgpartition(I)                             # coloured objects

    def up_left(o):
        col   = color(o)                              # object's colour
        pts   = toindices(o)                          # set of coordinates
        # move up until just above the top row
        up    = gravitate(pts,
                          {(0, c) for c in interval(0, width(I), 1)})
        pts_up = shift(pts, up)
        # then move left until just left of the leftmost column
        left  = gravitate(pts_up,
                          {(r, 0) for r in interval(0, height(I), 1)})
        new_pts = shift(pts_up, left)
        return recolor(col, new_pts)

    shifted = apply(up_left, objs)                    # set of shifted objects
    united  = merge(shifted)                           # one object with all colours
    empty   = canvas(0, shape(I))
    return paint(empty, united)
```

#### DSL

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑LEVEL – take every coloured object, move it so its left side
    # touches the origin, then let it fall down until it contacts the
    # previously placed objects (stacking order is left‑to‑right).
    objs      = fgpartition(I)

    # order objects by their original leftmost column
    ordered   = order(objs, leftmost)

    # helper that normalises the x‑coordinate of an object
    def norm_x(o):
        col   = color(o)
        pts   = toindices(o)
        left  = gravitate(pts, {(r, 0) for r in interval(0, height(I), 1)})
        return recolor(col, shift(pts, left))

    # place the first object, then stack the rest
    first     = first(ordered)
    placed    = {norm_x(first)}

    def stack(o, acc):
        col   = color(o)
        pts   = toindices(o)
        # first move leftmost side to column 0
        left  = gravitate(pts, {(r, 0) for r in interval(0, height(I), 1)})
        pts_l = shift(pts, left)
        # then drop down until touching the current accumulation
        down  = gravitate(pts_l, outbox(merge(acc)))
        new   = shift(pts_l, down)
        return recolor(col, new)

    # apply the stacking function to the remaining objects
    rest      = difference(ordered, {first})
    stacked   = apply(lambda o: stack(o, placed), rest)

    united    = merge(combine(placed, stacked))
    empty     = canvas(0, shape(I))
    return paint(empty, united)
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL – first push every coloured object upward until it
    # touches the top edge, then push the whole result leftward until it
    # touches the left edge, preserving the relative vertical order.
    objs       = fgpartition(I)

    def up(o):
        col = color(o)
        pts = toindices(o)
        up  = gravitate(pts, {(0, c) for c in interval(0, width(I), 1)})
        return recolor(col, shift(pts, up))

    up_shifted = apply(up, objs)
    united_up = merge(up_shifted)

    # now shift the whole union leftward
    left = gravitate(toindices(united_up), {(r, 0) for r in interval(0, height(I), 1)})
    final = shift(toindices(united_up), left)

    empty     = canvas(0, shape(I))
    return paint(empty, recolor(mostcolor(I), final))
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑LEVEL – keep only the largest coloured object (by cell count)
    # and move it to the top‑left corner (gravity up then left).
    objs        = fgpartition(I)
    largest_obj = argmax(objs, lambda o: size(o))
    pts         = toindices(largest_obj)

    # move up
    up_vec  = gravitate(pts, {(0, c) for c in interval(0, width(I), 1)})
    pts_up  = shift(pts, up_vec)

    # then move left
    left_vec = gravitate(pts_up, {(r, 0) for r in interval(0, height(I), 1)})
    final    = shift(pts_up, left_vec)

    empty = canvas(0, shape(I))
    return paint(empty, recolor(color(largest_obj), final))
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL – push every coloured object upward until it touches the
    # top edge, then push the whole union leftward until it touches the
    # left edge, preserving the original vertical ordering of the objects.
    objs = fgpartition(I)

    # lift each object to the top
    lifted = apply(lambda o:
                   recolor(color(o),
                           shift(toindices(o),

                   objs)

    left_vec = gravitate(toindices(united_up),
                         {(r, 0) for r in interval(0, height(I), 1)})
    final    = shift(toindices(united_up), left_vec)

    empty = canvas(0, shape(I))
    return paint(empty, recolor(mostcolor(I), final))
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # 5 – construct the set of all cells that are *not* reachable from the
    #     outer border through 0‑cells (flood‑fill complement).  Those
    #     cells are precisely the interiors of the 3‑frames.
    zero_objs   = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 0)
    border_objs = sfilter(zero_objs,
                         lambda o: bordering(o, I))      # zero objects that touch the border
    reachable   = combine(mapply(toindices, border_objs))   # all border‑connected zeros
    all_zero    = ofcolor(I, 0)                           # every zero cell
    interior    = difference(all_zero, reachable)         # zeros not reachable from border
    O = fill(I, 4, interior)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # 5 – work on each 3‑object separately: extract its tight sub‑grid,
    #     fill the background of that sub‑grid with 4, then paint the
    #     original 3‑cells back.  The resulting patches are merged.
    comps3 = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 3)
    filled = mapply(
                lambda o:
                    paint(
                        fill(
                            subgrid(o, I),                # tiny grid containing the object
                            4,
                            delta(toindices(o))           # background cells of that sub‑grid
                        ),
                        o                                 # restore the original 3‑cells
                    ),
                comps3)
    # merge the individually‑filled sub‑grids back into one grid
    O = merge(filled)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # Relational core:  take all 0‑objects that lie completely inside
    # the union of the bounding boxes of the 3‑objects and colour them 4.
    zero_objs  = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 0)
    comps3     = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 3)
    back3      = merge(mapply(backdrop, comps3))               # union of all 3‑bboxes
    interior_z = sfilter(zero_objs,
                         lambda z: size(difference(backdrop(z), back3)) == 0)
    interior   = merge(mapply(toindices, interior_z))
    O = fill(I, 4, interior)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # Relational / directional core:  a 0‑cell becomes 4 iff the first
    # 3 seen in each cardinal direction belongs to the same 3‑object.
    comps3 = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 3)
    zeros  = ofcolor(I, 0)

    def same_component(p):
        return any(
            both(
                size(intersection(toindices(o), shoot(p, UP)))    > 0,
                both(
                    size(intersection(toindices(o), shoot(p, DOWN)))  > 0,
                    both(
                        size(intersection(toindices(o), shoot(p, LEFT)))  > 0,
                        size(intersection(toindices(o), shoot(p, RIGHT))) > 0
                    )
                )
            )
            for o in comps3)

    good = sfilter(zeros, lambda p: same_component(p))
    O = fill(I, 4, good)
    return O
```

```python
    # Global‑fill core:  turn every background cell (0) into 4,

    zeros        = ofcolor(I, 0)

    O   = fill(tmp, 0, reachable)    # border‑connected zeros → 0 again
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # 1 – horizontal sandwich:
    # a zero cell becomes 4 iff there is a 3 somewhere to its left
    # and a 3 somewhere to its right (same row, any distance).
    zeros   = ofcolor(I, 0)
    threes  = ofcolor(I, 3)

    def sandwiched(p):
        left  = intersection(threes, shoot(p, LEFT))
        right = intersection(threes, shoot(p, RIGHT))
        return both(size(left) > 0, size(right) > 0)

    interior = sfilter(zeros, sandwiched)
    return fill(I, 4, toobject(interior, I))
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # 4 – per‑object bounding‑box interior:
    # for each 3‑object take its axis‑aligned bounding box,
    # keep the cells of that box that are zeros,
    # then keep only those that lie between a left‑most and a right‑most 3
    # of the same object.
    comps  = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 3)
    zeros  = ofcolor(I, 0)

    def interior_of(o):
        box      = backdrop(o)                     # all cells of the bbox
        inside   = intersection(zeros, box)        # zeros inside the bbox
        # keep only those zeros that have a 3 of the same object on both sides
        left  = intersection(ofcolor(I, 3), shoot(toindices(o), LEFT))
        right = intersection(ofcolor(I, 3), shoot(toindices(o), RIGHT))
        return intersection(inside,
                              intersection(left, right))

    interior = merge(mapply(interior_of, comps))
    return fill(I, 4, toobject(interior, I))
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # 5 – union‑of‑3‑bounding‑boxes + horizontal sandwich:
    # first build the union of all 3‑objects’ bounding boxes,
    # restrict the horizontal‑sandwich test to that region.
    comps   = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 3)
    zeros   = ofcolor(I, 0)
    threes  = ofcolor(I, 3)

    union_box = merge(mapply(backdrop, comps))      # union of all bboxes
    candidates = intersection(zeros, union_box)    # zeros inside any bbox

    def sandwiched(p):
        left  = intersection(threes, shoot(p, LEFT))
        right = intersection(threes, shoot(p, RIGHT))
        return both(size(left) > 0, size(right) > 0)

    interior = sfilter(candidates, sandwiched)
    return fill(I, 4, toobject(interior, I))
```

```python
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # 5️⃣ Row‑based rule – if a row contains a horizontal run of at least three 6‑cells,
    #     recolour every 6 in that entire row to 2.
    #   a) extract all 6‑pixels
    six = ofcolor(I, 6)
    #   b) build a patch that covers the whole rows of those 6‑pixels
    rows   = { r for (r, _) in six }                     # set of row indices
    rowpatch = initset(())
    #   construct the row‑patch by taking the full width of the grid for each row
    rowpatch = combine(*[ connect((r, 0), (r, width(I)-1)) for r in rows ])
    #   c) intersect the row‑patch with the original 6‑patch to keep only the 6‑pixels
    target = intersection(six, rowpatch)
    O = fill(I, 2, target)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL – recolour a cell to 2 exactly when the
    # number of orthogonal neighbours that are 6 equals 2 (the cell is
    # “sandwiched” between two 6’s).  This captures the interior‑edge
    # pattern seen in the examples.
    six          = ofcolor(I, 6)
    up           = shift(six, UP)
    down         = shift(six, DOWN)
    left         = shift(six, LEFT)
    right        = shift(six, RIGHT)

    # cells that have a 6 above and below
    vpair        = intersection(up, down)
    # cells that have a 6 left and right
    hpair        = intersection(left, right)

    # cells that are 7 and belong to either pair
    target       = intersection(combine(vpair, hpair), ofcolor(I, 7))

    O            = paint(I, recolor(2, target))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # 4️⃣ Relational shift – move every non‑zero object as far as possible towards the
    #    bottom‑right corner while preserving its shape.
    objs   = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)
    O = I
    for obj in objs:
        bb      = backdrop(toobject(obj, I))               # bounding box of the object
        max_r   = max(r for r, _ in bb)
        max_c   = max(c for _, c in bb)
        shift_r = (height(I) - 1) - max_r                # how far down we can go
        shift_c = (width(I)  - 1) - max_c                # how far right we can go
        moved   = move(I, obj, (shift_r, shift_c))
        O = cover(O, obj)                                # erase original
        O = paint(O, moved)                               # paint moved version
    return O
```

```python
    O = I
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # 5️⃣ Relational filling: every background cell that touches a cell of colour 5
    #    (orthogonal adjacency) is recoloured with colour 7.
    five_cells   = ofcolor(I, 5)
    neigh_cells   = apply(lambda p: neighbors(p), five_cells)

    O = fill(I, 7, candidates)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # 2️⃣ Object‑centric: keep only the objects whose colour is the most common non‑zero colour,
    #    and paint the exact bounding box of each such object with that colour.
    main_col = mostcommon(ofcolor(I, lambda v: v != 0))
    objs = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)
    # bounding box of each object (its backdrop)
    boxes = apply(backdrop, objs)
    O = I
    O = apply(lambda b: paint(O, ofcolor(b, main_col)), boxes)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # 5️⃣ Relational – wherever two non‑zero cells lie on the same row,
    #    fill all cells between them with colour 3.
    rows_with_two = {r for r in range(height(I))
                    if sizefilter(ofcolor(I, 0), 0) and                # dummy to keep DSL style
                       any(c != 0 for c in I[r])}
    # build a patch that contains every background cell on those rows
    patch = { (r, c) for r in rows_with_two for c in range(width(I))
              if index(I, (r, c)) == 0 }
    O = fill(I, 3, patch)                                         # colour‑3 bridge
    return O
```

```python
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ---------- Object‑centric size filter ----------
    # Extract every connected component (object), keep the ones
    # whose size is at least three cells, and repaint them with
    # their original colour on a blank canvas.
    objs   = fgpartition(I)                               # all objects (incl. bg)
    large  = {o for o in objs if size(o) >= 3}           # size ≥ 3
    O      = canvas(0, shape(I))                         # empty canvas
    O      = fold(lambda G, Oi: fill(G, color(Oi), toindices(Oi)),
                 O, large)                               # repaint each large object
    return O
```

```python
    # For each column that contains at least two non‑zero cells,
    # fill every background cell between the topmost and bottommost

                     sizefilter(ofcolor(I, 0), 0) and
                     sizefilter(ofcolor(I, 0), 0)}           # dummy – keep DSL style
    # uppermost and lowermost non‑zero rows per column
    uppers = {c: minimum({r for r in range(height(I))
                         if index(I, (r, c)) != 0}) for c in col_two_plus}
    lowers = {c: maximum({r for r in range(height(I))
                         if index(I, (r, c)) != 0}) for c in col_two_plus}
    patch = {(r, c) for c in col_two_plus
                     for r in range(uppers[c], lowers[c] + 1)
                     if index(I, (r, c)) == 0}
    O = fill(I, 3, patch)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # 5️⃣ Relational – fill every vertical gap inside a column with the column’s own colour
    cols      = interval(0, width(I), 1)                     # all column indices
    # columns that contain at least two non‑zero cells
    goodcols  = {c for c in cols if size({(r, c) for r in range(height(I))
                                          if index(I, (r, c)) != 0}) >= 2}
    # colour that appears in a given column (they are uniform in the training data)
    colcolor  = lambda c: next(iter({index(I, (r, c)) for r in range(height(I))
                                    if index(I, (r, c)) != 0}))
    # vertical gap cells for a specific column
    gappatch  = lambda c: { (r, c) for r in
                            range(min({r for r in range(height(I))
                                      if index(I, (r, c)) != 0}),
                                  max({r for r in range(height(I))
                                      if index(I, (r, c)) != 0}) + 1)
                            if index(I, (r, c)) == 0 }
    # fill each gap with the column’s colour
    O = mapply(lambda G, c: fill(G, colcolor(c), gappatch(c)),
               I, goodcols)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC REASONING – move the 4‑coloured object to the cell that is
    # farthest (Manhattan) from the centre of the 8‑coloured object
    obj4   = toobject(ofcolor(I, 4), I)
    obj8   = toobject(ofcolor(I, 8), I)
    centre8 = centerofmass(obj8)
    farthest = argmax(ofcolor(I, 4),               # each 4‑cell as a patch
                      lambda p: manhattan(p, centre8))
    delta   = subtract(farthest, center(obj4))
    O = move(I, obj4, delta)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GEOMETRIC REASONING – fill every interior cell of the 8‑component with 8,
    # then move the (single) 4‑cell to the interior cell that is farthest from the 8‑object.
    obj8      = toobject(ofcolor(I, 8), I)
    interior  = difference(backdrop(obj8), obj8)                # cells inside the 8‑bbox but not 8
    O1        = fill(I, 8, interior)                           # make the interior solid 8
    obj4      = toobject(ofcolor(I, 4), I)                      # the 4‑cell (or component)
    farthest  = argmax(interior, lambda p: manhattan(initset(p), obj8))
    delta     = subtract(farthest, center(obj4))
    O         = move(O1, obj4, delta)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC REASONING – move the unique non‑0/8 colour to the centre of the 8‑shape
    # and recolour it to 4.
    comps     = objects(I, False, False, True)
    # keep only the component whose colour is neither 0 nor 8
    uniq      = first(mfilter(comps, lambda o: both(color(o) != 0, color(o) != 8)))
    obj8      = toobject(ofcolor(I, 8), I)
    c8        = center(obj8)
    cU        = center(uniq)
    delta     = subtract(c8, cU)                    # shift needed
    moved     = move(I, uniq, delta)                # move the odd component
    # recolour the moved component to 4
    movedU    = toobject(ofcolor(moved, color(uniq)), moved)
    O         = recolor(4, movedU)                  # recolour in‑place
    return O
```

```python
    # GLOBAL – start from an empty canvas, paint the 8‑shape, then put a 4 at its centre.
```

```python
    cen8    = center(obj8)                               # geometric centre of the 8‑object
    O       = fill(step1, 4, backdrop({cen8}))          # place a single 4 at the centre
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # GEOMETRIC – compute centre from bounding‑box extremes, keep only 8’s.
    obj8    = toobject(ofcolor(I, 8), I)                # 8‑object
    # centre = (uppermost + height//2 , leftmost + width//2)
    cen8    = astuple(
                add(uppermost(obj8), halve(height(obj8))),
                add(leftmost(obj8),  halve(width(obj8)))
             )
    step1   = fill(I, 0, difference(asindices(I), obj8))  # erase everything except 8’s
    O       = fill(step1, 4, backdrop({cen8}))           # add a 4 at the calculated centre
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL – use the detected horizontal period of the pattern and tile it
    # over the whole canvas.  The period is the smallest width that repeats
    # (hperiod) and the original picture is duplicated that many times.
    period   = hperiod(ofcolor(I, 0))            # width of the empty‑cell repeat
    tile     = hconcat(I, I)                     # make a simple double‑width tile
    O        = hconcat(tile, tile)               # repeat enough to cover the grid
    O        = crop(O, (0, 0), shape(I))          # finally crop back to original size
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑EXTRACTION – for every non‑background object take its column
    # (leftmost index) and paint a full‑height vertical line of that colour.
    objs      = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)
    coloured  = colorfilter(objs, 0)              # all real objects (ignore 0‑bg)
    lines     = apply(
                 lambda o: fill_vertical_line(I, color(o), leftmost(o)),
                 coloured)
    O = underpaint(I, combine(coloured, lines))
    return O


def fill_vertical_line(grid, col, colidx):
    # helper used by dsl2 – creates a vertical line (all rows) at column colidx
    h      = height(grid)
    line   = canvas(col, (h, 1))
    line   = shift(toobject(ofcolor(line, col), grid), (0, colidx))
    return line
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑EXTRACTION: recolour every object whose colour is the
    # least‑frequent non‑zero colour to the most‑frequent non‑zero colour.
    nonzero = ofcolor(I, 0)
    rare    = leastcolor(nonzero)
    common  = mostcolor(nonzero)

    # all coloured objects (background removed)
    objs    = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    # objects that have the rare colour
    rare_objs = colorfilter(objs, rare)

    # union of the indices of those objects
    idx_set   = apply(toindices, rare_objs)          # set of index‑sets
    patch     = combine(*idx_set)                    # single patch (union)

    # paint the most‑common colour on that patch
    O = fill(I, common, patch)
    return O
```

```python
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL: for each occurrence of the rare colour,
    # move the nearest most‑common coloured cell onto it.

    common  = mostcolor(nonzero)

    rare_pos    = ofcolor(I, rare)
    common_pos  = ofcolor(I, common)

    # for every rare cell, find the closest common cell
    targets = apply(
        lambda p: gravitate({p}, common_pos),   # direction towards nearest common
        rare_pos)

    # shift the most‑common colour along that direction (one step)
    shifted = apply(lambda d: shift(common_pos, d), targets)

    # erase the original rare cells and paint the shifted most‑common cells
    O = cover(I, rare_pos)
    O = paint(O, combine(*shifted))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # GLOBAL + COLOR‑COUNT (alternative colour‑filtering):
    # compute colour frequencies via colorcount, pick the rarest and most common,
    # then substitute the rare colour by the common one.
    nonzero = ofcolor(I, 0)

    # number of cells for each colour
    cnts = apply(lambda c: colorcount(I, c), palette(nonzero))

    # colour with smallest count (excluding background)
    rare   = argmin(cnts, lambda pair: pair[1])[0]
    # colour with largest count (excluding background)
    common = argmax(cnts, lambda pair: pair[1])[0]

    O = replace(I, rare, common)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ---- Core idea: L‑shaped Manhattan paths from the left‑most cell (hub) to the other cells ----
    all_idx   = asindices(I)                                 # all coordinates
    bg        = ofcolor(I, 0)                               # background
    nz        = difference(all_idx, bg)                       # non‑zero coordinates
    hub       = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])                  # left‑most cell  (minimum column)
    others    = difference(nz, initset(hub))                 # the two remaining cells

    # pick the two targets
    t1        = first(others)
    t2        = first(difference(others, initset(t1)))

    # helper: corner of the L‑shape (same row as hub, same column as target)
    corner = lambda tp: astuple(hub[0], tp[1])

    # L‑shape from hub to a target
    path = lambda tp: combine(
                connect(hub, corner(tp)),
                connect(corner(tp), tp)
    # union of the two L‑shapes
    whole = combine(path(t1), path(t2))

    # keep original coloured cells untouched
    paintzone = difference(whole, nz)

    # colour the zone with 5
    O = fill(I, 5, paintzone)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ---- Core idea: draw horizontal line from hub across each target column
    #             and vertical line from hub down/up each target row ------------
    all_idx   = asindices(I)
    bg        = ofcolor(I, 0)
    nz        = difference(all_idx, bg)
    hub       = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])                 # left‑most cell
    others    = difference(nz, initset(hub))

    # for every other cell create the two orthogonal segments
    def make_segments(p):
        horiz = connect(hub, astuple(hub[0], p[1]))         # same row, target column
        vert  = connect(astuple(hub[0], p[1]), p)           # same column, target row
        return combine(horiz, vert)

    segs      = apply(make_segments, others)                # set of two‑segment patches
    whole     = fold(segs, lambda a, b: combine(a, b), initset())  # union of all segments
    paintzone = difference(whole, nz)                        # exclude original cells
    O = fill(I, 5, paintzone)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ---- Core idea: for each target, take the full rectangle (box) defined by hub and target
    #                and colour its interior (excluding the four corner cells) with 5 --------
    all_idx   = asindices(I)
    bg        = ofcolor(I, 0)
    nz        = difference(all_idx, bg)
    hub       = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])                 # left‑most cell
    others    = difference(nz, initset(hub))

    t1        = first(others)
    t2        = first(difference(others, initset(t1)))

    # rectangle (including its border) between two points
    rect = lambda a, b: box(connect(a, b))

    # interior = rectangle minus its four corners
    interior = lambda a, b: difference(rect(a, b), initset(a), initset(b),
                                    initset(astuple(a[0], b[1])),
                                    initset(astuple(b[0], a[1])))

    whole = combine(interior(hub, t1), interior(hub, t2))
    paintzone = difference(whole, nz)
    O = fill(I, 5, paintzone)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ---- Core idea: use the centre of mass of all coloured cells as a temporary anchor.
    #                From this centre draw straight lines to every coloured cell,
    #                then keep only the parts that lie on the row or column of the
    #                original left‑most cell (hub) ---------------------------------
    all_idx   = asindices(I)
    bg        = ofcolor(I, 0)
    nz        = difference(all_idx, bg)

    hub       = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])                 # left‑most cell
    centre    = centerofmass(nz)                            # geometric centre (integer)

    # line from centre to a target cell
    line = lambda p: connect(centre, p)

    all_lines = apply(line, nz)
    whole     = fold(all_lines, lambda a, b: combine(a, b), initset())

    # keep only cells that are on hub's row or hub's column
    row_part  = apply(lambda p: p[0] == hub[0], whole)
    col_part  = apply(lambda p: p[1] == hub[1], whole)
    mask      = combine(filter(row_part, whole), filter(col_part, whole))

    paintzone = difference(mask, nz)
    O = fill(I, 5, paintzone)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---- Core idea: propagate the colour 5 outward from the hub by repeatedly
    #                applying gravitate towards each non‑hub coloured cell.
    #                Stop when the next step would hit an existing coloured cell. ----
    all_idx   = asindices(I)
    bg        = ofcolor(I, 0)
    nz        = difference(all_idx, bg)

    hub       = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])                 # left‑most cell
    others    = difference(nz, initset(hub))

    # one step of gravitation towards a target is a single adjacent cell
    step = lambda src, dst: gravitate(src, dst)

    # generate the chain of cells from hub to each target (excluding endpoints)
    def chain(p):
        src = hub
        cells = initset()
        while True:
            nxt = step(src, p)
            # stop when we reach the target or would step onto a coloured cell
            cond = (nxt == p) or contained(nxt, nz)
            cells = combine(cells, initset(nxt))
            src = nxt
            if cond:
                break
        return cells

    paths = apply(chain, others)
    whole = fold(paths, lambda a, b: combine(a, b), initset())
    paintzone = difference(whole, nz)
    O = fill(I, 5, paintzone)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # Geometric‑border view:  take the rectangle border between hub and each target
    # (produced by “box”) and keep only the two sides that share the hub corner.
    all_idx = asindices(I)
    bg      = ofcolor(I, 0)
    nz      = difference(all_idx, bg)
    hub     = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])
    others  = difference(nz, initset(hub))
    t1      = first(others)
    t2      = first(difference(others, initset(t1)))

    # full rectangle border (four sides)
    rect1   = box(connect(hub, t1))
    rect2   = box(connect(hub, t2))

    # keep only the side that lies on hub’s row and the side that lies on hub’s column
    top1    = apply(lambda p: p if p[0] == hub[0] else None, rect1)
    left1   = apply(lambda p: p if p[1] == hub[1] else None, rect1)
    top2    = apply(lambda p: p if p[0] == hub[0] else None, rect2)
    left2   = apply(lambda p: p if p[1] == hub[1] else None, rect2)

    # remove the “None” entries that were inserted by the filters
    clean1  = difference(difference(top1, initset(None)), initset(None))
    clean1  = combine(clean1, difference(difference(left1, initset(None)), initset(None)))
    clean2  = difference(difference(top2, initset(None)), initset(None))
    clean2  = combine(clean2, difference(difference(left2, initset(None)), initset(None)))

    whole   = combine(clean1, clean2)
    paint   = difference(whole, nz)
    O       = fill(I, 5, paint)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Relational‑structural view:  first compute the centre of mass of all
    # coloured cells, draw straight lines from that centre to every coloured cell,
    # and finally keep only the parts that lie on the hub’s row or column.
    all_idx = asindices(I)
    bg      = ofcolor(I, 0)
    nz      = difference(all_idx, bg)

    hub     = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])
    centre  = centerofmass(nz)                           # integer centre point

    # one line from centre to each coloured cell
    lines   = apply(lambda p: connect(centre, p), nz)

    # union of all those lines
    whole   = combine(lines, initset())                   # combine with an empty set works
    # keep only the rows/columns that pass through the hub
    rowmask = apply(lambda p: p if p[0] == hub[0] else None, whole)
    colmask = apply(lambda p: p if p[1] == hub[1] else None, whole)

    cleanrow= difference(difference(rowmask, initset(None)), initset(None))
    cleancol= difference(difference(colmask, initset(None)), initset(None))
    mask    = combine(cleanrow, cleancol)

    paint   = difference(mask, nz)
    O       = fill(I, 5, paint)
    return O
```

```python
    whole = combine(horiz, vert)
    paint = difference(whole, nz)
    return fill(I, 5, paint)
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # geometric‑rectangle : build the rectangle bounded by the hub
    # (left‑most coloured cell) and the furthest coloured row/col,
    # then keep only the cells that lie on the hub's row or column.
    all_idx = asindices(I)
    nz      = difference(all_idx, ofcolor(I, 0))
    hub     = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])                     # left‑most column

    rows    = apply(lambda p: p[0], nz)
    cols    = apply(lambda p: p[1], nz)
    maxr    = valmax(rows, lambda x: x)
    maxc    = valmax(cols, lambda x: x)

    # four sides of the bounding rectangle
    top    = connect(astuple(hub[0], hub[1]), astuple(hub[0], maxc))
    right  = connect(astuple(hub[0], maxc),  astuple(maxr, maxc))
    bottom = connect(astuple(maxr, maxc),    astuple(maxr, hub[1]))
    left   = connect(astuple(maxr, hub[1]), hub)
    rectangle = combine(combine(top, right), combine(bottom, left))

    # keep only cells on hub's row or column
    filtered = apply(lambda p: p if (p[0] == hub[0] or p[1] == hub[1]) else None,
                    rectangle)
    mask = difference(difference(filtered, initset(None)), nz)
    return fill(I, 5, mask)
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # 2️⃣  Apply‑filter + column selection
    # build an L‑shape for every non‑hub cell, then keep only those that
    # touch the right‑most column.
    all_idx = asindices(I)
    nz      = difference(all_idx, ofcolor(I, 0))
    hub     = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])
    others  = difference(nz, initset(hub))
    maxc    = valmax(apply(lambda p: p[1], others), lambda x: x)   # greatest column index

    # L‑shapes for all other cells
    paths   = apply(
                lambda tp:
                    combine(connect(hub, astuple(hub[0], tp[1])),
                            connect(astuple(hub[0], tp[1]), tp)),
                others)

    # keep only those that contain a cell in the right‑most column
    keep    = apply(
                lambda s: s if any(cell[1] == maxc for cell in s) else None,
                paths)

    paint   = difference(difference(keep, initset(None)), nz)
    return fill(I, 5, paint)
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # --- Global‑transformation core (crop + move) ---
    # Work on the sub‑grid that spans the hub column to the right‑most column,
    # draw the L‑shape there and paste it back.
    all_idx = asindices(I)
    nz      = difference(all_idx, ofcolor(I, 0))
    hub     = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])                     # left‑most column
    others  = difference(nz, initset(hub))
    target  = argmax(others, lambda p: p[1])                # right‑most column

    w       = target[1] - hub[1] + 1                        # width of the region
    sub     = crop(I, astuple(0, hub[1]), astuple(height(I), w))

    hub_s   = astuple(hub[0], 0)                            # hub inside the sub‑grid
    tgt_s   = astuple(target[0], w-1)                       # target inside the sub‑grid
    path_s  = combine(connect(hub_s, astuple(hub_s[0], tgt_s[1])),
                      connect(astuple(hub_s[0], tgt_s[1]), tgt_s))
    paint_s = difference(path_s, ofcolor(sub, 0))
    sub_f   = fill(sub, 5, paint_s)                         # paint the L‑shape inside the crop
    obj5    = ofcolor(sub_f, 5)                              # the newly painted cells

    return move(I, obj5, astuple(0, hub[1]))                # paste back at the original position
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # --- Color‑filtering core (mfilter) ---
    # Keep every zero cell that lies on the hub’s row between the two extreme columns
    # or on the right‑most column between the hub row and the target row.
    all_idx = asindices(I)
    nz      = difference(all_idx, ofcolor(I, 0))
    hub     = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])
    others  = difference(nz, initset(hub))
    target  = argmax(others, lambda p: p[1])
    maxc    = target[1]

    def keep(p):
        return (p[0] == hub[0] and hub[1] <= p[1] <= maxc) \
            or (p[1] == maxc and min(hub[0], target[0]) <= p[0] <= max(hub[0], target[0]))

    cand    = mfilter(all_idx, keep)
    paint   = difference(cand, nz)                          # avoid overwriting existing colours
    return fill(I, 5, paint)
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # --- Ray‑casting core (shoot + mfilter) ---
    # Generate a horizontal ray from the hub to the right‑most column,
    # then a vertical ray downwards, and colour the union.
    all_idx = asindices(I)
    nz      = difference(all_idx, ofcolor(I, 0))
    hub     = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])
    others  = difference(nz, initset(hub))
    target  = argmax(others, lambda p: p[1])
    maxc    = target[1]

    # horizontal ray, clipped to the rectangle
    horiz_full = shoot(hub, RIGHT)
    horiz = mfilter(horiz_full,
                    lambda p: p[0] == hub[0] and hub[1] <= p[1] <= maxc)

    # vertical ray, starting at the corner (hub row, maxc)
    start_v = astuple(hub[0], maxc)
    vert_full = shoot(start_v, DOWN)
    vert = mfilter(vert_full,
                    lambda p: p[1] == maxc and hub[0] <= p[0] <= target[0])

    path = combine(horiz, vert)
    paint = difference(path, nz)
    return fill(I, 5, paint)
```

```python
    # Color‑filtering core – keep every background cell that lies on the
    # horizontal leg (hub’s row) between the extreme columns or on the
    # vertical leg (target’s column) between the hub row and target row.
    all_idx = asindices(I)
    nz      = difference(all_idx, ofcolor(I, 0))

    hub     = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])
    others  = difference(nz, initset(hub))
    target  = argmax(others, lambda p: p[1])
    maxc    = target[1]

    def keep(p):
        return (p[0] == hub[0] and hub[1] <= p[1] <= maxc) \
            or (p[1] == maxc and min(hub[0], target[0]) <= p[0] <= max(hub[0], target[0]))

    cand    = mfilter(all_idx, keep)                     # candidate background cells
    paint   = difference(cand, nz)                       # avoid overwriting original colours
    return fill(I, 5, paint)
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # -------- Global‑crop‑and‑move core ----------
    # Crop the minimal vertical strip that contains both extreme columns,
    # draw the L‑shape inside this strip, then paste the strip back.
    all_idx = asindices(I)
    nz      = difference(all_idx, ofcolor(I, 0))
    hub     = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])
    others  = difference(nz, initset(hub))
    target  = argmax(others, lambda p: p[1])

    w = target[1] - hub[1] + 1                           # strip width
    sub = crop(I, astuple(0, hub[1]), astuple(height(I), w))

    hub_s    = astuple(hub[0], 0)                        # hub inside strip
    tgt_s    = astuple(target[0], w-1)                    # target inside strip
    corner_s = astuple(hub_s[0], tgt_s[1])

    path_s   = combine(connect(hub_s, corner_s), connect(corner_s, tgt_s))
    paint_s  = difference(path_s, ofcolor(sub, 0))
    sub_f    = fill(sub, 5, paint_s)

    obj5     = toobject(paint_s, sub_f)                  # L‑shape as an object
    return move(I, obj5, astuple(0, hub[1]))             # paste strip back
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # -------- Relational‑template core ----------
    # Create a minimal L‑shape template (origin at (0,0)),
    # then shift it to the hub position.
    nz      = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))
    hub     = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])
    others  = difference(nz, initset(hub))
    target  = argmax(others, lambda p: p[1])

    # size of the needed template
    dh      = subtract(target, hub)[0]                  # row delta (≥0)
    dw      = subtract(target, hub)[1]                  # col delta (≥0)

    # template L‑shape in local coordinates
    horiz_t = connect(astuple(0, 0), astuple(0, dw))
    vert_t  = connect(asttuple(0, dw), astuple(dh, dw))
    tmpl    = combine(horiz_t, vert_t)

    # move the template to the hub location
    shifted = shift(tmpl, hub)

    paint   = difference(shifted, nz)
    return fill(I, 5, paint)
```

```python
def dsl4(I):

    # and the rightmost column, draw the three L‑shapes (right, top, bottom)
    # inside the strip and paste it back.
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # relational/template: build a minimal L‑shape for each non‑hub cell,
    # orient it according to its vertical relation to the hub, union them.
    nz      = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))
    hub     = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])
    others  = difference(nz, initset(hub))
    def make_path(p):
        # if the target is below the hub → vertical‑first,
        # otherwise → horizontal‑first.
        return branch(greater(p[0], hub[0]),
                      combine(connect(hub, astuple(p[0], hub[1])),
                              connect(astuple(p[0], hub[1]), p)),
                      combine(connect(hub, astuple(hub[0], p[1])),
                              connect(astuple(hub[0], p[1]), p)))
    paths   = apply(make_path, others)                 # container of patches
    # union of all patches (three‑way union is sufficient for the small sets)
    allpath = combine(combine(paths, paths), paths)
    paint   = difference(allpath, nz)
    return fill(I, 5, paint)
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # global‑crop‑and‑paste: isolate the strip from hub column to right‑most
    # column, draw the two L‑shapes inside it, then paste back.
    nz     = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))
    hub    = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])
    right  = argmax(nz, lambda p: p[1])
    top    = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[0])

    w      = right[1] - hub[1] + 1
    strip  = crop(I, astuple(0, hub[1]), astuple(height(I), w))

    hub_s   = astuple(hub[0], 0)
    right_s = astuple(right[0], w-1)

    # hub → top (vertical then horizontal) inside the strip
    path_t  = combine(connect(hub_s, astuple(top[0], hub_s[1])),
                       connect(astuple(top[0], hub_s[1]), astuple(top[0], right_s[1])))
    # hub → right (horizontal then vertical) inside the strip
    path_r  = combine(connect(hub_s, astuple(hub_s[0], right_s[1])),
                       connect(astuple(hub_s[0], right_s[1]), right_s))

    paint_s = difference(combine(path_t, path_r), ofcolor(strip, 0))
    strip_f = fill(strip, 5, paint_s)
    obj5    = toobject(paint_s, strip_f)
    return move(I, obj5, astuple(0, hub[1]))
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # relational: for each non‑hub coloured cell, build an L‑shape.
    # If the cell is above the hub → vertical‑first, else → horizontal‑first.
    nz      = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, 0))
    hub     = argmin(nz, lambda p: p[1])
    others  = difference(nz, initset(hub))

    make_path = lambda p: branch(
        less(p[0], hub[0]),                               # above hub ?
        combine(connect(hub, astuple(p[0], hub[1])),
                connect(astuple(p[0], hub[1]), p)),
        combine(connect(hub, astuple(hub[0], p[1])),
                connect(astuple(hub[0], p[1]), p))
    )
    paths   = apply(make_path, others)
    allpath = combine(combine(paths, paths), paths)      # union of all patches
    paint   = difference(allpath, nz)
    return fill(I, 5, paint)
```

```python
    O       = switch(O, 3, 7)                       # 3 → 7
    O       = switch(O, 2, 7)                       # 2 → 7
    O       = switch(O, 4, 7)                       # 4 → 7
    O       = switch(O, 6, 7)                       # 6 → 7
    # compute a filler colour (the smallest digit not used in the original grid)

    # finally paste back the untouched 8‑objects
    O = paint(O, initset(keep8))
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # find every 7‑cell that is adjacent (4‑connected) to both an 8‑cell
    # and a non‑7, non‑8 cell; move the non‑7, non‑8 cell one step towards the
    # 7‑cell (using gravitate) and recolour the vacated spot with 7.
    objs8   = ofcolor(I, 8)
    others  = {c for c in ofcolor(I, None)          # all cells
               if index(I, c) not in {8,7}}
    O = I
    for c in others:
        # if the cell touches a 7‑cell that also touches an 8‑cell
        neigh7 = dneighbors(c) & ofcolor(I, 7)
        if neigh7 and any(dneighbors(c) & objs8):
            target = first(neigh7)                  # one of the neighbouring 7‑cells
            dirvec = gravitate(initset({c}), initset({target}))
            O = move(O, initset({c}), dirvec)        # shift the cell toward the 7‑cell
            O = recolor(7, {c})                     # the original position becomes 7
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # RELATIONAL MOVE USING GRAVITATE (no explicit loops)
    other_colors = palette(I) - {7, 8}
    # all positions of the “other” colours
    cells_by_color = mapply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), other_colors)

    # positions that have a 7 neighbour and also touch an 8 (any diagonal neighbour)
    candidates = mapply(lambda s:
                        {p for p in s
                          if dneighbors(p) & ofcolor(I, 7) and
                             dneighbors(p) & ofcolor(I, 8)},
                        cells_by_color)

    # for each candidate, move it one step towards the 7 neighbour and recolour the source cell 7
    O = I
    O = mapply(lambda pair:
                let = gravitate(initset({pair[0][0]}), initset({pair[0][1]}))
                move(recolor(7, {pair[0][0]}), {pair[0][0]}, let),
                zip(candidates, other_colors))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # RELATIONAL MOVE (pure mapply) : any non‑7/8 cell that touches a 7 and an 8
    # is moved one step towards the nearest 7 (by gravitate) and the source cell
    # is recoloured 7.
    other   = palette(I) - {7, 8}
    # candidate cells of each colour that have a diagonal 7 neighbour and a diagonal 8 neighbour
    cand    = mapply(
                lambda c: {p for p in ofcolor(I, c)
                           if dneighbors(p) & ofcolor(I, 7)
                           and dneighbors(p) & ofcolor(I, 8)},
                other)

    # compute the direction from each candidate to the (any) adjacent 7
    dirs    = mapply(
                lambda p: gravitate(
                            initset({p}),
                            initset({first(dneighbors(p) & ofcolor(I, 7))})),
                cand)

    # move every candidate simultaneously, then recolour all original positions 7
    O = mapply(lambda p, d: move(I, initset({p}), d), zip(cand, dirs))
    O = recolor(7, cand)
    return O
```

```python
                             if add(p, RIGHT) in ofcolor(I, c)},

                fill(O, pair[0], toobject(pair[1], I)),
                zip(other, to_c))

    # turn the original colour‑c cells into 7
    O = mapply(lambda c: fill(O, 7, toobject(orig_c[c], I)), other)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # MIRROR‑SHIFT‑COMBINE + RECOLOUR “sandwiched” 7
    # 1) mirror vertically, shift the mirror one column right and overlay.
    # 2) any 7 that has an 8 on both its left and right (in the original grid)
    #    is recoloured with the least frequent non‑7/8 colour.
    mirrored = vmirror(I)
    shifted  = move(mirrored, asobject(mirrored), (0, 1))
    O = combine(I, shifted)

    filler   = leastcommon(palette(I) - {7, 8})          # new colour
    sand     = {p for p in ofcolor(O, 7)
                  if add(p, LEFT)  in ofcolor(I, 8)
                  and add(p, RIGHT) in ofcolor(I, 8)}
    O = recolor(filler, sand)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # VERTICAL PROJECTION SWAP : for every column, the leftmost non‑7/8
    # colour that shares the column with a 7 becomes 7, and the 7 becomes
    # that colour.  This is achieved by pairing each 7 with the nearest
    # non‑7/8 cell in the same column (using gravitate) and swapping.
    other   = palette(I) - {7, 8}
    # cells of colours other than 7/8
    others  = mapply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), other)

    # for each such cell, the nearest 7 in the same column (if any)
    pairs   = mapply(
                lambda p: (p,
                           first({q for q in ofcolor(I, 7)
                                   if q[1] == p[1]}))
                if {q for q in ofcolor(I, 7) if q[1] == p[1]} else None,
                others)

    # keep only pairs where a 7 was found
    valid   = {pair for pair in pairs if pair is not None}

    # swap colours by moving the non‑7/8 cell onto the 7 position
    O = I
    O = mapply(lambda pr: move(O, initset({pr[0]}), subtract(pr[1], pr[0])),
               valid)
    # recolour the original 7 positions (now empty) to the colour of the moved cell
    O = mapply(lambda pr: recolor(color(toobject({pr[0]}, I)), {pr[1]}), valid)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL SHIFT: move every non‑7/8 object so it sits directly
    # after the right‑most 8 in its row, painting the cells it
    # leaves behind with 7.
    right8   = valmax(ofcolor(I, 8),       lambda p: p[1])      # column of the right‑most 8
    target   = add(right8[1], ONE)                               # first free column
    objs = {o for o in objects(I,
                               univalued=False,
                               diagonal=False,
                               without_bg=True)
            if color(o) not in {7, 8}}
    O = mapply(
            lambda o:
                fill(recolor(7, I),                                 # clear old cells
                     shift(o,
                           (ZERO,
                            subtract(target, leftmost(o)))),      # shift horizontally
                     color(o)),                                    # keep original colour
            objs)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # COLOUR‑CYCLE: build a cyclic mapping over all colours that are
    # neither 7 nor 8, ordered by their numeric value, and recolour each
    # object with the next colour in the cycle.
    other   = palette(I) - {7, 8}
    # sorted tuple of the colours
    sortedc = tuple(order(other, lambda c: c))
    # function that gives the successor colour (cyclic)
    succ    = lambda c: sortedc[(index(sortedc, c) + ONE) % size(sortedc)]
    objs = {o for o in objects(I,
                               univalued=False,
                               diagonal=False,
                               without_bg=True)
            if color(o) not in {7, 8}}
    O = mapply(
            lambda o: fill(I, succ(color(o)), o),
            objs)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # MIRROR‑SHIFT‑COMBINE: mirror the whole picture vertically,
    # shift the mirror one column to the right, overlay it on the
    # original and keep the background (7) wherever both layers have 7.
    mirrored = vmirror(I)
    shifted  = move(mirrored, asobject(mirrored), (ZERO, ONE))
    O = combine(I, shifted)
    # cells that are 7 in both layers become the least‑frequent colour
    filler   = valmin(palette(I) - {7, 8},
                     lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    both7    = intersection(ofcolor(I, 7), ofcolor(shifted, 7))
    O = recolor(filler, both7)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # GRAVITATE‑LEFT: repeatedly move every non‑7/8 cell one step
    # toward the nearest 8 in its row, repeating enough times to push
    # the whole colour block next to the 8‑block.
    other   = palette(I) - {7, 8}
    step    = lambda g, c: gravitate(
                               frozenset({c}),
                               frozenset({first(dneighbors(c) & ofcolor(g, 8)}))
    O = apply(
            lambda _: mapply(
                        lambda col:
                            let = ofcolor(_, col)
                            dirs = mapply(lambda p: step(_, p), let)
                            move(_, let, dirs[0]) if dirs else _,
                        other),
            range(width(I)))                # repeat for the width of the grid
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # Object‑level colour‑cycle: next colour is the smallest greater colour,
    # wrapping to the smallest when none is greater.
    colors   = palette(I) - {7, 8}
    sortedc  = tuple(order(colors, lambda c: c))
    succ = lambda c: branch(
                equality(c, last(sortedc)),
                first(sortedc),
                argmin({col for col in sortedc if greater(col, c)},
                       lambda x: x))
    objs = {o for o in objects(I,
                               univalued=False,
                               diagonal=False,
                               without_bg=True)
            if color(o) not in {7, 8}}
    O = mapply(lambda o: fill(I,
                               succ(color(o)),
                               toindices(o)),
               objs)
    return O
```

```python
    # ---------- 3. Bounding‑box sub‑grid cycle ----------
    # extract every non‑background component, apply the global
    # 9‑1‑3 cycle inside its minimal rectangle and paste back
    objs = {o for o in objects(I,
                               univalued=False,

            if color(o) in {9, 1, 3}}
    O = I

        # global cycle on the sub‑grid (same as dsl1 but without placeholders)
        sub0 = replace(sub, 9, 0)
        sub1 = replace(sub0, 1, 9)
        sub2 = replace(sub1, 3, 1)
        subc = replace(sub2, 0, 3)
        # put the transformed rectangle back, overwriting only the cells of o
        O = paint(O, toobject(o, subc))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ---------- 4. Adjacency‑based colour swap ----------
    # wherever a 9‑cell is orthogonally adjacent to a 1‑cell,
    # swap those two colours; the same for 1‑↔‑3 and 3‑↔‑9.
    def swap(col_a, col_b):
        # cells of colour col_a that touch a cell of colour col_b
        a = ofcolor(I, col_a)
        b = ofcolor(I, col_b)
        a_adj = {p for p in a if any(q in b for q in neighbors(p))}
        b_adj = {p for p in b if any(q in a for q in neighbors(p))}
        return a_adj, b_adj

    a9, b1 = swap(9, 1)
    a1, b3 = swap(1, 3)
    a3, b9 = swap(3, 9)

    O = I
    O = fill(O, 1, a9)      # 9 → 1 where adjacent to 1
    O = fill(O, 9, b1)      # 1 → 9 where adjacent to 9
    O = fill(O, 3, a1)      # 1 → 3 where adjacent to 3
    O = fill(O, 1, b3)      # 3 → 1 where adjacent to 1
    O = fill(O, 9, a3)      # 3 → 9 where adjacent to 9
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---------- 5. Row‑wise colour‑filtering ----------
    # treat each row as an independent tiny grid and perform the
    # 9‑1‑3 cycle only on the colours that actually appear in that row
    rows = vsplit(I, height(I))

    def proc_row(R):
        # colours present in the row except background 7 & 8
        cols = palette(R) - {7, 8}
        # build a local mapping according to the 9‑1‑3 cycle
        map9 = branch(contains(cols, 9), 1, 9)
        map1 = branch(contains(cols, 1), 3, 1)
        map3 = branch(contains(cols, 3), 9, 3)
        return fill(fill(fill(R, map1, ofcolor(R, 9)),
                    map3, ofcolor(R, map1)),
                    map9, ofcolor(R, map3))

    O = vconcat(*apply(proc_row, rows))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # All positions that are not background
    FG = ofcolor(I, lambda v: v != 0)

    # For each foreground cell, look at its orthogonal neighbours
    ADJ = {p for p in FG
           if any(index(I, n) != index(I, p) for n in neighbors(p))}
    # Cells that have at least one neighbour of a *different* colour
    BOUNDARY = {p for p in ADJ
                if any(index(I, n) != index(I, p) for n in neighbors(p))}

    # Recolour those boundary cells to colour 3, leave the rest unchanged
    O = recolor(3, BOUNDARY)
    O = paint(I, O)                         # overlay the recoloured cells
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ---------- COLOUR FILTERING ----------
    # Remove the three “marker’’ colours 3, 5 and 8, and also delete any colour
    # that occurs only once in the whole grid.
    BAD_MARK   = combine(combine(ofcolor(I, 5), ofcolor(I, 8)), ofcolor(I, 3))
    ONE_OCC   = ofcolor(I, branch(equality(colorcount(I, mostcolor(I)), 1),
                         mostcolor(I), 0)        # cells of a colour that appears once
    BAD       = combine(BAD_MARK, ONE_OCC)
    O         = fill(I, 0, BAD)                   # replace them by background
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL TRIM + BACKGROUND FILL
    T   = trim(I)                                 # tight non‑zero bounding box
    O   = canvas(0, shape(T))                    # empty canvas of that size
    O   = paint(O, asobject(T))                  # copy the trimmed pattern
    C   = mostcolor(T)                           # dominant colour inside the box
    O   = fill(O, C, ofcolor(O, 0))              # recolour every remaining 0
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # COLOUR FILTERING: delete the marker colours 3,5,8 and any colour that occurs only once
    MARKERS = combine(combine(ofcolor(I, 3), ofcolor(I, 5)), ofcolor(I, 8))
    OBJ     = objects(I, univalued=False, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)
    SINGLE  = mfilter(OBJ, lambda o: equality(size(o), 1))   # objects of size 1
    SINGLE_IDX = initset(0)
    SINGLE_IDX = mapply(lambda o: o, SINGLE)                # union of singleton cells
    BAD = combine(MARKERS, SINGLE_IDX)
    O = fill(I, 0, BAD)                                     # replace them by background
    return O
```

#### DSL

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL‑INTERIOR‑FILL
    #   – for every coloured object compute its bounding box,
    #   – fill the empty cells inside that box with the most frequent colour of the object,
    #   – keep the original coloured cells.
    OBJ   = objects(I, univalued=False, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)
    O     = canvas(0, shape(I))
    # paint the original objects
    O = apply(lambda o: paint(O, o), OBJ)
    # fill each interior with the object's dominant colour
    O = apply(lambda o:
                let = mostcolor(subgrid(box(o), I));
                fill(O, let, delta(box(o))),
            OBJ)
    return O
```

```python
    O   = cellwise(I, M2, fallback=0)                        # original colours dominate
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # Object‑extraction – locate the vertical line of colour 5,
    # split the grid into three column zones (left, middle, right)
    # and recolour each zone with a constant (0, 3 and 6 respectively).
    five      = ofcolor(I, 5)                                 # indices of colour‑5 cells
    mincol    = valmin(apply(lambda p: p[1], five), lambda x: x)
    maxcol    = valmax(apply(lambda p: p[1], five), lambda x: x)

    all_idx   = asindices(I)
    left      = mfilter(all_idx, lambda p: p[1] < mincol)
    middle    = mfilter(all_idx, lambda p: mincol < p[1] < maxcol)
    right     = mfilter(all_idx, lambda p: p[1] > maxcol)

    base      = canvas(0, shape(I))                           # start with a blank canvas (all 0)
    O1        = recolor(3, middle)                           # colour 3 in the middle zone
    O2        = recolor(6, right)                            # colour 6 in the right zone
    O         = paint(paint(base, left), O1)                 # add the two coloured zones
    O         = paint(O, O2)                                 # final picture
    return O
```

```python
    O            = paint(cleared, moved_obj)                 # paint them at the new positions
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ---------- global‑style solution ----------
    # 1) locate the full rows/columns of 5s as horizontal/vertical lines
    h5      = apply(lambda p: p[0],
                    mfilter(ofcolor(I, 5),
                            lambda p: hline({p})))          # rows that belong to a horizontal line of 5
    v5      = apply(lambda p: p[1],
                    mfilter(ofcolor(I, 5),
                            lambda p: vline({p})))          # columns that belong to a vertical line of 5
    # 2) compute the limits of each block using the separators
    rcuts   = sort(combine({0}, combine(h5, {shape(I)[0]})))   # 0, each separator row, height
    ccuts   = sort(combine({0}, combine(v5, {shape(I)[1]})))   # 0, each separator col, width
    # 3) fill every block with its own most common colour
    O = I
    for rs in interval(0, size(rcuts) - 1, 1):
        for cs in interval(0, size(ccuts) - 1, 1):
            r0 = list(rcuts)[rs]
            r1 = list(rcuts)[rs+1]
            c0 = list(ccuts)[cs]
            c1 = list(ccuts)[cs+1]
            blk = crop(I, (r0, c0), (r1 - r0 - 1, c1 - c0 - 1))
            col = mostcolor(blk)
            idx = mfilter(asindices(I),
                         lambda p: p[0] > r0 and p[0] < r1 and p[1] > c0 and p[1] < c1)
            O   = paint(O, recolor(col, idx))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ---------- colour‑filtering solution ----------
    # swap 5 ↔ 0 so that separator lines become background (0),
    # then replace every non‑background cell by the dominant colour of its 3×3 neighbourhood.
    S       = switch(I, 5, 0)                       # separators become 0
    G       = smear(S, 3)                           # custom primitive that spreads colour in 3×3 neighbourhood
    O       = switch(G, 0, 5)                       # put the separators back
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ---------- geometric solution ----------
    # rotate the grid so that the separators become vertical,
    # apply a vertical majority‑colour fill, then rotate back.
    R       = rot90(I)                               # turn rows of 5 into columns
    cols5   = ofcolor(R, 5)
    vsep    = sizefilter(objs5, shape(R)[0])          # full vertical separators after rotation
    idx     = asindices(R)
    # fill each vertical strip (between separators) with its most common colour
    Otemp   = R
    for c0,c1 in zip([0]+sorted(apply(lambda p: p[1], vsep))+[shape(R)[1]],
                     sorted(apply(lambda p: p[1], vsep))+[shape(R)[1]]):
        strip = mfilter(idx, lambda p: p[1] > c0 and p[1] < c1)
        col   = mostcolor(subgrid(strip, R))
        Otemp = paint(Otemp, recolor(col, strip))
    O       = rot270(Otemp)                         # undo rotation
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---------- relational / structural solution ----------
    # each block is defined by the nearest separator cell in the four cardinal directions.
    five    = ofcolor(I, 5)
    # for every non‑5 cell locate its surrounding separator rectangle
    O       = I
    for p in mfilter(asindices(I), lambda q: index(I, q) != 5):
        up    = gravitate({p}, five)                # direction to nearest 5 upwards
        down  = gravitate({p}, five)                # direction downwards (same call works)
        left  = gravitate({p}, five)
        right = gravitate({p}, five)
        # compute the bounding rectangle limits (row_min,row_max,col_min,col_max)
        r0    = p[0] + up[0]
        r1    = p[0] + down[0]
        c0    = p[1] + left[1]
        c1    = p[1] + right[1]
        rect  = mfilter(asindices(I),
                        lambda q: q[0] > r0 and q[0] < r1 and q[1] > c0 and q[1] < c1)
        col   = mostcolor(subgrid(rect, I))
        O     = paint(O, recolor(col, {p}))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ---------- object‑extraction ----------
    # 1) turn the separator colour (5) into background (0) so that the
    #    remaining coloured regions become separate objects.
    S = switch(I, 5, 0)

    # 2) extract every object (connected component) from the modified grid.
    objs = objects(S, False, False, False)

    # 3) keep only the objects that do NOT contain the separator colour.
    #    (they are the original blocks)
    blocks = colorfilter(objs, 5)

    # 4) for each block compute its dominant colour in the ORIGINAL grid
    #    and recolour the whole block with that colour.
    recoloured = apply(
        lambda o: recolor(mostcolor(subgrid(o, I)), o),
        blocks
    )

    # 5) paint all recoloured blocks on top of the original input.
    O = paint(I, combine(recoloured))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ---------- colour‑filtering (local majority) ----------
    # 1) indices of all cells that are NOT a separator (5).
    non5 = mfilter(asindices(I), lambda p: index(I, p) != 5)

    # 2) for every such cell take its 3×3 neighbourhood (clipped at the border)
    #    and recolour the centre with the most frequent colour inside that neighbourhood
    #    (the neighbourhood still contains the original 5‑cells, but they are ignored
    #     because they are never the most frequent colour inside a block).
    patches = apply(
        lambda p: recolor(
            mostcolor(
                crop(
                    I,
                    (max(p[0] - 1, 0), max(p[1] - 1, 0)),
                    (min(3, shape(I)[0] - max(p[0] - 1, 0)),
                    (min(3, shape(I)[1] - max(p[1] - 1, 0)))
                )
            ),
            {p}
        ),
        non5
    )

    # 3) paint the obtained recolourings over the input.
    O = paint(I, combine(patches))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ---------- geometric (rotation‑based) ----------
    # 1) rotate so that rows of 5 become columns.
    R = rot90(I)

    # 2) positions of the separator columns (still colour 5 after rotation).
    v5   = apply(lambda p: p[1], ofcolor(R, 5))
    cuts = sort(combine({0}, combine(v5, {shape(R)[1]})))   # 0, each separator, width

    # 3) all indices of the rotated grid.
    idx = asindices(R)

    # 4) fill each vertical strip (between two consecutive separators)
    #    with the most common colour that appears in that strip in the ORIGINAL grid.
    strips = apply(
        lambda pair: recolor(
            mostcolor(subgrid(
                mfilter(idx, lambda q: q[1] > pair[0] and q[1] < pair[1]),
                R)),
            mfilter(idx, lambda q: q[1] > pair[0] and q[1] < pair[1])),
        zip([0] + list(rest(cuts)), list(rest(cuts)) + [shape(R)[1]])
    )
    Orot = paint(R, combine(strips))

    # 5) rotate back to the original orientation.
    O = rot270(Orot)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ---------- relational / structural ----------
    # 1) the set of all separator cells (colour 5).
    sep = ofcolor(I, 5)

    # 2) for each non‑separator cell locate the nearest separator in the
    #    four cardinal directions (up, down, left, right).
    non5 = mfilter(asindices(I), lambda p: index(I, p) != 5)

    # 3) build a patch consisting of all cells that share the same enclosing
    #    rectangle defined by those four nearest separators.
    #    The rectangle is described by the four limits:
    #    row_min = p[0] + gravitate({p}, sep)   (up direction)
    #    row_max = p[0] + gravitate({p}, sep)   (down direction)
    #    col_min = p[1] + gravitate({p}, sep)   (left direction)
    #    col_max = p[1] + gravitate({p}, sep)   (right direction)
    #    Because gravitate always returns the shortest vector that makes the source
    #    adjacent to the destination, the same call works for both opposite
    #    directions (the sign of the returned vector tells the direction).
    rects = apply(
        lambda p: recolor(
            mostcolor(
                subgrid(
                    mfilter(asindices(I),
                             lambda q: q[0] > p[0] + gravitate({p}, sep)[0] and
                                      q[0] < p[0] + gravitate({p}, sep)[0] and
                                      q[1] > p[1] + gravitate({p}, sep)[1] and
                                      q[1] < p[1] + gravitate({p}, sep)[1]),
                    I)),
            {p}),
        non5
    )
    O = paint(I, combine(rects))
    return O
```

#### DSL

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---------- global (periodicity‑based) ----------
    # 1) rows and columns that are completely filled with the separator colour (5).
    full_rows = apply(lambda p: p[0],
                     mfilter(ofcolor(I, 5), lambda p: hline({p})))
    full_cols = apply(lambda p: p[1],
                     mfilter(ofcolor(I, 5), lambda p: vline({p})))

    # 2) the vertical and horizontal periods of those separator lines.
    #    (the distance between two consecutive separators).
    vperiod = sub(minimum(full_cols), maximum(full_cols))   # not used directly, only to force a dependency
    hperiod = sub(minimum(full_rows), maximum(full_rows))

    # 3) cut positions (including the borders of the grid).
    rcuts = sort(combine({0}, combine(full_rows, {shape(I)[0]})))
    ccuts = sort(combine({0}, combine(full_cols, {shape(I)[1]})))

    # 4) generate every block by pairing consecutive cut lines.
    blocks = apply(
        lambda r: apply(
            lambda c: (list(rcuts)[r], list(ccuts)[c]),
            interval(0, size(ccuts) - 1, 1)
        ),
        interval(0, size(rcuts) - 1, 1)
    )

    # 5) for each block compute its dominant colour and recolour the whole block.
    recolours = apply(
        lambda corner: recolor(
            mostcolor(
                crop(
                    I,
                    corner,
                    (list(rcuts)[index(rcuts, corner[0]) + 1] - corner[0],
                     list(ccuts)[index(ccuts, corner[1]) + 1] - corner[1]))
            ),
            shoot(corner,
                  (list(rcuts)[index(rcuts, corner[0]) + 1] - corner[0],
                  (list(ccuts)[index(ccuts, corner[1]) + 1] - corner[1]))
        ),
        flatten(blocks)
    )
    O = paint(I, combine(recolours))
    return O
```

```python
    # ----------- global – periodic separators (full rows/cols of 5) -------------
    # objects that are whole separator lines
    sep_objs      = objects(I, True, False, False)
    full_rows    = mfilter(sep_objs, hline)
    full_cols    = mfilter(sep_objs, vline)

    # row / column indices of the separator lines
    rows = apply(lambda o: ulcorner(o)[0], full_rows)
    cols = apply(lambda o: ulcorner(o)[1], full_cols)

    # cut positions (including the outer borders)
    rcuts = order(combine({0}, combine(rows, {shape(I)[0]})), lambda a, b: a < b)
    ccuts = order(combine({0}, combine(cols, {shape(I)[1]})), lambda a, b: a < b)

    # recolour every rectangular block delimited by two consecutive cuts
    blocks = apply(
        lambda r: apply(
            lambda c: recolor(
                mostcolor(
                    crop(
                        I,
                        (list(rcuts)[r], list(ccuts)[c]),
                        (list(rcuts)[r + 1] - list(rcuts)[r],
                         list(ccuts)[c + 1] - list(ccuts)[c])

                )
            ),
            interval(0, size(ccuts) - 1, 1)
        ),
        interval(0, size(rcuts) - 1, 1)
    )
    O = paint(I, merge(flatten(blocks)))
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ------------------- object‑extraction (original idea) ----------------------
    # turn the separator colour (5) into background so that each coloured block
    # becomes a separate connected component.
    S = switch(I, 5, 0)

    # all connected components in the modified grid

    # keep only those components that do NOT contain the separator colour 5
```
