```python
    # recolour each block with its dominant non‑5 colour taken from the ORIGINAL grid
    recoloured = apply(
        lambda o: recolor(
            mostcolor(subgrid(o, I)),
            o
        ),
        blocks
    )
    O = paint(I, merge(recoloured))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ------------------- local colour majority (3×3 neighbourhood) -----------
    # work only on cells that are not separators (color 5)
    non5 = mfilter(asindices(I), lambda p: index(I, p) != 5)

    # for each such cell take its 3×3 neighbourhood (clipped at the border)
    # and recolour the centre with the most frequent colour inside the patch
    patches = apply(
        lambda p: recolor(
            mostcolor(
                crop(
                    I,
                    (max(p[0] - 1, 0), max(p[1] - 1, 0)),
                    (min(3, shape(I)[0] - max(p[0] - 1, 0)),
                     min(3, shape(I)[1] - max(p[1] - 1, 0)))
            ),
            {p}
        ),
        non5
    )
    O = paint(I, merge(patches))
    return O
```

```python
    sep_rows = mfilter(

            )) == shape(I)[1])
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # 1. collect every cell that is not background (color 0)
    nz = ofcolor(I, 1)                     # start with colour 1 …
    nz = combine(nz, ofcolor(I, 2))
    nz = combine(nz, ofcolor(I, 3))
    nz = combine(nz, ofcolor(I, 4))
    nz = combine(nz, ofcolor(I, 5))
    nz = combine(nz, ofcolor(I, 6))
    nz = combine(nz, ofcolor(I, 7))
    nz = combine(nz, ofcolor(I, 8))

    # 2. bounding box of the whole non‑zero object
    bb = backdrop(nz)                      # set of indices inside the box

    # 3. colour that appears most often inside the box (the “central” colour)
    central_colour = mostcolor(I, mostcommon(ofcolor(I, mostcolor(I, 0))))

    # 4. fill the entire row that contains the upper‑left corner of the box
    row_idx = uppermost(bb)
    row_patch = {(row_idx, c) for c in range(width(I))}   # all cells of that row
    O = fill(I, central_colour, row_patch)

    # 5. keep the original pattern unchanged
    O = paint(O, nz)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # 1. colours that actually occur (ignore 0)
    used = difference(palette(I), {0})

    # 2. produce a new background colour (choose 9 if available, else 0)
    new_bg = branch(contains(used, 9), 9, 0)

    # 3. replace every 0 with the new background colour
    O = switch(I, 0, new_bg)

    # 4. re‑paint the original coloured objects (so they stay on top)
    O = underpaint(O, ofcolor(I, mostcommon(used)))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # 1. all non‑zero cells as a set of coordinates
    nz = ofcolor(I, 1)
    nz = combine(nz, ofcolor(I, 2))
    nz = combine(nz, ofcolor(I, 3))
    nz = combine(nz, ofcolor(I, 4))
    nz = combine(nz, ofcolor(I, 5))
    nz = combine(nz, ofcolor(I, 6))
    nz = combine(nz, ofcolor(I, 7))
    nz = combine(nz, ofcolor(I, 8))

    # 2. for every cell generate four diagonal lines (↖︎, ↗︎, ↘︎, ↙︎)
    dirs = {(-1, -1), (-1, 1), (1, -1), (1, 1)}
    rays = initset(())
    for d in dirs:
        rays = combine(rays,
                       apply(lambda p: shoot(p, d), nz))

    # 3. colour each ray with the colour of its originating cell
    # (recolouring is done by taking the union of the original grid and the rays)
    O = I
    for d in dirs:
        O = paint(O,
                 apply(lambda p: recolor(index(I, p), shoot(p, d)),
                 )
    return O


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # 1. centre of mass of the non‑zero pattern
    mass = centerofmass(ofcolor(I, mostcommon(palette(I) - {0})))

    # 2. reflect every coloured cell across that centre (180° rotation around the centre)
    reflected = apply(
        lambda p: add(multiply(subtract(p, mass), (-1, -1)), mass),
        ofcolor(I, mostcommon(palette(I) - {0}))
    
    # 3. keep original colours, then paint the reflected copy on top
    O = I
    O = paint(O, reflected)
    return O
```

```python
    O = paint(O, nz)                                    # put the original objects back
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # Colour‑filtering – change the background to 9 if 9 already appears,
    # otherwise keep 0; keep the original coloured objects on top.
    used      = difference(palette(I), {0})               # colours that actually occur
    new_bg    = branch(contained(9, used), 9, 0)          # 9 if it is present, else 0
    O         = switch(I, 0, new_bg)                      # replace every 0 by the new bg
    O         = underpaint(O, ofcolor(I, mostcommon(used)))  # repaint original objects
    return O
```

```python
    # 5 → up‑right diagonal

    # 7 → down‑right diagonal

    # 8 → down‑left & down‑right diagonals

    O = paint(O, apply(lambda p: recolor(8, shoot(p, DOWN_RIGHT)), ofcolor(I, 8)))
```

```python
    nz6 = ofcolor(I, SIX)
    nz7 = ofcolor(I, SEVEN)
    nz8 = ofcolor(I, EIGHT)

    O = fill(I, col, whole_box)              # colour the whole box

    O = paint(O,
              apply(lambda p: recolor(index(I, p), {p}), nz1))
    O = paint(O,

    O = paint(O,
              apply(lambda p: recolor(index(I, p), {p}), nz8))
    return O
```

```python
                    ofcolor(I, SEVEN)))
    # 8 → down‑left & down‑right
    DL = add(DOWN, LEFT)
    O = paint(O,
              combine(
                apply(lambda p: recolor(EIGHT, shoot(p, DL)),
                      ofcolor(I, EIGHT)),
                apply(lambda p: recolor(EIGHT, shoot(p, DR)),
                      ofcolor(I, EIGHT))))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL – rotate the whole pattern of the most common colour
    # by 180° about its centre of mass and overlay it.
    target = ofcolor(I, mostcommon(palette(I) - {0}))
    com    = centerofmass(target)                       # centre of mass
    # reflect each point through the centre (180° rotation)
    refl   = apply(
                lambda p: add(multiply(subtract(p, com), (-1, -1)), com),
                target)
    # colour the reflected cells with their original colours
    reflobj = apply(lambda p: recolor(index(I, p), {p}), refl)
    O = paint(I, reflobj)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5 – RELATIONAL Map every coloured cell to its counter‑diagonal
    #                counterpart using explicit arithmetic on coordinates,
    #                then paint the mirrored points.

    h   = decrement(height(I))               # h‑1
    w   = decrement(width(I))                # w‑1
    # for each colour, compute the mirrored positions and repaint them
    O = I
    for c in (ONE, TWO, THREE, FOUR, FIVE, SIX, SEVEN, EIGHT):
        src   = ofcolor(I, c)                # original cells of colour c
        dst   = apply(lambda p: (subtract((w, h), (p[1], p[0]))), src)
        O = paint(O, recolor(c, dst))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑EXTRACTION – extend each coloured object from its centre to the
    #   far corner of the grid with a straight line.
    h   = decrement(height(I))               # last row index
    w   = decrement(width(I))                # last column index
    # for every non‑zero colour c
    O = I
    for c in (ONE, TWO, THREE, FOUR, FIVE, SIX, SEVEN, EIGHT):
        src   = ofcolor(I, c)                 # cells of colour c
        ctr   = apply(center, src)            # centre of each object (as a set)
        # shoot a line from the centre to the opposite corner
        line  = apply(lambda p: shoot(p, (w - p[1], h - p[0])), ctr)
        O = paint(O, recolor(c, line))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑EXTRACTION – for every non‑zero colour, fill its whole row
    #   with that colour (keeping the original column‑wise pattern) and
    #   also extend each cell towards the top‑left corner (diagonal copy).
    h = decrement(height(I))
    w = decrement(width(I))
    O = I
    for c in (ONE, TWO, THREE, FOUR, FIVE, SIX, SEVEN, EIGHT):
        src   = ofcolor(I, c)                                     # cells of colour c
        # horizontal fill: project every cell of src onto its entire row
        row_fill = apply(lambda p: {(p[0], j) for j in interval(0, width(I), 1)}, src)
        O = paint(O, recolor(c, row_fill))
        # diagonal copy towards the top‑left corner
        diag  = apply(lambda p: shift({p}, (-(p[1]), -(p[0])), ), src)
        O = paint(O, recolor(c, diag))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC – extend each coloured cell straight toward the nearest border.
    h     = decrement(height(I))
    w     = decrement(width(I))
    half_h = halve(h)
    half_w = halve(w)

    # direction towards the nearest horizontal border (up or down)
    dh = lambda p: branch(p[0] <= half_h,
                          -p[0],                     # up  : move -row
                          h - p[0])                  # down: move +row

    # direction towards the nearest vertical border (left or right)
    dw = lambda p: branch(p[1] <= half_w,
                          -p[1],                     # left  : move -col
                          w - p[1])                  # right : move +col

    # for a cell p, the target border cell is p shifted by (dh(p), dw(p))
    target = lambda p: shift({p}, (dh(p), dw(p)))

    seg   = merge(apply(target,
                       merge(apply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c),
                                  difference(palette(I), {0})))))
    O = paint(I, asobject(seg))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # DIAGONAL‑TO‑CORNER – for each coloured cell draw a line to the
    # nearest corner (Manhattan distance) and keep the original cells.
    h      = decrement(height(I))
    w      = decrement(width(I))
    corners = {(0,0), (0,w), (h,0), (h,w)}

    # nearest corner of a point p
    nearest = lambda p: argmin(corners,
                              lambda c: add(abs(p[0]-c[0]), abs(p[1]-c[1])))
    # segment from p to its nearest corner
    segment = lambda p: connect(p, nearest(p))

    cells   = merge(apply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c),
                    difference(palette(I), {0})))
    segs    = merge(apply(segment, cells))
    O       = paint(I, asobject(segs))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # GEOMETRIC‑SYMMETRY: mirror the existing 2‑pattern across the vertical and horizontal
    # axes of the 8‑border and combine the results.
    outer = ofcolor(I, 8)                                        # all 8‑pixels (the frame)
    bb = backdrop(outer)                                         # bounding box of the frame
    # extract the interior subgrid (crop)
    top_left = (uppermost(outer), leftmost(outer))
    size = (height(I) - 2 * uppermost(outer), width(I) - 2 * leftmost(outer))
    inner_grid = crop(I, top_left, size)
    # keep only the 2‑pixels of the interior

    # build symmetric copies

    h_sym = hmirror(inner_twos)                                   # horizontal mirror
    both_sym = vmirror(hmirror(inner_twos))                       # both axes
    all_twos = combine(combine(inner_twos, v_sym), combine(h_sym, both_sym))
    # write the symmetric 2‑pixels back into the original grid
    O = paint(I, all_twos)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # RELATIONAL‑STRUCTURE: for every pair of 2‑pixels inside the 8‑frame,
    # draw the straight Manhattan line connecting them.
    interior = delta(ofcolor(I, 8))
    twos = intersection(ofcolor(I, 2), interior)

        a, b = pair
        # direction from a to b
        dir_vec = gravitate(initset(a), initset(b))
        return shoot(a, dir_vec) | shoot(b, tuple(map(negate, dir_vec)))  # both ways

    lines = mapply(line_between, pairs)
    all_cells = combine(*lines)
    O = fill(I, 2, all_cells)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # GLOBAL‑TRANSFORMATION: compress the picture to its minimal bounding box,
    # replace the compressed interior with its vertical mirror, then upscale back.
    # (captures the idea that the interior should be vertically symmetric)
    frame = ofcolor(I, 8)
    bb = backdrop(frame)                                          # bounding box of the whole shape
    core = crop(I, (uppermost(bb), leftmost(bb)), shape(bb))      # minimal subgrid containing everything
    # compress to eliminate empty borders
    compact = compress(core)
    # make vertical symmetry
    sym = vmirror(compact)
    # restore original size
    O = upscale(sym, height(compact) // height(compact))           # dummy upscale to keep size unchanged
    # paste back into original grid (background stays 0)
    O = underpaint(I, asobject(O))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # RELATIONAL‑LINES: for every row that contains a 2 draw a horizontal line
    # spanning the full column range of the 2‑pixels; for every column that
    # contains a 2 draw a vertical line spanning the full row range.  The union
    # of those lines is the desired rectangle.
    interior = delta(ofcolor(I, 8))
    twos      = intersection(ofcolor(I, 2), interior)

    top    = uppermost(twos)
    bottom = lowermost(twos)
    left   = leftmost(twos)
    right  = rightmost(twos)

    rows = apply(lambda p: p[0], twos)   # set of row indices that contain a 2
    cols = apply(lambda p: p[1], twos)   # set of column indices that contain a 2

    vlines = apply(lambda c: connect((top, c), (bottom, c)), cols)
    hlines = apply(lambda r: connect((r, left), (r, right)), rows)

    rectangle = combine(combine(*vlines), combine(*hlines))
    O = fill(I, 2, rectangle)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # CANVAS‑MOVE: construct a filled rectangle of the correct size
    # and paste it at the upper‑left corner of the bounding box.
    interior = delta(ofcolor(I, 8))
    twos      = intersection(ofcolor(I, 2), interior)

    top    = uppermost(twos)
    bottom = lowermost(twos)
    left   = leftmost(twos)
    right  = rightmost(twos)

    h = add(subtract(bottom, top), ONE)   # height = bottom‑top+1
    w = add(subtract(right, left), ONE)   # width  = right‑left+1
    dims = astuple(h, w)

    rect_grid = canvas(2, dims)           # solid 2‑filled rectangle
    rect_obj  = asobject(rect_grid)       # turn grid into a patch
    O = move(I, rect_obj, (top, left))    # paste onto original grid
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # compute extreme rows/cols with `valmin` / `valmax` and build the rectangle
    interior = delta(ofcolor(I, 8))
    twos      = intersection(ofcolor(I, 2), interior)

    rows = apply(lambda p: p[0], twos)
    cols = apply(lambda p: p[1], twos)

    top    = valmin(rows,   lambda x: x)
    bottom = valmax(rows,   lambda x: x)
    left   = valmin(cols,   lambda x: x)
    right  = valmax(cols,   lambda x: x)

    left_side   = connect((top,    left),  (bottom, left))
    right_side  = connect((top,    right), (bottom, right))
    top_side    = connect((top,    left),  (top,    right))
    bottom_side = connect((bottom, left),  (bottom, right))

    outline = combine(combine(left_side, right_side),
                     combine(top_side, bottom_side))
    rect = backdrop(outline)
    O = fill(I, 2, rect)
    return O
```

```python
    left_side   = connect((top, left),   (bottom, left))
    right_side  = connect((top, right),  (bottom, right))
    top_side    = connect((top, left),   (top, right))
    bottom_side = connect((bottom, left),(bottom, right))

    outline = combine(combine(left_side, right_side),
                     combine(top_side, bottom_side))
    rect    = backdrop(outline)
    O = fill(I, 2, rect)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # Global‑crop / paste route: extract the bounding box, fill it, and paste back
    eight_box = backdrop(ofcolor(I, 8))                  # bounding rectangle of the 8‑border
    ul = ulcorner(eight_box)                            # upper‑left corner of the box
    lr = lrcorner(eight_box)                            # lower‑right corner

    h = add(1, subtract(lr[0], ul[0]))                  # height of the box
    w = add(1, subtract(lr[1], ul[1]))                  # width of the box

    sub   = crop(I, ul, (h, w))                         # subgrid that contains the whole shape
    interior_sub = difference(backdrop(ofcolor(sub, 8)), ofcolor(sub, 8))
    filled_sub  = underfill(sub, 2, interior_sub)       # fill interior inside the subgrid

    # turn the filled subgrid back into an object and paint it onto the original grid
    obj = asobject(filled_sub)
    O   = paint(I, obj)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # 2️⃣  Flood‑fill complement: start from any background cell on the grid border,
    #     grow a zero‑region outward (the exterior), then take the complement
    #     of that region inside the whole grid and colour it 2.
    border_zero = connect((0, 0), (0, width(I) - 1))      # all top‑row cells
    border_zero = combine(border_zero,
                          connect((height(I) - 1, 0), (height(I) - 1, width(I) - 1)))  # bottom row
    border_zero = combine(border_zero,
                          connect((0, 0), (height(I) - 1, 0)))                      # left column
    border_zero = combine(border_zero,
                          connect((0, width(I) - 1), (height(I) - 1, width(I) - 1))) # right column
    exterior   = ofcolor(I, 0)                           # all zero cells
    exterior   = intersection(exterior, border_zero)    # keep only those touching the border
    exterior   = underfill(I, 0, exterior)               # flood‑fill the exterior zero region
    interior   = difference(ofcolor(I, 0), exterior)     # zeros that are not exterior
    O = underfill(I, 2, interior)                        # paint interior with 2
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # 5️⃣  Symmetry‑fill: copy the upper‑left quadrant of the interior (found by
    #     intersecting the interior delta with the top‑left half of the bbox),
    #     mirror it horizontally and vertically to obtain the full interior,
    #     recolor it to 2 and paint it back.
    bbox          = backdrop(ofcolor(I, 8))
    interior_delta = difference(backdrop(ofcolor(I, 8)), ofcolor(I, 8))
    ul            = ulcorner(bbox)
    lr            = lrcorner(bbox)
    half_h        = halve(add(1, subtract(lr[0], ul[0])))   # half height of bbox
    half_w        = halve(add(1, subtract(lr[1], ul[1])))   # half width of bbox

    top_left_quad = crop(I, ul, (half_h, half_w))          # top‑left part of whole grid
    quad_mask     = intersection(ofcolor(top_left_quad, 0), interior_delta)  # keep interior cells

    horiz_mirror  = hmirror(quad_mask)
    vert_mirror   = vmirror(quad_mask)
    full_quad     = combine(combine(quad_mask, horiz_mirror),
                           combine(vert_mirror, hmirror(vert_mirror)))

    recolored     = recolor(2, full_quad)
    O = paint(I, recolored)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # work inside the tight 8‑border: crop, replace 0→2, paint back
    box        = backdrop(ofcolor(I, 8))
    ul         = ulcorner(box)
    lr         = lrcorner(box)
    h          = add(1, subtract(lr[0], ul[0]))
    w          = add(1, subtract(lr[1], ul[1]))
    subgrid    = crop(I, ul, (h, w))
    filled     = replace(subgrid, 0, 2)
    obj        = asobject(filled)
    O = paint(I, obj)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ---------- Global‑tiling + selective background ----------
    # 1. Build a 2×2 tile of the whole input.
    T = hconcat(vconcat(I, I), vconcat(I, I))

    # 2. Detect every row that contains at least one non‑zero cell.
    #    Objects of all non‑zero colours are collected, then their row
    #    indices are projected with leftmost / rightmost.
    nonzero_objs = colorfilter(fgpartition(T), 0)               # keep coloured objects
    rows_with_data = {uppermost(o) for o in nonzero_objs}       # set of row indices

    # 3. Construct a background canvas of colour 8.
    BG = canvas(8, shape(T))

    # 4. For rows that are *empty* (i.e. not in rows_with_data) replace the
    #    whole row on the canvas with a periodic 8‑0 pattern.
    pattern = lambda r: replace(row(BG, r), 8, {c for c in range(width(T)) if (r + c) % 2 == 0})
    BG = combine(
            BG,
            frozenset({(r, c) for r in range(height(T)) for c in range(width(T))
                       if r not in rows_with_data and (r + c) % 2 == 0})
          )
    # 5. Paint the original coloured cells on top of the background.
    O = underpaint(BG, combine(nonzero_objs, nonzero_objs))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # 1. 2×2 tiling by up‑scaling
    T = hupscale(vupscale(I, 2), 2)                     # shape (2h,2w)

    # 2. rows of the original that contain a non‑zero colour
    nz_orig   = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 0)
    rows_data = { uppermost(o) for o in nz_orig }      # {r}
    h, w      = shape(I)

    # 3. rows (and their duplicate) that are empty in the original
    dup_rows = {2*r for r in range(h) if r not in rows_data} \
             | {2*r+1 for r in range(h) if r not in rows_data}

    # 4. checker‑board mask on those rows (even parity → 8)
    mask = frozenset({(r, c) for r in dup_rows
                          for c in range(2*w) if (r + c) % 2 == 0})

    # 5. background canvas (all 0) and fill the mask with 8
    BG = canvas(0, (2*h, 2*w))
    BG = fill(BG, 8, mask)

    # 6. paint the original coloured cells (from the tiled grid) on top
    nz_tile = colorfilter(fgpartition(T), 0)
    O = underpaint(BG, combine(nz_tile, nz_tile))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # 1. build the 2×2 tiled grid by mirroring
    H = hmirror(I)                                      # horizontal mirror (h,2w)
    V = vmirror(I)                                      # vertical   mirror (2h,w)
    top    = hconcat(I, H)                              # (h,2w)
    bottom = hconcat(V, vmirror(H))                     # (h,2w)
    T = vconcat(top, bottom)                            # (2h,2w)

    # 2. rows that hold non‑zero colours in the original
    nz_orig   = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 0)
    rows_data = { uppermost(o) for o in nz_orig }
    h, w      = shape(I)

    # 3. duplicated empty rows
    dup_rows = {2*r for r in range(h) if r not in rows_data} \
             | {2*r+1 for r in range(h) if r not in rows_data}

    # 4. checker mask on those rows
    mask = frozenset({(r, c) for r in dup_rows
                          for c in range(2*w) if (r + c) % 2 == 0})

    # 5. background canvas and fill
    BG = canvas(0, (2*h, 2*w))
    BG = fill(BG, 8, mask)

    # 6. overlay the coloured cells
    nz_tile = colorfilter(fgpartition(T), 0)
    O = underpaint(BG, combine(nz_tile, nz_tile))
    return O
```

```python
    objs = colorfilter(fgpartition(I), 0)
```

```python
    BG   = canvas(0, (2*h, 2*w))
    BG   = fill(BG, 8, mask_rows)

    O    = underpaint(BG, tiled)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # Relational gravitation:
    #  - take the left‑most coloured cell of each colour,
    #  - move every other cell of that colour one step towards it,
    #  - repeat by applying the move until no change.
    colors = palette(I) - {ZERO}
    O = I
    for c in colors:
        pts = ofcolor(I, c)
        src = frozenset({min(pts, key=lambda p: p[0] + p[1])})
        O = move(O, pts - src, gravitate(src, pts - src))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Periodic replication:
    #  - find the smallest vertical period among all coloured objects,
    #  - replicate each object vertically according to that period,
    #  - overlay all copies on the original grid.
    objs = fgpartition(I, True, False, True)
    period = valmin({vperiod(o) for o in objs}, lambda x: x)
    O = I
    O = apply(lambda g: foldl(lambda acc, o: 
        foldl(lambda a, k: paint(a, move(o, (k*period, 0))), 
              range(0, shape(I)[0]//period), acc), objs), O)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # OBJECT‑EXTRACTION + ORDERED VERTICAL FILL
    # 1. Extract every coloured object (single‑colour blobs).
    # 2. Sort them by the row of their topmost cell (uppermost).
    # 3. For each object, draw a vertical line from the top of the grid
    #    down to the object's own topmost cell, but only on cells that are still background.
    #    This propagates the colour upward, and when several colours share the same column
    #    the uppermost colour occupies the upper part, the next colour the next part, etc.
    objs        = fgpartition(I, True, False, True)
    sorted_objs = order(objs, lambda o: uppermost(o))                 # top‑to‑bottom
    O = canvas(ZERO, shape(I))                                        # blank canvas
    O = foldl(lambda acc, o:
                underfill(acc,                               # fill only background cells
                         color(o),
                         connect((0, leftmost(o)),            # line from row 0
                                 (uppermost(o), leftmost(o)))),  # to its topmost row
                sorted_objs,
                O)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # GLOBAL TRANSFORMATION – HORIZONTAL MIRROR OVERLAY
    #  Create a horizontal mirror of the whole grid and keep, for each cell,
    #  the brighter (larger numeric) colour among the original and its mirror.
    V = hmirror(I)
    O = apply(lambda pair:
                tuple(tuple(max(pair[0][i][j], pair[1][i][j])
                           for j in range(len(pair[0][0])))
                      for i in range(len(pair[0]))),
              (I, V))
    return O
```

```python
    centre_col = shape(I)[1] // 2
    O = canvas(ZERO, shape(I))
    O = apply(lambda o:
                let_shift = (0, subtract(leftmost(o), centre_col)),   # horizontal offset only
                paint(O, shift(o, let_shift)),

    return O
```

#### DSL

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL – VERTICAL REPLICATION BY COMMON PERIOD
    #  Find the smallest vertical period that repeats among all objects,
    #  copy each object upward and downward by that period as many times as fits,
    #  and overlay all copies on the original grid.
    objs   = fgpartition(I, True, False, True)
    period = valmin({vperiod(o) for o in objs}, lambda x: x)          # smallest vertical period
    rows   = shape(I)[0]
    O = I
    O = apply(lambda o:
                foldl(lambda acc, k:
                        paint(acc, move(o, (k * period, 0))),
                      range(-rows // period, rows // period + 1),   # all integer multiples fitting the grid
                      acc),
              objs,
              O)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ------------------- Object extraction -------------------
    # 1. Extract every non‑zero object.
    # 2. For each object compute a vertical line that starts at the
    #    top of the grid (row 0) and ends at the object's lowest cell,
    #    staying in the object's leftmost column.
    # 3. Paint each line with the object's colour.
    objs = fgpartition(I)                                   # set of objects
    O    = canvas(ZERO, shape(I))                           # blank canvas
    # create a line for each object and paint it on the canvas
    O = apply(
            lambda o: underfill(
                         O,
                         color(o),
                         connect(
                             (ZERO, leftmost(o)),
                             (lowermost(o), leftmost(o)))),
            objs)
    # the previous step returns a tuple of canvases; union them by overlaying
    # (the last canvas in the tuple already contains all previous paints)
    O = last(apply(lambda x: x, O))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # build the answer on a blank canvas; for each object draw a vertical
    # segment that starts just below the highest row that already contains a
    # coloured cell (in the original input) and ends at the object’s lowermost row.
    objs = fgpartition(I)
    O = canvas(ZERO, shape(I))

    # rows that already contain a colour in the original input
    occupied_rows = {uppermost(o) for o in objs}

    def start_row(o):
        # highest occupied row that is strictly above o; if none, use -1 (so we start at 0)
        higher = {r for r in occupied_rows if r < lowermost(o)}
        return add(valmax(higher, lambda x: x), ONE) if higher else ZERO

    O = apply(
            lambda o: underfill(
                        O,
                        color(o),
                        connect((start_row(o), leftmost(o)),
                                (lowermost(o), leftmost(o)))),
            objs)
    return last(O)
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ---- relational – sequential upward fill (objects from top‑most to bottom‑most) ----
    objs = fgpartition(I)
    # process objects in increasing lowermost row (top‑most first)
    seq = order(objs, lambda o: lowermost(o))
    # turn each object into a “fill‑up” patch and compose the fills sequentially
    fills = apply(
                lambda o: lambda G: underfill(G,
                                            color(o),
                                            connect((ZERO, leftmost(o)),
                                                    (lowermost(o), leftmost(o)))),
                seq)
    # compose all fill functions (right‑most applied last) and run on the input
    O = rapply(fills, I)               # rapply returns the list of intermediate grids
    return last(O)                     # the last grid is the final result
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ---- colour‑filtering – replace every colour by the colour that appears most
    #                       frequently in its column (vertical majority)
    cols = interval(0, width(I), 1)
    def col_major(c):
        col_cells = ofcolor(I, c)
        # pick the colour that occurs most often in this column
        return mostcommon(apply(lambda p: index(I, p), col_cells))
    fill = apply(
                lambda c: recolor(col_major(c),
                                 ofcolor(I, c)),
            cols)
    O = underfill(I, ZERO, combine(fill))   # build the new grid from the recoloured patches
    return O
```

```python
    # -------- 1️⃣  Vertical propagation (generic colour) ----------
    # colour 1 cells that have a non‑zero / non‑4 colour below them
    ones   = ofcolor(I, 1)
    fours  = ofcolor(I, 4)

    prop_cols = mfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c not in {0, 1, 4})

    # for a given colour c, cells of colour 1 that see c somewhere below
    def conv(c):
        below = lambda cell: {(r, cell[1]) for r in range(cell[0] + 1, len(I))}
        return {cell for cell in ones
                if intersection(below(cell), ofcolor(I, c))

    changed    = merge(apply(conv, prop_cols))

    O = paint(I, merge(recoloured))                     # paint the new colours
    O = paint(O, recolor(1, ones - changed))           # keep the remaining 1‑cells
    O = paint(O, recolor(4, fours))                   # keep all 4‑cells
    return O
```

```python
        part   = recolor(tgt, ones)(part)
        return part

    O = hconcat(*(apply(swap, [p]) for p in parts))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # 1️⃣  Column‑wise colour swap (1 ↔ other colour) -----------------------
    ones   = ofcolor(I, 1)
    fours  = ofcolor(I, 4)

    # colours that may take part in a swap (everything except 0,1,4)
    others = mfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c not in {0, 1, 4})

    # 1 → c  : a 1‑cell that sees a c‑cell below it, with no 4 in‑between
    def up_to_c(c):
        below = lambda cell: {(r, cell[1]) for r in range(cell[0] + 1, len(I))}
        return {cell for cell in ones
                if intersection(below(cell), ofcolor(I, c))
                and not intersection(below(cell), fours)}

    # c → 1  : a c‑cell that sees a 1‑cell above it, with no 4 in‑between
    def down_to_one(c):
        above = lambda cell: {(r, cell[1]) for r in range(0, cell[0])}
        cs    = ofcolor(I, c)
        return {cell for cell in cs
                if intersection(above(cell), ones)
                and not intersection(above(cell), fours)}

    # recolour every eligible 1‑cell and every eligible c‑cell
    recol_up   = apply(lambda c: recolor(c, up_to_c(c)),   others)
    recol_down = apply(lambda c: recolor(1, down_to_one(c)), others)

    O = paint(I, merge(recol_up))
    O = paint(O, merge(recol_down))
    O = paint(O, recolor(4, fours))                # keep the 4‑cells
    return O
```

```python
    # 2️⃣  Object copy (lowest coloured block → highest 1‑block) -----------
    objs = fgpartition(I)                         # every coloured object

    # source = lowest object (by its lowermost cell)
    src  = argmax(objs, lowermost)

    # destination = highest object (by its uppermost cell)
    dst  = argmin(objs, uppermost)

    # bounding boxes of source and destination
    src_box = backdrop(src)
    dst_box = backdrop(dst)

    # shift vector that moves the source box onto the destination box
    shift_vec = (min(r for r, _ in dst_box) - min(r for r, _ in src_box),
                min(c for _, c in dst_box) - min(c for _, c in src_box))

    moved = shift(src, shift_vec)                 # move the source object

    O = paint(I, moved)                            # overlay it
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # 3️⃣  Global down‑scale / up‑scale colour propagation -----------------
    # downscale the whole picture (factor 2), recolour every 1 with the most
    # common non‑0/1/4 colour that appears in the down‑scaled version,
    # then upscale back to the original size.
    down  = downscale(I, 2)                        # becomes smaller
    # colour that will replace the 1‑cells (if any)
    repl  = mostcommon({c for c in palette(down) if c not in {0, 1, 4}})
    # recolour the 1‑cells in the down‑scaled grid
    changed = recolor(repl, ofcolor(down, 1))
    # bring the modified small grid back to the original dimensions
    up    = upscale(changed, 2)
    # paint the up‑scaled modification over the original picture
    O = paint(I, up)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # 4️⃣  Quadrant mirroring (lower‑right ↔ upper‑left) ------------------
    h, w = shape(I)

    # lower‑right quadrant (the part that contains the propagating colours)
    br = subgrid({(r, c) for r in range(h//2, h) for c in range(w//2, w)}, I)

    # mirror it vertically (top‑bottom flip) and then horizontally
    mir = hmirror(vmirlor(br))                      # vmirror → vertical, then hmirror → horizontal

    # move the mirrored quadrant to the upper‑left corner
    tl_coords = {(r, c) for r in range(h//2) for c in range(w//2)}
    shift_vec = (min(r for r, _ in tl_coords) - min(r for r, _ in backdrop(mir)),
                min(c for _, c in tl_coords) - min(c for _, c in backdrop(mir)))
    moved = shift(mir, shift_vec)

    # replace the original 1‑cells with the mirrored content
    O = paint(I, recolor(1, moved))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # 5️⃣  Horizontal strip‑wise colour swap (rows of 4 are separators) ---
    h, w = shape(I)

    # rows that are completely filled with colour 4 act as separators
    sep_rows = {r for r in range(h) if all(index(I, (r, c)) == 4 for c in range(w))}

    # number of strips = separators + 1   (hsplit splits into equal parts)
    n_strips = len(sep_rows) + 1
    strips   = hsplit(I, n_strips)                  # list of sub‑grids

    # per‑strip swap: 1 ↔ the unique non‑0/1/4 colour that appears in the strip
    def swap(part):
        other = mfilter(palette(part), lambda c: c not in {0, 1, 4})
        tgt   = next(iter(other), None)
        if tgt is None:
            return part
        return paint(part, recolor(tgt, ofcolor(part, 1)))   # 1 → tgt
               .paint(part, recolor(1, ofcolor(part, tgt))) # tgt → 1

    O = hconcat(*(apply(swap, [p]) for p in strips))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # 1️⃣  Column‑wise swap 1 ↔ any other colour (≠ 0,4) when they see each other
    ones   = ofcolor(I, 1)
    fours  = ofcolor(I, 4)

    # colours that may take part in a swap (everything except 0,1,4)
    others = sfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c not in {0, 1, 4})

    # a 1‑cell that sees a colour c below it, with no 4 in‑between
    up_to_c = lambda c: {
        cell for cell in ones
        if intersection(
                {(r, cell[1]) for r in range(cell[0] + 1, len(I))},
                ofcolor(I, c)
           )
        and not intersection(
                {(r, cell[1]) for r in range(cell[0] + 1, len(I))},
                fours)
    }

    # a colour‑c cell that sees a 1 above it, with no 4 in‑between
    down_to_one = lambda c: {
        cell for cell in ofcolor(I, c)
        if intersection(
                {(r, cell[1]) for r in range(0, cell[0])},
                ones
           )
        and not intersection(
                {(r, cell[1]) for r in range(0, cell[0])},
                fours)
    }

    recol_up   = apply(lambda c: recolor(c, up_to_c(c)),   others)   # 1 → c
    recol_down = apply(lambda c: recolor(1, down_to_one(c)), others) # c → 1

    O = paint(I, merge(recol_up))
    O = paint(O, merge(recol_down))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # 1️⃣  Horizontal‑strip split (rows of colour 4 are separators) → column‑wise swap
    h, w = shape(I)
    sep_rows = {r for r in range(h) if all(index(I, (r, c)) == 4 for c in range(w))}
    strips   = hsplit(I, len(sep_rows) + 1)

    def proc(seg):
        ones   = ofcolor(seg, 1)
        fours  = ofcolor(seg, 4)                     # empty – separators are outside the strip
        others = sfilter(palette(seg), lambda c: c not in {0, 1, 4})

        up_to_c = lambda c: {
            cell for cell in ones
            if intersection(
                    {(r, cell[1]) for r in range(cell[0] + 1, len(seg))},
                    ofcolor(seg, c))
               and not intersection(
                    {(r, cell[1]) for r in range(cell[0] + 1, len(seg))},
                    fours)
        }

        down_to_one = lambda c: {
            cell for cell in ofcolor(seg, c)
            if intersection(
                    {(r, cell[1]) for r in range(0, cell[0])},
                    ones)
               and not intersection(
                    {(r, cell[1]) for r in range(0, cell[0])},

        O = paint(O,   merge(recol_down))
```

```python
                {(r, cell[1]) for r in range(cell[0] + 1, len(I))},
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # Horizontal‑strip processing: each block delimited by full rows of colour 4
    # – if a block contains a colour ≠ 0,1,4, swap that colour with 1 inside the block
    h, w = shape(I)
    sep_rows = {r for r in range(h) if all(index(I, (r, c)) == 4 for c in range(w))}
    strips   = hsplit(I, len(sep_rows) + 1)

    def swap_in_strip(seg):
        other   = sfilter(palette(seg), lambda c: c not in {0, 1, 4})
        main    = branch(size(other) == 0,
                         None,
                         argmax(other, lambda c: colorcount(seg, c)))
        # no other colour → nothing to do
        O = seg
        O = branch(main is None,
                  O,
                  paint(O,
                        merge(apply(lambda c: recolor(c, ofcolor(seg, 1)), {main})),
                        merge(apply(lambda c: recolor(1, ofcolor(seg, c)), {main})))
        return O

    # re‑assemble the strips
    processed = apply(swap_in_strip, strips)          # tuple of processed strips
    # fold the tuple with vconcat (pairwise reduction)
    def fold_vconcat(t):
        return branch(size(t) == 1,
                     first(t),
                     vconcat(first(t), fold_vconcat(tail(t))))
    return fold_vconcat(processed)
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # Object‑wise copy: move the lowest non‑0/1/4 object onto the 1‑region and swap colours
    objs      = fgpartition(I)
    coloured  = sfilter(objs, lambda o: color(o) not in {0, 1, 4})
    src_obj   = argmax(coloured, lowermost)                     # source object
    src_box   = backdrop(src_obj)
    tgt_cells = ofcolor(I, 1)

    shift_vec = (min(r for r, _ in tgt_cells) - min(r for r, _ in src_box),
                 min(c for _, c in tgt_cells) - min(c for _, c in src_box))
    moved_src = shift(src_obj, shift_vec)

    O = paint(I, moved_src)                                      # source colour onto 1‑region
    O = paint(O, recolor(1, ofcolor(I, color(src_obj))))         # bring the 1’s onto former source cells
    return O
```

```python
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Column‑wise visibility using “gravitate” → swap 1 with the colour it sees
    ones   = ofcolor(I, 1)
    fours  = ofcolor(I, 4)
    others = sfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c not in {0, 1, 4})

    sees_up = lambda c: {
        cell for cell in ones
        if intersection(
                {(r, cell[1]) for r in range(cell[0] + 1, len(I))},
                ofcolor(I, c))
           and not intersection(
                {(r, cell[1]) for r in range(cell[0] + 1, len(I))},
                fours)
    }

    sees_down = lambda c: {
        cell for cell in ofcolor(I, c)
        if intersection(
                {(r, cell[1]) for r in range(0, cell[0])},
                ones)
           and not intersection(
                {(r, cell[1]) for r in range(0, cell[0])},
                fours)
    }

    recol_up   = apply(lambda c: recolor(c, sees_up(c)),   others)
    recol_down = apply(lambda c: recolor(1, sees_down(c)), others)

    O = paint(I, merge(recol_up))
    O = paint(O, merge(recol_down))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # per‑horizontal‑strip replacement
    h, w = shape(I)

    # rows that are completely filled with colour 4
    full4 = {r for r in range(h) if all(index(I, (r, c)) == 4 for c in range(w))}

    # split the grid into the strips that lie between those rows
    strips = apply(lambda _: _, hsplits(I, len(full4) + 1))

    # replace 1 with the most frequent other colour inside each strip
    def repl(seg):
        other = sfilter(palette(seg), lambda c: c not in {0, 1, 4})
        main  = branch(size(other) == 0,
                       None,
                       argmax(other, lambda c: colorcount(seg, c)))
        return branch(main is None,
                     seg,
                     paint(seg, recolor(1, ofcolor(seg, main))))
    proc = apply(repl, strips)

    # re‑assemble the strips (vertical concatenation)
    def fold(t):
        return branch(size(t) == 1,
                     first(t),
                     vconcat(first(t), fold(apply(tail, t))))
    return fold(proc)
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # PER‑HORIZONTAL‑STRIP rule – 4‑rows act as separators.
    # 1) erase the separator rows (turn them into 0) so the whole grid becomes one strip,
    # 2) apply the global rule inside each connected component that is bounded by 0‑cells,
    # 3) restore the original 4‑rows.
    no4          = paint(I, recolor(4, ofcolor(I, 4)))          # turn all 4‑rows into 0
    comps        = objects(no4, False, False, True)            # connected components (no 4)
    repl_one     = lambda comp:                                 \
        branch(contains(comp, (lambda p: index(I, p) == 1)),
               let(other = sfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c not in {0,1,4}),
                   main   = branch(size(other)==0,
                                 None,
                                 argmax(other, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))),
                   branch(main is None,
                         comp,
                         paint(comp, recolor(1, ofcolor(I, main))))),
               comp)
    new_comps    = apply(repl_one, comps)
    merged       = merge(new_comps)
    O            = paint(merged, recolor(0, ofcolor(I, 4)))     # put back the 4‑rows
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # QUADRANT‑MIRROR rule – mirror the lower‑right quadrant onto the upper‑left
    # and replace every 1 by the colour that appears at the same position in the
    # mirrored patch.
    h, w   = shape(I)

    # lower‑right quadrant as a set of indices
    br_idx = {(r, c) for r in interval(h//2, h) for c in interval(w//2, w)}
    quad   = subgrid(br_idx, I)                 # smallest sub‑grid that contains the quadrant

    # mirror vertically then horizontally (counter‑diagonal symmetry)
    mir    = hmirror(vmirror(quad))

    # move the mirrored quadrant to the upper‑left corner (now a patch of indices)
    moved  = shift(asindices(mir), (-h//2, -w//2))

    # replace 1’s by the colour that sits at the same coordinate in the moved patch
    O = paint(I, recolor(1, moved))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # COLUMN‑VISIBILITY rule – a 1 looks upward in its column; the first cell that is
    # a colour different from 0,1,4 and not blocked by a 4 becomes its new colour.
    ones   = ofcolor(I, 1)
    fours  = ofcolor(I, 4)
    others = sfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c not in {0, 1, 4})

    # cells that see a colour c above them (no 4 in between)
    sees_up = lambda c: {
        (r, col) for (r, col) in ones
        if intersection({(rr, col) for rr in interval(r+1, height(I))},
                       ofcolor(I, c))
           and not intersection({(rr, col) for rr in interval(r+1, height(I))},
                               fours)
    }

    # recolour those 1‑cells with the colour they see
    recol   = apply(lambda c: recolor(c, sees_up(c)), others)

    O = paint(I, merge(recol))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # PER‑STRIP: rows that consist entirely of 4 act as separators.
    # 1) turn those separator rows into 0 (so the whole picture is one strip);
    # 2) recolour all 1‑cells inside each connected component with the same
    #    dominant colour;
    # 3) restore the original 4‑rows.
    other   = sfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c not in {0, 1, 4})
    main    = argmax(other, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))

    # 1) erase the 4‑rows
    no4     = paint(I, recolor(0, ofcolor(I, 4)))

    # 2) recolour each component separately
    comps   = objects(no4, False, False, True)                     # connected components (0‑background)
    recol   = lambda comp: \
        branch(contains(comp, lambda p: index(I, p) == 1),
              paint(comp, recolor(main, ofcolor(I, 1))),
              comp)
    newc    = apply(recol, comps)
    merged  = merge(newc)

    # 3) put the 4‑rows back
    O       = paint(merged, recolor(4, ofcolor(I, 4)))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # PALETTE‑MAP: build a recolour‑patch for every colour in the palette,
    # keep all colours unchanged except colour 1,
    # which is remapped to the dominant non‑{0,1,4} colour.
    other   = sfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c not in {0, 1, 4})
    main    = argmax(other, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))

    # patches for all colours
    patches = apply(lambda c: branch(c == 1,
                                   recolor(main, ofcolor(I, 1)),
                                   recolor(c, ofcolor(I, c))),
                    palette(I))

    O = paint(I, merge(patches))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑EXTRACTION: recolour each connected component made of 1‑cells
    # to the dominant non‑{0,1,4} colour and paint them back.
    other = sfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c not in {0, 1, 4})
    main  = argmax(other, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))

    # binary mask that keeps only the 1‑cells
    mask = paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), recolor(1, ofcolor(I, 1)))

    # connected components of the mask (background = 0)
    comps = objects(mask, False, False, True)

    recol = lambda comp: recolor(main, comp)          # turn the whole component into “main”
    recoloured = apply(recol, comps)                  # recolour every component
    merged = merge(recoloured)                        # union of all recoloured patches

    O = paint(I, merged)                               # paint them over the original grid
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # PER‑STRIP (relational): rows consisting entirely of 4 are separators.
    # 1) erase those rows (turn 4 → 0);
    # 2) recolour every component that contains a 1 with the dominant colour;
    # 3) restore the original 4‑rows.
    other = sfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c not in {0, 1, 4})
    main  = argmax(other, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))

    # 1) erase the separator rows
    no4 = paint(I, recolor(0, ofcolor(I, 4)))

    # 2) recolour each component that touches a 1‑cell
    comps = objects(no4, False, False, True)
    recol = lambda comp: branch(
        greater(size(intersection(comp, ofcolor(I, 1))),  # component contains a 1?
        recolor(main, comp),                           # recolour it
        comp                                            # otherwise keep unchanged
    )
    newc   = apply(recol, comps)
    merged = merge(newc)

    # 3) restore the separator rows
    O = paint(merged, recolor(4, ofcolor(I, 4)))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Compute the centre of the whole picture, move each object one step
    # in the direction of that centre and redraw it.
    ctr = center(asobject(I))                              # centre of the whole grid
    objs = objects(I, True, False, True)                   # all coloured objects
    def move_toward(o):
        obj_ctr = center(o)
        dir_vec = gravitate({obj_ctr}, {ctr})              # direction toward global centre
        return shift(o, dir_vec)                           # one‑step shift
    moved = apply(move_toward, objs)
    O = I
    O = apply(lambda m: paint(O, m), moved)                # re‑paint the shifted objects
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # OBJECT‑LEVEL – compute the exact corner coordinates of the overall
    # occupied region, crop with those coordinates, then upscale.
    objs   = objects(I, True, False, True)
    all_ix = combine(apply(toindices, objs))
    start  = ulcorner(backdrop(all_ix))                 # upper‑left corner of the box
    end    = lrcorner(backdrop(all_ix))                 # lower‑right corner of the box
    dims   = add(subtract(end, start), (ONE, ONE))      # width × height of the box
    O      = crop(I, start, dims)                      # crop to the exact rectangle
    O      = upscale(O, 2)                             # double its size
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # OBJECT‑LEVEL – scale each individual object 2×, then repaint them
    # onto a freshly created canvas of the correct final size.
    objs          = objects(I, True, False, True)
    # size of the final canvas = size of (compress → upscale) of the whole picture
    canvas_size   = shape(upscale(compress(I), 2))
    O0            = canvas(0, canvas_size)

    # function that turns one object into a 2× enlarged patch and paints it
    def paint_scaled(obj):
        # extract the object's minimal subgrid
        sub       = subgrid(backdrop(toindices(obj)), I)
        # enlarge it
        big       = upscale(sub, 2)
        # locate where the original object's ul‑corner would map after scaling
        orig_ul   = ulcorner(toindices(obj))
        new_ul    = multiply(orig_ul, (TWO, TWO))
        # shift the enlarged patch to the correct place and paint it
        shifted   = shift(toobject(big, O0), new_ul)   # convert to object then shift
        return paint(O0, shifted)

    O = apply(paint_scaled, objs)                     # paint all scaled objects
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # OBJECT‑LEVEL – scale each colour separately and paint the enlarged
    # objects onto a fresh canvas that has the size of the globally enlarged
    # picture (compress → upscale gives the required canvas size).
    colours      = palette(I)                                 # all colours that appear
    canvas_sz    = shape(upscale(compress(I), 2))              # size of the final picture
    empty_canvas = canvas(0, canvas_sz)                        # blank canvas

    def scale_and_paint(col):
        pts   = ofcolor(I, col)                                # cells of this colour
        sub   = subgrid(backdrop(pts), I)                      # its minimal sub‑grid
        big   = upscale(sub, 2)                                 # enlarge 2×
        ul    = ulcorner(pts)                                   # original upper‑left corner
        new_ul = multiply(ul, (TWO, TWO))                      # where the enlarged block must be placed
        shifted = shift(toobject(big, empty_canvas), new_ul)    # move it to the right spot
        return paint(empty_canvas, shifted)                    # paint over the blank canvas

    # apply the above to every colour and keep the last (fully painted) canvas
    O = apply(scale_and_paint, colours)
    # `apply` returns a container of canvases; the last element is the fully painted one
    O = last(O)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # GLOBAL – remove the outer zero border, enlarge 2×,
    # then centre the enlarged pattern on the original canvas.
    trimmed = trim(I)                       # drop empty outer rows / cols
    big     = upscale(trimmed, 2)           # 2‑fold enlargement
    # compute the shift needed to centre the block:
    dh      = divide(subtract(shape(big), shape(I)), TWO)   # (height diff // 2, width diff // 2)
    shifted = shift(asobject(big), negate(dh))              # move by the negative offset
    base    = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = paint(base, shifted)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # COLOR‑FILTER – keep only non‑zero colours,
    # replace each pixel by a 2×2 checker‑board of that colour and zero,
    # then paint the resulting pattern on a clean canvas.
    nonzero = apply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), palette(I))
    checker = apply(
        lambda patch:
            cellwise(
                paint(canvas(0, shape(I)),
                      recolor(c, patch)),      # recolor the patch with its colour
                canvas(0, shape(I)),         # background of zeros
                ZERO),
        nonzero)
    base = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = paint(base, merge(checker))
    return O
```

```python
    O       = paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), merge(patches))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # RELATIONAL – enlarge the whole pattern and reposition it so that its centre of
    # mass coincides with the centre of mass of the original pattern.
    whole   = merge(objects(I, F, F, T))
    sub     = subgrid(backdrop(whole), I)
    big     = upscale(sub, TWO)
    c_orig  = centerofmass(toindices(whole))          # centre of original pattern
    c_big   = centerofmass(toindices(asobject(big))) # centre of enlarged pattern
    delta   = subtract(c_orig, c_big)                 # vector needed for alignment
    shifted = shift(asobject(big), delta)
    O       = paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), shifted)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # COLOR‑BY‑COLOR replication.
    #   – For each colour present, upscale the exact shape of that colour.
    #   – Paste a copy of the enlarged shape at every original pixel of that colour.
    #   – Keep the original pixels (they are reproduced by the copies).
    cols   = palette(I)
    # enlarged copies for each colour
    ups_per_col = apply(
        lambda c:
            apply(
                lambda p: shift(
                    asobject(upscale(subgrid(backdrop(ofcolor(I, c)), I), TWO)),
                p),
                ofcolor(I, c)),
        cols)
    ups    = merge(apply(lambda s: merge(s), ups_per_col))        # all up‑scaled copies
    olds   = merge(apply(lambda c: asobject(ofcolor(I, c)), cols))  # original pixels
    O      = paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), combine(ups, olds))
    return O
```

```python
    O       = fill(I, 3, area)                                   # colour the union with 3
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑LEVEL extraction – collect all 2‑ and 4‑objects, recolour them, and paint back.
    all_objs   = fgpartition(I)                       # every coloured object
    objs2      = colorfilter(all_objs, 2)              # only the 2‑objects
    objs4      = colorfilter(all_objs, 4)              # only the 4‑objects
    # turn each object into a set of its cell indices
    inds2      = apply(toindices, objs2)                # patches of the 2‑objects
    inds4      = apply(toindices, objs4)                # patches of the 4‑objects
    # unite all those patches
    patch2_4   = combine(merge(inds2), merge(inds4))    # union of the two groups
    # recolour the union to 3 and paint over the original grid
    O          = fill(I, 3, patch2_4)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # SET‑DIFFERENCE – keep only cells whose colour is neither 0 nor 8,
    # and turn those cells into 3.
    all_cells   = asindices(I)                     # every coordinate in the grid
    zero_cells  = ofcolor(I, 0)
    eight_cells = ofcolor(I, 8)
    background  = combine(zero_cells, eight_cells)   # cells that must stay unchanged
    target      = difference(all_cells, background) # everything else (2 and 4)
    O           = fill(I, 3, target)
    return O
```

```python
    # RELATIONAL – cells that are simultaneously on the border of a 2‑region
    # and a 4‑region are exactly the original 2‑ and 4‑cells, because the
    # two colours never touch each other.  Recolour that intersecting set.
    p2      = ofcolor(I, 2)

    b4      = delta(p4)          # cells adjacent to any 4‑cell
    common  = intersection(b2, b4)   # cells touching both colours
    # The only common cells are the original 2‑ and 4‑cells themselves.
    O       = fill(I, 3, common)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
```

```python
    # repaint the interior of that box with colour 3, and finally merge

    masks     = apply(lambda b: ofcolor(b, 2) | ofcolor(b, 4), boxes)
    filled    = apply(lambda m: fill(m, 3, m), masks)  # paint 3 where 2/4 were inside the box
    O = cover(I, merge(filled))                       # paste all filled boxes back
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC – mirror the whole 2/4‑region across the vertical line of 8s,
    # colour the original region 3 and the mirrored copy 8.
    p2   = ofcolor(I, 2)
    p4   = ofcolor(I, 4)
    union = combine(p2, p4)                # original 2/4 pattern
    # locate the vertical 8‑line (the first column that contains any 8)
    eight_cols = apply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, 8) & {c}, range(width(I)))
    axis = argmin(eight_cols, lambda s: size(s))   # left‑most 8‑column
    # mirror the union with respect to that column
    mirrored = hmirror(union)              # simple horizontal mirror of the patch
    # shift the mirrored patch so that its left edge aligns with the axis
    shift_vec = (0, axis - leftmost(mirrored))
    mirrored = shift(mirrored, shift_vec)

    O = fill(I, 3, union)                 # original 2/4 → 3
    O = fill(O, 8, mirrored)            # mirrored copy → 8
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL – compute the horizontal period of the 2/4‑pattern,
    # repeat that pattern to fill the whole row, recolouring 2/4 to 3
    # and the newly created cells to 8.
    p2   = ofcolor(I, 2)
    p4   = ofcolor(I, 4)
    union = combine(p2, p4)
    period = hperiod(union)                       # smallest horizontal repetition
    # build a row‑wide mask by repeating the union pattern
    repeated = repeat(union, width(I) // period + 1)
    rowmask = normalize(repeated)                # bring to origin
    O = fill(I, 3, union)                        # original cells → 3
    new_cells = difference(rowmask, union)        # cells added by repetition
    O = fill(O, 8, new_cells)                    # fill them with 8
    return O
```

```python
    O = fill(O, 4, shift(p8, (0, 1)))                        # right part of 8 → 4
    O = fill(O, 3, shift(p2, (0, 1)))                        # right part of 2 → 3
```

```python
        lambda o: fill(canvas(0, shape(I)),
                      4 if color(o) == 8 else 8,
                      o),

        lambda o: fill(canvas(0, shape(I)),
                      4 if color(o) == 8 else 3,
                      shift(toindices(o), (0, 1))),
        objs28)

    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = cover(O, merge(left))
    O = cover(O, merge(right))
    return O
```

#### DSL

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # 1️⃣ Global‑scale / periodicity extraction.
    #    Detect the fundamental vertical and horizontal period of the whole picture,
    #    then crop to the first period block.
    #    (objects → first → vperiod / hperiod → subgrid)
    whole      = objects(I, True, False, True)               # all non‑background objects
    first_obj  = first(whole)                               # any object (the picture is 1‑object)
    ph        = vperiod(first_obj)                          # height of a repeating tile
    pw        = hperiod(first_obj)                          # width  of a repeating tile
    O = subgrid(initset(astuple(0,0)), I)                    # start at origin
    # take only the top‑left tile of size (ph × pw)
    O = crop(I, (0, 0), (ph, pw))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # 5️⃣ Relational reasoning – intersect the objects of the two most common colours.
    #    (objects → colorfilter → combine → intersect → paint)
    objs        = objects(I, True, False, True)              # all coloured objects
    col1        = mostcolor(I)                               # most common colour
    # second most common colour: remove the first colour and recompute
    rest_grid   = replace(I, col1, -1)                        # temporary sentinel
    col2        = mostcolor(rest_grid)                       # next most common
    obj1        = first(colorfilter(objs, col1))              # first object of colour 1
    obj2        = first(colorfilter(objs, col2))              # first object of colour 2
    inter       = intersection(obj1, obj2)                   # overlapping cells
    blank       = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = paint(blank, inter)                                 # render the intersection
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # Global periodicity: find smallest tile that repeats both vertically and horizontally,
    # then upscale it back to original size.
    pic   = compress(I)                                   # remove outer empty margin
    obj   = first(objects(pic, True, False, True))         # the single coloured object
    ph    = vperiod(obj)                                   # vertical period of the pattern
    pw    = hperiod(obj)                                   # horizontal period of the pattern
    tile  = crop(pic, (0, 0), (ph, pw))                    # extract the basic tile
    O     = hupscale(vupscale(tile, ph // height(tile)), pw // width(tile))
    return O
```

```python
    blank    = canvas(0, shape(big_box))
    O        = fill(blank, col, difference(ofcolor(big_box, col), mask))  # remove the border colour
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Relational reasoning: intersect the two largest objects (by cell count)
    # and render the overlap.
    objs      = objects(I, True, False, True)
    sorted_o  = order(objs, lambda o: -size(o))            # descending by size
    first_obj = first(sorted_o)
    second_obj= first(tail(sorted_o))                      # second largest
    inter     = intersection(first_obj, second_obj)
    blank     = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O         = paint(blank, inter)
    return O
```

```python
    # Keep only the colours that appear at most twice
    nonzero   = difference(palette(I), initset(0))               # all non‑background colours

    blank     = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O         = fill(blank, 1, raremask)                        # paint them with colour 1
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # Crop a 3×3 window centred on the centre of mass of all non‑zero cells
    nonzero   = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    all_cells = mapply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), nonzero)         # patch of every non‑zero cell
    cen       = centerofmass(all_cells)                           # centre of mass (row, col)
    start     = subtract(cen, (1, 1))                           # top‑left corner of 3×3 window
    O         = crop(I, start, (3, 3))                           # extract the window
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Union of the two most frequent colours (excluding background)
    colours   = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    most1     = argmax(colours, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    rest      = difference(colours, initset(most1))
    most2     = argmax(rest, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    mask1     = ofcolor(I, most1)
    mask2     = ofcolor(I, most2)
    union     = combine(mask1, mask2)                # all cells of either colour
    blank     = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O         = fill(blank, most1, union)            # paint the union with the first colour
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL – outline the line that joins the centroids of the two most frequent colours,
    # using the second‑most‑frequent colour for the outline
    cols      = difference(palette(I), initset(0))                   # non‑background colours
    most1     = argmax(cols, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))              # most common colour
    rest      = difference(cols, initset(most1))
    most2     = argmax(rest, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))             # second most common colour
    mask1     = ofcolor(I, most1)
    mask2     = ofcolor(I, most2)
    c1        = centerofmass(mask1)                                   # centroid of colour most1
    c2        = centerofmass(mask2)                                   # centroid of colour most2
    direction = sign(subtract(c2, c1))                                 # unit step towards c2
    line      = shoot(c1, direction)                                 # cells along the line c1→c2
    outline   = combine(mask1, combine(mask2, line))                 # union of both colours and the line
    blank     = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O         = fill(blank, most2, outline)                          # draw outline in colour most2
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # colour that occupies the biggest rectangular block
    C   = argmax(palette(I), lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    P   = ofcolor(I, C)                     # patch of that colour
    B   = backdrop(P)                       # its bounding box (as a set of indices)

    # locate the four sides of the box
    top    = valmin(B, lambda p: p[0])
    left   = valmin(B, lambda p: p[1])
    bottom = valmax(B, lambda p: p[0])
    right  = valmax(B, lambda p: p[1])

    # crop to the exact rectangle
    G = crop(I, (top, left), (add(subtract(bottom, top), ONE), (add(subtract(right, left), ONE)))

    # down‑scale the rectangle uniformly until it becomes 7×7
    sf_h = divide(height(G), 7)   # integer factor
    sf_w = divide(width(G), 7)
    O = downscale(G, sf_h)        # both factors are equal for all training pairs
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # colours that appear as a full horizontal line somewhere
    horiz = apply(lambda c: hline(ofcolor(I, c)), palette(I))
    # colours that appear as a full vertical line somewhere
    vert  = apply(lambda c: vline(ofcolor(I, c)), palette(I))

    # the colour that is both a horizontal and a vertical line (the “frame” colour)
    frame_col = first(intersection(horiz, vert))

    # replace every other colour by the frame colour, then compress the margins
    O = replace(I, frame_col, frame_col)          # identity – forces a new object
    O = replace(O, frame_col, frame_col)          # double‑apply to keep only that colour
    O = compress(O)                               # removes empty border rows / columns
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ── GLOBAL – biggest solid rectangle, down‑scaled to 7×7 ──
    # colour that occupies the largest rectangular block
    C   = argmax(palette(I), lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    P   = ofcolor(I, C)                     # all cells with that colour
    B   = backdrop(P)                       # its bounding box (set of indices)

    # rectangle borders
    top    = valmin(B, lambda p: p[0])
    left   = valmin(B, lambda p: p[1])
    bottom = valmax(B, lambda p: p[0])
    right  = valmax(B, lambda p: p[1])

    # crop exactly the rectangle
    G = crop(I, (top, left),
                (add(subtract(bottom, top), ONE),
                 add(subtract(right, left), ONE)))

    # uniform down‑scale to 7×7 (both dimensions are divisible by 7)
    sf = divide(height(G), 7)
    O  = downscale(G, sf)
    return O
```

```python
    O = compress(isolated)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL – locate every pair of equal‑coloured horizontal neighbours,
    #              recolour the pair with the background colour,
    #              and render the result on a 7×7 canvas.
    cols       = palette(I)
    pairsets   = apply(lambda c:
                      intersection(ofcolor(I, c),
                                   shift(ofcolor(I, c), LEFT)),
                      cols)                               # all left‑right equal‑colour pairs
    pair_union = merge(pairsets)                         # union of all such pairs
    bgcol      = argmax(palette(I), lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    pat_obj    = recolor(bgcol, pair_union)              # colour the whole pattern with bg colour
    O          = canvas(bgcol, (7, 7))
    O          = paint(O, pat_obj)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # 1️⃣  Global‑bounding‑box extraction:
    #    Crop the minimal rectangle that contains every cell whose colour is **not** 8
    all_idx   = asindices(I)
    eight_idx = ofcolor(I, 8)
    target    = difference(all_idx, eight_idx)                # cells ≠ 8
    box       = backdrop(target)                              # bounding box of those cells
    tl        = ulcorner(box)                                 # top‑left corner of the box
    h         = add(subtract(lowermost(box), uppermost(box)), ONE)   # height  =  low‑top + 1
    w         = add(subtract(rightmost(box), leftmost(box)), ONE)     # width   =  right‑left + 1
    O         = crop(I, tl, (h, w))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # 4️⃣  Object‑centric extraction:
    #    Partition the grid into colour‑connected objects, keep the **largest** non‑8 object,
    #    and return its tight bounding box.
    objs      = fgpartition(I, False, False, True)               # objects, background ignored
    non8_objs = mfilter(objs, lambda o: not equal(color(o), 8))   # discard the 8‑background object
    biggest   = argmax(non8_objs, lambda o: size(o))             # largest remaining object
    bbox      = backdrop(biggest)
    tl        = ulcorner(bbox)
    h         = add(subtract(lowermost(bbox), uppermost(bbox)), ONE)
    w         = add(subtract(rightmost(bbox), leftmost(bbox)), ONE)
    O         = crop(I, tl, (h, w))
    return O
```

```python
    vparts    = vsplit(I, 3)                     # three vertical slices
    hparts    = hsplit(I, 3)                     # three horizontal slices
    middle_v  = list(vparts)[1]                  # the middle vertical slice
    middle_h  = list(hparts)[1]                  # the middle horizontal slice
    # intersect the two slices (they overlap exactly on the centre rectangle)
    O = cover(I, intersection(ofcolor(middle_v, -1), ofcolor(middle_h, -1)))   # dummy intersect trick
    return O
```

```python
    # Find the smallest repeating block using the horizontal and vertical periods,

    O        = list(hparts)[0]                               # top‑left tile
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ── Relational adjacency extraction ──
    # Find a cell of colour 2 that has a colour‑3 neighbour on its right;
    # treat that cell as the top‑left corner of the desired tile and crop the
    # region whose size equals the known tile dimensions (derived from the
    # distance to the next identical pattern using gravitate).
    twos        = ofcolor(I, 2)
    threes      = ofcolor(I, 3)
    # candidate corners: 2‑cells whose right neighbour is a 3
    cand        = mfilter(twos,
                          lambda p: contained(p + RIGHT, threes))
    anchor      = first(cand)                 # any one of the candidates
    # the tile height and width are the smallest vertical/horizontal periods
    # of the whole grid (as in dsl1) – we reuse that computation.
    idx         = asindices(I)
    obj         = asobject(idx, I)
    hp          = hperiod(obj)
    vp          = vperiod(obj)
    O           = crop(I, anchor, (vp, hp))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ── relational: move the largest non‑background object to the origin and cut it ──
    bg      = mostcolor(I)                                             # background colour
    all_objs= objects(I, False, False, False)                          # every colour object
    nb_objs = mfilter(all_objs,
                      lambda o: not equality(color(o), bg))             # discard background
    big_obj = valmax(nb_objs, lambda o: size(o))                       # biggest object
    origin  = astuple(negate(ulcorner(big_obj)[0]), negate(ulcorner(big_obj)[1]))
    shifted = shift(big_obj, origin)                                   # place its top‑left at (0,0)
    h       = add(subtract(lowermost(shifted), uppermost(shifted)), ONE)
    w       = add(subtract(rightmost(shifted), leftmost(shifted)), ONE)
    O       = crop(I, ulcorner(big_obj), astuple(h, w))               # crop the original area
    return O
```

```python
    rects    = mfilter(objs, lambda o: equality(o, box(o)))         # solid rectangles only
    rect     = first(rects)                                         # the unique rectangle
    bb       = backdrop(rect)                                       # its bounding box
    tl       = ulcorner(bb)                                         # top‑left corner of the box
    h        = add(subtract(lowermost(bb), uppermost(bb)), ONE)     # height
    w        = add(subtract(rightmost(bb), leftmost(bb)), ONE)       # width
    tile     = crop(I, tl, astuple(h, w))                            # extract the rectangle
    borderc  = mostcolor(border(tile))                               # colour that dominates the border
    O        = recolor(borderc, tile)                               # fill any interior background with that colour
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ── relational: use the centre of mass of all non‑background cells as the anchor,
    # take a window whose size equals the discovered vertical/horizontal periods,
    # then replace the background inside that window with the colour that appears most often
    bg      = mostcolor(I)                                          # background colour
    nb      = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, bg))               # all non‑background cells
    centre  = centerofmass(nb)                                      # centre of mass of the pattern
    hp      = hperiod(nb)                                           # horizontal period
    vp      = vperiod(nb)                                           # vertical period
    # top‑left corner of the window = centre – (vp‑1, hp‑1) // 2
    offset  = astuple(divide(subtract(centre[0], subtract(vp, ONE)), TWO),
                       divide(subtract(centre[1], subtract(hp, ONE)), TWO))
    tl      = add(ulcorner(nb), offset)                             # shift from an actual cell
    tile    = crop(I, tl, astuple(vp, hp))                          # extract the tile
    fillcol = mostcolor(tile)                                       # most common non‑bg colour in the tile
    O       = replace(tile, bg, fillcol)                            # recolour background cells
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # Global transformation:
    #   1. Remove the outer zero border.
    #   2. Turn the remaining background (0) into colour 1.
    #   3. Swap colours 2 and 3 (colour 4 stays unchanged).
    O = switch(replace(compress(I), 0, 1), 2, 3)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # Object‑extraction & re‑painting:
    #   1. Crop the zero border.
    #   2. Replace the interior background (0) with colour 1.
    #   3. Extract all non‑zero objects and paint them back unchanged.
    G   = compress(I)
    BG  = replace(G, 0, 1)                     # background → 1
    OBJ = fgpartition(G)                      # set of all coloured objects
    ALL = merge(OBJ)                           # unite the objects into one patch
    O   = paint(BG, ALL)                       # paint the objects onto the new background
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Relational / structural:
    #   1. Crop the zero border.
    #   2. Shift every coloured object leftwards until its
    #      leftmost cell touches column 0 (normalisation).
    #   3. Fill the emptied background with colour 1.
    G       = compress(I)
    OBJSET  = fgpartition(G)                                 # objects of colours ≠0
    SHIFTED = apply(lambda o: shift(o, (-leftmost(o), 0)), OBJSET)
    ALL     = merge(SHIFTED)                                 # unite shifted objects
    BG      = replace(G, 0, 1)                               # interior background → 1
    O       = paint(BG, ALL)                                 # paint normalised objects onto BG
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # Object‑extraction & recolouring:
    #   1. Crop the border.
    #   2. Replace interior 0 → 1.
    #   3. Extract all non‑zero objects.
    #   4. Recolour colour 2 objects to 3 and colour 3 objects to 2,
    #      keep colour 4 unchanged.
    #   5. Paint the recoloured objects back onto the new background.
    G   = compress(I)
    BG  = replace(G, 0, 1)
    OBJ = fgpartition(G)                                 # all coloured objects
    SET2 = colorfilter(OBJ, 2)                          # objects of colour 2
    SET3 = colorfilter(OBJ, 3)                          # objects of colour 3
    SET4 = colorfilter(OBJ, 4)                          # objects of colour 4
    SW2 = recolor(3, SET2)                               # 2 → 3
    SW3 = recolor(2, SET3)                               # 3 → 2
    ALL = merge({SW2, SW3, SET4})
    O   = paint(BG, ALL)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # Colour‑filtering via explicit patches:
    #   1. Crop the border.
    #   2. Convert interior 0 → 1.
    #   3. Build separate patches for colours 2, 3, 4,
    #      swap the colours of the first two patches,

    G   = compress(I)
    BG  = replace(G, 0, 1)
    P2  = ofcolor(G, 2)                                 # all cells of colour 2
    P3  = ofcolor(G, 3)                                 # all cells of colour 3
    P4  = ofcolor(G, 4)                                 # all cells of colour 4
    SW2 = recolor(3, P2)                                 # 2 → 3
    SW3 = recolor(2, P3)                                 # 3 → 2
    ALL = merge({SW2, SW3, P4})
    O   = paint(BG, ALL)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # Geometric reasoning via mirroring:
    #   1. Mirror the whole picture horizontally.
    #   2. Crop the zero border.
    #   3. Convert remaining background (0) to colour 1.

    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Sequential colour replacement with a temporary placeholder:
    #   1. Crop the border.
    #   2. Temporarily replace colour 2 with 9,

    T1  = replace(G, 2, 9)                                # 2 → temp 9
    T2  = replace(T1, 3, 2)                               # 3 → 2
    T3  = replace(T2, 9, 3)                               # temp 9 → 3
    O   = replace(T3, 0, 1)                               # background 0 → 1
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # Object‑extraction route:
    #   1. Crop the border.
    #   2. Replace interior 0 → 1 (background).
    #   3. Extract all coloured objects.
    #   4. Recolour objects of colour 2 → 3 and colour 3 → 2,
    #      keep colour 4 as‑is.
    #   5. Paint the recoloured objects on the new background.
    G   = compress(I)
    BG  = replace(G, 0, 1)
    OBJ = fgpartition(G)                     # all non‑zero objects
    SET2 = colorfilter(OBJ, 2)                # objects coloured 2
    SET3 = colorfilter(OBJ, 3)                # objects coloured 3
    SET4 = colorfilter(OBJ, 4)                # objects coloured 4
    SW2 = apply(lambda o: recolor(3, o), SET2)   # 2 → 3
    SW3 = apply(lambda o: recolor(2, o), SET3)   # 3 → 2
    ALL = combine(combine(SW2, SW3), SET4)     # union of all recoloured objects
    O   = paint(BG, ALL)
    return O
```
