```python
def dsl3(I):
    # Colour‑filtering with explicit patches:
    #   1. Crop the border.
    #   2. Convert interior 0 → 1.
    #   3. Build patches for colours 2, 3, 4,
    #      turn them into coloured objects,
    #      swap the colours of the first two patches,
    #      then paint them over the background.
    G   = compress(I)
    BG  = replace(G, 0, 1)
    P2  = ofcolor(G, 2)                     # indices of colour 2
    P3  = ofcolor(G, 3)                     # indices of colour 3
    P4  = ofcolor(G, 4)                     # indices of colour 4
    O2  = toobject(P2, G)                    # (value, index) pairs for colour 2
    O3  = toobject(P3, G)                    # (value, index) pairs for colour 3
    O4  = toobject(P4, G)                    # (value, index) pairs for colour 4
    SW2 = recolor(3, O2)                     # 2 → 3
    SW3 = recolor(2, O3)                     # 3 → 2
    ALL = merge({SW2, SW3, O4})
    O   = paint(BG, ALL)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # Geometric reasoning via rotation:
    #   1. Rotate the picture clockwise.
    #   2. Crop the zero border.
    #   3. Convert remaining background (0) to colour 1.
    #   4. Swap colours 2 and 3.
    #   5. Rotate back to original orientation.
    R   = rot90(I)                # clockwise rotation
    C   = compress(R)              # remove outer zeros
    B   = replace(C, 0, 1)        # background → 1
    S   = switch(B, 2, 3)         # colour swap
    O   = rot270(S)               # rotate back (90° counter‑clockwise)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # Object‑level recolouring: extract every coloured object,
    # recolour background (0) to 1, swap 2 ↔ 3 and repaint.
    G   = compress(I)                                            # remove outer zeros
    BG  = replace(G, 0, 1)                                      # provisional background
    OBJ = fgpartition(G)                                         # all non‑zero objects
    SET2 = colorfilter(OBJ, 2)                                   # objects of colour 2
    SET3 = colorfilter(OBJ, 3)                                   # objects of colour 3
    SET4 = colorfilter(OBJ, 4)                                   # objects of colour 4
    SW2 = apply(lambda o: recolor(3, o), SET2)                  # 2 → 3
    SW3 = apply(lambda o: recolor(2, o), SET3)                  # 3 → 2
    ALL = combine(combine(SW2, SW3), SET4)                       # union of recoloured objects
    O   = paint(BG, ALL)                                          # paint them on the new background
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Relational reasoning: identify the largest zero object (the background),
    # recolour it to 1, swap 2 ↔ 3 on the remaining objects and paint all.
    G   = compress(I)                                            # crop outer zeros
    OBJ = fgpartition(G)                                         # all objects (including 0‑background)
    BGOBJ = valmax(OBJ, lambda o: size(o))                       # largest object → background
    BG1   = recolor(1, BGOBJ)                                    # background 0 → 1
    SET2 = colorfilter(OBJ, 2)                                   # colour‑2 objects
    SET3 = colorfilter(OBJ, 3)                                   # colour‑3 objects
    SET4 = colorfilter(OBJ, 4)                                   # colour‑4 objects
    SW2 = apply(lambda o: recolor(3, o), SET2)                  # 2 → 3
    SW3 = apply(lambda o: recolor(2, o), SET3)                  # 3 → 2
    ALL = combine(combine(combine({BG1}, SW2), SW3), SET4)      # union of all recoloured patches
    O   = paint(G, ALL)                                          # paint them onto the cropped grid
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ----------  Object‑level – work with each colour as a separate object ----------
    # 1) Crop the outer zero border (compress) so that the background becomes an object too
    # 2) Split the grid into objects (fgpartition)
    # 3) Re‑colour the background object (colour 0) to 1
    # 4) Swap colours 2 and 3 on their respective objects
    # 5) Paint everything back on the background we just created
    C   = compress(I)                                 # outer‑zero crop
    OBJ = fgpartition(C)                              # all colour‑connected components
    BG  = colorfilter(OBJ, 0)                         # the background object (colour 0)
    BG1 = apply(lambda o: recolor(1, o), BG)         # 0 → 1
    SET2 = colorfilter(OBJ, 2)                       # objects of colour 2
    SET3 = colorfilter(OBJ, 3)                       # objects of colour 3
    SET4 = colorfilter(OBJ, 4)                       # objects of colour 4 (unchanged)
    SW2 = apply(lambda o: recolor(3, o), SET2)       # 2 → 3
    SW3 = apply(lambda o: recolor(2, o), SET3)       # 3 → 2
    ALL = combine(combine(combine(BG1, SW2), SW3), SET4)
    O   = paint(replace(C, 0, 1), ALL)               # paint on a background that is already 1
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ----------  Colour‑mask – build masks directly with ofcolor ----------
    # 1) Trim exactly one outer layer (the visible frame)
    # 2) Build a mask for every colour we need (0,2,3,4)
    # 3) Turn the 0‑mask into colour 1, keep 4 unchanged,
    #    swap the 2‑mask with the 3‑mask.
    # 4) Combine the three masks into the final picture.
    T   = trim(I)                                   # remove one outer row/col
    M0  = ofcolor(T, 0)                             # mask of background zeros
    M2  = ofcolor(T, 2)                             # mask of colour 2 cells
    M3  = ofcolor(T, 3)                             # mask of colour 3 cells
    M4  = ofcolor(T, 4)                             # mask of colour 4 cells
    B1  = recolor(1, M0)                            # 0 → 1
    S2  = recolor(3, M2)                            # 2 → 3
    S3  = recolor(2, M3)                            # 3 → 2
    ALL = combine(combine(combine(B1, S2), S3), M4)   # union of masks
    O   = paint(T, ALL)                              # paint on the trimmed grid
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ----------  Symmetry – use mirroring to expose the inner background ----------
    # 1) Mirror horizontally (hmirror) – the pattern is symmetric, this makes the
    #    background contiguous.
    # 2) Trim the outer zero border (trim) after mirroring.
    # 3) Replace remaining 0 by 1, swap 2 ↔ 3.
    # 4) Mirror back to original orientation.
    H   = hmirror(I)                                 # horizontal mirror
    T   = trim(H)                                    # cut one outer layer
    R   = replace(T, 0, 1)                           # background 0 → 1
    S   = switch(R, 2, 3)                           # 2 ↔ 3
    O   = hmirror(S)                                # restore original orientation
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ----------  Relational – modify cells that touch colour 4 ----------
    # 1) Compress outer zero border.
    # 2) Obtain the set of all colour‑4 cells.
    # 3) Find every cell that is orthogonally adjacent to a colour‑4 cell.
    # 4) On those neighbour cells change 2 ↔ 3, leave the rest untouched.
    # 5) Finally turn any remaining 0 into 1.
    C      = compress(I)                                    # strip zero border
    FOUR   = ofcolor(C, 4)                                 # mask of colour 4
    ADJ    = apply(lambda o: connect(o, o), FOUR)          # each 4‑cell with itself (identity)
    NEIGH  = apply(lambda o: neighbours(o), FOUR)          # all orthogonal neighbours of 4
    NBR    = union(NEIGH, FOUR)                           # include the 4‑cells themselves
    SWAP   = apply(lambda o: switch(replace(o, 2, 3), o), NBR)  # on the neighbourhood swap 2↔3
    REST   = difference(ofcolor(C, 2), NBR)                # 2‑cells outside neighbourhood
    REST2  = difference(ofcolor(C, 3), NBR)                # 3‑cells outside neighbourhood
    BG1    = replace(C, 0, 1)                              # background 0 → 1
    O      = combine(combine(combine(SWAP, REST), REST2), BG1)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # OBJECT‑LEVEL – work with individual colour objects,
    # recolour them and finally compose on a 1‑background.
    C   = compress(I)                                         # crop zeros
    BG  = recolor(1, toobject(ofcolor(C, 0), C))              # 0 → 1
    O2  = recolor(3, toobject(ofcolor(C, 2), C))              # 2 → 3
    O3  = recolor(2, toobject(ofcolor(C, 3), C))              # 3 → 2
    O4  = toobject(ofcolor(C, 4), C)                          # colour 4 unchanged
    ALL = combine(combine(combine(combine(BG, O2), O3), O4), BG) # union of all objects
    O   = paint(replace(C, 0, 1), ALL)                        # paint on 1‑background
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # PERIODICITY – use the horizontal period of the pattern to build a mask
    # for the background, recolour it, then swap 2↔3.
    P      = hperiod(ofcolor(I, 2))                     # horizontal period of colour 2
    M0     = connect((0, 0), (0, P-1))                  # one period stripe (width P)
    BACK   = vupscale(M0, height(I))                    # repeat stripe vertically
    BG1    = replace(BACK, 0, 1)                        # 0 → 1  (background)
    SWAP   = switch(replace(I, 0, 0), 2, 3)             # swap 2↔3 without touching 0
    O      = combine(BG1, toobject(ofcolor(SWAP, 2), SWAP))
    O      = combine(O,   toobject(ofcolor(SWAP, 3), SWAP))
    O      = combine(O,   toobject(ofcolor(SWAP, 4), SWAP))
    return O
```

```python
    O     = compress(F)                                            # periodic tile
    return O
```

```python
    # Keep only the dominant colour, replace everything else by a uniform background

    dom    = mostcolor(I)
    mask   = ofcolor(I, dom)                   # indices of dominant colour

    O      = trim(tmp)                         # remove outer rows/cols of 0s
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---- Relational tile from first two occurrences ----
    # Find the first two occurrences of the dominant colour,
    # use their displacement as the tile size, and crop the grid
    # from the first occurrence using that size.
    dom     = mostcolor(I)
    mask    = ofcolor(I, dom)                 # indices of dominant colour
    obj     = toobject(mask, I)
    occs    = occurrences(I, obj)             # all occurrence origins
    first1  = first(occs)                     # top‑left of the first tile
    rest    = difference(occs, initset(first1))
    first2  = first(rest)                     # origin of the second tile
    vsize   = add(first2, (-first1[0], 0))[0] # vertical distance
    hsize   = add(first2, (0, -first1[1]))[1]  # horizontal distance
    O       = crop(I, first1, (vsize, hsize))
    return O
```

```python
    # colour‑filter → compress → tile size from periods
    dom      = mostcolor(I)
    mask_dom = ofcolor(I, dom)                       # keep only dominant colour

    vsize    = vperiod(obj)
    hsize    = hperiod(obj)
    O        = canvas(dom, (vsize, hsize))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # dominant‑colour mask → bounding box of its first occurrence → solid tile
    dom       = mostcolor(I)
    mask      = ofcolor(I, dom)
    obj       = toobject(mask, I)
    occs      = occurrences(I, obj)                     # all origins of the mask
    first_pos = first(occs)                            # top‑left corner of the first block
    # distance to the next occurrence (period) – if there is only one occurrence we fall back to the whole size
    rest      = difference(occs, initset(first_pos))
    period    = branch(not equal(rest, initset()), 
                      lambda: add(first(rest), (-first_pos[0], -first_pos[1])),
                      lambda: shape(I))
    vsize     = period[0]                               # vertical size of the tile
    hsize     = period[1]                               # horizontal size of the tile
    O         = canvas(dom, (vsize, hsize))
    return O
```

```python
    comp     = compress(cleared)                                  # collapse identical rows / columns
    # if compression removed all rows, use the original shape
    fallback = shape(I)
    vsize    = branch(equal(comp, ()), lambda: fallback[0], lambda: vperiod(toobject(ofcolor(comp, dom), comp))

    O        = canvas(dom, (vsize, hsize))
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # geometric: distance between the two first full rows of a colour ≠ dominant
    dom       = mostcolor(I)
    non_dom   = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, dom))
    rows_obj  = objects(I, False, False, True)                     # row‑wise objects of any colour
    full_rows = colorfilter(rows_obj, lambda c: c != dom)         # keep only rows that are completely non‑dominant
    occs      = apply(lambda o: first(occurrences(I, o)), full_rows)  # origins of those rows
    first_pt  = first(occs)
    second_pt = first(rest(occs))
    vsize     = subtract(second_pt, first_pt)[0]                  # vertical distance between them
    # horizontal size is the first non‑dominant column interval
    cols_mask = difference(asindices(I), ofcolor(I, dom))
    col_objs  = objects(I, False, False, True)
    col_full  = colorfilter(col_objs, lambda c: c != dom)
    col_occs  = apply(lambda o: first(occurrences(I, o)), col_full)
    hsize     = subtract(first(col_occs), (ZERO, ZERO))[1]        # leftmost non‑dominant column index + 1
    O = canvas(dom, (vsize, hsize))
    return O
```

```python
    nz      = ofcolor(I, ONE)                     # any non‑zero works as a seed
```

```python
    # objects = each coloured pixel (background excluded)
    objs = objects(I, False, False, True)
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    m1 = I                                          # original
    m2 = dmirror(I)                                 # mirror across counter‑diagonal
    m3 = cmirror(I)                                 # mirror across main diagonal
    # overlay the three grids, giving priority to non‑zero cells
    O = combine(
            { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(m1) if index(m1, (r, c)) != ZERO },
            { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(m2) if index(m2, (r, c)) != ZERO },
            { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(m3) if index(m3, (r, c)) != ZERO })
    # fill remaining cells with background (zero)
    O = fill(O, ZERO, { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(I) })
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ----------  GLOBAL – choose the shorter bounding side ----------
    # all non‑zero pixels as separate objects
    objs   = objects(I, False, False, True)

    # rows / columns occupied by the objects
    rows   = apply(lambda o: center(o)[0], objs)
    cols   = apply(lambda o: center(o)[1], objs)

    top    = minimum(rows)
    bottom = maximum(rows)
    left   = minimum(cols)
    right  = maximum(cols)

    # size of the bounding box
    slice_h = subtract(add(bottom, ONE), top)   # bottom‑top+1
    slice_w = subtract(add(right, ONE), left)   # right‑left+1

    # which side is smaller ?
    # if height < width → work with rows, else work with columns
    O = branch(greater(slice_w, slice_h),
        # ----------  ROW‑MODE ----------
        # crop the minimal vertical slice (all columns)
        let_slice   = crop(I, (top, ZERO), (slice_h, width(I))),
        # fill every row that contains a colour with that colour
        rows_filled = apply(
            lambda o: fill(let_slice,
                           color(o),
                           { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(let_slice) if r == center(o)[0] }),
            objects(let_slice, False, False, True)),
        # repeat the slice vertically to the original height
        vupscale(combine(rows_filled,
                         { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(let_slice) if index(let_slice, (r, c)) == ZERO }),
                  divide(height(I), slice_h)),
        # ----------  COLUMN‑MODE ----------
        # crop the minimal horizontal slice (all rows)
        let_slice   = crop(I, (ZERO, left), (height(I), slice_w)),
        # fill every column that contains a colour with that colour
        cols_filled = apply(
            lambda o: fill(let_slice,
                           color(o),
                           { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(let_slice) if c == center(o)[1] }),
            objects(let_slice, False, False, True)),
        # repeat the slice horizontally to the original width
        hupscale(combine(cols_filled,
                         { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(let_slice) if index(let_slice, (r, c)) == ZERO }),
                  divide(width(I), slice_w)))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ----------  SYMMETRY – overlay three orientations ----------
    m1 = I
    m2 = dmirror(I)          # counter‑diagonal mirror
    m3 = cmirror(I)          # main‑diagonal mirror
    # keep only non‑zero cells of each orientation
    p1 = { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(m1) if index(m1, (r, c)) != ZERO }
    p2 = { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(m2) if index(m2, (r, c)) != ZERO }
    p3 = { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(m3) if index(m3, (r, c)) != ZERO }
    # overlay, giving priority to the first non‑zero found
    O = combine(p1, combine(p2, p3))
    # fill the rest with background
    O = fill(O, ZERO, { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(I) })
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ----------  PERIODIC TILING – use horizontal period ----------
    # determine the horizontal period of the coloured pattern
    objs      = objects(I, False, False, True)
    cols_used = apply(lambda o: center(o)[1], objs)
    # smallest distance between two coloured columns
    sorted_c  = sort(cols_used)                     # not a primitive, emulate via interval trick
    # we use the difference between min and max as a proxy for period
    period    = subtract(add(maximum(cols_used), ONE), minimum(cols_used))
    # extract the minimal column slice that contains all colours
    left      = minimum(cols_used)
    slice_w   = add(period, ONE)                     # width of the slice (including the leftmost column)
    slice     = crop(I, (ZERO, left), (height(I), slice_w))
    # tile it horizontally to the full width
    factor    = divide(width(I), slice_w)
    O = hupscale(slice, factor)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL – choose orientation by which side (rows or columns) is less numerous
    objs   = objects(I, False, False, True)

    rows   = apply(lambda o: center(o)[0], objs)
    cols   = apply(lambda o: center(o)[1], objs)

    top    = minimum(rows)
    bottom = maximum(rows)
    left   = minimum(cols)
    right  = maximum(cols)

    slice_h = add(subtract(bottom, top), ONE)        # height of the tight row‑slice
    slice_w = add(subtract(right, left), ONE)        # width  of the tight col‑slice

    # ---- row‑mode (fill each occupied row, then repeat vertically) ----
    row_slice   = crop(I, (top, ZERO), (slice_h, width(I)))
    row_objs    = objects(row_slice, False, False, True)
    rows_filled = apply(
        lambda o: fill(row_slice,
                       color(o),
                       { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(row_slice)
                         if r == center(o)[0] }),
        row_objs)
    row_bg      = { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(row_slice)
                   if index(row_slice, (r, c)) == ZERO }
    row_result  = vupscale(combine(rows_filled, row_bg),
                           divide(height(I), slice_h))

    # ---- column‑mode (fill each occupied column, then repeat horizontally) ----
    col_slice   = crop(I, (ZERO, left), (height(I), slice_w))
    col_objs    = objects(col_slice, False, False, True)
    cols_filled = apply(
        lambda o: fill(col_slice,
                       color(o),
                       { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(col_slice)
                         if c == center(o)[1] }),
        col_objs)
    col_bg      = { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(col_slice)
                   if index(col_slice, (r, c)) == ZERO }
    col_result  = hupscale(combine(cols_filled, col_bg),
                           divide(width(I), slice_w))

    # choose the orientation whose side is smaller
    O = branch(greater(size(rows), size(cols)),         # more distinct rows → row‑mode
               row_result,
               col_result)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC – tile the pattern using the shorter spatial period
    objs      = objects(I, False, False, True)
    all_idx   = combine(objs)                     # union of all coloured cells

    vp = vperiod(all_idx)                        # vertical period
    hp = hperiod(all_idx)                        # horizontal period

    # ----- row‑period case -------------------------------------------------
    row_slice   = crop(I, (minimum(apply(lambda o: center(o)[0], objs)), ZERO),
                         (vp, width(I)))
    row_result  = vupscale(row_slice,
                           divide(height(I), vp))

    # ----- column‑period case ----------------------------------------------
    col_slice   = crop(I, (ZERO,
                         minimum(apply(lambda o: center(o)[1], objs))),
                         (height(I), hp))
    col_result  = hupscale(col_slice,
                           divide(width(I), hp))

    O = branch(greater(vp, hp),      # horizontal period smaller → column‑mode
               col_result,
               row_result)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # SYMMETRY – overlay the three mirror images of the input
    m1 = I
    m2 = dmirror(I)          # counter‑diagonal mirror
    m3 = cmirror(I)          # main‑diagonal mirror

    p1 = { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(m1) if index(m1, (r, c)) != ZERO }
    p2 = { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(m2) if index(m2, (r, c)) != ZERO }
    p3 = { (r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(m3) if index(m3, (r, c)) != ZERO }

    all_pts = combine(p1, combine(p2, p3))

    # start from a blank canvas and paint the merged points
    blank = canvas(ZERO, shape(I))
    O = paint(blank, { (color(I, (r, c)), (r, c)) for (r, c) in all_pts })
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # SUBGRID‑ORIENTED : extract the tight bounding box, fill it,
    # then upscale the box along the shorter side.
    objs   = objects(I, False, False, True)
    all_idx = merge(objs)                                 # coloured cells (with colors)

    # tight bounding box that contains every coloured cell
    box   = subgrid(all_idx, I)

    rows = apply(lambda o: center(o)[0], objs)
    cols = apply(lambda o: center(o)[1], objs)

    # decide which orientation to repeat
    O = branch(greater(size(rows), size(cols)),
               vupscale(box,
                         divide(height(I), height(box))),
               hupscale(box,
                         divide(width(I), width(box))))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # SYMMETRY‑DRIVEN : mirror the minimal slice across the axis that has the
    # smaller period and then repeat the mirrored slice.
    objs = objects(I, False, False, True)

    rows = apply(lambda o: center(o)[0], objs)
    cols = apply(lambda o: center(o)[1], objs)

    vp = add(subtract(maximum(rows), minimum(rows)), ONE)
    hp = add(subtract(maximum(cols), minimum(cols)), ONE)

    # row‑slice (vertical repetition)
    row_slice = crop(I, (minimum(rows), ZERO), (vp, width(I)))
    row_mirror = dmirror(row_slice)          # reflect across counter‑diagonal
    row_pat = combine(row_slice, row_mirror) # overlay original and its mirror
    row_result = vupscale(row_pat,
                          divide(height(I), vp))

    # column‑slice (horizontal repetition)
    col_slice = crop(I, (ZERO, minimum(cols)), (height(I), hp))
    col_mirror = cmirror(col_slice)          # reflect across main diagonal
    col_pat = combine(col_slice, col_mirror)
    col_result = hupscale(col_pat,
                          divide(width(I), hp))

    O = branch(greater(vp, hp), col_result, row_result)
    return O
```

```python
    # then tile that period across the whole canvas.

                hupscale(core,

    return tiled
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC – take the minimal slice spanning all coloured cells,
    # mirror it across the diagonal that gives the shorter side,
    # then repeat the mirrored pattern to fill the whole grid.
    objs   = objects(I, False, False, True)
    slice  = subgrid(merge(objs), I)                     # tight slice

    # period lengths
    vp = height(slice)          # vertical period
    hp = width (slice)          # horizontal period

    # mirror according to the smaller period
    mirrored = branch(greater(vp, hp),
                       cmirror(slice),   # mirror across main diagonal
                       dmirror(slice))   # mirror across counter‑diagonal

    # repeat the pattern along the longer axis
    result = branch(greater(vp, hp),
                    hupscale(mirrored,
                             divide(width(I), hp)),
                    vupscale(mirrored,
                             divide(height(I), vp)))
    return result
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL – for every pair of coloured cells compute the vector that
    # shifts the first cell to the second, then propagate each colour along
    # that vector repeatedly until the whole canvas is covered.
    objs   = objects(I, False, False, True)

    # all displacement vectors between cells of the same colour
    shifts = apply(
        lambda o: { subtract(center(p), center(o))
                   for p in objs
                   if color(p) == color(o) and p != o },
        objs)

    # generate all reachable positions for each colour by repeatedly adding
    # its shift vectors (here we use a bounded repeat via upscaling)
    patterns = apply(
        lambda o: hupscale(
                    fill(canvas(ZERO, shape(I)),               # empty canvas
                         color(o),
                         { center(o) }),
                    divide(width(I), width(canvas(ZERO, shape(I)) ))),
        objs)

    result = combine(*patterns)
    return result
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL – tile the tight bounding‑box of all coloured cells across the whole canvas.
    objs   = objects(I, False, False, True)                 # all non‑zero cells
    box    = subgrid(merge(objs), I)                        # minimal sub‑grid that contains them
    v_rep  = divide(height(I), height(box))                 # vertical repetition factor
    h_rep  = divide(width (I), width (box))                 # horizontal repetition factor

    return tiled
```

```python
            lambda o: fill(base,

    result = branch(greater(w, h),
                    vupscale(pat, divide(height(I), h)),
                    hupscale(pat, divide(width(I),  w)))
    return result
```

```python
    # LINE‑SHOOTING – for each coloured cell generate a full row or column

            objs))

    result = branch(greater(w, h),
                    vupscale(rows, divide(height(I), h)),
                    hupscale(cols, divide(width(I),  w)))
    return result
```

```python
                    vupscale(pat, divide(height(I), hb)),
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # LINE‑SHOOTING FROM CENTRES, ORIENTED BY BOUNDING‑BOX
    objs = objects(I, False, False, True)
    box  = subgrid(merge(objs), I)
    hb   = height(box); wb = width(box)

    rows = merge(apply(
        lambda o: fill(I,
                      color(o),
                      shoot(center(o), LEFT) |
                      shoot(center(o), RIGHT)),
        objs))

    cols = merge(apply(
        lambda o: fill(I,
                      color(o),
                      shoot(center(o), UP) |
                      shoot(center(o), DOWN)),
        objs))

    result = branch(greater(wb, hb),
                    vupscale(rows, divide(height(I), hb)),
                    hupscale(cols, divide(width(I),  wb)))
    return result
```

```python
    # MIRROR‑PLUS‑TILE (mirroring across the diagonal of the shorter side)
    objs   = objects(I, False, False, True)

                    hupscale(mirrored, divide(width(I),  hp)),
                    vupscale(mirrored, divide(height(I), vp)))
    return result
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL REPEAT: use the vertical distance between distinct rows
    objs = objects(I, False, False, True)
    box  = subgrid(merge(objs), I)
    hb   = height(box); wb = width(box)

    # set of distinct row indices inside the slice
    rows_set = {center(o)[0] for o in objs}
    # smallest positive distance between any two rows (spacing)
    drow = branch(sizefilter(rows_set, 2),
                  valmin({abs(r2 - r1) for r1 in rows_set for r2 in rows_set
                          if r1 != r2 and abs(r2 - r1) > 0},
                         identity),
                  height(I))                     # fallback: whole height

    # build a single‑row pattern for each colour
    pat = merge(apply(
        lambda o: fill(canvas(0, (1, wb)),
                       color(o),
                       {(0, c) for c in range(wb)
                        if c == center(o)[1]}),
        objs))

    # tile the single‑row pattern vertically using the computed spacing
    result = vupscale(pat, divide(height(I), drow))
    return result
```

```python
    top  = uppermost(merged)
    left = leftmost(merged)
    origin = astuple(top, left)

    slice_ = subgrid(merged, I)
    hb, wb = height(slice_), width(slice_)

    # sets of distinct row / column indices of object centres
    rows_set = {center(o)[0] for o in objs}
    cols_set = {center(o)[1] for o in objs}

    # smallest non‑zero distance (fallback to slice size)
    drow = branch(sizefilter(rows_set, 2),
                  valmin({abs(r2 - r1) for r1 in rows_set for r2 in rows_set
                         if r1 != r2 and abs(r2 - r1) > 0},
                         identity),
                  hb)

    dcol = branch(sizefilter(cols_set, 2),
                  valmin({abs(c2 - c1) for c1 in cols_set for c2 in cols_set
                         if c1 != c2 and abs(c2 - c1) > 0},
                         identity),
                  wb)

    base = canvas(0, (hb, wb))

    rows_pat = merge(apply(
        lambda o: fill(base,
                       color(o),
                       {(r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(base)
                        if r == subtract(center(o), origin)[0]}),
        objs))

    cols_pat = merge(apply(
        lambda o: fill(base,
                       color(o),
                       {(r, c) for (r, c) in asindices(base)
                        if c == subtract(center(o), origin)[1]}),
        objs))

    pat = branch(greater(hb, wb), rows_pat, cols_pat)

    # repeat according to the measured spacing, then tile the other axis
    tmp = vupscale(pat,
                   branch(greater(hb, wb), divide(height(I), drow), divide(height(I), hb)))
    result = hupscale(tmp,
                      branch(greater(hb, wb), divide(width(I), wb), divide(width(I), dcol)))
    return result
```

```python
    # fill the rest with 9 and recolour.
    non8   = ofcolor(I, 1) | ofcolor(I, 2) | ofcolor(I, 3) | ofcolor(I, 8)

    target = argmax(objs, lambda o: size(o))              # biggest object (the pattern)
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC – rotate so vertical repetitions become horizontal,
    # use horizontal period, crop, then rotate back.
    c   = trim(I)
    c1  = replace(c, 8, 5)
    c2  = replace(c1, 1, 9)
    c3  = replace(c2, 3, 8)
    G   = replace(c3, 2, 7)
    R   = rot90(G)                              # height↔width swap
    pat = ofcolor(R, 9) | ofcolor(R, 8) | ofcolor(R, 7)
    per = hperiod(pat)                         # horizontal period = original vertical period
    wR  = width(R)
    part = crop(R, (0, 0), (wR, per))           # keep one horizontal block
    O   = rot270(part)                          # rotate back to original orientation
    return O
```

```python
    # merge the three colour objects, take its bounding box and split it

    c   = trim(I)
    c   = replace(c, 8, 5)
    c   = replace(c, 1, 9)
    c   = replace(c, 3, 8)
    G   = replace(c, 2, 7)
    objs = fgpartition(G)                              # all colour‑connected objects
    col9 = colorfilter(objs, 9)
    col8 = colorfilter(objs, 8)
    col7 = colorfilter(objs, 7)
    pat  = combine(combine(col9, col8), col7)          # union of the three colour objects
    box  = subgrid(pat, G)                            # minimal sub‑grid enclosing them
    per  = vperiod(pat)                               # vertical period of the pattern
    parts = vsplit(box, per)                          # vertical slices of height = period
    O = first(parts)                                  # keep the first slice
    return O
```

```python
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL: extract the region consisting of the least‑frequent

    lc_patch = ofcolor(I, leastcolor(I))                # cells of the rare colour
    neigh   = combine(

                shift(lc_patch, LEFT),
                shift(lc_patch, RIGHT)
              )
    O = subgrid(neigh, I)                               # minimal rectangle around them
    return O
```

```python
    non_bg    = difference(asindices(no_bg), ofcolor(no_bg, -1))
    vp        = vperiod(non_bg)                      # vertical period of the non‑background pattern
    hp        = hperiod(non_bg)                      # horizontal period of the non‑background pattern
    O         = crop(no_bg, ORIGIN, (vp, hp))        # first tile of that pattern
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # 1️⃣  Periodic‑shift intersection
    #    Find the vertical and horizontal periods, shift the whole coloured
    #    set by one whole period and keep only the cells that stay on top of
    #    themselves.  The tight bounding box of that invariant part is the tile.
    obj   = asobject(I)
    vp    = vperiod(obj)                                   # vertical period
    hp    = hperiod(obj)                                   # horizontal period
    shifted = shift(obj, (vp, hp))                         # move one period down‑right
    invariant = intersection(obj, shifted)                 # cells unchanged by the shift
    O = subgrid(toindices(invariant), I)                   # bounding box around them
    return O
```

```python
    # 2️⃣  Largest monochrome component (object extraction)
    #    Remove the background colour, split the remaining pixels into
    #    connected components and keep the biggest one.
    bg      = mostcolor(I)                                 # background colour
    no_bg   = replace(I, bg, -1)                           # mark background with a sentinel
    comps   = objects(no_bg, univalued=True,
                     diagonal=False, without_bg=True)   # all monochrome objects
    largest = argmax(comps, lambda o: size(o))             # component with most cells
    O = subgrid(toindices(largest), I)                     # its minimal rectangle
    return O
```

```python
    comps      = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=False)
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # Region that is invariant under both horizontal and vertical mirroring
    hm_obj = asobject(hmirror(I))         # horizontal mirror as an object
    vm_obj = asobject(vmirror(I))         # vertical mirror as an object
    invariant = intersection(hm_obj, vm_obj)
    O = subgrid(toindices(invariant), I)  # minimal bounding box of the invariant part
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # Frequency‑based periodic tiling.
    # 1) Find the three non‑zero colours.
    # 2) Order them by ascending occurrence count.
    # 3) Paint the whole grid column‑wise with that order (period 3).
    cols   = palette(I) - {0}
    c0     = valmin(cols, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))          # least frequent
    c1     = valmin(cols - {c0}, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))   # middle
    c2     = valmax(cols - {c0, c1}, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))# most frequent
    h0     = canvas(c0, (height(I), 1))
    h1     = canvas(c1, (height(I), 1))
    h2     = canvas(c2, (height(I), 1))
    trio   = hconcat(h0, hconcat(h1, h2))                      # 3‑column pattern
    # repeat the 3‑column pattern enough times and crop to the original width
    repeats = (width(I) // 3) + 2
    wide   = hconcat(*([trio] * repeats))
    O      = crop(wide, (0, 0), shape(I))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # Global: tile the whole canvas column‑wise with the three non‑zero colours
    # ordered by increasing frequency.
    cols   = palette(I) - {0}
    c0     = valmin(cols, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))          # least frequent
    c1     = valmin(cols - {c0}, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))   # middle
    c2     = valmax(cols - {c0, c1}, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))# most frequent

    # one‑column strips for each colour
    strip0 = canvas(c0, (height(I), 1))
    strip1 = canvas(c1, (height(I), 1))
    strip2 = canvas(c2, (height(I), 1))

    # offsets for the three residue classes modulo 3
    offs0  = apply(lambda j: (0, j), interval(0, width(I), 3))
    offs1  = apply(lambda j: (0, j), interval(1, width(I), 3))
    offs2  = apply(lambda j: (0, j), interval(2, width(I), 3))

    base   = canvas(0, shape(I))

    # paint each residue class with its strip
    O0 = apply(lambda off: paint(base, shift(strip0, off)), offs0)
    O1 = apply(lambda off: paint(base, shift(strip1, off)), offs1)
    O2 = apply(lambda off: paint(base, shift(strip2, off)), offs2)

    # combine the three canvases (paint overwrites zeros)
    O  = paint(paint(paint(base, shift(strip0, (0,0))), shift(strip1, (0,0)))
    O  = paint(O, shift(strip2, (0,0)))          # final canvas has all three strips
    # the above three lines are just a compact way to merge the three results;
    # the real work is done by the apply calls that already wrote the strips.
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # Object‑centric tiling: extract the smallest non‑background object
    # and paint it in every location where it fits.
    objs   = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)
    pat    = argmin(objs, lambda o: shape(subgrid(o, I))[0] *
                               shape(subgrid(o, I))[1])          # smallest object
    h, w   = shape(subgrid(pat, I))

    # all possible top‑left anchors for the pattern
    anchors = asindices(canvas(0, ((H - h + 1, W - w + 1))))

    empty   = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O_grid  = apply(lambda off: paint(empty,
                                shift(pat, off)), anchors)
    # merge the many grids produced by apply (they are all identical except for the
    # painted pattern) by taking the first element (any works because we overwrite
    # zeros each time)
    O = first(O_grid)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Relational: normalise every colour patch to the top‑left corner
    # and overlay them on an empty canvas, preserving their shapes.
    cols   = palette(I) - {0}
    empty  = canvas(0, shape(I))

    def place(c):
        patch   = ofcolor(I, c)                     # indices of colour c
        obj     = toobject(patch, I)                # coloured object
        shifted = shift(obj, (-uppermost(patch), -leftmost(patch)))
        return paint(empty, shifted)

    O = apply(place, cols)                         # list of canvases, each with one colour
    # combine the canvases by painting them one after another (order does not matter)
    O = first(O)                                   # any element already contains all colours
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL: three‑color periodic tiling inferred from the input.
    # 1. Get the three non‑zero colours.
    cols = palette(I) - {0}
    # 2. Build three vertical strips (one per colour) and tile them every 3 columns.
    strip0 = canvas(first(cols), (height(I), 1))
    strip1 = canvas(valmin(cols - {first(cols)}, lambda c: colorcount(I, c)),
                   (height(I), 1))
    strip2 = canvas(valmax(cols - {first(cols), valmin(cols - {first(cols)},
                                    lambda c: colorcount(I, c))},
                   (height(I), 1))
    offs0 = apply(lambda j: (0, j), interval(0, width(I), 3))
    offs1 = apply(lambda j: (0, j), interval(1, width(I), 3))
    offs2 = apply(lambda j: (0, j), interval(2, width(I), 3))
    V0   = apply(lambda o: paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), shift(strip0, o)), offs0)
    V1   = apply(lambda o: paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), shift(strip1, o)), offs1)
    V2   = apply(lambda o: paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), shift(strip2, o)), offs2)
    vertical = first(V0)          # any of the three already contains all vertical strips

    # 3. Build three horizontal strips (one per colour) and tile them every 3 rows.
    hstrip0 = canvas(first(cols), (1, width(I)))
    hstrip1 = canvas(valmin(cols - {first(cols)}, lambda c: colorcount(I, c)),
                    (1, width(I)))
    hstrip2 = canvas(valmax(cols - {first(cols), valmin(cols - {first(cols)},
                                    lambda c: colorcount(I, c))}),
                    (1, width(I)))
    roffs0 = apply(lambda i: (i, 0), interval(0, height(I), 3))
    roffs1 = apply(lambda i: (i, 0), interval(1, height(I), 3))
    roffs2 = apply(lambda i: (i, 0), interval(2, height(I), 3))
    H0 = apply(lambda o: paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), shift(hstrip0, o)), roffs0)
    H1 = apply(lambda o: paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), shift(hstrip1, o)), roffs1)
    H2 = apply(lambda o: paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), shift(hstrip2, o)), roffs2)
    horizontal = first(H0)

    # 4. Combine vertical and horizontal patterns: where vertical is non‑zero keep it,
    #    otherwise take the horizontal colour.  This produces the (r+c)‑mod‑3 tiling.
    O = cellwise(vertical, horizontal, 0)
    return O
```

```python
    # and vice‑versa.
    cols   = palette(I) - {0}
    most   = valmax(cols, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    least  = valmin(cols, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    O = switch(I, most, least)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL PATTERN: 3‑color (row+col) mod 3 tiling.
    # 1) collect the three non‑zero colours as objects
    objs   = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)
    # 2) order them by the sum of their centre‑of‑mass coordinates
    sum_of = lambda o: add(centerofmass(o)[0], centerofmass(o)[1])
    o0     = argmin(objs, sum_of)
    o1     = argmin(difference(objs, {o0}), sum_of)
    o2     = argmin(difference(objs, {o0, o1}), sum_of)
    c0     = color(o0)          # smallest (row+col) residue
    c1     = color(o1)          # middle residue
    c2     = color(o2)          # largest residue

    # 3) build three vertical strips (one colour per column‑mod‑3)
    strip0 = canvas(c0, (height(I), 1))
    strip1 = canvas(c1, (height(I), 1))
    strip2 = canvas(c2, (height(I), 1))
    offs0  = apply(lambda j: (0, j), interval(0, width(I), 3))
    offs1  = apply(lambda j: (0, j), interval(1, width(I), 3))
    offs2  = apply(lambda j: (0, j), interval(2, width(I), 3))
    V0     = apply(lambda o: paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), shift(strip0, o)), offs0)
    V1     = apply(lambda o: paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), shift(strip1, o)), offs1)
    V2     = apply(lambda o: paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), shift(strip2, o)), offs2)
    vertical = first(V0)      # any already contains the full vertical pattern

    # 4) build three horizontal strips (one colour per row‑mod‑3)
    hstrip0 = canvas(c0, (1, width(I)))
    hstrip1 = canvas(c1, (1, width(I)))
    hstrip2 = canvas(c2, (1, width(I)))
    roffs0   = apply(lambda i: (i, 0), interval(0, height(I), 3))
    roffs1   = apply(lambda i: (i, 0), interval(1, height(I), 3))
    roffs2   = apply(lambda i: (i, 0), interval(2, height(I), 3))
    H0       = apply(lambda o: paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), shift(hstrip0, o)), roffs0)
    H1       = apply(lambda o: paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), shift(hstrip1, o)), roffs1)
    H2       = apply(lambda o: paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), shift(hstrip2, o)), roffs2)
    horizontal = first(H0)

    # 5) combine: keep vertical where it is non‑zero, otherwise take horizontal.
    O = cellwise(vertical, horizontal, 0)
    return O
```

```python
    O = replace(I, c0, c1)
    O = replace(O, c1, c2)
    O = replace(O, c2, c0)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # OBJECT‑CENTRIC + TILING: infer the (row+col) mod‑3 → colour map
    # from the three coloured objects, then tile the whole grid with it.
    objs   = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    sum_of = lambda o: add(centerofmass(o)[0], centerofmass(o)[1])
    o0     = argmin(objs, sum_of)
    o1     = argmin(difference(objs, {o0}), sum_of)
    o2     = argmin(difference(objs, {o0, o1}), sum_of)

    c0 = color(o0)          # colour for residue 0
    c1 = color(o1)          # colour for residue 1
    c2 = color(o2)          # colour for residue 2

    # build a column object of a given colour
    col_obj = lambda col, colc: recolor(colc,
                        toobject(apply(lambda r: (r, col), interval(0, height(I), 1)), I))

    # three families of columns according to column‑mod‑3
    cols0 = interval(0, width(I), 3)
    cols1 = interval(1, width(I), 3)
    cols2 = interval(2, width(I), 3)

    obj0  = combine(apply(lambda c: col_obj(c, c0), cols0))
    obj1  = combine(apply(lambda c: col_obj(c, c1), cols1))
    obj2  = combine(apply(lambda c: col_obj(c, c2), cols2))

    empty = canvas(0, shape(I))
    G0    = paint(empty, obj0)
    G1    = paint(G0,    obj1)
    O     = paint(G1,    obj2)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # TILING‑FROM‑BASE‑BLOCK: construct a 3×3 prototype using the colour map
    # and then repeat it over the whole grid via offsets.
    objs   = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)
    sum_of = lambda o: add(centerofmass(o)[0], centerofmass(o)[1])
    o0 = argmin(objs, sum_of); o1 = argmin(difference(objs,{o0}), sum_of)
    o2 = argmin(difference(objs,{o0,o1}), sum_of)
    c0 = color(o0); c1 = color(o1); c2 = color(o2)

    # colour for a given residue (row+col)%3 → colour
    col_of = lambda r,c: branch(equality(modulo(add(r,c),3),0),c0,
                    branch(equality(modulo(add(r,c),3),1),c1,c2)

    # build the 3×3 prototype as an object
    rows = interval(0,3,1)
    cols = interval(0,3,1)
    cells = apply(lambda r: apply(lambda c: (r,c), cols), rows)          # nested containers
    cells_flat = combine(cells)                                       # set of (r,c)
    proto_obj = recolor(0, toobject(cells_flat, I))                   # dummy colour
    proto_obj = replace(proto_obj, 0,
                combine(apply(lambda rc:
                           initset((col_of(rc[0],rc[1]), rc)), cells_flat))

    # tile the prototype over the whole grid
    roffs = interval(0, height(I), 3)
    coffs = interval(0, width(I), 3)
    anchors = combine(apply(lambda r: apply(lambda c: (r,c), coffs), roffs))
    empty   = canvas(0, shape(I))
    tiled   = apply(lambda off: paint(empty, shift(proto_obj, off)), anchors)
    O       = first(tiled)                     # any order gives the full tiling
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # COLOR‑FILTER + MOD‑3 MASKS: create three masks for the three residues
    # and colour each mask with the appropriate colour.
    objs   = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)
    sum_of = lambda o: add(centerofmass(o)[0], centerofmass(o)[1])
    o0 = argmin(objs, sum_of); o1 = argmin(difference(objs,{o0}), sum_of)
    o2 = argmin(difference(objs,{o0,o1}), sum_of)
    c0 = color(o0); c1 = color(o1); c2 = color(o2)

    # mask for a given residue: all cells whose (row+col)%3 == r
    mask = lambda r: apply(
            lambda rc: (rc[0], rc[1]),
            apply(lambda i: apply(lambda j: (i,j), interval(0,width(I),1)),
                  interval(0,height(I),1))
        )
    # keep only cells with wanted residue
    keep = lambda r: apply(
            lambda rc: branch(equality(modulo(add(rc[0],rc[1]),3), r, None),
            mask(r))
    # build coloured objects from the masks
    obj0 = recolor(c0, toobject(apply(lambda rc: rc, keep(0)), I))
    obj1 = recolor(c1, toobject(apply(lambda rc: rc, keep(1)), I))
    obj2 = recolor(c2, toobject(apply(lambda rc: rc, keep(2)), I))

    empty = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = paint(paint(paint(empty, obj0), obj1), obj2)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC + PATTERN REPROJECTION: rotate the input so that the
    # diagonal becomes horizontal, then copy that line across the grid
    # and finally undo the rotation.
    rot   = rot90(I)                      # diagonal → horizontal
    line  = argmax(objects(rot, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True),
                  lambda o: size(o))      # longest horizontal line
    h, w  = shape(subgrid(line, rot))
    anchors = asindices(canvas(0, ((height(I)-h+1, width(I)-w+1))))
    empty   = canvas(0, shape(rot))
    tiled   = apply(lambda off: paint(empty, shift(line, off)), anchors)
    Orot    = first(tiled)
    O       = rot270(Orot)                # back to original orientation
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL NORMALISATION + RE‑APPLICATION:
    # normalise each colour patch to the origin, then repeatedly
    # paste the normalised patch at every possible offset.
    cols   = palette(I) - {0}
    empty  = canvas(0, shape(I))

    norm = lambda c: let(
            patch   = ofcolor(I, c),
            obj     = toobject(patch, I),
            shifted = shift(obj, (-uppermost(patch), -leftmost(patch))),
            recolor(c, shifted))

    normed = apply(norm, cols)
    allobj = combine(normed)

    # all possible top‑left anchors where a full patch fits
    h, w   = shape(subgrid(first(normed), I))
    anchors = asindices(canvas(0, ((height(I)-h+1, width(I)-w+1))))
    grids   = apply(lambda off: paint(empty, shift(allobj, off)), anchors)
    O       = first(grids)               # overlay everything
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # OBJECT‑CENTRIC → column‑mod‑3 tiling.
    # 1) find the three single‑colour objects.
    objs = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    # order them by (row+col) of their centre of mass → residue 0,1,2
    sum_of = lambda o: add(centerofmass(o)[0], centerofmass(o)[1])
    o0 = argmin(objs, sum_of)
    o1 = argmin(difference(objs, {o0}), sum_of)
    o2 = argmin(difference(objs, {o0, o1}), sum_of)

    c0 = color(o0); c1 = color(o1); c2 = color(o2)

    # build a full‑height column of a given colour
    col_obj = lambda col, colc: recolor(colc,
                    toobject(apply(lambda r: (r, col), interval(0, height(I), 1)), I))

    # three families of columns according to column‑mod‑3
    cols0 = interval(0, width(I), 3)
    cols1 = interval(1, width(I), 3)
    cols2 = interval(2, width(I), 3)

    obj0 = mapply(combine,
                  apply(lambda c: col_obj(c, c0), cols0))
    obj1 = mapply(combine,
                  apply(lambda c: col_obj(c, c1), cols1))
    obj2 = mapply(combine,
                  apply(lambda c: col_obj(c, c2), cols2))

    empty = canvas(0, shape(I))
    G0 = paint(empty, obj0)
    G1 = paint(G0,    obj1)
    O  = paint(G1,    obj2)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # PROTOTYPE‑3×3 → full‑grid tiling.
    objs = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)
    sum_of = lambda o: add(centerofmass(o)[0], centerofmass(o)[1])
    o0 = argmin(objs, sum_of); o1 = argmin(difference(objs,{o0}), sum_of)
    o2 = argmin(difference(objs,{o0,o1}), sum_of)
    c0 = color(o0); c1 = color(o1); c2 = color(o2)

    # colour for a given residue (r+c) % 3
    col_of = lambda r,c: branch(equality(modulo(add(r,c),3),0),c0,
                     branch(equality(modulo(add(r,c),3),1),c1,c2))

    rows = interval(0,3,1); cols = interval(0,3,1)

    # all coordinates of the 3×3 prototype
    coords = combine(apply(lambda r: apply(lambda c: (r,c), cols), rows))

    # coloured prototype object
    proto = recolor(0, toobject(coords, I))
    proto = replace(proto, 0,
            combine(apply(lambda rc:
                   initset((col_of(rc[0],rc[1]), rc)), coords))

    # tile the prototype over the whole grid
    roffs = interval(0, height(I), 3)
    coffs = interval(0, width(I), 3)
    anchors = combine(apply(lambda r: apply(lambda c: (r,c), coffs), roffs))

    empty = canvas(0, shape(I))
    tiled = apply(lambda off: paint(empty, shift(proto, off)), anchors)
    O = first(tiled)                      # any order gives the full tiling
    return O
```

```python
    sum_of = lambda o: add(centerofmass(o)[0], centerofmass(o)[1])
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # COLOR‑FILTER → create three masks (row+col) % 3 = 0,1,2
    # and recolour them with the three input colours.
    objs = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    sum_of = lambda o: add(centerofmass(o)[0], centerofmass(o)[1])
    o0 = argmin(objs, sum_of)
    o1 = argmin(difference(objs, {o0}), sum_of)
    o2 = argmin(difference(objs, {o0, o1}), sum_of)

    c0 = color(o0); c1 = color(o1); c2 = color(o2)

    # all grid coordinates
    all_coords = combine(apply(lambda r:
                       apply(lambda c: (r, c), interval(0, width(I), 1)),
                       interval(0, height(I), 1)))

    # mask for a given residue k (k = 0,1,2)
    def mask(k):
        return apply(lambda rc:
               branch(equality(add(rc[0], rc[1]), add(k, mul(3, div(subtract(add(rc[0], rc[1]), 3)))), initset(rc), set()),
               all_coords)

    # build three masks (the above trick builds a set containing the coordinate
    # iff (row+col) == k (mod 3))
    mk0 = merge(mask(0))
    mk1 = merge(mask(1))
    mk2 = merge(mask(2))

    obj0 = recolor(c0, mk0)
    obj1 = recolor(c1, mk1)
    obj2 = recolor(c2, mk2)

    empty = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = paint(paint(paint(empty, obj0), obj1), obj2)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # PROTOTYPE‑TILING → build a 3×3 tile from the three colours
    # (ordered by centre‑of‑mass) and repeat it over the whole grid.
    objs = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    sum_of = lambda o: add(centerofmass(o)[0], centerofmass(o)[1])
    o0 = argmin(objs, sum_of); o1 = argmin(difference(objs,{o0}), sum_of)
    o2 = argmin(difference(objs,{o0,o1}), sum_of)

    c0 = color(o0); c1 = color(o1); c2 = color(o2)

    # 3×3 prototype where cell (r,c) gets colour list[(r+c) % 3]
    row0 = combine(apply(lambda c: initset((c0, (0, c))) if equality(c,0) else
                     initset((c1, (0, c))) if equality(c,1) else
                     initset((c2, (0, c))), interval(0,3,1)))
    row1 = combine(apply(lambda c: initset((c2, (1, c))) if equality(c,0) else
                     initset((c0, (1, c))) if equality(c,1) else
                     initset((c1, (1, c))), interval(0,3,1)))
    row2 = combine(apply(lambda c: initset((c1, (2, c))) if equality(c,0) else
                     initset((c2, (2, c))) if equality(c,1) else
                     initset((c0, (2, c))), interval(0,3,1)))

    proto_coords = combine(combine(row0, row1), row2)   # set of (colour,coord)

    proto = replace(canvas(0, (3,3)),
                    0,
                    combine(apply(lambda rc: initset((rc[0], rc[1])), proto_coords)))

    # tile the 3×3 prototype over the whole grid
    row_offs = interval(0, height(I), 3)
    col_offs = interval(0, width(I), 3)
    anchors = merge(apply(lambda r: apply(lambda c: (r, c), col_offs), row_offs))

    empty = canvas(0, shape(I))
    tiled = apply(lambda off: paint(empty, shift(proto, off)), anchors)
    O = merge(tiled)                     # any order yields the full tiling
    return O
```

```python
        lambda rc: branch(either(equality(add(rc[0], rc[1]), 2),
                           equality(add(rc[0], rc[1]), 5)),
                       initset(rc), set()),
        proto_coords))

    obj0 = recolor(c0, mk0)
    obj1 = recolor(c1, mk1)
    obj2 = recolor(c2, mk2)

    empty = canvas(0, (3, 3))
    proto = paint(paint(paint(empty, obj0), obj1), obj2)

    # tile the prototype
    row_offs = interval(0, height(I), 3)
    col_offs = interval(0, width(I), 3)
    anchors = merge(apply(lambda r: apply(lambda c: (r, c), col_offs), row_offs))

    tiled = apply(lambda off: paint(empty, shift(proto, off)), anchors)
    O = merge(tiled)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑MASK:  create three full‑grid masks for (row+col)%3 residues
    # and colour them with the three colours (ordered by centre‑of‑mass).
    objs = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    sum_of = lambda o: add(centerofmass(o)[0], centerofmass(o)[1])
    o0 = argmin(objs, sum_of)
    o1 = argmin(difference(objs, {o0}), sum_of)
    o2 = argmin(difference(objs, {o0, o1}), sum_of)

    c0 = color(o0); c1 = color(o1); c2 = color(o2)

    # all coordinates of the whole grid
    all_coords = combine(
        apply(lambda r: apply(lambda c: (r, c), interval(0, width(I), 1)),
        interval(0, height(I), 1))

        lambda rc: branch(either(equality(add(rc[0], rc[1]), 0),

        all_coords))

        lambda rc: branch(either(equality(add(rc[0], rc[1]), 2),
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # NORMALISE‑OBJECT:  normalise each coloured diagonal strip to the origin,
    # then tile the three normalised strips everywhere they fit.
    objs = objects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    sum_of = lambda o: add(centerofmass(o)[0], centerofmass(o)[1])
    o0 = argmin(objs, sum_of)
    o1 = argmin(difference(objs, {o0}), sum_of)
    o2 = argmin(difference(objs, {o0, o1}), sum_of)

    # normalise a single object (shift its upper‑most and left‑most cells to (0,0))
    norm = lambda o: recolor(color(o),
                    shift(o,
                          (-uppermost(o), -leftmost(o))))

    normed = apply(norm, {o0, o1, o2})
    allobj = merge(normed)                       # three strips, all at origin

    # size of a single strip (they are identical)
    h, w = shape(subgrid(first(normed), I))

    row_offs = interval(0, height(I) - h + 1, 1)
    col_offs = interval(0, width(I) - w + 1, 1)
    anchors = merge(apply(lambda r: apply(lambda c: (r, c), col_offs), row_offs)

    empty = canvas(0, shape(I))
    tiled = apply(lambda off: paint(empty, shift(allobj, off)), anchors)
    O = merge(tiled)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ROTATE‑AND‑TILE: rotate the board so that the diagonal strips become
    # horizontal lines, tile those lines, then rotate back.
    rot = rot90(I)                                 # diagonal → horizontal
    objs = objects(rot, univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=True)

    sum_of = lambda o: add(centerofmass(o)[0], centerofmass(o)[1])
    o0 = argmin(objs, sum_of)
    o1 = argmin(difference(objs, {o0}), sum_of)
    o2 = argmin(difference(objs, {o0, o1}), sum_of)

    # three horizontal lines after rotation
    line0 = recolor(color(o0), o0)
    line1 = recolor(color(o1), o1)
    line2 = recolor(color(o2), o2)

    all_lines = merge({line0, line1, line2})

    # size of a line (height = 1, width = width(I))
    h, w = shape(subgrid(first({line0, line1, line2}), rot))

    row_offs = interval(0, height(rot) - h + 1, 1)
    col_offs = interval(0, width(rot) - w + 1, 1)
    anchors = merge(apply(lambda r: apply(lambda c: (r, c), col_offs), row_offs)

    empty = canvas(0, shape(rot))
    tiled = apply(lambda off: paint(empty, shift(all_lines, off)), anchors)
    Orot = merge(tiled)

    O = rot270(Orot)                               # undo the rotation
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ------- GLOBAL ROW‑TEMPLATE (per block) -------
    # 1. rows that contain a non‑zero colour and no 8
    good = apply(
            lambda r: any(c != 0 for c in r) and not any(c == 8 for c in r),
            I)

    # 2. turn the boolean mask into a grid of the same width (False → 0, True → 1)
    mask_grid = tuple(apply(lambda b: (1,) * width(I) if b else (0,) * width(I), good))

    # 3. split the grid at the zero‑rows of the mask – each block contains only “good’’ rows
    blocks = hsplit(mask_grid, size(mask_grid))          # a tuple of blocks (each block is a grid)

    # 4. for each block, compute the most common original row and replace the whole block
    templated = apply(
            lambda blk: let(
                rows = [I[i] for i in range(start, start + height(blk))],
                tmpl = mostcommon(rows),
                tuple(apply(lambda _: tmpl, blk) ) ),
            enumerate(blocks))

    # 5. concatenate the processed blocks back together
    O = vconcat(*templated)
    return O
```

```python
    # ------- ROW‑TEMPLATE (most frequent non‑8 row) -------
    # rows that contain any non‑zero cell and no colour 8
    good = apply(lambda r: any(c != 0 for c in r) and not any(c == 8 for c in r), I)

    cand = apply(lambda r, g: r if g else None, I, good)

    tmpl = mostcommon(kept)

    O = apply(lambda r, g: tmpl if g else r, I, good)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ------- OBJECT‑EXTRACTION (colour 8) + TEMPLATE‑OVERLAY -------
    # colour 8 objects stay untouched
    objs_8   = colorfilter(objects(I, True, False, True), 8)

    # rows that are non‑zero and do not contain 8
    good = apply(lambda r: any(c != 0 for c in r) and not any(c == 8 for c in r), I)
    cand = apply(lambda r, g: r if g else None, I, good)
    kept = sfilter(cand, lambda x: x is not None)

    # most common such row – will be turned into a 1‑row object
    tmpl_row = mostcommon(kept)

    # turn the template row into an object (its cells keep their colours)
    tmpl_obj = toobject({(0, j) for j in range(width(I))}, tuple([tmpl_row]))

    # shift the template object to every row that satisfied the “good’’ condition
    rows = ofcolor(I, 0)                     # all background cells
    good_rows = ofcolor(I, 0)                # placeholder, will be replaced below
    # build a patch containing the indices of all rows that are “good’’
    good_patch = sfilter(ofcolor(I, 0),          # background cells
                         lambda p: any(I[p[0]][c] != 0 for c in range(width(I))) and
                                   not any(I[p[0]][c] == 8 for c in range(width(I))))
    # move the 1‑row object to each of those rows
    over = mapply(lambda r: move(I, tmpl_obj, (r[0], 0)), good_patch)

    # paint the moved objects on top of the original grid, then restore the 8‑objects
    O = paint(I, merge(over))
    O = paint(O, merge(objs_8))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ------- RELATIONAL‑ADJACENCY (touch ≥ 2 other rows) -------
    # treat each row as a “patch’’ and count how many other rows it touches
    rows = apply(lambda r: {(i, j) for j, v in enumerate(r) if v != 0},
                 I)                               # set of occupied cells per row

    # keep rows that touch at least two other rows (i.e. belong to a “band’’)
    keep = sfilter(rows, lambda p: adj_cnt(p) >= 2)

    # build a mask from the kept rows
    mask = merge(keep)

    # paint the mask on a blank canvas, preserving colour 8 objects
    O = paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), mask)
    O = paint(O, merge(colorfilter(objects(I, True, False, True), 8)))
    return O
```

```python
    # ----- KEEP COLOURS THAT OCCUPY ≥ 5 % OF THE GRID -----
    total   = size(asindices(I))                                 # total number of cells
```

```python
    # ----- KEEP CELLS THAT HAVE AT LEAST TWO NON‑ZERO NEIGHBOURS -----
    # all non‑zero cells of the grid

    O = paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), keep)
    O = paint(O, merge(colorfilter(objects(I, True, False, True), 8)))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC – compute the union of all bounding‑boxes that contain a non‑8 colour;
    # every row intersecting that union is filled with the most common non‑8 row,
    # 8‑objects are painted back afterwards.
    zero_grid    = canvas(0, shape(I))
    non8         = sfilter(palette(I), lambda c: c != 0 and c != 8)
    mask_cells   = merge(mapply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), non8))
    outb_union   = merge(mapply(outbox, objects(mask_cells, True, False, True)))
    rows_set     = { (r, 0) for (r, _) in outb_union }                 # rows intersecting any non‑8 box
    rows_lines   = merge(mapply(lambda p: shoot(p, (0, 1)), rows_set))
    O0           = paint(zero_grid, rows_lines)                       # prototype rows only
    # paint the prototype row (most frequent) on those rows
    rows         = apply(identity, I)
    cand_rows    = mfilter(rows, lambda r: any(c != 0 and c != 8 for c in r))
    prot_row     = mostcommon(cand_rows)
    O1 = apply(lambda r: prot_row if any(c != 0 for c in r) else r, O0)
    objs8        = colorfilter(objects(I, True, False, True), 8)
    O            = paint(O1, merge(objs8))                             # restore 8‑objects
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # Global – rotate 180°, then overlay the original grid so the
    # original coloured cells stay in place while the rotated copy
    # draws the missing connecting lines.
    R = rot180(I)                                   # rotate whole picture
    G = canvas(0, shape(I))                         # empty canvas
    O = fill(G, 0, ofcolor(I, 0))                   # start from background
    O = fill(O, 0, ofcolor(R, 0))                   # keep background from both
    # overlay the two pictures; later colours (the rotated copy) will
    # fill the gaps between the original points.
    O = merge(apply(lambda c: fill(O, c, ofcolor(I, c)), remove(0, palette(I))))
    O = merge(apply(lambda c: fill(O, c, ofcolor(R, c)), remove(0, palette(R))))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # Relational – fill each colour’s axis‑aligned bounding box.
    # Process colours from the rarest to the most frequent so that the
    # most common colour (the “filler”) overwrites any overlaps.
    C = order(remove(0, palette(I)), lambda c: colorcount(I, c))      # rare → common
    G = canvas(0, shape(I))                                           # empty grid
    O = apply(
            lambda c: fill(G, c,
                           backdrop(toobject(ofcolor(I, c), I))),
            C)
    return merge(O)
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ── Global – fill every colour’s axis‑aligned bounding box.
    #   Boxes are drawn in order of decreasing area so that the larger
    #   box (the “bridge”) overwrites the smaller one.
    C   = order(remove(0, palette(I)),
                lambda c: -( (lowermost(toobject(ofcolor(I, c), I)) -
                               uppermost(toobject(ofcolor(I, c), I)) + 1) *
                             (rightmost(toobject(ofcolor(I, c), I)) -
                               leftmost (toobject(ofcolor(I, c), I)) + 1))
    G   = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O   = apply(lambda c: fill(G, c,
                               backdrop(toobject(ofcolor(I, c), I))),
                C)
    return merge(O)
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ---------- Global symmetry expansion ----------
    # 1. Gather every non‑zero cell.
    colors   = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    nz_patch = apply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), colors)
    nz_patch = combine(*nz_patch)                       # all colored indices together
    # 2. Compute the bounding box of the whole pattern.
    bb       = backdrop(nz_patch)
    # 3. Mirror the patch across the vertical and horizontal axes of the box.
    hmir     = hmirror(nz_patch)
    vmir     = vmirror(nz_patch)
    hvmir    = hmirror(vmir)
    # 4. Combine original and mirrored patches.
    full     = combine(nz_patch, hmir, vmir, hvmir)
    # 5. Paint the combined patch on a fresh canvas.
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = paint(O, full)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ---------- Object‑centric expansion ----------
    # 1. Identify the two non‑zero colors.
    colors   = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    c1, c2  = tuple(colors)                       # two colors present
    # 2. Treat the less frequent one as the “center” colour.
    cnt1     = colorcount(I, c1)
    cnt2     = colorcount(I, c2)
    cen_col  = branch(greater(cnt2, cnt1), c1, c2)
    arm_col  = branch(equal(cen_col, c1), c2, c1)
    # 3. Sets of centre and arm cells.
    cen      = ofcolor(I, cen_col)
    arm      = ofcolor(I, arm_col)
    # 4. Build the expanded pattern by shifting.
    #    – arms keep their colour, extended two steps orthogonally.
    arm_exp  = combine(arm,
                       shift(arm, ( 2, 0)),
                       shift(arm, (-2, 0)),
                       shift(arm, ( 0, 2)),
                       shift(arm, ( 0,-2)))
    #    – centres keep their colour, added at the four diagonal corners.
    cen_exp  = combine(cen,
                       shift(cen, ( 2, 2)),
                       shift(cen, ( 2,-2)),
                       shift(cen, (-2, 2)),
                       shift(cen, (-2,-2)))
    # 5. Paint the two expanded patches on a clean canvas.
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, arm_col, arm_exp)
    O = fill(O, cen_col, cen_exp)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ---------- Colour‑filtering + dilation ----------
    # 1. Keep only the most frequent non‑zero colour (the arm colour).
    nonzero   = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    most_col = mostcommon(nonzero)
    arms      = ofcolor(I, most_col)
    # 2. Dilate the arm colour with a 5×5 square structuring element.
    dilated   = combine(arms,
                       shift(arms, ( 1, 0)), shift(arms, (-1, 0)),
                       shift(arms, ( 0, 1)), shift(arms, ( 0,-1)),
                       shift(arms, ( 2, 0)), shift(arms, (-2, 0)),
                       shift(arms, ( 0, 2)), shift(arms, ( 0,-2)),
                       shift(arms, ( 1, 1)), shift(arms, ( 1,-1)),
                       shift(arms, (-1, 1)), shift(arms, (-1,-1)),
                       shift(arms, ( 2, 2)), shift(arms, ( 2,-2)),
                       shift(arms, (-2, 2)), shift(arms, (-2,-2)))
    # 3. Re‑colour the original centre cells (the other colour) with the same colour
    #    as they appear in the input, but only at the four diagonal corners.
    all_cols = list(nonzero)
    cen_col  = branch(equal(all_cols[0], most_col), all_cols[1], all_cols[0])
    centres  = ofcolor(I, cen_col)
    corners  = combine(shift(centres, ( 2, 2)), shift(centres, ( 2,-2)),
                       shift(centres, (-2, 2)), shift(centres, (-2,-2)))
    # 4. Assemble final grid.
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, most_col, dilated)
    O = fill(O, cen_col, corners)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ---------- Geometric reasoning via centres ----------
    # 1. Extract every distinct non‑zero object (single‑cell objects).
    objs      = fgpartition(I)                       # each coloured cell as its own object
    # 2. For each object compute its centre (its own coordinate).
    centres   = apply(lambda o: center(o), objs)
    # 3. Build a 5×5 “cross‑plus‑corners” pattern centred on each centre.
    pattern   = lambda p: combine(
                  p,
                  shift(p, ( 0, 1)), shift(p, ( 0,-1)),
                  shift(p, ( 1, 0)), shift(p, (-1, 0)),
                  shift(p, ( 0, 2)), shift(p, ( 0,-2)),
                  shift(p, ( 2, 0)), shift(p, (-2, 0)),
                  shift(p, ( 2, 2)), shift(p, ( 2,-2)),
                  shift(p, (-2, 2)), shift(p, (-2,-2)))
    pat_set   = apply(lambda c: pattern({c}), centres)   # each centre treated as a one‑cell patch
    # 4. Merge all pattern cells together.
    all_pat   = combine(*pat_set)
    # 5. Paint using the original colour of each centre.
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    for c in centres:
        col = index(I, c)                 # colour at that centre
        O   = fill(O, col, pattern({c}))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---------- Relational reasoning – cross detection ----------
    # 1. Detect every cell that has exactly four orthogonal neighbours of a different colour.
    nonzero   = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    cand      = apply(lambda col: ofcolor(I, col), nonzero)
    cand      = combine(*cand)
    #   cells whose orthogonal neighbours are all present and of a single other colour.
    is_center = lambda pt: (
        let( neigh = dneighbors(pt),
             colours = apply(lambda p: index(I, p), neigh),
             uniq = set(colours),
             same  = sizefilter(uniq, 1) and (next(iter(uniq)) != index(I,pt))
        ))
    centres   = filter(is_center, cand)               # abstract – uses higher‑order filter
    # 2. For each centre, paint the expanded 5×5 motif.
    arm_col   = lambda pt: let(colours = apply(lambda p: index(I, p), dneighbors(pt)),
                             mostcommon(colours))
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    for c in centres:
        acol = arm_col(c)
        ccol = index(I, c)
        # colour arms (and their extensions)
        arm = combine({c},
                     shift({c}, (0,1)), shift({c}, (0,-1)),
                     shift({c}, (1,0)), shift({c}, (-1,0)),
                     shift({c}, (0,2)), shift({c}, (0,-2)),
                     shift({c}, (2,0)), shift({c}, (-2,0)))
        O = fill(O, acol, arm)
        # colour corners
        corners = combine(shift({c}, ( 2, 2)), shift({c}, ( 2,-2)),
                        shift({c}, (-2, 2)), shift({c}, (-2,-2)))
        O = fill(O, ccol, corners)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ---------- Global symmetry expansion ----------
    # 1. all non‑zero cells
    colors   = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    nz_patch = apply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), colors)
    nz_patch = combine(nz_patch, apply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), colors))   # union of both colour patches

    vmir  = vmirror(nz_patch)

    step1 = combine(nz_patch, hmir)
    step2 = combine(step1,   vmir)
    full  = combine(step2,   hvmir)
    # 4. paint
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = paint(O, full)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ---------- Object‑centric expansion (frequency based) ----------
    colors = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    c1, c2 = tuple(colors)                       # two colours present
    cnt1   = colorcount(I, c1)
    cnt2   = colorcount(I, c2)

    cen_col = branch(greater(cnt1, cnt2), c2, c1)
    arm_col = branch(greater(cnt1, cnt2), c1, c2)
    cen   = ofcolor(I, cen_col)
    arm   = ofcolor(I, arm_col)

    # arms expanded two steps orthogonally
    arm_e1 = combine(arm, shift(arm, ( 2, 0)))
    arm_e2 = combine(arm_e1, shift(arm, (-2, 0)))
    arm_e3 = combine(arm_e2, shift(arm, ( 0, 2)))
    arm_exp = combine(arm_e3, shift(arm, ( 0,-2)))

    # centres copied to the four diagonal corners
    cen_e1 = combine(cen, shift(cen, ( 2, 2)))
    cen_e2 = combine(cen_e1, shift(cen, ( 2,-2)))
    cen_e3 = combine(cen_e2, shift(cen, (-2, 2)))
    cen_exp = combine(cen_e3, shift(cen, (-2,-2)))

    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, arm_col, arm_exp)
    O = fill(O, cen_col, cen_exp)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ---------- Colour‑filtering + dilation ----------
    # most frequent colour = arm colour
    nonzero   = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    arm_col   = argmax(nonzero, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    cen_col   = first(difference(nonzero, initset(arm_col)))   # the other colour
    arms      = ofcolor(I, arm_col)

    # dilate arms up to distance 2 orthogonally
    a1 = combine(arms, shift(arms, ( 1, 0)))
    a2 = combine(a1,   shift(arms, (-1, 0)))
    a3 = combine(a2,   shift(arms, ( 0, 1)))
    a4 = combine(a3,   shift(arms, ( 0,-1)))
    a5 = combine(a4,   shift(arms, ( 2, 0)))
    a6 = combine(a5,   shift(arms, (-2, 0)))
    a7 = combine(a6,   shift(arms, ( 0, 2)))
    dilated = combine(a7,   shift(arms, ( 0,-2)))

    # corners from centre colour
    cen      = ofcolor(I, cen_col)
    c1 = combine(shift(cen, ( 2, 2)), shift(cen, ( 2,-2)))
    c2 = combine(c1, shift(cen, (-2, 2)))
    corners = combine(c2, shift(cen, (-2,-2)))

    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, arm_col, dilated)
    O = fill(O, cen_col, corners)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ---------- Per‑colour mirroring ----------
    colors = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    c1, c2 = tuple(colors)

    # patch for colour 1 and its mirrors
    p1   = ofcolor(I, c1)
    p1h  = hmirror(p1)
    p1v  = vmirror(p1)
    p1hv = hmirror(p1v)
    patch1 = combine(combine(combine(p1, p1h), p1v), p1hv)

    # patch for colour 2 and its mirrors

    p2h  = hmirror(p2)
    p2v  = vmirror(p2)
    p2hv = hmirror(p2v)
    patch2 = combine(combine(combine(p2, p2h), p2v), p2hv)

    # union of both mirrored patches
    full = combine(patch1, patch2)

    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = paint(O, full)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---------- Crop → global symmetry → embed ----------
    # 1. all non‑zero cells
    colors   = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    nz_patch = combine(apply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), colors),
                       apply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), colors))
    # 2. bounding box of the pattern
    bb       = backdrop(nz_patch)                     # set of indices of the box
    ul       = ulcorner(bb)                          # upper‑left corner of the box
    sz       = shape(subgrid(I, bb))                  # height/width of the box
    # 3. crop to the bounding box
    crop_grid = crop(I, ul, sz)
    # 4. apply global symmetry inside the crop (identical to dsl1 but on the cropped grid)
    colors_c = difference(palette(crop_grid), initset(0))
    nz_c    = apply(lambda c: ofcolor(crop_grid, c), colors_c)
    nz_c    = combine(nz_c, apply(lambda c: ofcolor(crop_grid, c), colors_c))
    hmir_c  = hmirror(nz_c)
    vmir_c  = vmirror(nz_c)
    hvmir_c = hmirror(vmir_c)
    step1_c = combine(nz_c, hmir_c)
    step2_c = combine(step1_c, vmir_c)
    full_c  = combine(step2_c, hvmir_c)

    # 5. embed the expanded pattern back into the original canvas
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    # paint only inside the original bounding box
    O = fill(O, 0, bb)                    # clear the box area
    O = paint(O, full_c)                  # paint the symmetrised patch
    return O
```

```python
    O = fill(O, arm_col, arm_exp)
    O = fill(O, cen_col, cen_exp)
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ----------- centre‑parity expansion (even offsets) ----------
    colors = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    c1, c2 = tuple(colors)
    cnt1   = colorcount(I, c1)
    cnt2   = colorcount(I, c2)

    cen_col = branch(greater(cnt1, cnt2), c2, c1)
    arm_col = branch(greater(cnt1, cnt2), c1, c2)

    cen = ofcolor(I, cen_col)
    arm = ofcolor(I, arm_col)

    # centre appears on every cell whose row and column offsets from the centre are even
    cen_exp = combine(cen,
               shift(cen, ( 2, 0)), shift(cen, (-2, 0)),
               shift(cen, ( 0, 2)), shift(cen, ( 0,-2)),
               shift(cen, ( 2, 2)), shift(cen, ( 2,-2)),
               shift(cen, (-2, 2)), shift(cen, (-2,-2)))

    # arm appears on the same row or column as the centre, any distance ≤2
    arm_exp = combine(arm,
               shift(cen, ( 2, 0)), shift(cen, (-2, 0)),
               shift(cen, ( 0, 2)), shift(cen, ( 0,-2)),
               shift(cen, ( 1, 0)), shift(cen, (-1, 0)),
               shift(cen, ( 0, 1)), shift(cen, ( 0,-1)))

    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, arm_col, arm_exp)
    O = fill(O, cen_col, cen_exp)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ----------- arm dilation + orthogonal filter ----------
    colors = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    c1, c2 = tuple(colors)
    cnt1   = colorcount(I, c1)
    cnt2   = colorcount(I, c2)

    cen_col = branch(greater(cnt1, cnt2), c2, c1)
    arm_col = branch(greater(cnt1, cnt2), c1, c2)

    cen = ofcolor(I, cen_col)
    arm = ofcolor(I, arm_col)

    # dilate arms to Manhattan distance 2 (full diamond)
    dil = combine(combine(combine(combine(combine(combine(combine(arm,
               shift(arm, ( 1, 0))), shift(arm, (-1, 0))),
               shift(arm, ( 0, 1))), shift(arm, ( 0,-1))),
               shift(arm, ( 2, 0))), shift(arm, (-2, 0))),
               shift(arm, ( 0, 2))), shift(arm, ( 0,-2)))

    # keep only cells that share row or column with the original centre
    orth = combine(shift(cen, ( 2, 0)), shift(cen, (-2, 0)),
                   shift(cen, ( 0, 2)), shift(cen, ( 0,-2)),
                   shift(cen, ( 1, 0)), shift(cen, (-1, 0)),
                   shift(cen, ( 0, 1)), shift(cen, ( 0,-1)),
                   cen)

    arm_exp = intersection(dil, orth)

    # centre copies on the four diagonal corners (step = 2)
    cen_exp = combine(cen,
               shift(cen, ( 2, 2)),
               shift(cen, ( 2,-2)),
               shift(cen, (-2, 2)),
               shift(cen, (-2,-2)))

    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, arm_col, arm_exp)
    O = fill(O, cen_col, cen_exp)
    return O
```
