```python
                combine(shift(p2, (h, 0)), shift(p2, (h, w)))
              )

    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, c1, p1_full)
    O = fill(O, c2, p2_full)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ---------- 2️⃣  crop → concatenate → embed ----------
    c1, c2 = tuple(difference(palette(I), initset(0)))

    # whole non‑zero bounding box
    nz   = combine(ofcolor(I, c1), ofcolor(I, c2))
    bb   = backdrop(nz)
    ul   = ulcorner(bb)                     # upper‑left corner of the pattern
    sz   = shape(subgrid(I, bb))            # (h, w)

    # isolate the pattern (both colours) as a sub‑grid
    pat = crop(I, ul, sz)

    # make a 2×2 tiling of that sub‑grid (no mirroring)
    pat_h = hconcat(pat, pat)               # horizontal repeat
    pat_2x2 = vconcat(pat_h, pat_h)         # vertical repeat

    # bring the tiled pattern back to its original location
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    # colour‑by‑colour filling of the tiled grid
    O = fill(O, c1, shift(ofcolor(pat_2x2, c1), ul))
    O = fill(O, c2, shift(ofcolor(pat_2x2, c2), ul))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ---------- 3️⃣  functional offset generation ----------
    c1, c2 = tuple(difference(palette(I), initset(0)))

    # bounding box
    nz = combine(ofcolor(I, c1), ofcolor(I, c2))
    bb = backdrop(nz)
    h, w = shape(subgrid(I, bb))

    # list of the four displacement vectors
    offs = initset((0, 0), (0, w), (h, 0), (h, w))

    # helper: given a colour, produce the union of its four shifted copies
    def tile(col):
        base = ofcolor(I, col)
        shifted = apply(lambda o: shift(base, o), offs)   # container of 4 patches
        # fold the container with combine (binary)
        acc = first(shifted)
        rest = apply(lambda p: p, shifted)                # dummy to keep type‑checker happy
        # combine all elements (pairwise)
        def fold(a, b): return combine(a, b)
        return rapply(fold, shifted)                      # rapply folds left‑to‑right
    # above rapply works because combine takes two arguments

    p1_full = tile(c1)
    p2_full = tile(c2)

    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, c1, p1_full)
    O = fill(O, c2, p2_full)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ---------- 4️⃣  move‑based duplication ----------
    c1, c2 = tuple(difference(palette(I), initset(0)))

    # full non‑zero bounding box
    nz   = combine(ofcolor(I, c1), ofcolor(I, c2))
    bb   = backdrop(nz)
    h, w = shape(subgrid(I, bb))

    # start from the original grid (contains the pattern once)
    O = I

    # duplicate each colour by moving its original patch
    O = move(O, ofcolor(I, c1), (0, w))
    O = move(O, ofcolor(I, c1), (h, 0))
    O = move(O, ofcolor(I, c1), (h, w))

    O = move(O, ofcolor(I, c2), (0, w))
    O = move(O, ofcolor(I, c2), (h, 0))
    O = move(O, ofcolor(I, c2), (h, w))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---------- 5️⃣  overlay with cover ----------
    c1, c2 = tuple(difference(palette(I), initset(0)))

    nz   = combine(ofcolor(I, c1), ofcolor(I, c2))
    bb   = backdrop(nz)

    # start from a blank canvas
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))

    # original patches
    p1 = ofcolor(I, c1)
    p2 = ofcolor(I, c2)

    # place original patches
    O = fill(O, c1, p1)
    O = fill(O, c2, p2)

    # place shifted copies and remove possible overlaps with cover
    O = cover(O, shift(p1, (0, w)))
    O = cover(O, shift(p1, (h, 0)))
    O = cover(O, shift(p1, (h, w)))

    O = cover(O, shift(p2, (0, w)))
    O = cover(O, shift(p2, (h, 0)))
    O = cover(O, shift(p2, (h, w)))

    # finally colour the newly added cells (cover only removes background, we need to repaint)
    O = fill(O, c1, combine(shift(p1, (0, w)),
                         shift(p1, (h, 0)),
                         shift(p1, (h, w))))
    O = fill(O, c2, combine(shift(p2, (0, w)),
                         shift(p2, (h, 0)),
                         shift(p2, (h, w))))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # 2️⃣  Per‑colour shift‑tiling (explicit displacement of each colour)
    c1, c2 = tuple(difference(palette(I), initset(0)))
    nz = combine(ofcolor(I, c1), ofcolor(I, c2))
    bb = backdrop(nz)
    h, w = shape(subgrid(I, bb))

    def tile(col):
        base = ofcolor(I, col)
        # four copies shifted by (0,0), (0,w), (h,0), (h,w)
        return combine(
            combine(base, shift(base, (0, w))),
            combine(shift(base, (h, 0)), shift(base, (h, w)))
        )

    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, c1, tile(c1))
    O = fill(O, c2, tile(c2))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ---------- core idea ----------
    # 1️⃣  Find the two non‑background colours.
    # 2️⃣  The most frequent is the “primary” colour, the other (or SIX) is the “secondary”.
    # 3️⃣  Tile the primary colour by four orthogonal shifts of the pattern’s bounding‑box.
    # 4️⃣  Fill every cell inside the tiled bounding‑box that is still empty with the secondary colour.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    cols      = difference(palette(I), initset(0))                 # non‑zero colours
    prim      = argmax(cols, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))           # most common colour
    sec0      = other(cols, prim)                                 # the other colour (if any)
    sec       = branch(equality(sec0, prim), SIX, sec0)           # default to colour 6
    prim_pat  = ofcolor(I, prim)                                 # primary‑colour cells
    bb        = backdrop(prim_pat)                               # its bounding box
    h, w     = shape(subgrid(I, bb))                             # height & width of the pattern
    # four shifted copies of the primary pattern
    tiled = combine(combine(prim_pat,
                             shift(prim_pat, (0, w))),
                     combine(shift(prim_pat, (h, 0)),
                             shift(prim_pat, (h, w))))
    # cells inside the tiled area that are still background
    gap = difference(backdrop(tiled), tiled)
    # paint result
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, prim, tiled)
    O = fill(O, sec,  gap)
    return O
```

```python
    # ---------- mirroring replication ----------
    # Extract the minimal pattern (both colours),
    # mirror it horizontally and vertically, then assemble the four quadrants.
    cols = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    nz   = combine(ofcolor(I, argmax(cols, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))),
                  ofcolor(I, other(cols, argmax(cols, lambda c: colorcount(I, c)))))
    bb   = backdrop(nz)
    pat  = crop(I, ulcorner(bb), shape(subgrid(I, bb)))          # minimal pattern
    pat_h = hmirror(pat)

    pat_hv = hmirror(pat_v)
    top   = hconcat(pat, pat_h)
    bot   = hconcat(pat_v, pat_hv)
    full  = vconcat(top, bot)
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, color(pat), ofcolor(full, color(pat)))
    O = fill(O, other(cols, color(pat)), ofcolor(full, other(cols, color(pat))))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ---------- periodic‑tiling ----------
    # Determine the pattern’s vertical and horizontal periods,
    # then repeat the whole pattern by those periods.
    cols = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    prim = argmax(cols, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    sec  = other(cols, prim)
    pat  = ofcolor(I, prim)                     # we tile only the primary colour
    hper = vperiod(pat)                         # vertical period (pattern height)
    wper = hperiod(pat)                         # horizontal period (pattern width)
    # four orthogonal translations of the primary patch
    tiled = combine(combine(pat,
                             shift(pat, (0, wper))),
                     combine(shift(pat, (hper, 0)),
                             shift(pat, (hper, wper))))
    # cells that remain empty inside the tiled rectangle become secondary colour
    gap = difference(backdrop(tiled), tiled)
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, prim, tiled)
    O = fill(O, sec,  gap)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ---------- object‑wise shift‑tiling ----------
    # Treat the whole multi‑colour object as one piece and shift it.
    cols = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    obj  = combine(ofcolor(I, argmax(cols, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))),
                   ofcolor(I, other(cols, argmax(cols, lambda c: colorcount(I, c)))))
    bb   = backdrop(obj)
    h, w = shape(subgrid(I, bb))
    # four copies of the whole object
    p0 = obj
    p1 = shift(obj, (0, w))
    p2 = shift(obj, (h, 0))
    p3 = shift(obj, (h, w))
    tiled = combine(combine(p0, p1), combine(p2, p3))
    # fill the gaps with the secondary colour (or SIX if missing)
    sec0 = other(cols, argmax(cols, lambda c: colorcount(I, c)))
    sec  = branch(equality(sec0, initset(0)), SIX, sec0)
    gap = difference(backdrop(tiled), tiled)
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, argmax(cols, lambda c: colorcount(I, c)), tiled)
    O = fill(O, sec, gap)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---------- upscale‑then‑mask ----------
    # Upscale the minimal pattern by factor 2, then keep only the cells
    # that belong to the original colours; the newly created cells become
    # the secondary colour.
    cols   = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    prim   = argmax(cols, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    sec0   = other(cols, prim)
    sec    = branch(equality(sec0, prim), SIX, sec0)
    obj    = combine(ofcolor(I, prim), ofcolor(I, sec0))
    bb     = backdrop(obj)
    pat    = crop(I, ulcorner(bb), shape(subgrid(I, bb)))      # minimal pattern
    pat2x  = hupscale(pat, 2)                                 # horizontal upscale
    pat2x  = vupscale(pat2x, 2)                               # vertical upscale → 2×2 tiling
    # cells that were created by up‑scaling (i.e. not present in the original pattern)
    extra  = difference(backdrop(pat2x), combine(ofcolor(pat2x, prim),
                                                      ofcolor(pat2x, sec0)))
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, prim, ofcolor(pat2x, prim))
    O = fill(O, sec,  extra)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # upscale the minimal pattern (both colours) by 2×2, then keep only the original colours;
    # the newly created cells become the secondary colour (or 6 if missing)
    cols   = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    prim   = argmax(cols, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    sec0   = other(cols, prim)
    sec    = branch(equality(sec0, initset(0)), SIX, sec0)

    pat_cells = combine(ofcolor(I, prim), ofcolor(I, sec0))
    bb        = backdrop(pat_cells)

    # crop the pattern without using the buggy subgrid primitive:
    top   = uppermost(bb)
    left  = leftmost(bb)
    h = subtract(add(lowermost(bb), top), ONE)          # height
    w = subtract(add(rightmost(bb),  ONE), left)        # width
    # extract the pattern by shifting its cells to the origin
    pat   = shift(pat_cells, (-top, -left))

    # upscale 2× vertically and horizontally
    pat2  = vupscale(hupscale(pat, 2), 2)

    extra = difference(backdrop(pat2),
                       combine(ofcolor(pat2, prim), ofcolor(pat2, sec0)))

    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, prim, ofcolor(pat2, prim))
    O = fill(O, sec,  extra)
    return O
```

```python
    # with the secondary colour (or 6 if the secondary colour is absent)
    cols   = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    prim   = argmax(cols, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    sec0   = other(cols, prim)
    sec    = branch(equality(sec0, initset(0)), SIX, sec0)

    all_cells = combine(ofcolor(I, prim), ofcolor(I, sec0))
    bb        = backdrop(all_cells)

    interior = difference(bb, all_cells)          # background cells inside the bbox
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, prim, ofcolor(I, prim))
    O = fill(O, sec,  interior)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # -------------------  OBJECT‑WISE TILING (RELATIONAL) -------------------
    # most frequent non‑zero colour = primary, the other = secondary (or 6)
    prim = argmax(difference(palette(I), initset(0)),
                  lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    sec0 = other(difference(palette(I), initset(0)), prim)
    sec  = branch(equality(sec0, initset(0)), SIX, sec0)

    # split the picture into its foreground objects
    objs = fgpartition(I)                     # each object = set of (col,(i,j))

    # tile one object
    def tile_one(o):
        idx      = toindices(o)                       # plain indices
        prim_pat = intersection(idx, ofcolor(I, prim)) # primary cells of this object
        bb       = backdrop(idx)                       # its bounding box
        h = subtract(add(lowermost(bb), ONE), uppermost(bb))
        w = subtract(add(rightmost(bb), ONE), leftmost(bb))

        tiled = combine(combine(prim_pat,
                                 shift(prim_pat, (0, w))),
                        combine(shift(prim_pat, (h, 0)),
                                 shift(prim_pat, (h, w))))
        gap   = difference(backdrop(tiled), tiled)     # cells that become secondary
        prim_obj = recolor(prim, tiled)
        sec_obj  = recolor(sec , gap)
        return combine(prim_obj, sec_obj)

    # apply to every object and merge the recoloured pieces
    objs_recoloured = merge(apply(tile_one, objs))

    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = paint(O, objs_recoloured)
    return O
```

```python
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = paint(O, recoloured)
    return O
```

```python
    # -------------------  UPSCALE MINIMAL PATTERN (GLOBAL) -------------------
    prim = argmax(difference(palette(I), initset(0)),
                  lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    sec0 = other(difference(palette(I), initset(0)), prim)
    sec  = branch(equality(sec0, initset(0)), SIX, sec0)

    # crop the smallest non‑zero pattern present in the whole picture
    all_pat = combine(ofcolor(I, prim), ofcolor(I, sec0))
    bb      = backdrop(all_pat)
    top     = uppermost(bb)
    left    = leftmost(bb)
    pat     = shift(all_pat, (-top, -left))          # move to origin

    # 2× upscale in both directions
    pat2    = vupscale(hupscale(pat, 2), 2)

    # keep original colours, everything else becomes secondary
    extra   = difference(backdrop(pat2),
                         combine(ofcolor(pat2, prim), ofcolor(pat2, sec0)))
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, prim, ofcolor(pat2, prim))
    O = fill(O, sec , extra)
    return O
```

```python
    prim = argmax(difference(palette(I), initset(0)),
                  lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    sec0 = other(difference(palette(I), initset(0)), prim)
```
```python
    sec   = branch(equality(sec0, initset(0)), SIX, sec0)
```

```python
    objs = fgpartition(I)
```

```python
        r180 = rot180(prim_obj)

                        combine(r270, r180))
        gap   = difference(backdrop(tiled), tiled)
        return combine(recolor(prim, tiled), recolor(sec, gap))

    recol = merge(apply(mirror_one, objs))
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = paint(O, recol)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL PERIODIC TILING OF THE MINIMAL NON‑ZERO PATTERN
    prim = argmax(difference(palette(I), initset(0)),
                  lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    sec0 = other(difference(palette(I), initset(0)), prim)
    sec  = branch(equality(sec0, initset(0)), SIX, sec0)

    # minimal pattern (all non‑zero cells)
    pat   = combine(ofcolor(I, prim), ofcolor(I, sec0))

    # horizontal / vertical periods of that pattern
    hp    = hperiod(pat)
    vp    = vperiod(pat)

    # all shifts that tile the whole canvas
    hs    = interval(0, width(I), hp)
    vs    = interval(0, height(I), vp)

    # shifted copies of the pattern
    shifted = mapply(lambda dv, dh: shift(pat, (dv, dh)), vs, hs)

    # union of all copies
    tiled = merge(shifted)

    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, prim, ofcolor(tiled, prim))
    O = fill(O, sec , ofcolor(tiled, sec))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑WISE SCALING OF EACH OBJECT'S PRIMARY SHAPE TO ITS BBOX
    prim = argmax(difference(palette(I), initset(0)),
                  lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    sec0 = other(difference(palette(I), initset(0)), prim)
    sec  = branch(equality(sec0, initset(0)), SIX, sec0)

    objs = fgpartition(I)

    def scale_one(o):
        idx      = toindices(o)
        bb       = backdrop(idx)                     # object's bounding box
        prim_pat = intersection(idx, ofcolor(I, prim))   # primary cells only
        # extract as a grid, upscale to the size of the bbox, then recolor
        pat_grid = subgrid(prim_pat, I)
        hs       = divide(width(bb), width(pat_grid))
        vs       = divide(height(bb), height(pat_grid))
        big      = vupscale(hupscale(pat_grid, vs), hs)
        # paint the scaled primary shape back, fill the rest of the bbox with secondary
        result   = combine(recolor(prim, ofcolor(big, prim)),
                          recolor(sec , difference(backdrop(big), ofcolor(big, prim))))
        return result

    tiled = merge(apply(scale_one, objs))
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = paint(O, tiled)
    return O
```

```python
        hp       = hperiod(prim_pat)
        vp       = vperiod(prim_pat)

        hs       = interval(0, width(bb), hp)
        vs       = interval(0, height(bb), vp)

        shifted  = mapply(lambda dv, dh: shift(prim_pat, (dv, dh)), vs, hs)
        tiled    = merge(shifted)

        # paint tiled primary, fill remaining cells of the object's bbox with secondary
        result   = combine(recolor(prim, ofcolor(tiled, prim)),
                          recolor(sec , difference(backdrop(tiled), ofcolor(tiled, prim))))
        return result

    recol = merge(apply(tile_one, objs))
    O = canvas(0, shape(I))
    O = paint(O, recol)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ⑤ Relational – find pairs of adjacent objects of the same colour,
    #     colour‑merge them, then return the resulting picture.
    bg      = mostcolor(I)
    objs    = fgobjects(I, univalued=True, diagonal=False)
    # pick every pair of objects that share the same colour and are adjacent
    pairs   = { (a,b) for a in objs for b in objs
                if a is not b
                and color(a) == color(b)
                and adjacent({a},{b}) }
    # merge each pair into a single recoloured object (colour = original colour + 1)
    merged  = { recolor(add(color(a), ONE), a | b) for (a,b) in pairs }
    # paint all merged objects over the original grid
    O = I
    for m in merged:
        O = paint(O, m)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # Global aggregation – counts of all non‑background colours above a fixed threshold,
    # sorted descending.
    bg      = mostcolor(I)                                            # background colour
    colors  = difference(palette(I), initset(bg))                     # other colours
    counts  = apply(lambda c: colorcount(I, c), colors)              # multiset of counts
    thresh  = 100                                                    # ignore small colours
    filt    = mfilter(counts, lambda n: n > thresh)                  # keep large colours
    sorted  = order(filt, lambda n: -n)                               # descending order
    O       = totuple(sorted)                                         # tuple of results
    return O
```

```python
    # Object‑extraction – for each foreground object compute its size,
    # keep objects larger than a size threshold, then report the distinct sizes
    # in descending order.
    bg      = mostcolor(I)
    objs    = objects(I, True, False, True)                           # foreground objects
    big     = { o for o in objs if size(o) > 150 }                    # large objects only
    sizes   = apply(lambda o: size(o), big)                           # their sizes
    uniq    = set(sizes)                                              # distinct sizes
    sorted  = order(initset(*uniq), lambda n: -n)                      # descending
    O       = totuple(sorted)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # Colour‑filter – replace background with 0, then count remaining colours,
    # keep only those whose count exceeds the mean of all non‑background counts,
    # and output the counts sorted descending.
    bg          = mostcolor(I)
    switched    = switch(I, bg, 0)                                    # make bg zero
    cols        = difference(palette(switched), initset(0))            # colours present
    cnts_set    = apply(lambda c: colorcount(switched, c), cols)      # counts
    mean_cnt    = divide(add(*cnts_set), size(cnts_set))              # integer mean
    filtered    = mfilter(cnts_set, lambda n: n > mean_cnt)           # above‑mean
    sorted_cnt  = order(filtered, lambda n: -n)                       # descending
    O           = totuple(sorted_cnt)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # Geometry – mirror across the main diagonal, keep the lower‑right triangle,
    # then count the colours that remain (non‑zero) and output their frequencies
    # sorted descending.
    M          = dmican = dmian = dm?  # placeholder to satisfy DSL syntax
    # (The geometric core is mirror and triangle mask; the rest is counting.)
    M          = dmirror(I)                                          # diagonal mirror
    idx        = asindices(M)
    mask       = {p for p in idx if p[0] >= p[1]}                     # lower‑right half
    masked     = fill(I, 0, mask)                                    # zero out others
    cols       = difference(palette(masked), initset(0))
    cnts       = apply(lambda c: colorcount(masked, c), cols)
    sorted_cnt = order(cnts, lambda n: -n)
    O          = totuple(sorted_cnt)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---------- Relational / object‑size list ----------
    # 1. Extract all foreground objects (individual connected components).
    # 2. Compute the size of each object.
    # 3. Sort the individual object sizes descending.
    bg   = mostcolor(I)
    objs = objects(I, True, False, True)            # all objects, separated by colour
    fg   = { o for o in objs if color(o) != bg }    # keep only foreground objects
    sizes = apply(lambda o: size(o), fg)
    sorted_s = order(sizes, lambda n: -n)
    O = totuple(sorted_s)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # relational / structural: rotate, compress (which removes the empty column
    # that became an empty row), then rotate back
    sep = first(
            extract(palette(I),
                    lambda c: both(vline(ofcolor(I, c)),
                                   size(ofcolor(I, c)) == height(I))))
    R = rot90(replace(I, sep, 0))   # column → row
    C = compress(R)                  # removes the empty row
    O = rot270(C)                    # rotate back to original orientation
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # Global cropping: locate the two full‑length separator objects, then cut the region
    # that is left of the vertical line and below the horizontal line.
    sep = extract(palette(I),
                  lambda c: either(equality(height(box(ofcolor(I, c))), height(I)),
                                   equality(width(box(ofcolor(I, c))), width(I))))
    # vertical separator (spans whole height)
    vert = extract(sfilter(fgpartition(I),
                           lambda o: both(equality(color(o), sep),
                                         equality(height(o), height(I)))),
                   lambda o: True)
    # horizontal separator (spans whole width)
    horz = extract(sfilter(fgpartition(I),
                           lambda o: both(equality(color(o), sep),
                                         equality(width(o), width(I)))),
                   lambda o: True)
    start = astuple(add(uppermost(horz), ONE), ZERO)
    dims  = astuple(subtract(height(I), add(uppermost(horz), ONE)), leftmost(vert))
    O = subgrid(I, start, dims)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # Object extraction: keep only objects that lie strictly below the horizontal
    # separator, then crop to their combined bounding box.
    sep = extract(palette(I),
                  lambda c: either(equality(height(box(ofcolor(I, c))), height(I)),
                                   equality(width(box(ofcolor(I, c))), width(I))))
    sep_objs = sfilter(fgpartition(I), lambda o: equality(color(o), sep))
    # horizontal separator (full‑width)
    horz = extract(sfilter(sep_objs,
                           lambda o: equality(width(o), width(I))),
                   lambda o: True)
    non_sep = sfilter(fgpartition(I), lambda o: color(o) != sep)
    below   = sfilter(non_sep,
                       lambda o: greater(lowermost(o), uppermost(horz)))
    merged  = merge(below)
    O = subgrid(box(merged), I)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Relational / structural: delete separator, keep non‑zero objects,
    # shift them to the origin, then crop and compress.
    sep = extract(palette(I),
                  lambda c: either(equality(height(box(ofcolor(I, c))), height(I)),
                                   equality(width(box(ofcolor(I, c))), width(I))))

    merged   = merge(non_zero)
    norm     = normalize(merged)
    O = compress(
            subgrid(I,
                     ulcorner(norm),
                     shape(norm)))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ---- Relational bounding‑box computed from extreme coordinates ----
    sep      = extract(palette(I),
                        lambda c: either(equality(height(box(ofcolor(I, c))), height(I)),
                                      equality(width(box(ofcolor(I, c))),  width(I))))
    cleaned  = replace(I, sep, 0)
    objs     = sfilter(fgpartition(cleaned), lambda o: color(o) != 0)
    merged   = merge(objs)

    top      = uppermost(merged)
    bottom   = lowermost(merged)
    left     = leftmost(merged)
    right    = rightmost(merged)

    dims     = astuple(add(subtract(bottom, top), ONE),
                       add(subtract(right, left), ONE))
    O        = subgrid(cleaned, start, dims)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---- Geometric trick: mirror, compress (removes empty borders), mirror back, trim ----
    sep = extract(palette(I),
                   lambda c: either(equality(height(box(ofcolor(I, c))), height(I)),
                                 equality(width(box(ofcolor(I, c))),  width(I))))
    erased   = replace(I, sep, 0)                                   # delete the cross
    mirrored = vmirror(erased)                                      # bring bottom zeros to top
    compact  = compress(mirrored)                                  # drop empty outer rows/cols
    unmirrored = vmirror(compact)                                   # restore original orientation
    O = trim(unmirrored)                                            # final border cleanup
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # colour that forms a full‑height or full‑width line (the separator)
    sep = extract(palette(I),
                  lambda c: either(equality(height(box(ofcolor(I, c))), height(I)),
                                 equality(width(box(ofcolor(I, c))),  width(I)))
    # erase the separator
    cleaned = replace(I, sep, 0)

    # bring the internal zero column to a border, compress, bring it back;
    # then do the same for a possible internal zero row.
    step1 = vmirror(cleaned)                     # vertical mirror
    step2 = compress(step1)                      # remove outer zero columns
    step3 = vmirror(step2)                       # restore orientation
    step4 = hmirror(step3)                        # horizontal mirror
    step5 = compress(step4)                      # remove outer zero rows
    step6 = hmirror(step5)                       # restore orientation

    O = trim(step6)                              # final border cleanup
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    sep = extract(palette(I),
                  lambda c: either(equality(height(box(ofcolor(I, c))), height(I)),
                                 equality(width(box(ofcolor(I, c))),  width(I)))
    cleaned   = replace(I, sep, 0)                         # erase separator
    sepcol    = leftmost(ofcolor(I, sep))                  # column index of the separator

    objs      = fgpartition(cleaned)                       # all coloured objects
    left_grp  = merge(sfilter(objs,
                               lambda o: rightmost(o) < sepcol))   # objects left of the line
    right_grp = merge(sfilter(objs,
                               lambda o: leftmost(o) > sepcol))    # objects right of the line

    # shift each side to the origin
    left_norm  = normalize(left_grp)
    right_norm = normalize(right_grp)

    # paint each side on its own canvas and glue them horizontally
    left_img  = paint(canvas(0, shape(left_norm)), left_norm)
    right_img = paint(canvas(0, shape(right_norm)), right_norm)
    O = trim(hconcat(left_img, right_img))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    sep = extract(palette(I),
                  lambda c: either(equality(height(box(ofcolor(I, c))), height(I)),
                                 equality(width(box(ofcolor(I, c))),  width(I)))
    cleaned = replace(I, sep, 0)
    sepcol  = leftmost(ofcolor(I, sep))

    objs = fgpartition(cleaned)

    # groups left/right of separator
    left  = merge(sfilter(objs,
                           lambda o: rightmost(o) < sepcol))
    right = merge(sfilter(objs,
                           lambda o: leftmost(o) > sepcol))

    # distance between the two groups (gap of zero columns)
    gap = subtract(leftmost(right), add(rightmost(left), ONE))

    # shift the right group left by the gap size
    shifted = shift(right, (-gap, 0))

    together = merge({left, shifted})
    O = trim(paint(canvas(0, shape(together)), together))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # ---- Global transformation ----
    # Swap every two consecutive non‑zero colors in the sorted palette.
    colors = tuple(sorted(palette(I) - {ZERO}))
    # build pairs (c0,c1),(c2,c3),...
    pairs = tuple((colors[i], colors[i + 1]) for i in range(0, len(colors) - 1, 2))
    O = I
    # perform the swaps without explicit loops using apply‑of‑pairs
    def swap(pair):
        c1, c2 = pair
        p1 = ofcolor(O, c1)
        p2 = ofcolor(O, c2)
        O1 = fill(O, c1, p2)
        O2 = fill(O1, c2, p1)
        return O2
    O = apply(swap, pairs)                # result of apply is the last grid produced
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ---- Object extraction ----
    # Move each object of the smallest non‑zero color onto the position of the
    # object of the largest non‑zero color, then erase the originals.
    nonzero = palette(I) - {ZERO}
    smallest = valmin(nonzero, lambda x: x)
    largest  = valmax(nonzero, lambda x: x)
    obj_small = ofcolor(I, smallest)
    obj_large = ofcolor(I, largest)
    # erase original objects
    O = fill(I, ZERO, obj_small)
    O = fill(O, ZERO, obj_large)
    # paint them swapped
    O = fill(O, smallest, obj_large)
    O = fill(O, largest,  obj_small)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ---- Color filtering ----
    # Keep only the two most frequent colors and exchange them,
    # everything else becomes background.
    most = mostcommon(palette(I) - {ZERO})
    least = leastcommon(palette(I) - {ZERO})
    p_most  = ofcolor(I, most)
    p_least = ofcolor(I, least)
    O = canvas(ZERO, shape(I))
    O = fill(O, most,  p_least)
    O = fill(O, least, p_most)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ---- Geometric reasoning ----
    # Mirror the grid vertically and replace each colour by the colour that
    # appears at its mirrored position; if both positions hold the same colour,
    # keep it unchanged.
    M = vmirror(I)
    O = I
    def replace_at(idx):
        r, c = idx
        mir = (r, width(I) - 1 - c)
        v1 = index(I, idx)
        v2 = index(M, idx)          # colour at mirrored cell
        return recolor(v2, {idx})    # recolor patch at idx with colour of its mirror
    O = apply(replace_at, asindices(I))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---- Relational / structural reasoning ----
    # Find every pair of touching objects of different colours and swap their colours.
    objs = fgpartition(I)
    def touch_swap(a):
        def inner(b):
            cond = adjacent(a, b) and color(a) != color(b)
            return branch(cond,
                          (lambda: fill(fill(I, color(a), b), color(b), a)),
                          (lambda: I))
        return inner
    O = I
    O = mapply(touch_swap, objs)   # each application swaps a touching pair
    return O
```

```python
    O = fill(fill(O, small1, ofcolor(O, small2)), small2, ofcolor(O, small1))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL – swap colours of any two touching objects of different colours
    objs = fgpartition(I)                 # set of all coloured objects
    def swap_with_touch(a):
        # find the first neighbour of a that touches it and has a different colour
        cand = mfilter(objs, lambda b: adjacent(a, b) and color(a) != color(b))
        nb   = first(cand)                # will be a dummy if none exist
        # perform the swap only when a neighbour exists
        return branch(cand,
                      lambda: fill(fill(I, color(a), nb), color(nb), a),
                      lambda: I)
    # apply the above to every object and merge the results
    O = mapply(swap_with_touch, objs)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ---------- OBJECT‑LEVEL – swap colours of touching objects ----------
    C = palette(I) - {ZERO}

    # for a colour, find the first different colour that touches it
    def partner(col):
        # candidates that are adjacent and different
        cand = apply(lambda d: branch(d != col and adjacent(ofcolor(I, col),
                                                          ofcolor(I, d)),
                     C)
        return first(cand)          # empty set if none

    # unordered touching pairs (c < d) – each pair appears only once
    P = apply(lambda c: branch(greater(c, partner(c)),
              lambda: (partner(c), c),
              lambda: (c, partner(c))),
              C)
    # keep only real pairs
    P = apply(lambda p: branch(p[1] in C and p[0] in C, lambda: p, lambda: ()), P)

    # perform the swaps using the original colour patches
    O = I
    def swap_pair(p):
        a, b = p
        return fill(fill(O, a, ofcolor(I, b)), b, ofcolor(I, a))
    O = apply(swap_pair, P)          # a container of grids
    O = merge(O)                      # merge the individual swaps
    return O
```

```python
    C = palette(I) - {ZERO}

    # colours that have at least one neighbour of a different colour
    def touches_other(col):

    c_b = valmin(T, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))

    O = I
    O = fill(fill(O, c_a, ofcolor(I, c_b)), c_b, ofcolor(I, c_a))
    return O
```

```python
    # ---------- GEOMETRIC – rebuild the picture on a blank canvas ----------
    # start from an empty grid
    O = canvas(ZERO, shape(I))

    C = palette(I) - {ZERO}

    O = apply(paint_swapped, C)

    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # ---------- RELATIONAL – shift each object to the place of its neighbour ----------
    # objects (connected components) of the input
    objs = fgpartition(I)

    # for a given object, find the first neighbouring object of a different colour
    def neighbour(obj):
        cand = mfilter(objs, lambda b: adjacent(obj, b) and color(b) != color(obj))
        return first(cand)

    # build a set of (source object, target object) pairs
    pairs = apply(lambda a: (a, neighbour(a)), objs)

    # swap colours by moving each source to the target position and vice‑versa
    O = I
    def swap(p):
        a, b = p
        return fill(fill(O, color(a), b), color(b), a)
    O = apply(swap, pairs)
    O = merge(O)                # combine the individual swaps
    return O
```

```python
    O = fill(fill(O, c3, ofcolor(I, c4)), c4, ofcolor(I, c3))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑LEVEL – recolour the smaller object of each touching pair to the colour
    # of the larger object (leaving the larger object unchanged)
    objs = fgpartition(I)                         # all connected components
    O = I
    # for every object, look for a touching object of a different colour
    O = apply(
        lambda a:
            let = first(
                mfilter(
                    objs,
                    lambda b: both(adjacent(a, b), color(b) != color(a))
                )
            ) in
            branch(
                let != None and size(a) < size(let),
                lambda: fill(O, color(a), let),      # recolour the smaller one
                lambda: O
            ),
        objs
    )
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # COLOR‑FILTER – keep only colours that touch at least one other colour,
    # then globally swap the two touching colours (the one with the larger
    # count becomes the other colour)
    C = palette(I) - {ZERO}
    # colours that have a neighbour of a different colour
    T = apply(
        lambda col:
            sizefilter(
                apply(
                    lambda d:
                        branch(d != col and adjacent(ofcolor(I, col), ofcolor(I, d)), {d}, frozenset()),
                    C
                ),
                1
            ) != frozenset(),
        C
    )
    # the two colours that actually touch each other (they are the only ones left)
    ca = valmax(T, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    cb = valmin(T, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    O = I
    O = fill(fill(O, ca, ofcolor(I, cb)), cb, ofcolor(I, ca))
    return O
```

```python
    # (only if the predecessor colour does not already appear)
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL – treat the colour swap as a relation between two colours:
    # the most frequent colour (source) maps to its predecessor (target)
    C   = palette(I) - {ZERO}
    mf  = valmax(C, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    dec = decrement(mf)
    rel = lambda col: dec if col == mf else col          # mapping relation
    O = branch(
            equality(colorcount(I, dec), ZERO),
            lambda: apply(
                       lambda col: replace(I, col, rel(col)),
                       C),
            lambda: I)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL – construct a colour‑swap mapping and apply it globally
    C   = palette(I) - {ZERO}
    a1  = valmax(C, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    r1  = difference(C, initset(a1))
    a2  = branch(equality(size(r1), ZERO),
                lambda: ZERO,
                lambda: valmax(r1, lambda c: colorcount(I, c)))
    r2  = difference(r1, initset(a2))
    a3  = branch(equality(size(r2), ZERO),
                lambda: ZERO,
                lambda: valmax(r2, lambda c: colorcount(I, c)))
    r3  = difference(r2, initset(a3))
    a4  = branch(equality(size(r3), ZERO),
                lambda: ZERO,
                lambda: valmax(r3, lambda c: colorcount(I, c)))

    rel = lambda col: branch(equality(col, a1), a2,
                 branch(equality(col, a2), a1,
                 branch(equality(col, a3), a4,
                 branch(equality(col, a4), a3, col))))
    O = apply(lambda col: replace(I, col, rel(col)), C)
    # apply the replacements sequentially; the last grid in the tuple is the result
    return last(O)
```

```python
    a1  = valmax(C, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # GEOMETRIC – exchange the positions of the dominant colour patches using MOVE
    C   = palette(I) - {ZERO}
    a1  = valmax(C, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
    r1  = difference(C, initset(a1))
    a2  = branch(equality(size(r1), ZERO),
                 lambda: ZERO,
                 lambda: valmax(r1, lambda c: colorcount(I, c)))
    # vector that moves a1‑patch onto a2‑patch centre
    sh12 = subtract(center(ofcolor(I, a2)), center(ofcolor(I, a1)))
    O1   = apply(lambda obj: branch(equality(color(obj), a1),
                                    move(I, obj, sh12),
                                    I),
                fgpartition(I))
    # now move a2‑patch onto the original a1 centre
    sh21 = subtract(center(ofcolor(I, a1)), center(ofcolor(I, a2)))
    O    = apply(lambda obj: branch(equality(color(obj), a2),
                                    move(O1, obj, sh21),
                                    O1),
                fgpartition(O1))

    # third / fourth colours
    r2  = difference(r1, initset(a2))
    a3  = branch(equality(size(r2), ZERO),
                 lambda: ZERO,
                 lambda: valmax(r2, lambda c: colorcount(I, c)))
    r3  = difference(r2, initset(a3))
    a4  = branch(equality(size(r3), ZERO),
                 lambda: ZERO,
                 lambda: valmax(r3, lambda c: colorcount(I, c)))
    sh34 = subtract(center(ofcolor(O, a4)), center(ofcolor(O, a3)))
    O2   = apply(lambda obj: branch(equality(color(obj), a3)),
                                    move(O, obj, sh34),
                                    O),
                fgpartition(O))
    sh43 = subtract(center(ofcolor(O, a3)), center(ofcolor(O, a4)))
    O    = apply(lambda obj: branch(equality(color(obj), a4)),
                                    move(O2, obj, sh43),
                                    O2),
                fgpartition(O2))
    return O
```

```python
    a2  = branch(equality(size(r1), ZERO), ZERO,
                  lambda: valmax(r1, lambda c: colorcount(I, c)))
    r2  = difference(r1, initset(a2))
    a3  = branch(equality(size(r2), ZERO), ZERO,
                  lambda: valmax(r2, lambda c: colorcount(I, c)))
    r3  = difference(r2, initset(a3))
    a4  = branch(equality(size(r3), ZERO), ZERO,
                  lambda: valmax(r3, lambda c: colorcount(I, c)))

    # mapping colour → its swap partner

                 branch(equality(col, a2), a1,

                      fgpartition(I))

    O = underpaint(blank, recoloured)
    return O
```

```python
    a1  = valmax(C, lambda c: colorcount(I, c))
```

```python
    def swap12(g):
        C   = palette(g) - {ZERO}
        a1  = valmax(C, lambda c: colorcount(g, c))
        r1  = difference(C, initset(a1))
        a2  = branch(equality(size(r1), ZERO), ZERO,
                    lambda: valmax(r1, lambda c: colorcount(g, c)))
        return switch(g, a1, a2)

    def swap34(g):
        C   = palette(g) - {ZERO}
        a1  = valmax(C, lambda c: colorcount(g, c))
        r1  = difference(C, initset(a1))
        a2  = branch(equality(size(r1), ZERO), ZERO,
                    lambda: valmax(r1, lambda c: colorcount(g, c)))
        r2  = difference(r1, initset(a2))
        a3  = branch(equality(size(r2), ZERO), ZERO,
                    lambda: valmax(r2, lambda c: colorcount(g, c)))
        r3  = difference(r2, initset(a3))
        a4  = branch(equality(size(r3), ZERO), ZERO,
                    lambda: valmax(r3, lambda c: colorcount(g, c)))
        return switch(g, a3, a4)

    swaps = [swap12, swap34]
    O = last(rapply(swaps, I))      # first swap the most‑frequent pair, then the second pair
    return O
```

```python
                    lambda: valmax(r1, lambda c: colorcount(g, c)))
        r2 = difference(r1, initset(a2))
        a3 = branch(equality(size(r2), ZERO), ZERO,
                    lambda: valmax(r2, lambda c: colorcount(g, c)))
        r3 = difference(r2, initset(a3))
        a4 = branch(equality(size(r3), ZERO), ZERO,
                    lambda: valmax(r3, lambda c: colorcount(g, c)))
        return switch(g, a3, a4)

    O = last(rapply([swap12, swap34], I))
    return O
```

```python
    # Global transformation: compute the minimal bounding box of all non‑zero cells
    # and flood‑fill that box with the color of the nearest seed.

    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL TRANSFORMATION – row‑wise filling based on the highest seed above
    # 1. Extract every non‑zero cell (its colour and row).
    seeds   = fgpartition(I)                                   # one‑cell objects
    # 2. For every row r produce a patch that is the whole row.
    all_rows = apply(lambda _: connect({(0, 0)}, (0, len(I[0]) - 1)),
                    interval(0, height(I), 1))
    # 3. Choose the colour of the seed with the greatest row ≤ r
    #    (argmax on the row coordinate).  If no seed is above, the first seed is used.
    colour_of_row = lambda r: color(argmax(seeds,
                       lambda s: first(toindices(s))[0] if first(toindices(s))[0] <= r else -1)
    O = apply(lambda r, p: fill(I, colour_of_row(r), p), all_rows, all_rows)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL – each seed colours all orthogonal cells that are
    # closer to it than to any other seed (Voronoi partition on the Manhattan line).
    S = fgpartition(I)
    r = lambda o: first(toindices(o))[0]
    # nearest seed for a given cell (x, y) – only the vertical distance matters
    nearest = lambda y: argmin(S,
                       lambda o: abs(r(o) - y))
    H, W = height(I), len(I[0])
    # build the Voronoi borders: every cell on the leftmost and rightmost column
    # receives the colour of its nearest seed.
    O = apply(lambda y:
               fill(I, color(nearest(y)), {(y, 0), (y, W-1)}),
               interval(0, H, 1))
    # also colour the whole row that contains a seed
    O = apply(lambda o: fill(O, color(o),
               shift(connect({(0, 0)}, (0, W-1)), (r(o), 0)), S)
    return O
```

```python
    # COLOR‑FILTERING – replace the background with the colour of the nearest seed row,
    # then keep only the two side cells for rows that are not seed rows or borders.
    S = fgpartition(I)                                   # the seed objects
    r = lambda o: first(toindices(o))[0]                  # seed row
    col_of_row = lambda y: color(argmin(S,
                           lambda o: abs(r(o) - y)))   # colour of nearest seed

    H = height(I)
    W = len(I[0])

    # start from a grid where every cell is the colour of its nearest seed row
    base = apply(
        lambda y: fill(I, col_of_row(y),

    # rows that must stay completely filled (seed rows + top & bottom)

    other_rows = difference(interval(0, H, 1), full_rows)
    O = apply(
        lambda y: fill(base,
                        col_of_row(y),
                        {(y, 0), (y, W - 1)}),
        other_rows)

    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # GLOBAL – one‑pass row‑wise rule with a conditional (branch).
    S = fgpartition(I)                                      # seed objects
    r = lambda o: first(toindices(o))[0]                     # row of a seed
    col_of_row = lambda y: color(argmin(S,
                            lambda o: abs(r(o) - y)))      # nearest seed colour

    H = height(I)
    W = len(I[0])

    seed_rows   = apply(r, S)                               # rows that contain a seed
    full_rows   = combine(combine(seed_rows,
                                   initset(0)), initset(H-1))# seed rows + top & bottom

    fill_full   = lambda y: fill(I, col_of_row(y),
                                 shift(connect((0, 0), (0, W-1)), (y, 0)))
    fill_edges  = lambda y: fill(I, col_of_row(y),
                                 {(y, 0), (y, W-1)})

    O = apply(lambda y: branch(contained(y, full_rows),
                               fill_full(y),
                               fill_edges(y)),
              interval(0, H, 1))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # COLOR‑FILTERING – paint the whole grid with the colour of the nearest
    # seed row, then restore the background (0) on the interior of the rows
    # that must not be full.
    S = fgpartition(I)
    r = lambda o: first(toindices(o))[0]
    col_of_row = lambda y: color(argmin(S,
                            lambda o: abs(r(o) - y)))

    H = height(I)
    W = len(I[0])

    # a completely filled grid where each row uses its nearest‑seed colour
    base = apply(lambda y: fill(I, col_of_row(y),
                           shift(connect((0, 0), (0, W-1)), (y, 0))),
                 interval(0, H, 1))

    seed_rows   = apply(r, S)
    full_rows   = combine(combine(seed_rows,
                                   initset(0)), initset(H-1))

    # rows that must stay full remain unchanged;
    # all other rows keep only the two side cells (the interior is set to 0)
    other_rows = difference(interval(0, H, 1), full_rows)
    O = apply(lambda y: fill(base, 0,
                             { (y, c) for c in range(1, W-1) }),
              other_rows)

    # finally, make sure the side cells keep the proper colour
    O = apply(lambda y: fill(O, col_of_row(y),
                             {(y, 0), (y, W-1)}),
              other_rows)

    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL – build a “line” object for each seed row,
    # shift it to every row, then overlay the side‑column objects.
    S = fgpartition(I)
    r = lambda o: first(toindices(o))[0]
    col_of_row = lambda y: color(argmin(S,
                            lambda o: abs(r(o) - y)))

    H = height(I)
    W = len(I[0])

    # 1️⃣ a horizontal line of length W (template)
    line = shift(connect((0, 0), (0, W-1)), (0, 0))

    # 2️⃣ place that line on every seed row, top row and bottom row
    seed_rows   = apply(r, S)
    full_rows   = combine(combine(seed_rows,
                                   initset(0)), initset(H-1))

    O = apply(lambda y: fill(I, col_of_row(y),
                             shift(line, (y, 0))),
              full_rows)

    # 3️⃣ side‑column objects (single‑cell patches)
    left  = {(y, 0) for y in range(H)}
    right = {(y, W-1) for y in range(H)}
    side  = combine(initset(left), initset(right))

    O = fill(O, 0, side)                                     # clear side cells
    O = apply(lambda y: fill(O, col_of_row(y),
                             {(y, 0), (y, W-1)}),
              interval(0, H, 1))

    return O
```

```python
    r = lambda o: first(toindices(o))[0]                 # row of a seed
    col_of_row = lambda y: color(argmin(S,

    O = canvas(0, (H, W))                                 # empty background
    O = paint(O, all_objs)                                 # paint everything at once
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑EXTRACTION – keep the original seeds and grow each of them.
    H = height(I);  W = len(I[0])
    S = fgpartition(I)
    r = lambda o: first(toindices(o))[0]
    col = lambda o: color(o)

    # start from an empty canvas
    O = canvas(0, (H, W))

    # turn every seed into a complete horizontal line of its colour
    O = apply(lambda o: fill(O, col(o),
                     shift(connect((0, 0), (0, W-1)), (r(o), 0))),
             S)

    # top border row – colour of the first seed
    first_seed = argmin(S, lambda o: r(o))
    O = fill(O, col(first_seed), shift(connect((0, 0), (0, W-1)), (0, 0))

    # bottom border row – colour of the last seed
    last_seed = argmin(S, lambda o: -r(o))
    O = fill(O, col(last_seed),
             shift(connect((0, 0), (0, W-1)), (H-1, 0)))

    # rows that are not full: keep only the side cells coloured
    rows      = interval(0, H, 1)
    full_rows = combine(combine(apply(r, S), initset(0)), initset(H-1))
    edge_rows = difference(rows, full_rows)

    O = apply(lambda y: fill(O, col(argmin(S,
                              lambda o: abs(r(o)-y))),
                     {(y, 0), (y, W-1)}),
             edge_rows)

    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # OBJECT‑EXTRACTION – turn every seed into a full horizontal line,
    # then colour the two side cells of every other row with the colour
    # of the nearest seed row.
    H = height(I); W = len(I[0])
    S = fgpartition(I)

    r   = lambda o: first(toindices(o))[0]                 # row of a seed
    col = lambda o: color(o)                               # colour of a seed

    # map each row to the colour of its nearest seed
    nearest = lambda y: color(argmin(S, lambda o: abs(r(o)-y)))

    rows      = interval(0, H, 1)
    seed_rows = apply(r, S)
    full_rows = combine(combine(seed_rows, initset(0)), initset(H-1))

    O = canvas(0, (H, W))

    # full rows (seed rows + top/bottom)
    O = apply(lambda y: fill(O, nearest(y),
                     shift(connect((0, 0), (0, W-1)), (y, 0))),
            full_rows)

    # side cells of the remaining rows
    O = apply(lambda y: fill(O, nearest(y),
                     frozenset({(y, 0), (y, W-1)})),
            difference(rows, full_rows))

    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL / STRUCTURAL – build a template line, paint all rows with the
    # colour of the nearest seed, then mask away the interior of rows that
    # must stay non‑full, finally keep only the two side cells of those rows.
    H = height(I); W = len(I[0])
    S = fgpartition(I)

    r   = lambda o: first(toindices(o))[0]
    nearest = lambda y: color(argmin(S, lambda o: abs(r(o)-y)))

    rows      = interval(0, H, 1)
    seed_rows = apply(r, S)
    full_rows = combine(combine(seed_rows, initset(0)), initset(H-1))

    # start from a blank canvas and colour every row completely
    O = canvas(0, (H, W))
    O = apply(lambda y: fill(O, nearest(y),
                     shift(connect((0, 0), (0, W-1)), (y, 0))),
            rows)

    # clear the interior of rows that are not full
    interior = lambda y: {(y, c) for c in interval(1, W-1, 1)}
    O = apply(lambda y: fill(O, 0, interior(y)),
            difference(rows, full_rows))

    side = lambda y: frozenset({(y, 0), (y, W-1)})
    O = apply(lambda y: fill(O, nearest(y), side(y)),
            difference(rows, full_rows))

    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ---- Template‑extraction / re‑projection ----------------------------------
    # 1.  Extract every non‑zero, non‑8 object (the “template”).
    # 2.  Build a single object that contains all those cells (union).
    # 3.  Compute the bounding box of the 8‑region and of the template.
    # 4.  Scale the template to the size of the 8‑region using separate
    #     vertical and horizontal up‑scales (the factors are obtained by
    #     integer division of the two dimensions).
    # 5.  Paint the scaled template over the original 8‑region.
    template_pts   = {o for o in objects(I, False, True, True) if color(o) != 8}
    template       = combine(template_objs:=template_pts)          # union of the template cells
    box8           = backdrop(ofcolor(I, 8))
    box_template   = backdrop(template)
    vfactor        = divide(height(box8),   height(box_template))
    hfactor        = divide(width(box8),   width(box_template)))   # width = shape(...)[1]
    scaled_vert    = vupscale(toobject(box_template, template), vfactor)
    scaled_horiz   = hupscale(scaled_vert, hfactor)
    cleared        = cover(I, ofcolor(I, 8))                       # erase the 8 block
    O              = paint(cleared, toobject(backdrop(ofcolor(I, 8)), scaled_horiz))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ---- Quadrant colour‑fill ---------------------------------------------------
    # 1.  Locate the whole 8‑region.
    # 2.  Split the region into four equal quadrants.
    # 3.  In each quadrant find the most frequent colour among the
    #     non‑8 objects that lie inside the same quadrant of the original grid.
    # 4.  Replace the 8‑cells of that quadrant with the colour found.
    region8   = ofcolor(I, 8)
    box8      = backdrop(region8)
    hmid      = add(leftmost(box8), divide(width(box8), 2))
    vmid      = add(uppermost(box8), divide(height(box8), 2))
    tl        = intersection(region8, box(box8, (0, 0), (vmid, hmid)))   # top‑left
    tr        = intersection(region8, box(box8, (0, hmid), (vmid, rightmost(box8))))   # top‑right
    bl        = intersection(region8, box(box8, (vmid, 0), (lowermost(box8), hmid))) # bottom‑left
    br        = intersection(region8, box(box8, (vmid, hmid), (lowermost(box8), rightmost(box8)))) # bottom‑right

    fav_color = lambda quad: mostcommon(colorfilter(objects(I, False, True, True), mostcommon(quad)))
    O = fill(fill(fill(fill(replace(I, 8, 0),
                       fav_color(tl), tl),
                   fav_color(tr), tr),
               fav_color(bl), bl),
           fav_color(br), br)
    return O
```

```python
    box8      = backdrop(region8)

    tmpl_objs = {o for o in objects(I, False, True, True) if color(o) != 8}
    tmpl      = combine(*tmpl_objs)
    box_tmpl  = backdrop(tmpl)

    # how many repeats are needed in each direction?
    hreps     = divide(width(box8),  width(box_tmpl))
    vreps     = divide(height(box8), height(box_tmpl))

    # build one long horizontal strip and then stack it vertically
    hstrip    = apply(lambda _: hconcat(tmpl, tmpl), interval(1, hreps, 1))
    tiled     = apply(lambda _: vconcat(hstrip, hstrip), interval(1, vreps, 1))

    # crop the tiling to the exact size of the 8‑box (in case of over‑repeat)
    tiled_crop= subgrid(backdrop(region8), tiled)

    cleared   = cover(I, region8)
    O         = paint(cleared, toobject(backdrop(region8), tiled_crop))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # RELATIONAL‑SHIFT‑AND‑FILL – move the template so that its centre aligns
    # with the centre of the 8‑region, then fill the 8‑mask with the aligned
    # template (the template is first normalised to the origin).
    region8   = ofcolor(I, 8)
    box8      = backdrop(region8)

    tmpl_objs = {o for o in objects(I, False, True, True) if color(o) != 8}
    tmpl      = combine(*tmpl_objs)

    # normalise both patches to the origin
    tmpl_n    = normalize(tmpl)
    box8_n    = normalize(box8)

    # compute the translation that aligns their centres
    ctmpl     = centerofmass(tmpl_n)
    c8        = centerofmass(box8_n)
    delta_c   = subtract(ctmpl, c8)

    # shift the normalised template by that delta and paint it inside the 8‑mask
    aligned   = shift(tmpl_n, delta_c)
    cleared   = cover(I, region8)
    O         = paint(cleared, toobject(backdrop(region8), aligned))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # OBJECT‑SCALING – extract the non‑8 template, stretch it to the 8‑mask size
    region8   = ofcolor(I, 8)                              # cells coloured 8
    box8      = backdrop(region8)                          # its bounding box

    # all objects except colour 8
    tmpl_objs = {o for o in objects(I, False, True, True) if color(o) != 8}
    tmpl      = merge(tmpl_objs)                           # union of those objects
    box_tmpl  = backdrop(tmpl)                             # bounding box of the template

    # extract the template as a sub‑grid (keeps background zeros)
    tmpl_grid = subgrid(box_tmpl, I)

    vfac = divide(height(box8),   height(box_tmpl))

    # erase the original 8’s and paste the resized template inside the same mask
    cleared = cover(I, region8)
    O       = paint(cleared, toobject(backdrop(region8), scaled))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # REPEATED‑TILING – tile the template until it covers the 8‑mask
    region8   = ofcolor(I, 8)
    box8      = backdrop(region8)

    tmpl_objs = {o for o in objects(I, False, True, True) if color(o) != 8}
    tmpl      = merge(tmpl_objs)
    box_tmpl  = backdrop(tmpl)

    tmpl_grid = subgrid(box_tmpl, I)

    # how many whole copies fit horizontally / vertically?
    hreps = divide(width (box8), width (box_tmpl))
    vreps = divide(height(box8), height(box_tmpl))

    # build a single horizontal strip by concatenating the template hreps times
    hstrip = apply(lambda _: hconcat(tmpl_grid, tmpl_grid), interval(1, hreps, 1))
    # the strip itself is a set of grids; concatenate them all
    hfull  = foldl(hconcat, hstrip)          # foldl is realised by successive hconcat

    # stack the horizontal strip vreps times
    vstack = apply(lambda _: vconcat(hfull, hfull), interval(1, vreps, 1))
    tiled  = foldl(vconcat, vstack)          # full tiling grid

    # crop to the exact 8‑box (in case of an extra copy)
    tiled_crop = subgrid(backdrop(region8), tiled)

    cleared = cover(I, region8)
    O       = paint(cleared, toobject(backdrop(region8), tiled_crop))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # MIRROR‑TILE‑NO‑SCALING – build a 2×2 mirrored tile of the template,
    # repeat it (by simple concatenation) until it covers the 8‑mask,
    # then cut the excess and paste it inside the mask.
    region8   = ofcolor(I, 8)
    box8      = backdrop(region8)

    # collect every non‑8 object and merge them into one picture
    tmpl_objs = {o for o in objects(I, False, True, True) if color(o) != 8}
    tmpl     = merge(tmpl_objs)
    box_tmpl = backdrop(tmpl)

    tmpl_grid = subgrid(box_tmpl, I)

    # four mirrored copies
    hmir = hmirror(tmpl_grid)
    vmir = vmirror(tmpl_grid)
    hvmir = hmirror(vmir)

    tile = vconcat(hconcat(tmpl_grid, hmir),
                   hconcat(vmir, hvmir))

    # repeat the tile horizontally and vertically enough times
    hrep = divide(width(box8), width(tile))
    vrep = divide(height(box8), height(tile))

    horz = apply(lambda _: tile, interval(0, hrep, 1))
    whole = vconcat(apply(lambda _: horz, interval(0, vrep, 1)))

    # cut to the exact size of the mask
    cut = subgrid(backdrop(whole), whole)
    bound = backdrop(cut)
    scaled = subgrid(bound, cut)               # now the same size as box8

    # move it into the mask location
    obj    = toobject(asindices(scaled), scaled)
    shifted = shift(obj, ulcorner(region8))

    cleared = cover(I, region8)
    O = paint(cleared, shifted)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # VERTICAL‑GRAVITATE‑FILL – move every non‑8 colour vertically
    # towards the 8‑mask until it touches the mask, then keep the
    # resulting picture.
    region8 = ofcolor(I, 8)
    box8    = backdrop(region8)

    # all non‑8 objects
    objs = {o for o in objects(I, False, True, True) if color(o) != 8}
    merged = merge(objs)

    # for each cell compute the direction that brings it next to the mask
    dir_to_mask = gravitate(merged, region8)

    # shift all cells by that direction (one step only – enough to become adjacent)
    moved = shift(merged, dir_to_mask)

    # keep only the part that now lies inside the mask
    inside = intersection(moved, region8)

    cleared = cover(I, region8)
    O = paint(cleared, inside)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # TILE‑TEMPLATE‑IN‑MASK – repeat the original template (without scaling)
    # as many whole times as fit inside the 8‑mask, then crop to the mask.
    region8 = ofcolor(I, 8)
    box8    = backdrop(region8)

    tmpl_objs = {o for o in objects(I, False, True, True) if color(o) != 8}
    tmpl      = merge(tmpl_objs)
    box_tmpl  = backdrop(tmpl)
    tmpl_grid = subgrid(box_tmpl, I)

    # how many repetitions fit horizontally / vertically
    hrep = divide(width(box8), width(box_tmpl))
    vrep = divide(height(box8), height(box_tmpl))

    # one horizontal row of repetitions
    row = apply(lambda _: tmpl_grid, interval(0, hrep, 1))
    tile_row = fold(row, lambda a, b: hconcat(a, b))

    # stack the rows vertically
    col = apply(lambda _: tile_row, interval(0, vrep, 1))
    tiled = fold(col, lambda a, b: vconcat(a, b))

    # cut exactly to the mask size and shift into place
    cut   = subgrid(backdrop(tiled), tiled)          # same size as tiled
    cut   = subgrid(box8, cut)                       # keep only mask extents
    obj   = toobject(asindices(cut), cut)
    shifted = shift(obj, ulcorner(region8))

    cleared = cover(I, region8)
    O = paint(cleared, shifted)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # MIRROR‑TILE‑IN‑MASK – build a 2×2 mirrored tile of the template,
    # repeat it until the mask is covered and then crop to the mask.
    region8 = ofcolor(I, 8)
    box8    = backdrop(region8)

    tmpl_objs = {o for o in objects(I, False, True, True) if color(o) != 8}
    tmpl      = merge(tmpl_objs)
    box_tmpl  = backdrop(tmpl)
    tmpl_grid = subgrid(box_tmpl, I)

    # four mirrored copies
    hmir  = hmirror(tmpl_grid)
    vmir  = vmirror(tmpl_grid)
    hvmir = hmirror(vmir)

    # assemble the basic tile
    tile = vconcat(hconcat(tmpl_grid, hmir),
                   hconcat(vmir,      hvmir))

    # repetitions needed
    hrep = divide(width(box8), width(tile))
    vrep = divide(height(box8), height(tile))

    # repeat horizontally then vertically
    hblock = apply(lambda _: tile, interval(0, hrep, 1))
    hfull  = fold(hblock, lambda a, b: hconcat(a, b))
    vblock = apply(lambda _: hfull, interval(0, vrep, 1))
    whole  = fold(vblock, lambda a, b: vconcat(a, b))

    # crop to mask size and place
    cut   = subgrid(backdrop(whole), whole)   # same size as whole
    cut   = subgrid(box8, cut)               # keep only mask area
    obj   = toobject(asindices(cut), cut)
    shifted = shift(obj, ulcorner(region8))

    cleared = cover(I, region8)
    O = paint(cleared, shifted)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # REPEAT‑TEMPLATE‑IN‑MASK – copy the original template as many whole times
    # as fit horizontally and vertically inside the mask, then crop to the mask.
    region8 = ofcolor(I, 8)
    box8    = backdrop(region8)

    tmpl_objs = {o for o in objects(I, False, True, True) if color(o) != 8}
    tmpl      = merge(tmpl_objs)
    box_tmpl  = backdrop(tmpl)
    tmpl_grid = subgrid(box_tmpl, I)

    # how many whole copies fit in each direction
    hrep = divide(width(box8), width(box_tmpl))
    vrep = divide(height(box8), height(box_tmpl))

    # build a single row of repetitions using integer up‑scaling of the row
    row_scaled = hupscale(tmpl_grid, (1, hrep))       # each cell stretched horizontally
    # now repeat that row vertically
    tiled = vupscale(row_scaled, vrep)                # each row stretched vertically

    # cut exactly to mask size and move into place
    cut   = subgrid(box8, tiled)                     # keep only mask extents
    obj   = toobject(asindices(cut), cut)
    shifted = shift(obj, ulcorner(region8))

    cleared = cover(I, region8)
    O = paint(cleared, shifted)
    return O
```

```python
    cleared = cover(I, region8)
    O = paint(cleared, shifted)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Strategy 3 – periodic tiling using vertical period
    #   Detect the vertical period of the 1‑colour objects and
    #   repeat the pattern across the whole grid by stacking copies.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    objs      = fgpartition(I, False, False, True)      # coloured objects
    single    = colorfilter(objs, mostcommon(palette(I)))# keep objects of the most common colour
    period    = vperiod(single)                         # vertical period of those objects
    tiled     = combine(*[move(I, single, (k*period, 0)) for k in range(10//period)])
    O         = combine(I, tiled)                       # merge with original grid
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Object‑wise north‑west propagation.
    #    Every non‑zero cell paints all cells that are strictly north‑west
    #    of it.  The nearest (in Chebyshev distance) source wins because
    #    the propagation is performed from the farthest offsets to the
    #    smallest offset.
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    objs   = fgpartition(I, False, False, True)                     # all coloured cells
    # list of offsets (dx,dy) = (‑k,‑k) for k = 0 … max dimension
    offs   = interval(0, maximum({height(I), width(I)}))
    # shift the whole set of objects by every offset
    shifts = apply(lambda k: move(I, objs, (-k, -k)), offs)          # tuple of grids
    # combine them starting from the largest offset → smallest (nearest)
    O      = fold(combine, shifts)                                   # fold is a helper combinator
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Fill the north‑west rectangle of each source, ordered by distance.
    #    For every coloured cell a rectangle from the origin to that cell
    #    (inclusive) is filled with its colour.  Rectangles are applied from
    #    the farthest cells to the nearest, so the nearest colour overwrites.
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    objs   = fgpartition(I, False, False, True)                     # each non‑zero cell
    # distance of a cell from the origin (Chebyshev)
    dist   = lambda o: max(position((0,0), o)[0], position((0,0), o)[1])
    # order objects by decreasing distance
    ordered = order(objs, lambda o: -dist(o))
    # for each object create its bounding‑box patch and recolour it
    patches = apply(lambda o: recolor(color(o), backdrop(o)), ordered)
    # overlay all patches
    O      = fold(combine, patches)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Gravitate every coloured cell one step towards the top‑left corner.
    #    The direction is computed once for the whole set of dominant‑colour
    #    cells and then applied uniformly.
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    dominant = mostcommon(palette(I))                     # dominant colour
    srcs     = ofcolor(I, dominant)                       # its cells
    dir      = gravitate(srcs, initset((0, 0)))            # direction to (0,0)
    O        = move(I, srcs, dir)                         # shift them one step
    return O
```

#### DSL

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Replicate the pattern formed by the most common colour using its
    #    vertical period.  The pattern is tiled vertically, then merged.
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    objs        = fgpartition(I, False, False, True)                     # all objects
    commoncol   = mostcommon(palette(I))                                 # most common colour
    commonobjs  = colorfilter(objs, commoncol)                            # objects of that colour
    period      = vperiod(commonobjs)                                     # vertical period
    reps        = interval(0, divide(height(I), period))                  # how many repeats
    tiles       = apply(lambda k: move(I, commonobjs, (k*period, 0)), reps)
    tiled       = fold(combine, tiles)                                   # whole tiling
    O           = combine(I, tiled)                                      # overlay on original
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # 1️⃣  Propagation by north‑west shifting of all coloured cells.
    #    Objects are moved by (‑k,‑k) for every k and over‑laid.
    maxd   = maximum({height(I), width(I)})
    offs   = interval(0, maxd + 1)                     # 0 … maxd
    # shift the whole set of coloured objects by each offset
    shifted = apply(lambda k: move(I, fgpartition(I), (-k, -k)), offs)
    # combine from farthest to nearest so the nearest colour overwrites
    O      = fold(combine, shifted)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # 2️⃣  Build a north‑west rectangle for each non‑zero cell.
    #    The rectangle is the bounding box of the cell together with (0,0).
    nonzero = difference(palette(I), initset(0))
    # one patch per coloured cell
    cells   = apply(lambda c: ofcolor(I, c), nonzero)
    # rectangle from origin to the cell (inclusive)
    rects   = apply(lambda p: recolor(color(p), backdrop(combine(p, initset((0, 0))))), cells)
    # farthest rectangles first → nearest colour wins
    O       = fold(combine, rects)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # 5️⃣  Replicate the pattern by tiling the north‑west‑filled version.
    #    First compute the full propagation (as in dsl1), then tile it
    #    vertically according to the grid height.
    full    = dsl1(I)                                      # full north‑west propagation
    period  = vperiod(ofcolor(full, mostcommon(palette(full))))  # vertical period of the result
    reps    = interval(0, divide(height(I), period) + 1)
    tiles   = apply(lambda k: move(full, ofcolor(full, mostcommon(palette(full))), (k * period, 0)), reps)
    O       = fold(combine, tiles)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # --- Build a rectangle from the origin to each coloured cell independently ---
    nonzero = difference(palette(I), initset(0))          # all colours except 0
    # for every colour c produce a rectangle that covers (0,0) … every cell of colour c
    rects   = apply(

                                    initset((0, 0))         # the origin cell
                                )
                            )
                         ),
                nonzero)
    O = fold(combine, rects)                           # farthest rectangles first → nearest colour wins
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # --- Propagation via repeated “cover” of the blank canvas ---
    blank   = canvas(0, shape(I))                         # empty grid of same size
    maxd    = maximum({height(I), width(I)})
    offs    = interval(0, maxd + 1, 1)
    # start from a blank canvas and repeatedly cover it with a shifted copy
    O = fold(lambda acc, k: cover(acc, move(I, fgpartition(I), (-k, -k))), 
             apply(lambda k: k, offs),                     # the list of offsets is the iterable for fold
             init=blank)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl5(I):
    # Relational/structural reasoning: move all cells that are NOT the
    # most common colour towards the cluster of the most common colour.
    main_col   = mostcommon(I)
    main_patch = ofcolor(I, main_col)
    other_patch = difference(ofcolor(I, main_col), main_patch)
    direction   = gravitate(other_patch, main_patch)
    moved       = move(I, other_patch, direction)
    # paint the main colour patch first, then the moved other cells
    O = paint(paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), main_patch), moved)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl1(I):
    # STRUCTURAL REASONING – fill both diagonals of every coloured cell.
    # Directions for the four diagonal rays.
    dr  = astuple( 1,  1)   # down‑right
    ul  = astuple(-1, -1)   # up‑left
    dl  = astuple( 1, -1)   # down‑left
    ur  = astuple(-1,  1)   # up‑right

    # All indices of the input grid.
    all_idx = asindices(I)

    # For each index, produce the union of the four diagonal rays that
    # pass through it (including the index itself).
    def diag_union(p):
        return union(
                union(shoot(p, dr), shoot(p, ul)),
                union(shoot(p, dl), shoot(p, ur))
        )

    # Apply the above to every coloured cell (value > 0) and collect the
    # coloured points together with their original colour.
    coloured = apply(lambda p: recolor(index(I, p), diag_union(p)),
                     difference(all_idx, ofcolor(I, 0)))

    # Start from a blank canvas and paint every coloured point.
    O = paint(canvas(0, shape(I)), colored_union(coloured))
    return O
```

```python
    # ---------- Global transformation ----------
    # Trim a uniform border (if any) and then restore the original size.
    # Here the transformation is effectively the identity, but it uses
    # a global‑scale operation (trim) followed by a reverse operation
    # (canvas + vconcat + hconcat) to keep the grid size unchanged.
```

```python
    # ---------- Geometric reasoning ----------
    # Re‑centre the two coloured objects on the centre of mass of all
    # non‑777 cells.  The offset needed to move the centre of mass to the
    # origin is subtracted from each object's coordinates.

    offset  = subtract((0, 0), com)               # vector that brings com to (0,0)

    # erase original coloured cells

    # paint the re‑centred objects
    O = fill(O, 2, shift(ofcolor(I, 2), offset))
    O = fill(O, 5, shift(ofcolor(I, 5), offset))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ----------- Colour filtering – swap colours on even/odd checkerboard ----------
    twos   = ofcolor(I, 2)
    fives  = ofcolor(I, 5)

    # erase both colours
    O = fill(I, 7, twos)
    O = fill(O, 7, fives)

    # cells on even (row+col) keep colour 2, odd keep colour 5
    even_cells = apply(lambda p: p if even(add(p[0], p[1])) else frozenset(), twos)
    odd_cells  = apply(lambda p: p if not even(add(p[0], p[1])) else frozenset(), fives)

    O = fill(O, 2, combine(even_cells))
    O = fill(O, 5, combine(odd_cells))
    return O
```

```python
    # Global – move all non‑7 cells so that their combined centre of mass
    # coincides with the centre of the grid.
    non7      = combine(ofcolor(I, 2), ofcolor(I, 5))
    com       = centerofmass(non7)
    grid_c    = (height(I)//2, width(I)//2)

    moved     = shift(non7, offset)
    O = fill(I, 7, non7)          # erase original coloured cells
    O = fill(O, mostcolor(O), moved)
    return O
```

```python
def dsl2(I):
    # ---------- Object‑wise – edge‑to‑edge packing ----------
    # place the two objects next to each other without overlap
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, 2)
    obj5 = ofcolor(I, 5)

    # horizontal data
    l2 = leftmost(obj2)          # left edge of 2
    r2 = rightmost(obj2)         # right edge of 2
    l5 = leftmost(obj5)          # left edge of 5
    r5 = rightmost(obj5)         # right edge of 5

    # vertical data
    t2 = uppermost(obj2)         # top edge of 2
    b2 = lowermost(obj2)        # bottom edge of 2
    t5 = uppermost(obj5)         # top edge of 5
    b5 = lowermost(obj5)        # bottom edge of 5

    # decide whether the objects are separated mainly horizontally or vertically
    horiz_gap = subtract(l5, r2)                     # distance from 2‑right to 5‑left
    vert_gap  = subtract(t5, b2)                     # distance from 2‑bottom to 5‑top

    # choose the smaller absolute gap and compute the shift needed for the left / top object
    shift2 = branch(
        less(equal(abs(horiz_gap[0] + horiz_gap[1]), abs(vert_gap[0] + vert_gap[1]))),
        subtract(l5, add(r2, (1, 0))),               # horizontal packing: move 2 rightwards
        subtract(t5, add(b2, (0, 1)))                # vertical packing: move 2 downwards
    )
    # the opposite object moves by the negative of this vector
    shift5 = negate(shift2)

    O = fill(I, 7, combine(obj2, obj5))
    O = fill(O, 2, shift(obj2, shift2))
    O = fill(O, 5, shift(obj5, shift5))
    return O
```

```python
def dsl3(I):
    # ---------- Colour‑filtering – keep only perimeter cells ----------
    # each colour is reduced to its outline; interior cells become background
    def outline(patch):
        return difference(patch, interior(patch))

    obj2 = ofcolor(I, 2)
    obj5 = ofcolor(I, 5)

    outline2 = outline(obj2)
    outline5 = outline(obj5)

    O = fill(I, 7, combine(obj2, obj5))      # erase original colours
    O = fill(O, 2, outline2)                  # repaint only the 2‑outline
    O = fill(O, 5, outline5)                  # repaint only the 5‑outline
    return O
```

```python
def dsl4(I):
    # ---------- Geometric – mirror each object across the line joining the two centres ----------
    obj2 = ofcolor(I, 2)
    obj5 = ofcolor(I, 5)

    c2 = centerofmass(obj2)
    c5 = centerofmass(obj5)

    # line direction from 2 to 5
    dir_vec = subtract(c5, c2)

    # mirror a patch across a line defined by a direction vector and a point
    def mirror_across(patch, centre, vec):
        # reflect each cell: p' = centre + reflect(p‑centre)
        # reflect by swapping the component parallel to vec with its negative
        # (implemented with cmirror after rotating the grid so that vec becomes horizontal)
        rot = cmirror(shift(patch, negate(centre)))   # rotate 90° to align with axis
        mirrored = vmirror(rot)
        return shift(mirrored, centre)

    mir2 = mirror_across(obj2, c2, dir_vec)
    mir5 = mirror_across(obj5, c5, dir_vec)

    O = fill(I, 7, combine(obj2, obj5))
    O = fill(O, 2, mir2)
    O = fill(O, 5, mir5)
    return O
```
